### 36. Author-list splitting protects balanced parentheses and a closed environment

**Rule.** `split_tokens` (`latexml_engine/src/base_utilities/tokens.rs:96`, Perl's `SplitTokens`,
Base_Utility.pool.ltxml) does not cut at a delimiter (`,`, ` and `, `\and`, `\quad`, …) inside balanced `(…)`
(`paren_close_offset`, :39; an unbalanced `(` is an ordinary token, so it cannot swallow a later `\\`), as it already
did not inside braces and math; nor inside an environment whose `\end{name}` follows (`environment_closes_ahead`,
`frontmatter/classify/preprocess.rs:233`). **Perl** protects braces and math only, so `\author{Alessio Martini\\(Scuola
Normale Superiore, Pisa)\\…}` gave a second `<personname>Pisa)`. The parentheses are the unambiguous signal; a bare
comma or ` and ` in an affiliation (`MIT, Cambridge`) and `Lastname, Firstname` stay Perl's over-split.
- A cut by meaning keeps the rule (`inside_balanced_parens`, tokens.rs:56): an affiliation list's cut at the kernel's
  `\and` (`classify::affiliation_lines`, `classify/separators.rs:247`) leaves beamer's `\inst{1}Univ A (North \and
  South)` one entry (#48). An alignment environment around the names' lines is read in the frontmatter pipeline
  (`trailing_alignment_as_lines`, `observer/resolver/mod.rs:449`; #980).
- A delimiter also matches an alias of its own definition (Perl's `Equals`, Token.pm:321-327, compares catcode and
  name only): `\AND` `\let` to `\and` splits as `\and`; a delimiter `\let` to another command (an `\and` a
  `\maketitle` disabled to `\relax`) matches itself alone (`delimiter_token_matches`, tokens.rs:77).
- Witnesses: 0804.0870 (`(Scuola Normale Superiore, Pisa)`), hep-ex0007011 (`(On behalf of the H1 and ZEUS
  collaborations)`), 2609.01563, 2609.17357, 2609.33831 (an environment), 2609.15009.
- Guard: `perfect_kernel_batch61::frontmatter_digest_cluster_2609` (the alias guard
  `perfect_kernel_batch59::relax_aliases_do_not_split_a_late_author` was deleted at DEL1; its shape is unguarded).

*Live rule: OD #993.*

### 48. Author heuristic splits font-wrapped name lists; affiliation "and" preserved

**Decision:** the superscript-marker author/affiliation heuristic
(`\lx@add@authors`, Base_Utility.pool) gains two beyond-Perl corrections
in the "author" arm (`split_author_line`):

1. **Font-wrapped name lists are split per-author.** When a line
   classified as authors is a single whole-line font wrapper
   `\textbf{A$^1$, B$^1$, C$^1$}`, the separating commas are
   brace-hidden, so `SplitTokens` (which skips delimiters inside `{…}`)
   collapses the wrapper into ONE creator that then hoards every `$^n$`
   marker as a duplicate affiliation. We detect the whole-line wrapper
   (`whole_line_cs_wrapper`), split the inner list, and re-apply the
   wrapper to each name so every author is its own creator with the
   correct single affiliation.
2. **Affiliation names keep their "and".** The literal word " and " is
   removed from the line-level `author_affil_splits` (Perl includes it)
   and applied only in the author arm. That split runs BEFORE
   author/affiliation classification, so on the mixed block it shredded
   institution names — "Princeton Language **and** Intelligence" →
   "Princeton Language" + "Intelligence, …" rejoined without a space.
   Authors written "Alice and Bob" still split, because " and " is a
   name separator inside `split_author_line`. (An affiliation list's
   lines are cut by the same list since P6d, which folded the former
   `affil_splits` into `author_affil_splits`, and first at the kernel's
   `\and` by meaning since P6f, `classify::affiliation_lines`: a
   document's macro holding it or a `\csname and\endcsname` cuts as the
   spelled `\and`, the line after it an entry of its own. The cut by
   meaning keeps #36's parentheses rule (`tokens::inside_balanced_parens`),
   and runs its rehearsal only where the list holds a `\csname`, a
   kernel-`\and` copy no spelling matches or a macro no binding made
   (`observer::may_hold_kernel_separator`; P6f2, revP6f S1/S2). A `\let`
   copy of the current `\and` is cut by spelling (`delimiter_token_matches`)
   and, since P6f, starts an entry (`classify::parts_entries`).)

**Why:** arXiv 2605.00347 (colm2026 class) lists 13 authors across three
`\textbf{…}` lines with `$^{1,2,3,*}$` affiliation markers. Perl and the
pre-fix Rust both lumped the two bold lines into 2 mega-creators, each
carrying 3–5 copies of the "Princeton…" affiliation, and dropped the
"and". Post-fix the assignment exactly matches the PDF: ¹→11 authors,
²→Lu, ³→Yang, \*→the three equal-contributors, one affiliation each.
Perl is broken the same way (confirmed same-host); surpass-Perl scope,
user-directed 2026-07-05. Unit tests: `author_split_tests` in
base_utilities/author_split_tests.rs.

**63z extension.** The descent applies to each piece of a names line, not only a whole line: a wrapper — a command over
its last braced argument (`\textbf`, `\scalebox{.9}`, `\href{url}`) or a group opening with declarations — holding two or
more names with only marks and notes after it (`\textbf{A$^1$, B$^2$}\thanks{…}`, 2303.16563). A separator at a
wrapper's edge or a wrapper holding only one (`\textbf{Name,}`, `{\rm and}`) is moved out first; one in math, a script
argument or a mark's argument stays put. An author argument that is one parameterless macro is read through its body (a
`\newif` toggle's branch taken). KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #552.

*Live rule: OD #993.*

### 52. Structured author↔affiliation recovery from abused frontmatter idioms

**Decision:** Two beyond-Perl hardenings of `\lx@add@authors` / `\lx@add@thanks`
(`base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_fields.rs`) that recover *structured* author/affiliation metadata from
two idioms arXiv authors routinely abuse, where both Perl LaTeXML and a literal
port emit garbage. Both are **surpass-Perl divergences** (same-host Perl
reproduces the bad output — witnesses below), authorized under the
PDF-fidelity/beyond-Perl policy.

**(a) `\thanks`-abuse → affiliations.** `\thanks` is semantically an
acknowledgement footnote, but authors smuggle affiliations into it, linked to
authors by a leading superscript mark:
`\thanks{$^{1}$Univ. Bordeaux… $^{2}$School… $^{3}$Instituto…}`. Because
`\lx@add@thanks` reads its content **Semiverbatim** (faithful to Perl
`Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:661` — it protects `~ # % &` in URL/email-bearing
notes), `$^{1}$` freezes to catcode-*other* and surfaces as a literal `$^1$` in
one opaque `role="thanks"` blob (witness arXiv:2606.00313). The fix keys off a
**leading NUMERIC superscript mark as the abuse signature**
(`starts_with_affiliation_mark` — content begins with `$^1…`/`$^{1}…`/
`\textsuperscript{1}…`): affiliation linking is by *number*, so a digit mark is
the reliable signal. Crucially this **excludes footnote-symbol marks**
(`$^*$`, `$^\dagger$`, `$^\ddagger$`, `$^\S$`) and lettered marks — those head
*legitimate* acknowledgements (corresponding-author, equal-contribution,
present-address notes) that must stay `role=thanks`; re-routing them would
create an affiliation that fails to link and could be discarded, silently losing
the note (an early "any superscript" heuristic did exactly this — caught in
review). When the numeric signature fires we re-tokenize with normal catcodes,
split the blob at each embedded mark (`split_before_affiliation_marks` — the
marks, not `\\`, delimit the entries; a mark is only a boundary when preceded by
whitespace, so a superscript *inside* an institution name like "Center for
R$^2$ Studies" does not split it), and feed each segment through the existing
`\lx@affiliation@withsup` machinery, which sets the `affiliation:N` label that
the authors' own marks *already* request (`relocate_annotations` then links
author↔affiliation). Every non-numeric-mark `\thanks` stays the parity-faithful
Semiverbatim contact, byte-identical. This detects the abuse without a class
allow-list — the numeric mark generalizes across `ieeeconf`, generic `article`,
springer, etc.

**(b) NeurIPS comma-address → fake authors/emails.** The no-marker author
heuristic split author *groups* on `author_splits()`, which (like Perl's
`@authorsplits`, `Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:679`) **includes the comma**. A
multi-part address then shreds at its commas into fake authors —
`\author{… Nam Q. Le \\ Johns Hopkins…, Laurel, MD 20723 \\ \texttt{…@jhuapl.edu} \and …}`
produced personnames "Laurel", "MD 20723" and mislabeled the email as an
affiliation (witness arXiv:2606.00315). The fix splits groups on the `\and`
family / `\quad` only (`author_group_splits()` — comma excluded); within a group
the first `\\`-line is the name list (comma/" and "-split by `split_author_line`,
so "Alice, Bob" still separates) and each remaining `\\`-line is an affiliation
attached to the group's last author. A bare `user@host` line (visible text has
`@` and no whitespace — institution names always have spaces; `line_is_email`)
is relabeled `role="email"`. Simple shapes (`A \and B`, `A, B, C`, `A, B \\ MIT`)
are unchanged; an empty `\\`-leading name list keeps a single empty author so its
affiliations are not dropped. `author_affil_splits()` already carried the comment
"NO comma in affiliations!!!"; this extends that discipline to the no-marker arm.

**(c) Short author names in a marker-labeled line.** The marker-labeled arm
classifies each `\quad`/`\\`-split line as author vs affiliation by where its
superscript sits. The original proxy — a marker within the first 8 tokens ⇒
affiliation ("¹CMU") — misread a **short author name** whose trailing mark landed
under the threshold: "Min Xu" is 7 tokens, so `Min Xu\textsuperscript{1}` was
demoted to an affiliation and the author lost (witness arXiv:2606.08234,
html_feedback#6614). Replaced by the length-independent signal
`name_precedes_marker`: a line reads "Name\textsuperscript{n}" (letter text
before the marker ⇒ author, split into creators) or "\textsuperscript{n}Affil"
(the marker leads the line ⇒ affiliation). Here Rust surpasses Perl, which keeps
the four authors but ALSO emits the affiliation line itself as phantom author
creators.

**(d) Multi-line author block with a trailing `\quad\\`.** In the no-marker arm,
author *groups* split on `\quad`/`\and` and each group then splits on `\\` into a
name line + trailing affiliations. When a line ends with `\quad \\` (a common
NeurIPS/ACL idiom for wrapping a long author list), the `\\` leaks to the HEAD of
the next `\quad`-group, so that group's first `\\`-piece is empty and its real
first author was demoted to an affiliation under an empty `<personname/>`. Fixed by
dropping empty `\\`-pieces before choosing the name line: the first NON-empty piece
is the names, the rest affiliations. Witness arXiv:2507.06670 (acl): line 2's first
author "Ruiqi Li" was an empty personname + a bogus "Ruiqi Li" affiliation; now an
author. Same-host Perl 0.8.8 mangles it identically (SHARED-FAILURE) — recorded as
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #91.
**(e) Phantom empty creators from comma-split `\IEEEmembership`/`\thanks`.** A flat
comma author list with interspersed non-name commands — `\author{Alice,
\IEEEmembership{…}, and Bob, …\thanks{…}}` (html_feedback#4539, witness 2508.00603) —
comma/" and "-splits into pieces where the `\IEEEmembership{…}` pieces digest to
nothing, surfacing as empty `<ltx:personname/>` creators; a trailing `\thanks` then
strands its affiliation/email on a nameless creator, and the reader sees a stray "`,
,`" between authors. `insert_frontmatter`'s `coalesce_empty_creators` drops
name-empty author creators, moving any contacts they carry to the preceding real
author (a `\footnotemark`-note keeps a personname non-empty, so real authors with a
marker — 2507.06670 "Yu Zhang" — are untouched). Same-host Perl 0.8.8 emits the same
empty creators (SHARED-FAILURE); Rust surpasses. Guard:
`06_cluster_frontmatter::frontmatter_ieee_membership_no_phantom`. When no named author is
left to take them, the first nameless creator carrying any keeps them all (#949), never
dropping a printed word.

**(f) Multiple `\textsuperscript{n}Affil` on one space-separated affiliation line.** A
marker-led affiliation line may carry several numbered institutions with only spaces
between them — `\textsuperscript{1}University A \textsuperscript{2}University B`
(html_feedback#6242, arXiv:2510.02340). The marker-branch classified the whole line as
ONE affiliation, merging both (and attaching them to a single author). Now the line is
split at each whitespace-preceded mark (reusing `split_before_affiliation_marks`, the
`\thanks`-abuse splitter — which by construction never breaks a superscript glued
INSIDE an institution name, e.g. "Center for R$^2$ Studies"), so each numbered
institution becomes its own affiliation and `relocate_annotations` attaches it to the
authors bearing that number. Perl produces no structured creators for this superscript
idiom at all, so Rust already surpasses; this refines the surpass. Guard:
`06_cluster_frontmatter::frontmatter_multi_affil_superscript`. (Residual, separate: when
a `\texttt{…}` email is glued to the last affil with no `\\`, it still bleeds into that
affiliation — a distinct email-boundary defect.)
The same split runs in `affiliation_calls`' marked branch (62zk), the affiliation-list path of
`\lx@add@affiliations` (iopart `\address`, beamer `\institute`, llncs, ijcai), the class stores
(`\lx@add@store@affiliations`), the author-block tail (frontmatter_stores.rs) and
`\lx@add@affiliation@marked` (informs `\AFF`): a line that starts with a mark is split at each
whitespace-preceded mark, where the last mark had labelled the whole line (`$^1$Univ A; $^2$Univ B`
gave author 1 nothing and author 2 both; 2609.21347, 22690); a line with text before its first mark
(`Present address: $^2$Univ C`) stays whole. `trim_trailing_separator` drops a trailing `;` as well
as a trailing `,`. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch61::{marked_affiliation_lines_split_at_their_marks,
informs_author_marks_link_affiliations}`.
In the same marked branch an unmarked line continues the affiliation before it, its `\\` put back
(`$^1$Department\\University` is one affiliation; each line had been its own, the unmarked ones placed by position —
2609.19448), as an unmarked line continues an entry in `\lx@add@authors` — not across `\and`, which ends an entry there
too (#52(g)), nor a line opening with a footnote symbol (`* Equal contribution`, `$\dagger$ …`, `\dag …`), a legend
for the whole block (llncs `\institute`, 2609.06094); a line of addresses goes through `email_line_calls`, which
both paths now share, placed as #52(j) says. A declaration opening a line (`\large`, `\color{blue}`; only the NFSS
selectors and `\color` take brace arguments — `\textbf{Ann}` is content) is no text before its mark. The splitter cuts only outside groups, and a line opening with a font
command or a group that holds the marks (`\textit{$^1$A, $^2$B}`, `{\small …}`, `{\color{blue} $^1$A, …}`,
`\small{$^1$A, $^2$B}. Email: …`) is split inside it, the wrapper (a group with its opening declarations and their
arguments) repeated on each piece and what follows split at its own marks; a `\thanks{…}` wrapper is unwrapped, its
mark-led content being the affiliation list as in `\lx@add@thanks` (`split_wrapped_affiliation_marks`,
`marker_leads`, 62zl; 2609.00995, 24896). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch61::{marked_affiliation_continuation_lines_stay_with_it,
marked_affiliations_inside_a_font_group_keep_the_font, marked_affiliation_wrappers_and_legends,
marked_affiliation_review_shapes}`.

**(g) `\and` is a HARD author boundary in the superscript-marker branch.** The
marker-branch flat-split `\and`/`\quad`/`\\` into one list, then appended any
marker-less line to the PREVIOUS entry. When a 2nd/3rd author's superscript is
macro-delivered — `Alice\mk$^*$ \and Bob\mk \and Carol\mk`, where `\mk` expands to a
`$^…$` marker so `Bob\mk`/`Carol\mk` carry no *literal* `^` — those segments merged
back across the `\and` into one `<personname>AliceBobCarol</personname>`
(html_feedback#1021 F2 residual, arXiv:2403.11905). Now the branch groups on the `\and`
family FIRST and only appends a marker-less line to an entry created WITHIN the same
`\and` group, so `\and`-separated authors never merge. Groups carry no `\and`, so the
intra-group split (reusing `author_affil_splits`) is equivalent to splitting on
`\quad`/`\\`; the *only* behavior change is that a marker-less first line of a non-first
`\and` group becomes a new author instead of merging — verified by an OLD-vs-NEW full-XML
diff over all 30 frontmatter fixtures, exactly ONE (this case) changed. Guard:
`06_cluster_frontmatter::frontmatter_and_hard_author_boundary`. (Residual, separate —
deferred as Phase 2: a marker delivered *purely* by macro with no literal `^` anywhere on
its line, e.g. `\handPointerZ Johns Hopkins University`, is still appended to the author
name rather than recognized as an affiliation, because classification keys on a literal
marker and does not expand macros. So arXiv:2403.11905's Kate Sanders now separates from
Kevin Xu but still carries her institution in the name; full attachment needs
expansion-aware marker detection.)
**(h) authblk `\author{A, B, C}` comma list splits into separate creators.** authblk's
`\author` routes a no-`\and` argument to `\lx@add@creator` (a single creator), so a
comma list `\author{Alice One, Bob Two, Carol Three}` was kept as ONE
`<personname>Alice One, Bob Two, Carol Three</personname>` (html_feedback#6255,
googledeepmind). The DEFAULT `\author` already routes to `\lx@add@authors`, which splits
a comma / " and " list into separate creators via `split_author_line`. authblk's
`\author` now routes to `\lx@add@authors` too when the argument has a top-level comma (or
`\and`), so the comma list resolves to individual creators — matching the default and the
PDF. A single name that legitimately contains a comma ("Smith, Jr.") is mis-split, but
that is the pre-existing #52 comma tradeoff the default `\author` already makes, not a new
divergence; the label and single-name (no-comma) authblk paths stay Perl-faithful. Guard:
`06_cluster_frontmatter::frontmatter_authblk_comma_list`.

**Batch 108a: every separator the kernel's author read parts a block at reaches it.** An unlabelled authblk `\author`
with no `\and`, comma, "and" word or end mark was one name: `A\thanks{…} \qquad B\thanks{…} \qquad C\thanks{…}` one
`personname` holding the three, every note after it, each note's author lost; `A\thanks{…}\\ Dept. of Physics` the name
`ADept. of Physics`. Perl's authblk has the single creator too (`\and`/`\And` only, authblk.sty.ltxml:52-55); plain
`article` parted them. `authblk_sty::has_separated_names` now routes to `\lx@add@authors@list` when
`has_author_block_separator` finds two non-empty pieces: `normalize_hspace_separators` (so `\hspace`, `\hfill`, a spacing
run, `$\qquad$` count, and the space a name sets before its own note or `\footnotemark` does not, `own_marks_end`:
`Zhengyi Han\hspace{0.1em}\protect\footnotemark[1]`, 2609.40220, in plain `article` too, a creator of the mark alone) then
`split_tokens` at
`author_group_splits` and `author_affil_splits`' line breaks, which skips notes, groups and math; a group or font command
around the whole is transparent, as for the "and" word. No `\thanks` boundary is a separator (simulated on 64 papers: 6-7
wrong, none fixed whole). What the kernel read then does with a line is article's, including its misreadings:
`Dr.\quad Ann Able`, `Ann Able\quad Ph.D.` and `J.\hspace{1pt}Smith` part as two (0 real cases in about 54k papers; RED
`authblk_title_suffix_one_name` (green since ST1), `authblk_small_hspace_in_name` (green since ST1)). Witnesses: 2610.06709 (`\qquad`), 2610.18435 (`\hspace{2.5em}`), 2610.28573 (`\quad\quad`),
2610.06737, 2610.23936, 2605.10201 (one creator → 8, its legends read); 2609.17614, 2303.15964, 1509.08403, 2610.10873
(`\\`); 2609.29752, 2610.11655, 2610.13276, 2610.24224 (the mark no creator); unchanged 2610.39888, 2610.04525,
2610.19494, 2610.17900, 2610.03185. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch108a`; updated
`perfect_kernel_batch77n::{authblk_mark_before_a_line_stays_in_place, authblk_glued_symbols_in_one_author_block}`, which
pinned the line inside the name and the merge.

**Batch 108a round 2 (review rev108a): an Error goes only because the output became right.**
- *A line under the names that reads as a name.* The kernel's read gives it to the names above as their affiliation
  (Perl's first-line rule), so the new route silenced the merged Error with a false attribution: 2610.38214's "Stefano
  Soatto" an affiliation of the other eleven. No word tells such a line from an organization: `\\ Waymo LLC` (2404.19531),
  `\\ Physical Intelligence` (2505.23705), `\\ UC San Diego` (2601.06328), `\\ World Agents` (2610.37518), `\\ Welo Data`
  (2610.27304) stand under rows of names exactly so, so `row_of_names` is unchanged and a lone last row is not read as
  names by its place. The rule, authblk's only (`rows::lines_under_names_read_as_names`: every line under the names a name
  by its words, styled as the names line, no address, link, note or mark, no mixed-case acronym): with an `\affil` next the
  block's institution is printed there, so each line is more names (`authblk_sty::lines_of_names_before_affil`, the line
  breaks written `\quad`); otherwise `has_separated_names` declines and the argument stays one name, base's output with
  the `merged_creators` Error counted (`Ann Able\\ Bob Baker`, `Ann Able\quad Bob Baker\\ Cat Cole`, `Ann Able\\ Google
  DeepMind`). A line with an institution word, an acronym (`Meta AI`), an address, or other markup still goes under the
  names. Plain `article` keeps Perl's silent reading.
- *The `\affil` run.* `run:N` counts the queued authors; the writer may part a queued author the kernel welded (`Ann
  Able$^*$ \\ Bob Baker$^*$ \\ Cat Cole$^\dagger$`), which took the first name out of the run (2609.33075). The cap now ends
  a run only between two `\author` calls (`Resolver::record_run`, `RCreator::source`), and `repart::plan`'s `same_run`
  lets such a run reach the parted names.
- *A glued mark.* `split_glued_symbol` reads symbol-first too (`\textsuperscript{*1}`, 2505.22662, whose `*1` was lost
  silently on the comma route as well); `glued_marks` parts a list (`$^{1,2*}$`, `$^{*1,2}$`) and writes marks and symbols
  in the order they print. An unanswered mark shows before a symbol written after it (`show_unanswered_marks`, by the
  order of `_annotations`: 2610.07087's `1*` read `*1`). A glued mark that leads a line labels it by its number
  (`glued_line_marks_as_marks`: `$^{*1}$Kyoto University`, 2606.23258; `$^{1*}$Univ X` read "* Univ X"). A composite mark
  no entry answers and nothing shows is counted (`count_lost_marks`, `Warning:frontmatter:unanswered_mark_lost`: `$^{a-b}$`);
  a label keyed by a macro's spelling is not, nothing saying what it prints.
- *A piece with no name is no person* (as the marked path's address rule, rev97a S1, OD #944). In the unmarked read an
  address-only piece or line (`rows::address_only_line`) is a line under the names before it, a row's addresses one list
  (`Xinyu Wu \quad Jiansong Deng\\ \texttt{xinyu97@…}\quad \texttt{dengjs@…}`, 2609.02424; also plain `article`, `\{manning`
  a creator on 2505.13898), and what follows it stays under the row unless a space-parted row of names goes on (`\\ Princeton
  Language and Intelligence`, 2606.11499; `\\ {\it DeepMind Paris, France}`, 2201.12909). Before any name it waits for the first
  name; with none in the call it is a nameless author's contact. A link printing a bare address over an address line names
  the block (`{\LARGE \href{https://sherpa.ai/}{Sherpa.ai}}\\ research@sherpa.ai`, 2609.25082). A piece printing only an
  icon is the name's before it (`rows::names_no_one`: `Ann Able\quad\orcidlink{…}`); a macro may print a name, so `\AuthorOne
  \quad \AuthorTwo` stays two.
- *An empty mark.* `\affil{\textsuperscript{}~UCLA \quad \textsuperscript{2}~Northwestern…}` (2505.14999): the first piece, no
  mark, is the block's (`unmarked_before_carried_marks`; ruling R12), the marked rest goes by its marks: UCLA is not on
  `Luo$^2$`. An author whose number no line answers keeps it shown.

**Batch 108a round 3 (review rev108a2): a glyph and an order stay as written; a line or an address its author's block owns
stays there.**
- *The glyph (charter §4).* A star glued to a mark in math shows the `∗` it prints, its key `*` (`symbols::keepsup_in_math`):
  `$^{1,2*}$`, `$^{1*}$` (2505.11121, 2202.12090, 2306.07841); `\textsuperscript{1,2*}` keeps its text `*`. A lone `$^{*}$`
  keeps base's text `*`, a branch of its own.
- *The order.* `glued_marks` keeps each part where it prints (`GluedPart`): `$^{1*,2,3}$` shows `1`, `∗`, `,2,3`, on the route
  that keeps the math as on the route that shows unanswered marks (2609.14365). `$^{1*}$$^{2}$`, unanswered, reads `1∗,2`: a
  comma it does not print, known and left (no real case read).
- *A row of addresses.* The pieces a space parts join at a `\quad` (`dispatch`), the one separator no contact text reaches;
  `email_lines::address_tokens` reads each piece as written, its own font and link (S1: 2609.05531; 27 papers flagged), and
  the ties around it and the comma or semicolon it ends with are no text of an address (`without_row_spacing`: 2505.22665's
  `˜˜`, 2610.06195, 2505.05785).
- *The owner of a row.* By spelling, then by the list's order only where a spelled address on the same line confirms it: a row
  on one line under three names with one spelled resolves whole (`\texttt{a@x} \quad \texttt{b@y} \quad \texttt{snhong@x}`);
  the same addresses over two lines leave the two unspelled to the block (`owners_by_elimination`: nothing bounds them). So
  `cpo@`/`ceo@` (2606.13556) resolve and 2609.16617 does not.
- *An `\and` block of one name* (`owners_of`'s `owns_its_lines`) owns every address under it unless another name spells it or it is a role mailbox;
  elimination stays inside it (2609.05531's `john3678@`). One after names with no lines of their own stays the row's
  (2409.18978's `\{rbohrer,aneth\}@`), and so does a piece space parts, an institution read as a name (2404.19007). A line under a row kept apart by its legend reads the whole row's names, a lone spelled
  address its name's (2609.03842's `snhong@`).
- *A place right under an unmarked institution of the row* goes with it (`row_line_calls`, `Continuing::carriers`; `Seoul,
  Republic of Korea`, 2609.03842; `Nebraska, USA`, 2609.30627); a place with none above it stays the block's, R12.
- *An Error falls only because the output is right.* A piece that is one macro printing a link alone keeps the argument one
  name and the Error counted (`rows::holds_a_macro_printing_a_link`, 2601.07891's `\githubrepo`). A raw class's store is no
  `\affil` in the observer's reading of `\AB@thenote` (`thenote_affil`, `_store`): 2610.36456's Feng Xie no longer requests
  entry 1, under commas too.
- *Open, a note's owner.* A `\footnote` on a line under a sole author is a `pubnote` under authblk now, as it is in plain
  `article`: parted from the name it digests in the line's contact, where `\footnote` is `\lx@add@pubnote`. **Perl keeps it a
  note on the creator under authblk (2601.20363, run; a `pubnote` only without authblk), and so did base, inside the merged
  name.** The text is kept and the owner is lost, against charter §4's sole author; RED
  `authblk_footnote_line_under_sole_author` (green since ST1) (2601.20363, 2605.13069), for the Link step. 2610.07278's `pubnote`, an IEEE
  copyright line, is right.
- *Settled, not changed.* `zhanfa@` (2606.04547) is spelled by no name: base's holder was the order among misread names, and with
  `niwangze@` open (its author's row an affiliation in both) elimination holds. `\textsuperscript{*1}` asks for 1, so an entry
  is cut by its marks and an address under it follows the numeric route's carriers (2412.13509: seven affiliations right,
  `hmfu@` the block's, as `\textsuperscript{1}` on base; guard `batch107g`).

Guards `perfect_kernel_batch108a` (10 more). Updated: `perfect_kernel_batch86d::ieee_membership_kept_after_closing_stop` and
`perfect_kernel_batch104c::a_control_return_parts_marked_entries`, which pinned a printed star lost or welded to its list.

**(i) `\hspace` separates co-authors; footnote-symbol marks render instead of vanishing.**
Two composable normalizations applied to the `\author` argument BEFORE branch selection
(`normalize_hspace_separators` + `rewrite_symbol_superscripts`), addressing
html_feedback#6637 (arXiv:2506.06941, "The Illusion of Thinking", plain `article`), where
the six authors were welded into one `<personname>` with "Apple" glued on and Iman
Mirzadeh's literal `$^{*}$` silently dropped — Perl 0.8.8 (the arXiv production engine)
produced byte-identical output, so this is a surpass, not a Rust-only fix.
- **`\hspace{len}` / `\hspace*{len}` / `\hfill` → `\quad`.** Authors laid out with
  `A \hspace{1cm} B \hspace{1cm} C` (a regular poor-man's separator) collapsed into one
  creator, because the splitter only knew `\and`/`\quad`. `\quad` is already a hard
  separator in every author/affiliation split set, so the rewrite needs no new plumbing;
  `\hspace`'s optional `*` and mandatory length are consumed so the length cannot leak; a length written as zero
  (`\hspace{0pt}`, `\z@`) inside a group, a mark's argument or math prints no gap and is dropped (`\textsuperscript{1\hspace{0pt}2}` is the one label 12, #919); at the top level of the author line it stays the separator (`Ann Able\hspace{0pt}Bob Baker` two creators). A space right before a
  name's own mark or note is the name's, no separator, and an `\enskip` right after a mark or note and a
  spacing-only math group (`$\qquad$`) separate too (78m, #840).
- **Footnote-SYMBOL superscripts (`$^{*}$`, `${}^{\dagger}$`, `\textsuperscript{\ddagger}`)
  → a visible `\lx@frontmatter@keepsup` sup.** These are equal-contribution / corresponding
  notes, NEVER affiliation numbers (the same note-vs-affiliation split already encoded in
  `starts_with_affiliation_mark`). Rewriting them onto a sentinel the `\lx@author@withsup`
  hijack does not touch means they (1) render as a real superscript instead of being consumed
  into an `affiliation:*` label that matches nothing and is discarded, and (2) no longer count
  as an affiliation-marker trigger, so a block whose ONLY superscript is such a note-mark takes
  the clean no-marker branch. NUMERIC/lettered affiliation marks (`$^{1}$`) are untouched, and
  a superscript with a non-empty base (`$x^2$`) is real math, left alone.
- **Combined effect on the witness:** removing Mirzadeh's `$^{*}$` (its only literal `^`)
  drops the whole block into the no-marker branch, where the `\quad`s split all six authors,
  "Apple" becomes the last author's affiliation, and Shojaee keeps his two `\thanks`. Verified
  by an OLD-vs-NEW full-XML diff over all 57 author-bearing fixtures: exactly the THREE new
  fixtures changed, zero existing regressions. Guards:
  `06_cluster_frontmatter::{frontmatter_hspace_author_split, frontmatter_thanks_literal_mark_mix}` and the
  `frontmatter_symbol_superscript_mark` row of `perfect_kernel_batchhg1::hollow_guards_restored_read_as_printed` (since
  HG1b; its text asterisk written as U+2217, RED `author_textsuperscript_asterisk_stays_the_text_asterisk_red`). (This is also why (g)'s guard fixture now uses a
  numeric `$^{1}$` marker: a symbol `$^{*}$` there is now a note-mark and would reroute out of
  the marker branch it is meant to exercise.)
- **Residual (out of scope):** the *exact* `\fnsymbol` marks the author intended next to
  Shojaee's name (∗ for footnote 1, † for footnote 2) are not reconstructed — `\thanks`
  becomes a `role=thanks` contact note, not a numbered superscript. And an author block that
  mixes marked and UNMARKED authors while still carrying a NUMERIC affiliation mark stays in
  the marker branch, where marker-less horizontally-separated co-authors can still append; the
  clean recovery above depends on the note-marks being the *only* superscripts.

**(j) A shared author-email line distributes per author instead of bunching on the last.**
`\email{a@x, b@y, c@z}` (or a single `\email` covering several authors) attached every address to
whichever creator was open when the line digested — usually the LAST — leaving the rest
email-less. The `Email` author-line branch now resolves the individual addresses and, when there
are no more than one per author, hands each to `\lx@add@email` with `labelseq=author`, so address
*i* relocates to creator *i*'s own `author:N` label:
- **Distributed (`a@x, b@y, c@z`)** → email *i* to author *i*, in declaration order.
- **Grouped brace-expansion (`{a,b,c}@dom`)** → expand to `a@dom, b@dom, c@dom` first, then
  distribute; the expansion is never glued into an affiliation label.
- **A single shared address** → `author:1`, the LEAD author, never a trailing one.
A whole-line wrapper (`\texttt`, `\small`, `\url`, …) is re-applied per address; an email command's (`\email`,
`\mailto`, `\emailaddr` — a name containing `mail`) is dropped, as nested in `\lx@add@email` it made a second, empty
contact and advanced the `labelseq` count twice. MORE addresses than authors cannot map cleanly, so the line is kept
as one contact (the prior behavior), without the email command's wrapper. Witness arXiv:2605.23553
(`frontmatter_ieee_linebreak_optarg`). The same `email_line_calls` (62zl) serves address lines in a marked
affiliation list (`affiliation_calls` → `place_address_runs`), placed as runs of consecutive address lines once the
whole list is read. An address claims an author only where the list says whose it is, by that author's queue
position (an explicit `author:N` label; `labelseq=author` counts every earlier email contact, which had made a creator
with no name):
- **The list puts addresses under its affiliations** (it has one marked affiliation, or a run sits above another
  that is not a footnote-symbol legend such as `$^\dagger$ Corresponding author`; 2609.19448) → one address under an affiliation exactly one author requests is that author's,
  carrying the mark that placed it (`_placedbymark`, distinct from the set side's `_bymark` mark keys):
  where the reading parts that call into several names
  (`\IEEEauthorblockN{Ann Able\IEEEauthorrefmark{1} Bob Baker\IEEEauthorrefmark{2}}`, REVTeX's `\author{A$^1$ and
  B$^2$}`), an address none of them spells is the one's showing that mark (`Resolver::entry_owners`; it had gone to a
  nameless creator: 2510.10414, P28m3), the block's still where several show it; any other run under
  an affiliation continues it, as the PDF prints it — an affiliation several authors share, or several addresses
  under one author's, which may be everyone's.
- **Otherwise the runs are the block's** → one address for each author goes to the authors in order (llncs
  `\institute{$^1$A \\ $^2$B \\ \email{a@x} \\ \email{b@y}}`); any other goes to the shared creator below the
  authors (#159), one contact an address (a line whose addresses are not read, one contact; 77o: the raw line was one
  Semiverbatim contact, 1802.07182's `\{jrr41,$\,$wct23,…\}@cam.ac.uk` printed `{jrr41,$ $wct23,…}`) — 2609.06094's four addresses for six authors had gone, by order, Jindong Gu's to Runjia
  Li, and by the mark of the affiliation they follow, three to the wrong author.
`\and` ends a run as it ends an entry. A line with one address is kept as written (`\href{mailto:a@x}{a@x}` stays a link; `email_addresses` reads past
`\href`'s URL and a `mailto:`). An `\author` call's tail (`author_tail_calls`) is placed so only at `\maketitle` when
that call made every author; before a later `\author`, its unmarked lines stay its own creators' rows. A marked
iopart `\address` before any `\author` keeps its labelled affiliations for the authors to come. Residuals: an
unwrapped llncs `\email` loses the class's `E-mail` contact name for the generic `Email:`; the `\lx@add@authors`
email line still places by `labelseq=author`; a trailing `$^\dagger$` legend makes a one-affiliation list count as
several, so its addresses go by order rather than continue the affiliation (neither misplaces one); apa7
affiliations given with no names are not kept.
An address line carrying a note (`\texttt{a@x, b@y}\thanks{Submitted …}`) is still an address line (101b): the reader
reads the printed text, so read whole the note's words made the line an affiliation — of the last name in a marked
block (2605.23553's second line, "cy.cole@…, dan.dorn@…", Dan Dorn's), of every name in an unmarked one. One helper,
`defs/frontmatter_api/email_lines.rs` `address_line_notes`, takes the notes off a line whose rest is an address line by the
caller's own reader (the marked block's `line_is_email_list` / `labelled_email_line`, the unmarked block's
`line_emails`, a marked list's `entry_calls`), and makes them the document's pubnotes, added after the block's calls in
print order among themselves — not among the block's other notes: a note on a later affiliation line is added in
place, so it now precedes an earlier address line's note (RED repro `address_line_note_order_after_a_later_note`, review
rev101b finding 1; base kept print order) — as they digested in the contact before (`\thanks` → `\lx@add@pubnote@thanks`, `\footnote` →
`\lx@add@pubnote`, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:331-332; the one conversion `notes.rs` `document_note_call`, shared with
`notes_the_names_request`). A per-author class's cautious reading keeps giving a line's notes to its name, as Perl adds
that `\author` whole. A note of another kind (`\thanksref`, `\altaffilmark`, `\thanks[…]{…}`) leaves the line read as
before; `email_addresses` itself still reads the note, since `address_tokens` would drop a note it skipped. The
observer's writer holds a block note on an address line (`note:address-line`) as today's pubnote
(`emitter/plan.rs` `held_as_pubnote`), so both engines read these lines alike. Perl: no e-mail contact, every address
welded into an affiliation (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #75). Witnesses 2605.23553, 2304.05485, 1710.01254, 1803.07937,
2603.09888, 2608.24641; guards `perfect_kernel_batch101b`.
Guards `06_cluster_frontmatter::frontmatter_shared_email_distribution` (fixtures
`frontmatter_email_{distributed,grouped,single_shared}.tex`), `perfect_kernel_batch61::marked_affiliation_review_shapes`.

**(k) Marks and their authors (62zp).** Four readings of an author block Perl gets wrong: marks glued to a comma (`Ann
Able,\textsuperscript{a} Bob Baker\textsuperscript{b}`, or `Ann\textsuperscript{1},\textsuperscript{2},`) are the
name's before it when the line does not open with a mark (Perl gives Bob both; 2609.25924), a `\thanks` glued among
them too (2609.37343) — a mark after the comma's space (`Ann Able$^{1}$, $^{*}$Bob Baker`) stays with the name it
leads; a first line whose marks lead the names (`\textsuperscript{a}Ann Able, \textsuperscript{b}Bob Baker`, also
after a declaration such as `\large`) is names, as an author block opens with authors (Perl reads it as affiliations
and drops the authors), and so is the first line of each later `\and` group once the first line set that convention,
when its mark is one no author before it requests and no affiliation has been read (a requested one leads that
author's affiliation, `\and` separating the affiliations, and so does every group after one); a footnote-symbol author
mark (`$^{*}$`, `\inst{\dagger}`), still shown, also requests the affiliation of its symbol, so a list labelling an
entry with it gives that entry to its author (informs4's `\AFF{$^*$Corresponding author}`, 2609.38842) — the request
is on creators only, and one nothing answers is unused; an equal-contribution legend labelled with the symbol
(`\AFF{$^*$Equal contribution}`) therefore attaches, as an affiliation-role contact, to each starred author rather
than standing alone; an ordinal suffix superscript after a numeral (`5 \textsuperscript{th} floor`, `$5^{th}$`,
`2\textsuperscript{\rm nd}`, `5$^{\mathrm{th}}$` shown as `\textrm`, likewise `\mathit`/`\mathbf`/`\mathsf`) is shown,
not taken for an affiliation mark (iopart, 2609.01831). Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch61::author_marks_link_their_affiliations`.

**(l) An author's notes keep their math (62zq).** `\lx@add@thanks` and `\lx@add@note` (an author's `\thanks` and
`\footnote`) read an ordinary argument, as LaTeX's `\thanks` and a title's `\lx@add@pubnote@thanks` do, where Perl's
are Semiverbatim (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:661/663) and print their math as text; a note's content in a marked author
line keeps its superscripts as text, not marks (`\lx@frontmatter@plainsups`), save a leading mark that authors
request on a note that is one legend, which labels the note so that the legend goes to them
(`\thanks{\textsuperscript{$\dagger$} School ...}`, 2609.00885, 2609.19600; `note_body`); a note of several legends
stays whole with its author, its marks shown (2609.39576; RED
`thanks_with_several_legends_goes_to_each_legends_authors`). An author's own requests are its marks outside its notes
(`author_mark_operands`). KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #515. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch61::author_thanks_and_footnote_keep_their_math`.

**Scope/limits:**
- The `*` equal-contribution suffix on a combined author mark (`$^{1*}$`) still
  labels `affiliation:1*`, so it does not yet match a plain `affiliation:1`
  (2606.00313's first two authors stay unlinked — strictly better than the
  former literal blob, no regression).
- Dropping the comma from group-level splitting makes one previously-handled
  shape worse: `\author{Alice\\MIT, Bob\\CMU}` (comma separating two
  author+affiliation groups, where the standard idiom is `\and`) now yields a
  single author *Alice* with affiliations "MIT, Bob" and "CMU" — *Bob* is folded
  into affiliation text and lost. This is the unavoidable dual of fixing the
  common address case: "MIT, Bob" (affil, author) and "…Laboratory, Laurel"
  (address parts) are structurally identical, so no heuristic separates them.
  Multi-author docs overwhelmingly use `\and`, so this is rare; the frequent
  address-shredding it trades against is the right call.
- A numeric abuse-mark note that fails to link to any author is shown as a
  `role=affiliation` contact attached to the last creator (mislabeled, but not
  lost). Email relabeling is applied in the no-marker author arm only.

Full suite green (1532/0); clippy clean.


**(m) A labelled email line of a marked author block is the authors' (64k).** In `\lx@add@authors`' marked path a
marker-less line continued the affiliation above it (Perl Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:701-703), so `E-mail: \email{x}`
under the last `\llap{$^d$}` affiliation became that affiliation's — every author marked d had the address (0903.0326:
four New Mexico authors for D. Muna's), or, nested in it, none did. A labelled email line (`labelled_emails`, its lead
and tail of blank lines or spacing aside: 1112.1037, 1311.3535) is now an entry of its own, each address placed by
`author:N` (which counts every numbered author: those of an earlier `\author` call, 1805.09245's collaboration, and
those an earlier flush kept): to the one author whose surname its local part spells (`address_owners`; 1710.00802's
`aleder@` is A. Leder's though under a "Corresponding Author" note); else a lone address, after a note naming the corresponding
author, to the one author that note's own mark names (`$^\spadesuit$ Corresponding author\newline E-mail: …`, 1305.7027,
the note in a later `\author` call than F. Simon; one spelling several only if among them) — the mark of the note's own
marker-led line, never that of an affiliation a symbol-marked note (`$^*$`, read as a footnote symbol) continues, for
the next labelled email line only, unless an author or affiliation line comes first; else a lone address to the one author whose `\thanks`/`\footnote` (optional
argument aside) names them corresponding ("corresponding author", "correspondence"; `S.~Bityukov$^a$\thanks{Corresponding
author.}` over `Serguei.Bitioukov@cern.ch`, 1302.2651), one spelling several to that author only if among them; else one
contact of the whole block (`label=addresses:block`, #159). The address is the contact's content, not the class's email
command around it (a JINST copy as `arxiv.cls` kills `\email` at begin-document: 1111.1180). A line after it continues
the entry before it (1503.08624's proceedings line, welded to the email and both lost); after an email under a name, or
after only email lines in its `\and` group, its own entry, not part of a name or a new author. Residuals: an email line
inside a braced affiliation, with no `\\` before it, still goes with that affiliation (1905.04066, 0910.1682, 1304.6289,
2406.11067); an address under the last mark that only one author holds, spelling no one, goes to the block, not to that
author (1605.02067's `ravi2ramana@`, which continuing the mark had given K. Raveendrababu; the `place_address_runs`
one-requester rule would also send 1302.0278's `elmaddin@` to Madatov, wrongly); a `$^*$` note's mark is not resolved
against the authors' marks (`C.~Cole$^{a,*}$`), so its address goes to the block; a replacing `\author` after digested authors
with no later `\maketitle` to supersede them numbers its own from 1, while those authors stay (as in Perl), so its
`author:N` names an old creator; the spelling is matched on surnames only, so `xwang@` under a note marking Y. Wang goes to
Y. Wang, not X. Wang (the old continuation did the same); a later `\author{$^\spadesuit$ Corresponding author\\ E-mail: …}`
(JINST appends) reads its marker-led first line as a name, a creator `Corresponding author`, its email the block's
(before: 2 errors, the address lost).
Guard `perfect_kernel_batch64::marked_block_email_line_owner` (eleven variants).

**(n) Name lists that read as no names (64zd).** The per-author class bindings' cautious split (`\lx@add@authors@append`:
revtex, aastex/aas, amsart, sprocl) splits a name list only where its visible text reads as two or more names
(`split_author_line_cautious`, `name_count`); four shapes read as none, so the list stayed one personname, and a block
of alternating plain lines lost a name:
- a `\cite` note mark after a name: its key read as a word (`Itay Furman \cite{itay} and Ofer Biham \cite{ofer}`,
  cond-mat9611093; cond-mat9912430). `\cite` is a name annotation (`NAME_ANNOTATIONS`). The same for a surname set in
  math to carry its mark (`M. ${\rm Schreiber}^{*}$`, cond-mat9402093): a run of two or more letters in math, outside
  its scripts and their operands (`$^\mathrm{ab}$`), is name text, a lone letter (`$e^+e^-$`) none; a byline's leading
  "by" is dropped (hep-ph9507223, hep-ph9404319); a run of bare asterisks after a comma is a mark (`S. F. Pereira,* Z.
  Y. Ou,** and H. J. Kimble`, quant-ph0003094). Guards `revtex_marked_author_list_splits_each_name`,
  `revtex_asterisk_marked_authors_split_red`; hep-ex9910016's 190 `$^{n}$`-marked BES names split again.
- initials glued to a surname in capitals (`M.CACCIA, R.CAMPAGNOLO`, hep-ex9910019): `unglued_initials` unglues before
  a capitals surname of three letters or more, not before an abbreviation's last letter (`I.N.F.N`). Guard
  `author_caps_glued_initials_split`.
- a doubled separator (`Barrientos, \& and Omar López-Cruz`, astro-ph9612009): a separator alone is no part
  (`name_parts`), and an "and" opening a piece after a separator is the separator too (`split_author_names`). Guard
  `author_doubled_separator_ampersand_and`.
- in an article author block of alternating lines, a name line carrying an author's `\thanks`/`\footnote` after
  affiliation lines opens the next author when the block's first names carry the same note command (`name_groups`,
  `author_note_of`; `A.M. Green\thanks{…},\\ … \\ C. Michael\thanks{…},\\ DAMTP …`, hep-lat9404004; 1410.7277,
  1706.02584, 1403.1404); under plain names a noted affiliation stays one (`Ann Able and Bob Baker\\ Department of
  Physics\\ Ohio State\footnote{Visiting.}`). Guards `author_note_name_line_opens_next_author`,
  `author_noted_affiliation_stays_affiliation_red`. With no notes the same alternation opens the next author when a gap,
  the names' styling or a person's name over an institution says so (#900); residual (RED
  `article_plain_name_line_between_affiliations`): a cue-less `Bob Baker` over `Univ Y, …` with none of these, a place
  reading as a name too (1908.10448's `Zach Shahn \\ IBM Research,`). The note command must be the first names' own
  (`\thanks` names over a `\footnote`d affiliation: the affiliation stays one; guard
  `author_other_note_command_stays_affiliation_red`); with `\footnote` on names and affiliations alike the block is
  ambiguous and a noted affiliation name-shaped line opens an author (RED `author_footnote_everywhere_ambiguous`).
Residual: `$^{a}$Sahng-kyoon.Yoo and $^{b}$D.K.Park` (hep-th9707026; a surname glued at a period) stays one creator.

**(o) Spacing runs part names; a `\let` alias of a mark is the mark; spacing in a mark parts its labels (77p, user
ruling 2026-10-19).** Three readings of an author block Perl gets wrong (it merges, or loses the affiliations):
- A run of two or more spacing commands — `\ `, `\:`, `\>`, `\;`, `~`, `\enspace`, mixed, spaces between them; the
  control return a line ending in `\ ` leaves (`\^^M`, latex.ltx `\ `) — between two names at the block's top level,
  outside math, is a separator, rewritten to `\quad` with (i)'s `\hspace`/`\hfill` (`normalize_hspace_separators`,
  `spacing_run_separator`): `\textbf{Ann Able}\textsuperscript{1}\;\;\textbf{Bob Baker}` (2610.20409), `\ \ \ \ \ `
  (2310.10873, 1202.3179), ACL's `~~`/`~~~~` (2603.20851, 2605.30274), `\:\:` (1503.08895, 1811.10830), 1702.05821,
  1508.00093, 2009.12421, 1005.1466, 1009.3124, cs0207008 (its runs end their lines). What the code tests, in order:
  the run is at the top level outside math, and a name letter came since the last separator on its line — a letter
  outside math, a mark's argument and an optional argument, at the top level or in a plain or font group (`{\scshape
  …}`, `\textbf{…}`), not in another command's argument (`\raisebox{-0.3ex}{\includegraphics[height=1.1em]{…}}\;\;
  Daedalus Research Team`, 2604.10005); the token before it, a blank line's `\par` aside, is no separator (`\\`,
  `\and`, `\quad`, `\hspace`, a comma, `;`, `\&`) and no initial (one letter and its period after no letter: `R.~~Beyer`,
  2603.17646; `L.~~Caballero-Ontanaya`, 2604.25437; `Rafa\l ~R.\ ~Suszek`, 2603.20914 — one person); the word before it
  is not "and" nor a byline's "by", in any case (`By~~{\scshape Vitaly~Bergelson}~~and~~…`, 2603.25922, 2604.12864,
  2603.27258, 2604.07186; the leading "By", "BY" is dropped from the names as "and" is); a run before the word "and" —
  in any case, alone or the only word of one wrapper, a group or a font command's argument (`and_word_end`:
  `Cat Cole~~and~~Dan Dorn`, `~~AND~~`, `~~And~~`, `~~{and}~~`, `~~\textrm{and}~~`, 2606.27261's
  `\;\;\textnormal{AND}\;\;`, 2607.03677's `~~ {and}~~`) — parts with the word and the spacing after it, written as
  the plain word between spaces every author split reads (`RunSeparator`; 77p r4: the r3 rule read the word only
  lowercase and bare, so "AND" and "And" became creators and a wrapped "and" an affiliation of the name before it),
  and a piece that prints only that word (`\quad \textnormal{and} \quad`, 2608.24427; `is_and_piece`) is skipped as
  a separator in both branches, never a name or an affiliation; on a line of a marked block that opens with a mark,
  the next mark parts the entries (`$^1$The University of Hong Kong~~~~~~$^2$Zhejiang Lab`, 2310.15160), "and" in the
  run too (`$^1$Univ A~~and~~$^2$Univ B`, 77p r5) — a mark being what the branch choice reads as one, so in a block
  marked only with footnote symbols (`rewrite_symbol_superscripts`: no mark) a symbol-led line is read as any line off
  the names line (2609.35807's `$^{*}$\daplablogo\ Columbia University\ \ \ $^{\dagger}$University at Buffalo` had
  made a creator "†University at Buffalo", 77p r4; the re-review's probes h1-h3); else the next token opens a name — a letter, a group, a command that is no
  mark, note or separator (`Gus Gray~~\thanks{…}`, `Hal Hunt\ \ $^{1}$` keep their note and mark) — and the piece up to
  the next separator (a comma, `;`, a line separator, another run) holds a name letter (not `~~\JMorcid,`, 2605.12398;
  `~~\mbox{\orcidlink{…}}`, 2605.06250). Only the names line — the block's first line, or the first after an `\and`; a
  line break ends it (`beside_prefix_marked_names`'s concept) — is parted so; on a later line both sides must read as
  names (`name_count`; a name's notes aside, the piece after it read up to the mark that ends its name: `Rui
  Wang$^{*, 2}$ <blank line> \vspace{2pt} $^1$Ant Group`, 2603.19223; `Xinlei He\textsuperscript{1}\thanks{…\href{…}{…}}`,
  2605.30366), not as an affiliation (`reads_as_affiliation`), an address (`@`) or a link (`\url`, `\href`,
  `\texttt`): `Ann Able \\ Department of Physics~~~~University of X` and 2605.28131's `\url{…}~~~ \url{…}` part
  nothing. In an unmarked block a run off the names line parts only the line right after it, and only when that line is
  a row of names going on with the names line (`row_of_names`, 77p r4): it lists another number of names than the
  names line, which holds two or more (2603.09835's rows of five, four and two; 2607.07318 five over three, 2603.07624,
  2603.16856 two over four), or a line follows it that is no row of as many entries — the address under all the rows
  (2605.24414's `\\[0.2em]` rows of six over six over three, then `\textit{JIUTIAN Research}`; 2608.21409 three over
  three over its e-mail line, split over two lines; 2607.09029 five over five over `LiAuto Inc.`) — but over a line of
  e-mail addresses only when an address spells one of the row's pieces (`row_spelled_by_addresses`) or the addresses
  number the names of both rows together (77p r5: `Ann Able~~~~Bob Baker \\ Carnegie Mellon~~~~Johns Hopkins \\
  \texttt{\{aa,bb\}@x.edu}` had made the institutions creators, the re-review's probes v1, v3); the break between them becomes a `\quad`
  (2603.09835's `\textbf{Pratham Grover}\\ \textbf{Ramakrishna B.~Bairi}\ \ \textbf{Ritabrata Maiti}`: Ramakrishna B.
  Bairi had read as Pratham Grover's address line). A row of institutions under the names, one under each name (`Ann
  Able~~~~Bob Baker \\ Carnegie Mellon~~~~Johns Hopkins`; `\textbf` names over `\textit` institutions; one name over
  two institutions: the r3 re-review's probes, which had made them creators) — which ends the block or has a row of as
  many entries under it, their e-mails — is not parted, nor is a row of names under
  an affiliation line (`Ann Able \\ Univ A \\ Bob Baker~~~~Cat Cole`, read as int34a reads it, a SYNC_STATUS residual):
  the line is the names' shared address line. Markup does not tell the two apart — 2607.07318's and 2603.16856's second
  rows open with `{\bf`/`\bf` under plain first rows. Off the names line a piece that opens with a
  mark after its size or font, `$^1$` or `\(^1\)` (`{\footnotesize $^{1}$Univ A} \ \ \ \small $^{2}$Univ B`, 2603.27970,
  2308.10525, 2605.24043, 2605.22036; `\(^{1}\)Huawei Technologies, Canada~~\(^2\)University of Alberta`, 2604.12896;
  `after_leading_markup`, `starts_with_mark`) parts at a run as a mark-led line does, and an e-mail row parted by a
  run is read as its addresses, not parted (2603.04592, 2603.12193, 2605.06264). A name in a group of its own after a
  run already parted stays a name (`~~ {Kyungtae Lim}`, 2605.30545). One spacing command stays inside a name (`J.~Smith`, `Ann\ Able`, `van~der~Berg`), and a run after a
  line-leading mark is the mark's space (`$\ast$~~Department of Physics`, hep-ph9708397). A blank line's `\par` is no
  separator: the block is set in a `c` column (latex.ltx's `\@maketitle`), restricted horizontal mode, where `\par` ends
  no paragraph (tex.web §1094, §1096 `end_graf` acts only when `mode=hmode`): 2009.12421's `Ehsan
  Shareghi$^\spadesuit$$^\clubsuit$ <blank line> \ \ Nigel Collier` is one row of two names.
- Names parted by horizontal space alone — a spacing run, `\quad`, `\qquad`, (i)'s `\hspace`/`\hfill` — share the
  address lines under them in the unmarked branch, as comma-parted names of one group do (user ruling 2026-10-19,
  77p r2): pdflatex prints the lines under the whole row. Perl's `@authorsplits` parts the names at `\quad` as at the
  comma and hands the lines to the last name (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:676, 720-725), as the Rust splitter did. The
  `\quad`-parted blocks of `author_group_splits` are joined into one group (`add_authors_calls_sectioned`, the
  `blocks` pass) when only horizontal space parts them and the earlier block's last names have no lines of their own;
  a space before the line break ends no list, so the next row of names joins too (`Zhiyuan Zhu\quad \\
  \textbf{Ruiqi Li} \quad … \\ Zhejiang University`, 2507.06670). The group's e-mails go to the names they spell
  (`\texttt{\{say,abuzer\}@boun.edu.tr}`, 1009.3124). Witnesses 1508.00093 (`Yuxi Fu \ \ \  Han Zhu \\ BASICS, …`),
  1009.3124, 1202.3179 (`\alignauthor Ke Wang \ \ … Chao Han`), 1503.08895 (`\:`-runs under `\And`); 2304.13998
  waits on the user-macro mark row below.
- A line's e-mail addresses go to the names they spell best (`spelled_owners`, `NameKeys`): each name scores the
  letters of its keys the local part holds — a surname, or its first six letters; the given name the local part opens
  with, or holds when it has four letters or more; a joined spelling it opens with, the first word's initial and a later
  word (`psingh1_be22@…` Prathamjyot Singh's among three Singhs and `kbatra_be22@…` Karamvir Singh Batra's, 2608.10670;
  `tli104@…` Tianjian Li's, 2606.23525) or a later word and the first (`wufei@…` Fei Wu's, `chengyu@…` Yu Cheng's,
  2509.10377); the initials when the local part is only they (`aa@…` Ann Able's; also the first and last, `jw2423@…`
  Joseph G. Wallwork's, 2407.00382) — a name scoring the better of its words apart and a joined spelling, never their
  sum (77p r6: `khan.muhammad@` had scored 24 for Muhammad Haris Khan, "khan", "muhammad" and "khanmuhammad", over 12
  for Khan Muhammad, 2602.07835) — and the highest score owns the address, a tie going to the surname's spelling (`fucheng.fuc@…` is Cheng Fu's, not Jiawei Chen's, 2403.00801;
  `wangchiew@…` Wang-Chiew Tan's, 2104.01371; `yipengzhang97@…` Yipeng Zhang's, 2406.06326). The ones no name spells go
  by elimination only where the order confirms it, one rule for both branches (`owners_by_elimination`; main-session
  decision 2026-10-20, 77p r4, superseding r3's elimination by order whenever as many addresses as names were left):
  the pool is the names no address spells on any e-mail line of the block (2605.06223's `kyle.min@…` on the next line
  leaves `treejhk@…` Junhyuk Kwon's); exactly one address and one name left, the address is that name's (`lzhang@…`
  Li Zhang's, then `zhangw@…` Wei Zhang's); else the addresses the names spell must stand in name order (one at least),
  and the addresses left go in order to the names left when there are as many and that order holds with the spelled ones
  (it fails on 2606.04646, where the position read swapped `dishkw@` and `e0556732@`, and on 2605.26032's `congyued@` before
  `billf@`, whose `jzxchen@`, `billf@` and `soljacic@` it once placed right by luck; 108a, rev108a3 B3), else those between two of them, or before the first or after the last, go in order to the names
  between their owners when there are as many, every author there counted, spelled on another line or not, and none
  of them spelled or given an address — never a run before the first or after the last, which only the list's end
  bounds (user ruling R10 2026-10-20, 77p r10: no position placement at a list's end; 77p r9 had waited on the other
  lines, the r5 re-review's probe q7; 2509.10377's `12421181@`, `230249457@` are the block's, on the shared creator,
  neither Yixiao Zhou's and Dongzhou Cheng's by their places, as r6 had them, nor the last name's, as r9) (77p r6: 2602.23777's `nnwang@` between `xu_zhipeng@` and `dcheng@` had gone to

  2603.24730's `j8675309@mit.edu` to Jennifer E. Corbett; 2303.11225's `xuta@…`, `musclewu@…` between `tianyuhe@…`,
  `tabaltru@…`, `runnan.li@…`). The one-left and as-many-left rules wait on the other e-mail lines: while one holds
  an address no name spells and no rule placed, no name is free to give (77p r6, the r5 re-review's probe q6:
  `\{aable,q77,ddorn\}@x.edu \\ \{bbaker,z99\}@y.edu` had given `q77@` to Cat Cole; in the unmarked branch the
  group's other lines, or the block's when the line holds more addresses than its group has names; 2609.02349's
  `xiahou@` now stays on the last name, as 2605.30274's `zhangmin186@` does, the five authors spelled on other lines
  before Shimin Tao counted in its run). A
  list not in name order (by institution: 2509.10377, 2406.06326) or with none spelled
  (`\{bb,aa\}@x.edu` — the initials decide, not the order) places no address by its place, and a role mailbox (RFC
  2142's `info@`, `support@`, …, and `contact@`, `office@`, `admin@`; `is_role_mailbox`) is no person's. An address no
  rule settles is the block's, on the shared nameless creator below the authors (#159, `label=addresses:block`), in
  both branches (user ruling R10 2026-10-20, 77p r10; it had gone to the unmarked group's last name, and stayed one

  boliu@cqupt.edu.cn}` had shown "~~~"; `AddressPlacement::Settled`). The order path (`addresses_in_order`, the
  `labelseq` count) takes a line only when every address spells the author at its place (77p r10, user ruling R10: an
  address no name spells is never placed by its place — a single shared `contact@lab.org` had gone to the lead author,

  2603.24730's `\{yuqihu,~ahna,~vasha\}@berkeley.edu \ \ \ \{vasha,~j8675309\}@mit.edu` (a brace list's domain ends at

  answers no mark (`answered_labels`; 2403.00801's `jiawei2020@…` on the second author had hidden every unanswered mark
  "2"). An argument that prints no letter is no letter of an address, a label or a link's text — one table,

  (`\fontfamily`, `\fontseries`, `\fontshape`, `\fontencoding`, `\fontsize`, `\usefont`), graphicx's boxes
  (`\scalebox`, `\rotatebox`, `\raisebox`, `\resizebox`; `\includegraphics` whole) and the skips (`\hspace`,
  `\vspace`, a space), each by its xparse-style signature (77p r10, the r6 re-review's finding 5: 2609.25669's

  `0.9aable@`, w15's `911aable@`; the colours since 77p r9: 2604.19440's `\texttt{\{}\href{mailto:…}{\color{black}\texttt{xinhao.zhang},}

  address of a line keeps the mailto link the line gives it (`address_tokens`). A labelled list of addresses or links
  (`Emails: \href{mailto:a}{a}, \href{mailto:b}{b}`, probe u22), a footnote symbol before the label (`$^*$Corresponding
  author: \href{mailto:…}{…}`, probe u23; 2605.01567, 2605.30150) and a size, font or group around the whole line (`\tt\small
  {Email Address: songyuxinbb@outlook.com}`, 2603.19228: was an affiliation of the last name) are e-mail lines too
  (77p r9). In a marked block a line under an e-mail line that is not addresses is its own entry, welded into neither the
  e-mail line nor an entry above it (a labelled e-mail line is still skipped, the line after it going on with the
  affiliation above: 1503.08624's proceedings line, batch 64k), and so is a line that is only a link anywhere — `\href{…}{…}`, `\url{…}`, in the
  groups, sizes and fonts it is set in, after a label ending in a colon (`is_link_line`; 77p r6: 2602.22394's
  `{\footnotesize \url{…}}`, 2602.23802's `{\tt{\small{\url{…}}}}`, 2602.09509's `Demo Code:~\url{…}` had welded into
  the e-mail line, which then placed no address; a bare `\url` line had skipped it into "Univ B"; 2403.08629,
  2605.06223). Such a link line, in either branch, is a URL contact (`\lx@add@contact[role=url]`, as a class's
  `\homepage` is), not an affiliation: the line is its content, a "Label:" before the link its text (`Demo Code:`,
  `\textbf{Code}:`), the link an `ltx:ref` (user ruling 2026-10-20, 77p r7; `is_url_line`, `url_contact_call`). It is
  the whole block's — the shared creator below the authors (#159, `label=addresses:block`; a sole author's) — when the
  call makes the document's whole author list: the project pages of 2605.06223, 2602.08439, 2604.12896, 2602.22394,

  affiliation, the unmarked branch to every name of the group: 2603.16856, 2604.15215, 2605.25477). In an `\and`
  column it is the column's: a marked block's column of one author while other columns hold authors gives it to that
  author, who the PDF prints it under; an unmarked group's to its one name, or to its names as the group's lines
  (`annotate=N`) when the block has other groups; a per-author class's call (`replace` false) to its author. A link to a
  mailbox (`\textbf{Correspondence:} \href{mailto:…}{…}`, `Email: \href{mailto:…}{…}`) is no URL but an e-mail line
  (user ruling 2026-10-20, 77p r8; `mailto_line`, read by `labelled_emails` in both branches): the text before the
  link, as printed without its font, names the e-mail contact (`name="Correspondence: "`, as a labelled e-mail line's

  prints none (`address_text`; 2601.07974's placeholder target `mailto:email@domain`) — goes to the name it spells
  (2601.00240's `gaomin@` to Min Gao, 2601.07974, 2604.23002, 2606.03014; 2605.18563's `thclark@` to Thomas Hikaru
  Clark alone, no longer on every name of the group; r7 had kept it an affiliation of the last author or of every
  name); one no name spells is placed as an unsettled address is — the block's, or the `\thanks`-named corresponding
  author's —, never on every name. So is a link to a bare address without `mailto:`, target or printed text — a local
  part, an `@` and a dotted domain, no web page's target (`is_bare_address`, `links_a_mailbox`; 77p r10: a handle,

  URL contact; 77p r9). A link is a URL contact by what it says and where it goes, not by the shape of its words
  (`is_url_line`, 77p r10, the r6 re-review's finding 2): a `\url`, an `\href` printing a web address, or a link word
  in its text or the label before it (`LINK_WORDS`, `link_words`: page, website, homepage, code, repository, GitHub,

  and 2604.15404's `Substack Article`, which 77p r9's name-shape test had made affiliations of the shared creator);
  else one printing an institution or a name is that linked, and one to a page below a site's root (or printing no

  `link_prints_an_institution`: `\href{https://www.google.com}{Google}`, `\href{https://x.ai}{xAI}`, probes x10, w8),

  shared creator since r7; the r5 re-review's probes u32, u33, u35, u38), one printing a name its author; a link that
  prints nothing (`\url{}`, 2601.02680) is none. A link line opening an author block or an `\and` column is no name when
  it prints a URL (`prints_a_url`; probes u4, u16, u17 had made creators named by their URLs; an ORCID-linked name there
  stays its author, 2608.24427, 2602.15968, 2603.04124), and a marked column of several names takes its link line as its
  names', as its institution (ruling 9; probe u6m). A name's contacts follow the order its column prints them (77p r9,

  group shares, digested under its last name — are given by a label of the name's own (`placed_label`,

  is.naist.jp}`, 1906.01834) still continues it, and a line that prints nothing (`\large{~~}`, a blank line's `\par`)

- A command LaTeX's own footnote marks print — in `\@fnsymbol`'s body (latex.ltx: `\TextOrMath \textsection
  \mathsection`, `\textparagraph`/`\mathparagraph`, `\textbardbl`, …) and printing a symbol, or a macro of such
  commands — is a footnote symbol as `\dagger` is (`is_symbol_command`; 77p r6, main-session decision 2026-10-20 to
  generalise the set: 2601.02680's `$^\mathsection$` had read as an affiliation mark nothing answers, the § dropped and
  "Xibin Zhao Pengfei Su† Dong Li†" one creator). A math symbol outside `\@fnsymbol` (`\clubsuit`, `\heartsuit`)
  stays an affiliation mark: taken as a footnote symbol it moves a comma-parted block (2601.05633) to the unmarked
  branch, where every address line goes to every name.
- A run of distinct symbol commands in a mark is a label each, as `$^{1,2}$` is two (`SYMBOL_COMMAND_RUN` in
  `clean_frontmatter_labels`): 1811.10830's `Ali Farhadi$^{\spadesuit\heartsuit}$` reaches both `$^\spadesuit$` and
  `$^\heartsuit$` lines (was a nameless creator holding the Allen Institute); a font switch inside a mark is no part of
  its label (`FONT_SWITCH` with `\normalfont`, `\textnormal`, `\upshape`, …): 2604.24532's
  `\textbf{Ying-Tu Chen\textsuperscript{\normalfont{1},}…}` reaches the `\textsuperscript{1}` line.
  Unchanged: names with lines of their own (`Ann Able \\ Univ A \quad Bob Baker \\ Univ B`), names an `\and` parts,
  marked authors (the marks decide), and a row of addresses parted by space too (`Cat Cole \quad Dan Dorn \\ Univ C
  \quad Univ D`, set under the names by position, whose pieces take no names after them either: 2609.25833's e-mail
