### 715. A printed `\@title` or `\@author` is the field's ink by its tokens' provenance, lifted where the frontmatter is placed (Perl: the structured copy and the print both shown)

Frontmatter model M3, stage S1 (field provenance only; user rulings 2026-10-17, design study
agent_reports/2026-10-16_frontmatter_design_study.md §6; the title-print study's rule R3, its stage 3; main-session
ruling 2026-10-17: out-of-band provenance, not in-band mark tokens). Perl takes the frontmatter from the setter call
(`\lx@add@title` at latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1059-1063, `\lx@add@authors` at :1076-1079) and renders the header from
that copy; a document that also typesets the stores itself — no `\maketitle`, `{\Large\bf \@title\par}` (lrec's
`\maketitleabstract`: 2402.14614, 1603.09631), 1605.00182's own `\centerline{\Large\bf{\noindent\@title}}`, puthesis's
`\LARGE \@title` (1503.06457) — shows the title (and the author line) twice, in Perl as here before (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
#935); the title copy went only by the text-matching dedup (#146), the author's not at all.

**Provenance, out of band.** `Token` (latexml_core token.rs) has a `prov: u16` field (`0` = none) in what was the
struct's padding: `Token` stays 8 bytes (`token_size_invariant`; 12 under `token-locators`, as before), laid out
`#[repr(C)]` `text`, `code`, `prov` with a two-byte `Catcode` (`#[repr(u16)]`) so it has no pad byte and `code` stays
at byte 4 (`token_layout_code_at_byte_4`; see Cost). It is not part
of TeX's token: `PartialEq` ignores it (so `\ifx`, `\meaning`, xstring, `\pdfstrcmp` compare as pdflatex), it is never
written or dumped, and whatever builds a token from characters (`\string`, `\detokenize`, `\scantokens`, `\write`,
`\csname`) builds one without it. The kernel `\title` and `\author` (sect05.rs) stamp their store once the frontmatter
has its copy: `\lx@field@mark\gdef\@title{title}` / `\lx@field@mark\def\@author{author}` (base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_fields.rs) redefine the
store with the same tokens, each carrying "token *i* of field *F*" (`field_prov`: 2 bits field, 14 bits position; the author
field is the top bit alone, 15 bits, which only the observer's per-call positions reach past 16,383, #837), and
record the field's extent (`lx_field_extent_<F>`): the position of every token of the value that makes ink — a letter,
an other character, a control sequence, an active character; not a space, brace, `$`, `^`, `_`, `&`, `#`, whose effect
the tokens around them cover. Each `\title` (`\author`) call's positions follow the previous call's
(`lx_field_base_<F>`), so a copy of an earlier value (`\let\oldtitle\@title`, then `\title{Short}`) is no print of the
current one (fms1 re-review finding 7; guard `field_prov_earlier_value_copy_kept`), and a print is judged on the
current call's positions only (`lx_field_range_<F>`: a run's cover is clipped to them, and a run that consumes an
earlier call's positions is joined with none — round 3 joined `\title{A Title}`'s print with the next call's and lifted
both: round-3 review finding 2, probes r12, r13; guards `field_prov_title_calls_kept`, `field_prov_edef_calls` (also the
copies in reverse order), `field_prov_author_calls_kept`, `field_prov_title_after_maketitle_kept`); a field whose calls
pass 16,383 tokens in all is not stamped (and no earlier copy of it is whole).
Nothing is added to the store, so every token operation sees exactly what pdflatex sees (the round-1 in-band marks made
`\ifx\@title\same`, `\equal`, `\IfStrEq`, `\pdfstrcmp` false, `\StrLen` 6 for "Same", `\@gobble`/`\@car`/`\StrLeft`
take a mark, and `\csname\@title\endcsname` err — fms1 review finding 3; guard `field_prov_token_tests`, every line =
pdflatex). An empty or blank value is left unstamped.

The provenance travels the way the tokens do: copies keep it (macro bodies, arguments, `\edef`/`\protected@xdef`,
titling's `\thetitle` set by the after-slot from the stamped store); the expansion of a stamped token inherits it
(gullet `invoke_expansion` and the partial-expansion loop, `inherit_field_prov`: an `\and` in `\@author` expands to
author ink); a case change keeps it (`\uppercase`, the kernel `\MakeUppercase`'s `\lx@latex@changecase` change the
character, not the provenance). What a stamped token digests to carries it (stomach `invoke_token`: the box or whatsit's
`fieldProv` property), with what its invocation consumed of the value: its own position up to the next stamped token
still in the pushback (`gullet::field_cover_of`: a primitive's or constructor's arguments, `\hspace{1em}`'s `1em`,
`\\[2pt]`'s `[2pt]`, a formula from its `$`), merged with the cover of a boxless invocation just before it (a font
switch, `\relax`, a macro still to be expanded: `token::field_cover_set_pending`; a macro's position and arguments are
covered by its expansion's boxes). Each such cover is recorded in digestion order in the field ledger
(`token::field_ledger_push`, the box's `fieldSerial`). The document builder (core `Document::absorb`) turns the boxes into
runs of field ink: a box of field *F* opens a run with `<?ltx-field-mark begin F id?>` where its ink goes (the open text
node closed first), the next boxes of *F* at that absorb level continue it while they go on in the value's order, and
the run closes with `<?ltx-field-mark end F id serials?>` (the ledger serials of the boxes it absorbed) before the
first box without that field, or when the absorb that opened it ends (a table cell's, an environment body's). A box
whose cover ends at or before a position a box of the run started at reads the value again: it
closes the run and opens one of its own (`\StrLeft{\@title}{3}\@title`, the second print's `T`; a construct's own box
absorbed around what its argument made, `\textsc{One}`'s whatsit after `One`, covers it and goes on). A re-read from
the value's first position starts where a macro's expansion does (all its boxes at the macro's position), so a run is
also no whole print when it holds a box of one character of the value twice (`lx_field_chars_<F>`, the letters and
other characters: `\StrLeft{\@title}{1}\@title`'s two `T`s; a print digests each character once). Round 3 made such
a line one run covering the whole value and lifted "TwiTwice Title" (round-3 review finding 4, probes r4, r5; guards
`field_prov_reprint_order_kept`, also fragment/whole/fragment, and `field_prov_whole_twice_lifted`: the whole title
twice on one line is two whole prints, each lifted). What a field-ink whatsit absorbs is its ink, whatever its parts'
provenance. No run opens in math, at any depth of an `ltx:Math` (an `\mbox` in a formula is no print of the field).
A run's cover is what the ledger recorded for the boxes it absorbed (`token::field_ledger_cover`), and for what an
alignment took between and right after them: a row's end marker (a value's `\\` set in a `tabular`), digested and
consumed by `digest_alignment_body` and never absorbed, is kept on the alignment's whatsit
(`document::field_ink_taken_serials`, `FIELD_TAKEN_PROPERTY`) and taken (`token::field_ledger_take`) only when
`Document::absorb` absorbs that whatsit: an alignment never shown — in an unused `\setbox`, `\sbox`, `{lrbox}` —
takes nothing (round 4 flagged the marker at digestion, so the `\\` of such a tabular joined title fragments printed
around it, or completed a print it ends, and they were lifted — round-4 review finding 2, probes s25, s27, s28, controls
s26, s29; guards `field_prov_unshown_alignment_kept`, `field_prov_unshown_alignment_trailing_kept`; a box holding the
alignment used twice takes it twice, `field_prov_alignment_box_used_twice_lifted`). Never an entry absorbed elsewhere or never absorbed: round 3 extended a run over the
ledger's next entries of the field that no run held, so a fragment beside the rest of the value in an unused
`\setbox`, or in a formula's `\mbox`, was taken for whole and lifted (round-3 review finding 1, probes r19, r20; guards
`field_prov_unused_boxes_kept` — also `\sbox`, `\savebox`, `{lrbox}` — `field_prov_math_mbox_kept` and
`field_prov_box_in_math_and_text`, where the formula use of a box was lifted with its paragraph). A box used twice is in
each run that absorbs it (`field_prov_box_used_twice_lifted`). A run set in invisible ink (`\phantom`, `\vphantom`:
`<ltx:text class="ltx_phantom">`) is no print and joins none (`field_prov_phantom_kept`). The marks are processing
instructions (no node of content to the block built around them; an element mark made a `{center}` a logical-block —
settled dead end), and a run's two marks carry its id, so they pair by construction, never with another print's (the
round-1 begin/end pairing took `\StrLeft{\@title}{5}`'s begin and `\StrGobbleLeft{\@title}{6}`'s end and removed the
paragraph between them — finding 2; guard `field_prov_fragments_kept`). One print split by the structure it is set in
(article's author `tabular`s: one run per cell, `\and`'s `\end{tabular}…\begin{tabular}`) is joined back: a run that
goes on with the field's later positions, with no ink between the two, is one run with the one before when both
consume the current call's positions only and their covers, with what the alignment took between them (the cells'
`\\`), cover every extent position from where the first stopped to where the second starts (`field_ink_runs`;
1605.00182, 0706.0979, 1004.2125; guard `field_prov_author_tabular_lifted`). A second print
starts over and stays a run of its own, and two slices with a gap (`\StrLeft{\@title}{2}\par\StrRight{\@title}{2}`,
nothing of the gap digested) stay two runs, neither whole (round 2 joined them by their endpoints and removed both —
re-review finding 2, probe q16; guard `field_prov_two_slices_kept`). What an alignment took right after a run's last
box, of its field and continuing its cover, is the run's too, past an entry that covers no position of the extent (the
space the cell drops before it): a value's closing `\\` (1605.00182's `\author{… \\ }`; guard
`field_prov_author_trailing_cr_lifted`).
The work is gated: none in a conversion that stamped no field (`note_field_prov_stamped`), and none after the
placement settled the ink — the builder marks no run and the stomach records no ledger entry
(`token::field_ledger_live`, `field_ledger_settle`; guard `field_ledger_take_cover_and_settle`). That thread state is
per conversion: `document::reset_field_provenance` (the stamped gate, the ledger, its settled flag, the pending
cover) runs at every conversion's start, in `reset_conversion_state` (the session's `initialize_report`), not only in `reset_thread_engine` — a
persistent `cortex_worker` thread, a streaming restart and the CLI's supplements convert on one thread without an
engine reset, and round 4's settled ledger made every document after the first lift nothing (round-4 review finding
1, probe two/; guard `field_prov_second_conversion_lifted`, two conversions on one thread).

**The lift.** Where the frontmatter is placed — `\lx@frontmatterhere` (the `\maketitle` flush) and the fallback's
non-abstract branch (the first sectional unit or `\end{document}`) — `lift_marked_field_ink` runs once
(`lx_field_ink_settled`, `Document::settle_field_ink`: the open run closed, no runs after) and removes each run's ink,
with the wrappers it empties (not a `labels` one), when:
- the run is the whole field: its cover holds every position of the field's extent (`covers_extent`), a macro's too,
  so a slice the document takes of it (`\StrLeft`, `\StrMid`, `\@car`, `\@gobble`) is its own text and stays — also one
  that stops before a macro of the value (`\StrLeft{\@title}{5}` of `About \nm`: round 2 judged the first and last
  character only and lifted "About" — re-review finding 2, probe q2; guard `field_prov_slice_before_macro_kept`), while
  a print of a value holding a macro, `\\[2pt]`, `\hspace{1em}`, a font switch and a formula is whole
  (`field_prov_args_whole_lifted`);
- the run is in the document's title block: no body text precedes it in the document's content order
  (`field_runs_after_body_text`): no text before its begin mark, the text before it in its own block too, except a
  field's ink (between a run's marks: a title before its author), what is set apart from the page's flow (a frontmatter
  element, a note, a float, an error's markup, an index mark — round-4 review finding 4, probe s31,
  `field_prov_indexmark_lifted` — `ltx_phantom` ink, the `_Capture_` marks), and the text of a TeX box that does not
  hold the run. A box is decided by the TeX mechanism, not by the element it builds (main-session call 2026-10-17 on
  round-4 review finding 3), and a box marks only the element its own constructor opened, at the point it opens it
  (main-session call on round-5 review finding 1, option B; `Document::mark_field_box`, the `_fieldbox` bookkeeping
  attribute stripped at finalize): a constructor declared `mode => "restricted_horizontal"` outside math
  (`DeclaredMode::restricted_box`; `Constructor::digest_to_whatsit` sets the `fieldBox` whatsit property and the first
  element its absorption opens, before it absorbs anything, is marked, `Document::open_element`; one that opens none
  marks nothing; the digest-time mark waits for the live ledger only, not for a stamped field, since a header box may be
  digested before the body declares `\title` — the stamp is applied at absorb time, int22 on the r6 review finding 1): `\hbox` (so `\rightline`/`\leftline`/`\centerline`, each `\hbox to\hsize`, and `\colorbox`,
  color.sty's `\color@b@x`), `\mbox`, `\makebox`, `\raisebox`, `\fcolorbox`,
  `\scalebox`/`\resizebox`/`\rotatebox`/`\reflectbox`, amsmath's `\text` and `\eqref` outside math (an `\mbox`, an
  `\hbox`), `\shortstack`, `\put`, the pstricks frame boxes, `\turnbox`; `\framebox`/`\fbox` (no declared mode: its text
  branch, `\@frameb@x`'s `\hbox`); the capture of `insert_block` — `\vbox`, `\vtop`, `\parbox`, a minipage, a `p`
  column, a framed box (framed, mdframed, ascmac, a cuted strip, a tabularray box) — the mark riding its rename, its
  paragraph move and the lone child that takes its attributes, while a capture unwrapped into the context marks nothing;
  an environment whose begin code opens a box group (`TexGroup::Box`, latex.ltx's `\setbox\@tempboxa\vbox\bgroup`),
  checked behind the field-ink gate; an alignment's container (armed around its `open_container`). An element merged up
  by the font collapse (`auto_collapse_children`: an `\mbox` alone in its paragraph) leaves its mark on the element it
  merged into, which then holds only that box's material. Material a `\vbox`/`\vtop` absorbs straight into its context
  (a `\vbox` in a `\vbox`) marks nothing: round 5 marked "the current element if still empty", so
  `\noindent\vbox{\vbox{\hbox{X}}} Lorem…` marked the empty paragraph and its body text stopped counting (probes b2,
  b10, b11; guards `field_prov_nested_vbox_body_kept`, `field_prov_nested_vtop_body_kept`,
  `field_prov_nested_vbox_quote_kept`). Not boxes: `mode => "text"` constructors (`\textbf`), `\textsuperscript`
  (latex.ltx's `\mbox` is inside math), `{center}`/ `{flushright}` (`aligning_environment`'s capture is unmarked). Of
  the 54 constructors declared `restricted_horizontal` (each audited against its package), those that are no TeX box in
  the original: `\@index` (`\index` writes, prints nothing; `ltx:indexmark` is set apart anyway),
  `\lxDeclare`/`\@lxDefMathDeclare` and `\textbb` (bbold's font command; both open no element, so mark nothing),
  `\lx@acm@addresspart@` (acmart's `\institution`/`\city`…, plain text of `\affiliation`; marked, inside the
  frontmatter's contact, which is set apart), and `\tablenotemark` (an `\rlap` box in agupp.sty and the old aastex,
  `\textsuperscript` in aastex701.cls:8494; marked, but emitted as an `ltx:note`, which is set apart in a table or out
  of one, deluxetable_sty.rs:226-227). Round 4 took the element names
  `ltx:inline-block`/`inline-logical-block`/`inline-para`/`tabular` for boxes, so `\makebox`, `\mbox`, `\fbox`,
  `\raisebox` and `\rightline` (all an `ltx:text`) were body text and `\parbox` not. A cover's header box (the
  preprint-number `\parbox` of 0706.0979 and 1605.00182, a `\rightline{LA-UR-…}`, a `\makebox[\textwidth][r]{…}`, an
  `\mbox{preprint …}`, a `\colorbox`, an `\fcolorbox`, a `\scalebox`) is no body text
  (`field_prov_header_parbox_lifted`, `field_prov_header_rightline_lifted`, `field_prov_header_makebox_lifted`,
  `field_prov_header_mbox_lifted`, `field_prov_header_colorbox_lifted`, `field_prov_header_fcolorbox_lifted`,
  `field_prov_header_scalebox_lifted`; probes r16, r17, h1-h4). Paragraph material in a list environment
  (`{flushright}`, `{center}`, `quote`, an aligned display) is body text (`field_prov_header_flushright_kept`), and so
  is material no box constructor opened an element for (`\unhbox`/`\unvbox`, a capture unwrapped): the print kept
  (fail-safe). A letter
  that ends `\noindent\@author` signs it where pdflatex prints the name, and keeps it, its body in the paragraph flow
  (round 2 lifted it at the `\end{document}` fallback — re-review finding 3, probe q3; guard
  `field_prov_signature_after_body_kept`), in `{flushleft}` or in a `{quote}` in the signature's own paragraph (round 3
  took aligned and quoted text, and the text of the print's own block, for no body, and lifted the signature —
  round-3 review finding 3, probes r9, r18; guards `field_prov_letter_flushleft_kept`, `field_prov_letter_quote_kept`).
  Header cases that therefore stay (kept, as before S1): a header line before the title block in the flow or in a
  list environment — plain text (`Preprint ABC-123\hfill\today`, probe r11; `field_prov_header_text_kept`),
  `{flushright}` (`field_prov_header_flushright_kept`), a centred subject line; and text the title block sets before a
  print (a `\textsuperscript{*}` after the title, a `by`, an affiliation
  line before a second print: review probe q9, whose three prints round 3 lifted), which keeps the prints after it;
- the frontmatter displays the field, by the XSLT's rule: no `<ltx:titlepage>` at document level (beside one the title
  template is skipped and a creator renders nothing, LaTeXML-structure-xhtml.xsl:374-375, :687-692 = Perl :358-359)
  and a document-level `<ltx:title>`, resp. author `<ltx:creator>` (round 1 also lifted an author print beside a
  titlepage, leaving the HTML without an author — finding 1; guard `field_prov_author_beside_titlepage_kept`); so a
  print beside or inside a titlepage is the displayed copy and stays (1304.0681, 1503.03277);
- every ancestor of both marks is a title-block wrapper (`is_field_ink_wrapper`: para, p, logical and inline blocks,
  text, emph, a cover tabular) and none is framed: never inside a titlepage, a float, a note, a frontmatter element or a
  frame (`\fbox{\@title}`), as the dedup (68s review finding 4);
- the prints fill their lines: the paragraph or table cell around each mark holds nothing but the runs being lifted
  (all fields judged together, until none drops out: a title and its author on one line go together — finding 5;
  guard `field_prov_title_author_one_line`) and line breaks (`\centerline`'s, which go with it), so a mention in prose
  (`This report, \@title, …`, `Title: \thetitle`) keeps its words.

**Every whole print is lifted** (user ruling 2026-10-17, "lift every whole print"): a title or author the document
prints N times as a whole in its title block shows once, in the frontmatter element (field_mark_uppercase: pdflatex
"UPPER TITLE" twice, here the `<h1>` only).

The lift is judged where the frontmatter is placed, mid-build: `\noindent\@title\maketitle{} and then …` (re-review
probe q15) lifts the title from a paragraph that the document's text continues, which is right because latex.ltx's
`\maketitle` begins with `\par`, so the print is a paragraph of its own; a print and `\maketitle` inside one `{center}`
(probes q13, q14) is not lifted by provenance (the dedup, or kept, as before S1).

Residuals (missed lifts; the print stays, as before S1): a value that ends in a primitive's argument
(`\title{Foo\vspace{2pt}}`) or in a macro whose arguments its expansion drops is no whole print (nothing stamped
follows to bound what it consumed); a value holding a `\footnote` (`\title{Foot Title\footnote{…}}` printed, round-3
review probes r7, r8); a value built from an earlier one (`\let\oldtitle\@title`, `\title{\oldtitle\\[1ex]\large Sub
Title}`: the expansion of `\oldtitle` carries the earlier call's positions, so the current call's `\oldtitle` is never
covered, probe r14); an `\edef` copy of an earlier call whose value the next call repeats (`\edef\xa{\@title}
\title{Same Title}`, probe r15: the copy carries the earlier call's positions); the header cases above; a value whose
print digests one of its characters twice (a document macro that sets its argument twice inside `\title{…}`), taken
for a re-read (above).

Every mark goes with the lift; marks still in the tree at `\end{document}` are removed with their ink kept
(`settle_field_marks`), and the core finalize drops a stray one (document.rs, `FIELD_MARK_TARGET`). A lifted title
print sets `lx_title_ink_dedup_done`, so the dedup is left for a copy no provenance explains. Each lift logs
`Info:frontmatter:field_ink`. `\pdfstringdef` is a `\gdef` here (hyperref_sty.rs) and the `pdftitle=` RDF value the
unexpanded keyval (Perl's `ToString`).

Cost: no `Token` growth (8 bytes; the `token-locators` origin handle `loc` cannot carry it without making that build
the default, 12 bytes per token); the stamping, the expansion inheritance, the covers and the absorb runs touch only
stamped tokens and the boxes absorbed before the placement settles the ink. The measured cost (user ruling 2026-10-17:
accepted, plus one profiling pass) was the token layout: Rust's default layout put `prov` at byte 4 and `code` at 6
with a pad byte, so every move of a token on the gullet's read path (`Option<Token>`, `CheckedRead::Tok`, the `Result`
slot of `read_internal_token_checked`) became a field-wise copy (agent_reports/2026-10-17_fms1_profile.md). `perf stat
-e instructions:u`, bench builds, 3 runs each, against the base a034d4e7f5: empty article +1.29 % (round 2) → +0.65 %
(`repr(C)` + two-byte `Catcode`; `repr(C)` alone +1.14 %, the pad byte still copied as a 3-byte blob); 2311.18489
+3.27 % → +1.66 % (938.6M / 950.7M / 944.7M and 4738.0M / 4892.8M / 4816.8M instructions). XML identical; peak RSS +0.1-0.5 % (round 2).
What remains is the read path's token handling, not reworked (one bounded pass): `read_internal_token_checked`'s
return writes three stores (`text`, `code`, `prov`; base two, round 2 four with the pad), and the `Option<Token>`
niche test of the pushback pop is still a 64-bit mask on the whole token.

Not in S1 (stages S2-S5 of the study): the lock is unchanged, no call observer, no mechanism deleted; bindings' own
`\title`/`\author` (revtex4_support, ams_support, iopart_support, mn2e_support, …) do not stamp; the deposit of a
refused class `\maketitle` still nulls `\@title`/`\@author`, so a class's title page prints nothing stamped; display
stays "lift" (the in-place display is S5, after a ruling). A/B: see SYNC_STATUS (fms1). Repros
sectioning-frontmatter/field_mark_*, field_prov_*; guards `perfect_kernel_batchfms1`.

*Live rule: OD #262.*

### 741. A neurips copy's stored `\@projectpage`/`\@emailaddress` are the paper's contacts (TeX: printed as text at its abstract's end; Perl: no binding for the setters)

**TeX**: 2605.09681's neurips_2026.sty copy adds `\newcommand{\projectpage}[1]{\gdef\@projectpage{#1}}` and
`\emailaddress` (:410-411; the distributed style has neither) and prints the non-empty stores at the end of its renewed
`{abstract}` (:445-458): "Project Page: \texttt{…}", "Email Address: …".

**Perl**: neurips.sty.ltxml defines neither; the copy's abstract is not read, so the values are lost (with the copy's
setters) or `\projectpage` is undefined (without).

**Rust** (73a r4; user 2026-10-18, option C, superseding int23's Fallback-origin setters): the binding defines no
setter — the copy's own are provided as usual (#731) and store — and its `\end{abstract}` (neurips_sty.rs, the kernel's
`\lx@end@abstract` after) emits a non-empty `\@projectpage` as a `role=url` contact named "Project Page: " and
`\@emailaddress` as a `role=email` contact named "Email Address: " (`\lx@neurips@contacts`, `\lx@add@contact`), where
the copy's abstract prints them — frontmatter, not text. Without such a copy nothing is defined: `\projectpage` errs
undefined, as in TeX. Witness 2605.09681 (both contacts kept). Repros stand-in-copies/neurips_contact/copy_setters_are_contacts
(with the copy) and stand-in-copies/neurips_no_copy/projectpage_undefined_without_a_copy (in a directory without one); guards `perfect_kernel_batchint23::neurips_copy_setters_are_contacts`,
`perfect_kernel_batch73a::neurips_projectpage_undefined_without_a_copy`.

### 753. A table of contents inside a frontmatter container goes after it; `\tableofcontents` begins as a heading

**Perl behavior**: latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:725-743 binds `\tableofcontents`, `\listoffigures` and `\listoftables`
to `<ltx:TOC …>` constructors inserted where they stand. Inside a balanced `{abstract}` (`abstract_model` = Block.model,
no TOC) that is `malformed:ltx:TOC <ltx:TOC> isn't allowed in <ltx:p>` (or `<ltx:abstract>`), the TOC left inside, the
document invalid; after a brace-less `\abstract` the same, since the TOC does not end it (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #978).
**Rust behavior**: (1) `insert_toc` (sect04.rs) puts the TOC of an insertion point inside a frontmatter container
(`ltx:abstract`, `ltx:acknowledgements`, `ltx:keywords`, `ltx:classification`, `ltx:creator`) at the nearest open
ancestor that admits it (`Document::float_out_of_frontmatter`: Perl's `floatToElement`, Document.pm:1052-1077, closing
form; the container cannot auto-close, so the insertion point comes back): after the abstract, and the text after it
stays the abstract's. Elsewhere the TOC is inserted as before (in a `{quote}` the inline logical block of #271's bridge).
(2) The kernel's three begin `\par\@startsection@hook` (in `\lx@kernel@listof{<ext>}{<title>}`, which
`\lx@kernel@tableofcontents`/`…listoffigures`/`…listoftables` call,
`\protected` as `\section*` is robust, still the user name's only token before `\lx@kernel@listbody`: tocbasic.sty:1175-1179's
`\edef` of `\newcommand*\csname listof\tb@nt@types\endcsname{…}`, KOMA's `\DeclareNewTOC`, expands `\listoffigures`
and must meet one token), as the `\section*{\contentsname…}` they are in article.cls,
report.cls and amsart.cls (`\chapter*` in book.cls) does: a paragraph ends, and after a brace-less `\abstract` or inside
an unclosed `\abstract{` the TOC ends the abstract as a `\section` does (sect05.rs `\abstract`), the hook's other
members running as at any heading (the frontmatter fallback of a document without `\maketitle`, a bibliography's end).
A raw class's own `\tableofcontents` replaces the kernel's, as before (memoir's and oblivoir's lists, which read
a `.toc` LaTeXML never writes, are `\lx@kernel@listof` again: memoir_cls.rs, MEM1; the list's name is read
`Undigested`, as Perl's literal `'toc'`, since a Greek font typeset it "τος": 0712.0401). A TOC inside a balanced abstract goes after it while the
abstract's text after it stays the abstract's, where a `\section`/`\section*` there ends the abstract and starts the
body with the text after it (#755, `\lx@heading@ends@frontmatter` at sect04.rs:202-205; the TOC's
`\@startsection@hook` does not read it): the TOC follows the schema and Perl's own placement of an element its context
refuses.
**Why**: pdflatex prints the TOC inside the abstract's quotation (`\section*` in the `quotation` list), where the schema
has no place for it; after the abstract keeps both whole and in order. Witnesses — a balanced abstract ending with
`\tableofcontents{}` (LyX; amsart/article/revtex4): 1011.3976, 1310.0349, 1509.04736, 1404.7641, 0809.1270, 1509.03167,
1706.09575, 2105.04928, 2401.08592, 2403.19281, 2408.04858, 2408.11452, 2509.01284; mid-abstract 1602.08755; an
unclosed `\abstract`/`\abstract{` (article/report): 2007.03709, 2202.05904, 2411.02384, 2506.07991, 2512.04732,
2602.15970, hep-lat9910044; mdpi's template under article 2104.05770; sapthesis 1603.02077 (its `\mainmatter` after
the TOC was read inside the unclosed abstract, its chapters' sections unnumbered: now numbered as in the PDF). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch74a::{toc_at_the_end_of_a_balanced_abstract_follows_it, toc_mid_abstract_follows_it_and_the_text_stays,
toc_ends_an_unclosed_abstract, toc_ends_an_unclosed_braced_abstract, lists_of_figures_and_tables_follow_the_abstract,
toc_outside_the_frontmatter_is_unchanged}`; repros `sectioning-frontmatter/{toc_inside_balanced_abstract_at_its_end,
toc_inside_balanced_abstract_mid_text, toc_ends_an_unclosed_abstract, toc_ends_an_unclosed_braced_abstract,
lists_of_figures_and_tables_inside_abstract}`.

### 754. A frontmatter body left open at `\end{document}` ends there and keeps its text (Perl: an empty document)

An abstract (or keywords) is read as a deferred frontmatter body up to its terminal (`\lx@add@frontmatter@until …
\lx@end@abstract`, base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_fields.rs). Left open — an unclosed `\begin{abstract}`, an unbalanced `\abstract{`, a
brace-less `\abstract` no sectioning command ends — that body ran to the end of input: it held the finalizer and the
rest of the document, and nothing placed it, so the output was an empty `<document/>` with 0 errors (Perl: resources
only, 1 error). pdflatex prints every word. `\end{document}` now begins with `\lx@end@open@frontmatter` (sect02.rs):
when the nearest open frontmatter body is such a body, its terminal is read first, the body ends with its text (one body
per pass, so keywords left open inside an abstract end both, int26 review p8), and the end-document code runs at the
document's level, as an unclosed `{itemize}` keeps its list (65c). Diagnostics as pdflatex's: the
unclosed `\begin{abstract}` is LaTeX's error (`\@checkend`: "\begin{abstract} … ended by \end{document}"; Perl errs
too), raised once, on the first pass, naming the innermost environment begun with `\begin` (`\@currenvir`:
stomach.rs `begun_environment` — `\begin`'s `current_environment`, or `lx@until@begun`, which the kernel's
`\begin{abstract}`, no environment frame of its own, leaves in its body's frame; the IEEEtran binding's
`\begin{IEEEkeywords}` now sets `\@currenvir` as `\begin` does), and only at the body's own level (an environment open
inside it, a `{minipage}`, keeps its Warning, as before). A begin code called as a command opens no environment LaTeX
checks, so it reports nothing: the brace-less `\abstract`, mn2e's `\keywords{…}`, spconf's `\keywords …` (an int26 A/B
fix: four papers had gained a spurious Error, 1004.2791, 2201.07008, 2309.07195, 1401.5657); the unbalanced `\abstract{`
reports its open group (`until_terminal_inside_group`). A heading after an unclosed `\begin{abstract}` ends it (#755).
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #980. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch74b::{braceless_abstract_unclosed_at_end_document_keeps_its_text,
braced_abstract_unclosed_at_end_document_keeps_its_text, environment_abstract_unclosed_at_end_document_errs_and_keeps_its_text}`;
repros `sectioning-frontmatter/{braceless,braced}_abstract_unclosed_at_end_document_keeps_the_document`,
`sectioning-frontmatter/unclosed_abstract_at_end_document_keeps_the_document`.
**Why**: the status code must be honest (user 2026-10-18): a whole document lost with 0 errors counted as a success.

### 755. A sectioning heading inside an abstract ends the abstract (Perl: an error, the heading nested)

User ruling 2026-10-18: "A \section inside an abstract should close/complete the abstract". `\@startsection` (sect04.rs)
at section level or above (`\part`, `\chapter`, `\section`, starred or not) first reads `\lx@heading@ends@frontmatter`
(sect05.rs): when the nearest open frontmatter body is an abstract or keywords, its terminal is read before the heading,
so the body ends with the text before it and the heading starts the document's body with the text after it — as the
brace-less `\abstract` already ended at `\@startsection@hook`. Keywords alike (int26 A/B fix round): an environment's
begin code called as a command has no extent — mn2e.cls:993-1003 and mnras.cls:1122-1131 `\keywords` open a `\list` no
`\endkeywords` closes, spconf's and ieeeconf's are labels — and the text the author gave it ends where the paper's first
section begins; read as the open body, the whole document went into `<ltx:keywords>`, every section an Error
(`<ltx:section> isn't allowed in <ltx:keywords>`, then in `<ltx:section>`): 1004.2791, 2201.07008, 2309.07195 (28
Errors → 0, words unchanged). A keywords body a command form opened inside the abstract ends with it
(base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_fields.rs `\lx@end@abstract`; ieeeconf `\begin{abstract} … \keywords \MyKeywords \end{abstract}`, 1401.5657). The `\end{abstract}` that follows is then a no-op; one a
heading-ended `\begin{abstract}` never gets is LaTeX's "\begin{abstract} ended by \end{document}" at `\end{document}`
(sect02.rs `\lx@end@open@frontmatter`). Not inside a replayed class begin code (its `\section*{\abstractname}` is the
class's own heading, discarded with the replay, #482), and not where a class rebinds `\section` inside the abstract
(frontiersFPHY's `\absection`: a run-in label, no heading). An abstract the heading closed before its first line (the structured-abstract idiom, scrartcl
`\begin{abstract}\section*{Abstract:} …`, 1507.08575) holds nothing and adds no entry: `\lx@add@frontmatter@until`
keeps no body that typesets nothing (abstract, keywords, classification), so an empty environment leaves no empty
element either (Perl: an empty `ltx:abstract`). Lower levels (`\subsection`…`\subparagraph`) do not close
it; pdflatex sets the heading inside the abstract's text block either way. Perl: `<ltx:section> isn't allowed in
<ltx:abstract>` (1 error); ours kept it nested, schema-invalid (74a row (b)). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch74b::{section_inside_balanced_abstract_closes_it,
environment_abstract_unclosed_at_end_document_errs_and_keeps_its_text, keywords_command_form_ends_at_first_section,
keywords_label_inside_abstract_ends_with_it}`; repros `sectioning-frontmatter/{abstract_section_closes_the_abstract,
keywords_command_form_ends_at_first_section, class_keywords/keywords_label_inside_abstract_ends_with_it}`.

### 756. The `\maketitle` replay gate reads a class body as TeX runs it (Perl: the class body is never run)

`body_vocabulary_is_defined` (sect05.rs; the gate of the #265 `\maketitle` replay and the #482 setter replays) asks
whether every control sequence a refused class body would run is defined. It now reads the body as TeX does:
- the parameter text and replacement text of a `\def`/`\gdef` (any prefix) and the default and body of a
  `\newcommand`-family definition are stored, not run (tex.web §473 `scan_toks` with `xpand` false): they are checked
  where the body calls the macro, once (`BodyDefinee`), and a macro the body never calls is not checked;
  `\edef`/`\xdef` replacement texts are expanded as they are defined (§1218) and stay checked in place;
- the delimiters a called macro's parameter text matches (`Match`/`Until` parameters, tex.web §392-399) are
  matched, not run (`delimiter_positions`); the arguments themselves stay checked;
- what a called macro's body defines counts as defined after the call;
- `\futurelet` defines what it lets, as `\let` does (§1221);
- a token `\ifx`, `\ifdefined`, `\string` or `\meaning` only compares or shows is not checked (#906).
The gate itself never reports: a parameter text is read by its own `gate_parameters` — `None` (no delimiters matched,
the call's arguments checked as tokens) for one holding an argument of the enclosing macro (an `ARG` token), a doubled
`#` or parameters out of order — and never by `parse_def_parameters`, whose ParamSpec Fatal is sticky (a class
`\renewcommand{\author}[1]{\expandafter\def\csname tp@au#1\endcsname##1{##1}…}` marked a clean paper Fatal). A name `\csname` makes has its tokens run in place, and an `\expandafter` chain expands the one token after the
replacement text's brace (`expandafter_definee`: `\expandafter\def\expandafter\x\expandafter{\y\z}` defines `\x` and
checks `\y`); the rest of either's replacement text is stored like any `\def`'s (tex.web §473), so only an
`\edef`/`\xdef` reads it in place (round 3). A called
macro's definitions count only for a control sequence undefined here, from its live branches and outside the stored
replacement texts of the definitions it makes (`callee_definees`), so a real meaning is never shadowed. A body whose own
definitions call one another more than 8 deep is refused with an Info, not admitted unread.
jpsj.sty:170-173's own `\twocolumn`, replayed with its `\maketitle`, sets `\@twocolumntrue` globally, so its `{full}`
equations become `ltx:float[figure]` with their two rules (cond-mat0011490), as pdflatex lays them out (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
#901: `\twocolumn` sets the flag).
sig-alternate-05-2015.cls:726-737's `\maketitle` defines `\@makefnmark` (article.cls:206, reading `\@thefnmark`, which
latex.ltx defines only when a footnote is made): "not replayed: it uses \@thefnmark" stopped 204 of the 3,000
sample papers' replays, which now run (1505.04771's `\toappear` "pre-print of an article appearing at KDD'16"; the
ACM copyright/permission blocks of 0712.1016, 1301.5612, 1609.02839, cs0404029; the NeurIPS venue lines of
1506.04304, 1704.05155, 2111.02813; 2407.00478's author notes). nowfnt.cls:552-583's `\author` calls
`\nowfnt@splitauthor#2,!,!,\@nil` and reads the `\nowfnt@lastname` it defines (1912.00312: the replay now runs; its
`\maintitleauthorlist` is a separate residual, SYNC_STATUS 75a). A/B over those 204 papers and 40 more (the
two-refusal `\maketitle` and wiley/nbdt/CSML papers of the sample) against 67int27: E 1,933 → 1,924, F 2 → 2, no paper
with more errors, none losing more than 1 % of its words, no doubled creator. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch75a::{maketitle_replay_skips_stored_replacement_text, maketitle_replay_skips_called_delimiters,
maketitle_replay_gate_reads_csname_def_silently, maketitle_replay_expandafter_def_reads_in_place,
maketitle_replay_gate_stores_csname_and_expandafter_definitions}`; repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/class_title_page/maketitle_replay_{skips_*,gate_reads_csname_def_silently,expandafter_def_reads_in_place,
gate_stores_csname_and_expandafter_definitions}`.

### 763. an.cls, apa.cls and cclayout.sty title-page stores are the frontmatter (Perl: OmniBus for the classes, an Error on `{subject}`)

Under the raw classes (OD #444) three class stores that only a class's own title page prints were lost with 0 errors
(silent-loss inventory #11, #23). Each is now the frontmatter element where the class or package defines its setter:
- **an.cls** (Astronomische Nachrichten; not in TeX Live, the papers ship it): `\abstract` is the class's `\aaabstract`
  (an.cls:98 `\AtEndOfClass{\let\abstract=\aaabstract}`, :414 `\gdef\@abstract{#1}`, read by `\@maketitle` :718), so
  the text was a plain paragraph of the deposited title block. A new stand-in binding (latexml_contrib `an_cls.rs`,
  listed in `AUTHOR_FILE_STAND_INS`) reads the shipped copy raw and redefines `\aaabstract` as `\lx@add@abstract`
  before the end-of-class hook copies it; without a copy it is OmniBus, with the loader's missing-file status and
  "Can't find binding for class an (using OmniBus)" Warning (latexml_package `shipped_class::omnibus_without_copy`,
  which the cimento, compositio, jinst and apa-family stand-ins share; the binding's presence had kept the loader from
  raising it). Witness astro-ph0611016 (0 errors before and after; the abstract now `ltx:abstract`, its text once).
  v1.03 (2002/07/04, astro-ph0306340) prints the class's label before the store (`\@maketitle` :662
  `\noindent{\bfseries\abstractname}\ \@abstract`; v1.09a and later comment it out): there the setter passes
  `name={\abstractname}` and the title-page deposit takes that line out of `\@maketitle` (sect05.rs
  `note_title_page_part`, a `\lx@replay@records` record), so no lone bold "Abstract" paragraph stays in the title
  block; `\abstractname` is not changed. With the store given empty, a paper using the class's `{abstract}`
  environment keeps the deposited title block (keywords line, © line), which the deposit dropped while `\@abstract`
  was undefined there. The binding's name makes it the prefix fallback (Perl Package.pm:2717-2728: `my ($alternate)
  = grep` :2723, the Warning :2728) for classes whose name starts with `an` and that have no binding: andp2012.cls
  (1504.05091, 1810.06303) is read raw by it as before, with no `\aaabstract` to redefine — XML byte-identical — plus
  the "Can't find binding for class andp2012 (using an)" Warning; so is the 2014 v1.12 an.cls, which defines
  `\abstract` itself (:422; 1810.02388, 2103.06625).
- **apa.cls** `\acknowledgements` (:461 `\long\def\@acks{#1}`, printed by the doc/jou title pages :1262-1267,
  :1549-1557, and in man mode as a closing section :760-764) is `ltx:acknowledgements` named by `\acksname` ("Author
  Note"), in every mode (apa6_cls.rs `define_notes`, beside `\note`). In man mode this moves the text from the class's
  closing `\AtEndDocument` "Author Note" section (:760-764 `\section{\acksname}\@acks`, which the raw class
  produced) into the frontmatter: semantic markup over PDF placement. `ltx:acknowledgements` is `Inline.model` (the
  schema, as Perl's), so each paragraph of a multi-paragraph argument is a line of it (#766), where the man-mode
  section had kept `<p>`s.
- **cclayout.sty** (cc.cls:229-230): `\Abstract{…}` (:66) and `{subject}` (:76-81) are `ltx:abstract` named
  `\ccabstractname` and `ltx:classification` named `\ccsubjectclassificationname` (latexml_contrib `cclayout_sty.rs`,
  which reads the package raw first); `{keywords}` stays K11's collected-body reroute.

Perl has no binding for any of the three: an.cls and apa.cls fall to OmniBus (an abstract, and `<acknowledgements
name="Acknowledgements">` with `\note` undefined, 1 Error), cc.cls to OmniBus with `{subject}` undefined (1 Error,
"68Q15, 68Q17" a plain paragraph). Repros `sectioning-frontmatter/class_notes/{an_abstract_store_is_the_abstract,
an_v103/an_v103_abstract_label_is_its_name, an_abstract_environment_keeps_the_title_block, apa_acknowledgements_kept,
cclayout_abstract_and_subject_kept}`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch74b::{an_abstract_store_is_the_abstract,
an_v103_abstract_label_is_its_name, an_abstract_environment_keeps_the_title_block, an_without_its_class_warns,
apa_acknowledgements_are_kept_in_every_mode, cclayout_abstract_and_subject_are_kept}`. **Why**: the authored text in its

### 765. Author-name separators beside a control word, a line break or a mark, and in a mark's math (Perl: " and " between spaces only)

Perl's author splitter knows the word "and" only between two space tokens (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:678), and so did
ours, with the ties and `{\ and}` added. TeX skips the spaces after a control word, so `Ann Able\space and Bob`, jfm's
`Badr~Kaoui$^{3,4}$\break and Jens~Harting`, `Chang Liu \ns and Dennice F. Gayme` (jfm.cls:1025 `\newcommand\ns{\kern
.5em\relax}`), `\linebreak and`, a line ending in `\` (latex.ltx:558 `\def\^^M{\ }`), `\thanks{…}and`, `and\;`,
svmult's `Ann Able\orcidID{…} and\\ Bob Baker` and `Sun$^\ast$\&Fei` hold no space token beside the separator pdflatex
prints between the names; every such pair became one author, flagged `Error:frontmatter:merged_creators` or silently
("Lyubov Sveshnikova andVladimir Ptuskin"). Two other shapes merged too: cimento.cls:1525-1526 (every shipped copy)
`\newcommand{\atque}{{\normalfont\MakeLowercase{and\ \ignorespaces}}}`, whose "and" the separator-macro reader
(`separator_macro_text`) gave up on, and a comma written inside a name's mark math (`Wittor$^{1}, $Brüggen`,
`Iacobuta$,^{5,6,7}$ Mabel`, `Manoj$^{2},$ Chandra`), which the split never sees (it does not look inside math).

`split_author_names` now writes these as the split reads them first (`spaced_name_separators`, base_utilities/author_block/separators.rs, at
the line's top level and again in each wrapper's content the split re-reads): the word "and" between two word
boundaries, or `\&` after one, becomes ` and ` / ` \& `, the spacing beside it dropped: spaces, ties, the spacing
commands of `leading_spacing_end` (`\newline` among its parameterless ones, `PARAMETERLESS_SPACING`), the line breaks
of `SEPARATOR_LINE_BREAKS` (`\\`, `\break`, `\linebreak`, `\allowbreak`, `\^^M`) and parameterless macros whose body is
only spacing (`prints_only_spacing`, a spacing command's braced argument its own: `\hspace{1em}`); a space before
declarations that typeset nothing ahead of the word (`\sc Ann Able \rm and`, the frontmatter `LAYOUT` list) goes too.
A boundary is a space or tie, a control word that is no letter or accent command (`parts_words`: a name of two
characters or more, or of one letter — tex.web §354-356, after which TeX skips the spaces), a note's or mark's argument
(`\thanks{…}`, `NAME_ANNOTATIONS`), a group whose text does not end in a letter or a control symbol, or a math span
holding only a superscript. A control symbol skips no space and prints inside the word: `\-` (a discretionary hyphen)
and `\/` (an italic correction) keep "and" in it (`Rol\-and Smith` is "Roland Smith", `Bertr\/and Smith` "Bertrand
Smith"); a spacing one (`\,`, `\;`, `\ `) is a gap. A letter, a letter command (`\L`, `\ss`, `\dj`, `\th`, `\ng` and
their capitals, T1) or an accent's argument beside the word keeps it in its name ("Rand", "Anders", `Zo\"{e}and`,
`{\O}and`, `\textbf{Bak}and` which prints "Bakand"), and `AT\&T` stays one word. The split's name-count gates — the
whole-line group, a wrapper piece (`names_in_wrapper`) and the per-author bindings' cautious split
(`split_author_line_cautious`: amsart, revtex) — count the names with these separators written
(`separated_name_count`), so `{\bf Ann Able\break and Bob Baker}`, `{\bf Ann Able\thanks{…}and Bob Baker}` and amsart's
`\author{Ann Able\break and Bob Baker}` split as their top-level forms do (1801.10166: `\parbox[t]{\textwidth}{Philip
F.~Hopkins\altaffilmark{1}, \&\ Jonathan Squire\altaffilmark{1}}`, merged with `merged_creators` before). A comma at the edge of a math span holding only a superscript mark
moves outside it (`$^{1}$,`, `,$^{5}$`), where the existing rule gives a mark glued after the comma to the name before
it. `separator_macro_text` reads `\ignorespaces` as printing nothing and applies `\MakeLowercase`/`\MakeUppercase`/
`\lowercase`/`\uppercase` to its group's letters, or to the one token after it when no group follows. SHARED with Perl (it merges every one of these, silently); a reading of
the author's intent, beyond what pdflatex prints: TeX drops the space after a control word, so a pair the author typed
apart can print glued (`The ATLAS\thanks{x}and CMS Collaborations` "ATLAS∗and CMS", `Bob Baker \LaTeX and Cat`
"LATEXand Cat", a macro whose expansion ends in a word before `and`; 2005.00317 `\thanks{…}and`) and is still two
creators here; a group ending in a note (`{Ann Able\thanks{x}}and`) continues the word and is not split. A/B (67int29 vs 77d) over the 78 `merged_creators` papers of
the projection samples: 29 of the 55 sole-cause papers to 0 Errors — the six cimento papers (0711.2584, 0801.3557,
1402.1844, 2109.08173, 2309.14694, hep-th0703055), nineteen S2 papers (1311.3650, 1503.04190, 1505.06278, 2005.00317,
1912.02168, 2509.22118, 1504.03105, 1607.04619, 2004.02831, 2404.12084, 2502.11348, astro-ph9704233, 1707.03934,
2401.17237, 2506.15327, 2509.11693, 2403.07875, 2512.18788, 2603.27055), three S3 papers (1610.00129, 2108.04461,
2402.11182) and 1911.02873, whose `\&` now parts the last name while the first two (`FLORIAN REETZ$^1$ \ns PRIYA
SUBRAMANIAN$^{2,3}$`, apart only by a mark and jfm's `\ns`, which also spaces a name's words: `TOBIAS M.\ns SCHNEIDER`)
stay one creator; the merge check (`flag_merged_creators`) reads a personname's `ltx:sup` as ending the name before it
when its text alone reads as fewer than two names, so that creator keeps its `Error:frontmatter:merged_creators`; `merged_creators` also gone from 1012.2722, 1109.2895,
astro-ph9804111, gr-qc0308071; Errors 239 → 207, 0 papers worse, every split checked against the source. On 239
multi-author control papers from pop67int23 one output changed (2409.19958, svmult `and\\` split, its
`merged_creators` gone). 1012.2722's Error count holds: icrc2009.cls's raw `\IEEEauthorblockN` (`#1\crcr`, :3310-3322), re-applied to
each name the wrapper held, errs once per name ("\noalign cannot be used here"), now three names. Not covered: 1706.05664
(its `$^{1}, $` names reach pasj01's own per-author `\author`, not this split) and the S6 shape of the root-cause (a
class's list `\author`; S4 and S5 are 77n's, below).
Not caught either: a pair still merged with nothing but glued text to show it ("Ann Ableand Bob Baker") — "Ableand
Bob" cannot be told from "Ferdinand Smith" by its text, so the merge check does not try. Repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/{author_and_after_a_control_word, author_and_beside_a_line_break,
author_separator_macro_lowercase, author_comma_in_mark_math, author_and_inside_a_word_stays_the_name,
author_and_after_a_break_in_a_wrapper}`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch77d::*`.

**77n: separators inside a wrapper (S4), note commands among the names (S5).** A wrapper's names split inside it
(`names_in_wrapper`) when what follows the wrapper prints nothing but marks and notes, its spacing and paragraph breaks
aside (`without_spacing`: `\emph{Wenzhuo Ouyang, Atilla Eryilmaz, and Ness B. Shroff} \vspace{-9pt}\par \vspace{-5pt}
\thanks{…}`, 1108.3768), and a piece of marks and notes only, inside the wrapper, is the name's before it
(`notes_to_the_name_before`, which also leaves out a line break at a piece's edge: `{Ann Able},~\IEEEmembership{…},\\
{Cat Cole}`) instead of keeping the wrapper whole (`Chia-Hsun Chuang,\thanks{…} \thanks{…} and Yun Wang` in a parbox,
1205.5573; 2112.09769, 2603.10769, 2209.12464). Each name keeps the wrapper's styling (`\emph`, `\uppercase` — the case
TeX prints —, a group's declarations); a layout box (`LAYOUT_BOXES`: `\parbox[pos]{width}{…}`, `\mbox`, `\makebox`,
`\hbox`) styles no name and is left out, with the paragraph layout its content opens with (`\centering`), its other
opening declarations put around each name (`\parbox{…}{\centering\large A, B}`: both large): spconf's
`\name{{\parbox[c]{\textwidth}{\centering A$^{1}$, B$^{2}$, …}}}` (2504.03146), and a name list already split from
its parbox no longer puts each name in a text-wide box of its own (1801.10166, 1011.3045, 2306.06320). A command over an
optional argument is content, not an opening declaration (`{\parbox[c]…}`), and a control word's optional argument,
glue (`\vskip 0.3in`, `\hskip`, `\kern`), a graphic's file name and a link's address are no name text
(`visible_name_text`; hep-ph0107182, whose REVTeX 3 cautious split read "0.3in" as part of the last name;
`\href{…}{\includegraphics[scale=0.06]{orcid.pdf}\hspace{1mm}Hossein Bahak, Farzaneh Taheri}`, 2312.07592). The word "and" opening or closing a wrapper is a separator of the line
(`hoist_wrapped_separators`: mdpi's `\mbox{and {Thomas~P.} Krichbaum $^{5}$}`, 2108.09054), and a row ending in a
wrapped comma reads as unfinished (`names_list_continues` reads the row with its wrapped separators hoisted:
`\textbf{Seth Ebner}$^{\diamondsuit}$\textrm{,} \\ \textbf{Brandon Smock}, …`, 2512.18601). The note commands of a
name (`is_name_annotation`) are `NAME_ANNOTATIONS` with `\footnotetext` (revtex4-1 2201.11098; amsppt
`D. Logachev\footnotemark \footnotetext{…}`, 2209.04044), elsarticle's `\corref`/`\fnref`/`\tnoteref` (`… and Anil
Bhardwaj \corref{cor1}`, 1201.6291) and `\institute` (ecai.cls 2020:450 `\newcommand{\institute}[1]{\thanks{#1}}`,
2008.02735), and a document's own note macro, one whose every argument goes into a `\thanks` or `\footnote` of its
body (`is_note_macro`: `\blackthanks`, 2506.03876; a macro printing an argument itself is none). An author block's
`\begin{footnote}{text}…\end{footnote}` is read as LaTeX reads it, `\footnote{text}` and the rest
(`note_environments_as_commands`: the comma after the first note parts `Velibor \v{Z}eli` and `Du\v{s}an Zorica`,
1703.02032; the environment's `\begingroup`/`\endgroup` is not kept, as it would open in one name and close in the
next), and its math-active `^`/`_` (catcode 12, mathcode "8000, as mathstyle.sty:233-236, :251-258 sets them from
`\begin{document}`, which breqn loads) are
the superscript and subscript TeX reads (`math_active_scripts`; 2504.02633, and 2404.16541, whose affiliation marks
had left an author with no name). SHARED with Perl for S4 and S5 (SplitTokens passes over groups,
Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:152-165: latexml 0.8.8 keeps each wrapped list one author, and every note command among names
merges them too), except the `{footnote}` environment, which Perl, not keeping an environment whole, splits at its
inner comma with its `\begin` and `\end` in different authors (6 Errors on the repro). Bindings: IEEEtran's grades
become their names' membership contacts inside a wrapper too, a note's argument aside (since P5a the reading's,
`\lx@IEEE@grade`, OD #1016); authblk's unlabelled `\author` holding the word "and" is a list (`\lx@add@authors@list`: `Ajay
Chandra$^{1}$\orcidlink{…} and Harprit Singh$^2$\orcidlink{…}`, 2405.16615, preprint.cls + authblk); ecai's `\author`
holding a top-level `\and`, or the current class's `\author[A,D]{…}`, is read as a per-author class's
(`\lx@add@authors@append`), so the 2020 class's `\author{A\institute{…} \and B$^1$}` gives two authors and the current
class's one-name `\author[A,D]{…}` stays one; any other block is one author as written, as Perl adds it (1606.03244's
`\`-parted names with a `\\` line of more names). r2: authblk's comma and `\and` lists are added after the authors
before them (`\lx@add@authors@list`, not the replacing `\lx@add@authors`, as authblk.sty:114-145 always appends:
`\author{Ann Able\thanks{Dept. X, Univ Y}}\affil{…}\author{Bob Baker\thanks{…, …}}`, sent there by the note's comma,
replaced Ann Able, 0 Errors, int31a too — AIAA new-aiaa.cls papers 2610.21324 and 2008.05535 kept 1 of 3 authors;
Perl's `\and` branch replaces the same way, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #992); consecutive unlabelled `\affil`s go to every

no one (`is_name_qualifier`: `Cat Cole, et al.`), and an "and" opening a wrapper before them stays in it, in its font

outside its notes is a list too (`has_author_marks`; since r4 only when they end what it prints), so its marks request
the affiliations they label on every path (`\author{Ann Able$^{1,2}$}\author{Bob Baker$^{2}$}` had left Bob Baker
without affiliation 2, his mark requesting nothing on `\lx@add@creator`); an unlabelled `\affil` goes to at most the
authors since the last `\affil`

or declarations that print nothing (`\affil{\vspace{-1.05em}$^2$\normalsize{…}}`, 2605.11124) opens with that mark

### 767. A raw class's title-page stores are judged by a speculative run of its title page; an off-table store no kept run typesets is handed on (Perl: dropped)

Silent-loss #5 (a), the generic rule for the stores K11's table (`STORE_SETTERS`) does not name (75a row (a);
agent_reports/2026-10-18_k11_offtable_reach.md), and the 77h/77i follow-ups on what the title page prints. **Perl** drops
a raw class's title page whole (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1105 `\global\let\@maketitle\relax`, its refused
`\maketitle`, State.pm:502-517), and with it every value only that page prints.

**Which stores.** At the raw class's end (frontmatter_stores.rs `survey_off_table_stores`) every one-argument command
the class defined without an `@` in its name, outside the table and the kernel's setters, whose body is a pure store of
its argument (`setter_stores`) into one control sequence of the class's that only its title-page code reads — rule (a)'s
reader scan with the class's own `\@title`/`\@author`/`\@date` counted as title-page code, LaTeX's `\@maketitle`
printing them (`ClassReaders::read_only_by_the_title_page_or_fields`) — is recorded with its class default
(`lx_offtable_stores`; Info names them) and the label its title page prints before it (`ClassReaders::label_in`, below).

**TeX decides what the title page prints** (`before_title_page_runs`, called at the head of `\lx@deposit@maketitle`,
sect05.rs, in the state the deposit and the replay meet). Each candidate store is given a unique sentinel value and
title-page code is digested speculatively (sect05.rs `title_page_probe_run`: output discarded, every assignment
undone by the assignment journal, diagnostics discarded, terminal output muted under a guard that also ends on a panic
(`SuppressLogOutputGuard`, reset in `reset_thread_engine`), groups left open closed in a reading context of their own;
frontmatter frozen and no setter replayed while it runs). Each run is made twice, the stores given letters sentinels
(`LxSentinel<a-p>zZ`, mixed case, matched lower-cased) and then digits ones (`9090<1-8>0909`, `sentinel`; the second run only when the first printed a
sentinel, `sentinel_runs`): a store is printed by it when both its sentinels reach the digested text
(`sentinels_printed`) — a numeric context consumes the digits while TeX's "Missing number" recovery typesets the letters
(`\setcounter{page}{\@fp}`, gammas.cls:305, kluwer.cls:1049; review probe `num`, where one sentinel invented
`<pubnote>17</pubnote>`). A store run (1) finds printed whose value is plain text (characters and spaces) is confirmed
by one more run with the document's own values (`confirmed_printed`): its letters and digits must be in that run's
text, in their case unless the sentinel run printed the mixed-case sentinel in another (`\MakeUppercase`,
`\MakeLowercase`) — `\ifx\@vc\@open OPEN\else\@vc\fi` with "open" prints the class's word, not the value (review probe
`ctx2`, which invented `<pubnote>open</pubnote>`). Letters and digits only (`alphanumerics`), on both sides: TeX typesets
`'`, ``` `` ``` and `''` as ’ “ ”, `--` as a dash, and 77i r4's comparison of the source characters lost "Women’s
Workshop" and "“Quoted” words" (review probes `q3`, `q4`; 0 errors). The
digested text is `ink_text` (base_utilities/util_text.rs): box characters, never a whatsit's reversion, and only the arguments a
whatsit shows (`shown_arguments`, by declared parameter type: none of an image; a verbatim argument only when the
whatsit's constructor prints it, the arguments `VERBATIM_PRINTERS` names for it (`(name, shown mask)`: llncs's `\url`,
`\nolinkurl`, aas's `\@@email`, `\lx@doi`, `\harvardurl`, each its one argument; a two-verbatim `\href` would name
its second); a constructor's replacement is compiled, so what it puts in its element cannot be read off the whatsit —, never a reference's or citation's key, `\ref{\@vb}` printing "1" (review probe `ctx3`, which
invented `<pubnote>sec:intro</pubnote>`); url.sty's and hyperref's `\url` keep their text in an argument of their own;
`\href{<url>}{Home}` prints "Home"; never keyvals; review probe `logo`'s `\includegraphics{\@logo}` and
`\href{\@url}{Home}`). The print run typesets footnotes and `\thanks` (`\@firstofone`: a store the title page prints in
one is printed, review probes `fn`, `fnt`); it gobbles `\label`, `\index`. A Fatal of a speculative run that is not a
resource Fatal of the conversion (deadline, memory budget, token budget, conditional ids) and whose run was undone is
the run's alone — a runaway limit of the run's own expansion (the pushback, a recursion) too, the latch unset
(`unlatch_runaway_fatal`), the box lists the run left open unwound, and the stack of tokens being invoked and the
active conditionals put back as the run found them, however it ended (`stomach::StomachMark`; 2502.10606, 2003.03814)
(user ruling 2026-10-19:
VisionStyle.cls's `\MakeUppercase` of a title holding its non-robust `\small` loops in pdflatex too, astro-ph0203021;
guard `perfect_kernel_batch77r::speculative_title_run_runaway_is_discarded`) — a sentinel value
may cause it —: it is discarded with the run's diagnostics (an Info says so) and run (1) printed nothing
(`SpeculativeRun::Aborted`, which `decide_unset_nulls` counts as no "fewer characters": `\relax` stays); an aborted
deposit or replay run, (2) or (3), is no run (`sentinel_runs`): the walk decides, since a Fatal the sentinel value alone
caused does not stop the real deposit printing the store. Three
runs: (1) the class's whole title page with the document's values (`title_page_print_tokens`: its refused `\maketitle`
when replayable, else LaTeX's, which runs the class's or a binding's `\@maketitle`, else article.cls:209-229's printing
of the fields; a call of the kernel's `\maketitle` from the class's, `\let\@origmaketitle\maketitle`, runs LaTeX's
`\@maketitle` there), with the off-table stores the document set and the rerouted stores handed to the frontmatter as
candidates (`lx_sentinel_printed`); (2) and (3) the deposit and the replay exactly as they then run
(`title_page_deposit_tokens`, `title_page_replay_tokens`, shared with `\lx@deposit@maketitle`), the off-table candidates
given sentinels (`lx_sentinel_deposit`, `lx_sentinel_replay`). A class's own booleans (sigplanconf.cls:87-90
`\def\@true{TT}`/`\def\@false{FL}`, :1118 `\if \@copyrightwanted …`), `\newif` switches (aiaa-tc.cls:199-200
`[handcarry]`), `\@ifundefined`/`\ifx…\@empty` tests, and what it only boxes or puts in a running head (`\setbox`,
`\markboth`: degruyter-journal-a.cls:574-586, 620, 1704.03582; acmlarge.cls:1021, 1508.03599) are then what they are in
pdflatex. A run that errors still gives its text (TeX's recovery typesets on; an internal our emulation of the class
lacks becomes an `<ltx:ERROR>` holding its name). Without a run (a journal already open, or a run whose assignments
could not be undone, `SpeculativeRun::Unavailable`; an Info says so, for sweeps to count) the stores' readers are walked
instead (`walked_title_page_reads`: the live code, `\newif`/kvoptions switches and `\if`/`\ifx` on parameterless macros
of characters evaluated, `evaluated_switch`; only the code that runs, `executed_code`).

**Labels.** The label a title page prints before a store is read off the class's code (`ClassReaders::label_in`,
`line_label_before`: label material and layout from the line's start — the macro's start, a `\par`, a `\\`, an
environment's `\begin{…}`/`\end{…}`, another value, the open brace of the store's group — up to the store; the phrase
right before the store, a sentence before it in the line staying where it is: `\footnote{Funded. KW: \@keywords}` names
the keywords "KW:" and the footnote keeps "Funded.", review probe `fnm`), and is the entry's name only when TeX's output
says so: at `\maketitle`, before the stores are handed on (`\lx@store@defaults`), one more speculative run of the whole
title page with the labelled stores given letters sentinels must print the label's text right before the store's
sentinel (`verify_title_page_labels`, `printed_right_before`, letters and digits compared: the class's `Author's
keywords:` is typeset "Author’s keywords:", review probe `ap`; once per document). `\href{mailto:\@vg}{\@vg}` read
"mailto:" off the URL argument (review probe `ctx3`; modernposter.cls, skdoc.cls have the shape), which the page does not
print. A rejected label stays in the title page and the entry is unnamed; without a run, a label in a group that is a
control sequence's argument (not a font command's) is rejected.

**What is handed on** (`hand_untypeset_stores`, at `\lx@store@untypeset` after the deposit and the replay): each
off-table store the document set (no longer the class default, not blank; once per store, sigplanconf.cls:939-942's
`\copyrightDOI` and its `\let` `\copyrightdoi`) that run (1) printed and no kept run typeset (run (2) or (3) for a kept
deposit or replay, `lx_title_page_{deposit,replay}_kept`), in the order the title page prints them, with no visible label
of ours — the meta XSLT shows a note's `@role` as a visible label (LaTeXML-meta-xhtml.xsl:79-85), which 77i r1's
`note[role=<setter>]` made "titre:", "auteurs:", "copyrightDOI:" — as: the document's `ltx:title` when the class's own
refused `\title` hands its argument to the store's setter and the document has no title (`class_field_setter`:
jfpc.cls:122 `\renewcommand{\title}[1]{\titre{#1}}`, its `\@title` :176-186 printing `\@letitre`); the document's authors
(`\lx@add@authors@adaptive`) when there is no creator and the store holds the names the class's own `\@author` prints —
the one its refused `\author` hands its argument to (:126 → `\auteurs`), else the first store its `\@author` reads
(`lx_offtable_author_reads`); a store the class's `\@author` prints beside the names (jfpc.cls:188-191
`\@lesinstitutions`, `\@lesmels`) rows of the creators' author block (`\lx@add@store@authorblock`, `role=authorblock`,
as an `\author` call's tail is, its label as printed before it) — the creators' data, attached to them as any
affiliation is, where 77i r2's `pubnote` made them a note on the document (under the default `ltx_authors_1line` layout
both are hover popups, LaTeXML.css:74-88 and :107-120: the gain is what the rows are, not where they show); a store
that only repeats the creators' names — the class prints no label before it, every word of each of its lines (split at
`\and`, `\\`, `\newline`, `\par`) is a word of a creator's name, and every creator's words are among its words — is a
duplicate, not handed on (`repeats_creator_names`; "Corresponding author: \@corr" with one author's name is a role, kept:
review probe `corr`); any other store an `ltx:pubnote` (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:634, a note about the document),
its `\and` between authors' blocks a line break, named by the label the title page prints before it with the space
printed before the store kept as a tie (jfpc's `\@lannee`: `name="Actes JFPC~"`, "Actes JFPC 2015", :177, as
acmart_cls.rs:218's `name={Price:~}`). 1503.05530 had lost its title, authors, institutions and e-mail. The same run (1) settles #6b (`settle_placed_stores`, `\lx@store@hand`): a handed store's
setter called again after `\maketitle` only re-sets the store when run (1) printed the store (OD #154 addendum).

**The deposit's unset stores** (77h/23b; `decide_unset_nulls`, `\lx@captured@stores`): a rerouted store the paper never
set, still undefined, is defined in the deposit and the replay — undefined, it raised an error that dropped the whole
deposit (an.cls:532 `\ch@ckobl{institute}{…}` runs in the class's own `\maketitle`; the "Key words" line lost, 23b) — as
`\relax` or `\@empty`: a "prints fewer characters" rule over the text TeX typesets for each candidate, from speculative
runs of the deposit and the replay (all `\relax`, all `\@empty`, then each store alone `\@empty`; a tie keeps
`\relax`): `\relax` where a class tests
`\@ifundefined{@pubinfo}`/`{@recdate}` (ptptex.cls:88-104; hep-th9803240, 1309.6905, 0911.1235, 0708.3877, 0801.2466,
1009.4028, 1007.1507, cond-mat0411234; jpsj 0903.1491, 0912.1097, 1101.2977, 1203.5392), `\@empty` where it tests
`\ifx\@institute\@empty` after its own `\maketitle` defaulted the store so (no orphan "Institute:").

**Duplicates and furniture.** A store a kept run typesets is not handed on (CONTROL
`offtable_store_typeset_by_the_deposit_stays_there`); one printed only under a switch that is off, or only in a box or a
running head, is not printed and not handed on (the page-furniture ruling); page-furniture and metadata stores read by
code outside the title page are not recorded (nature_djm `\pubdate`, cedram `\CDRorcid`). nowfnt.cls:798-804's
`\maintitleauthorlist` ("AUTHORS FOR COVER PAGE", 2308.02698 main.tex:44) is the cover's author block printed beside
the abstract page's `\author[n]{Surname, First}`/`\affil` lines (main-session decision under the page-furniture ruling:
print flourish dropped, semantic notes kept, no content lost): in 2308.02698 it holds the names alone, a repeat of the
creators, dropped (`repeats_creator_names` — by words, as nowfnt's `\author[1]{Sung, Yoonchang}` gives two creators,
SYNC_STATUS row "nowfnt creators"); in 2108.12618 it carries the affiliations and e-mails, which reach the document
nowhere else (nowfnt's `\affil` is not captured), and stays a pubnote, its `\and` line breaks between the authors (77i
r2 ran "…mkokotov@gmail.com Matan Gavish"). **Cost:** the speculative runs digest title-page code at most 8 + 2 + N
more times per raw-class `\maketitle` (the print, deposit and replay runs, each with letters and digits sentinels; the
label run when a store is labelled and the confirming run when a store found printed has a plain value; N = unset
rerouted stores, `decide_unset_nulls`'s all-`\relax` and all-`\@empty` runs then one per store; measured +0.03–0.29%
`instructions:u` in 77i r3 — 1309.6905 +0.03%, 1503.05530 +0.07%, 1603.03011 +0.29%, the r3 review's run of 1603.03011
+0.23%, 10.0017e9 → 10.0251e9 — and, over r3, +0.06% (1503.05530), +0.23% (1603.03011), +0.98% (1309.6905: its labelled keywords add the label and
confirming runs) in 77i r4). **Residuals:** what the assignment journal does not undo — the raw-read paths list
(`RAW_READ_PATHS`, content.rs:2437) and the pending field-provenance cover (`FIELD_COVER_PENDING`, token.rs:919) —, unlikely to
be reached by title-page code; a run whose assignments could not be undone (its groups changed) keeps the global
assignments it made with sentinel values (a class's `\xdef\@x{\@store}` would carry "LxSentinel…zZ" into the document),
and the walk then decides; a test of the value takes its branch with the sentinel's value, not the document's —
`\ifnum\@x<100 No.~\@x\fi` with 7 takes the other branch with the digits and `\romannumeral\@va` prints neither sentinel
(pdflatex prints "No. 7" and "iii"; the store counts as not printed and is not handed on: review probes `ctx2`, `ctx`) —
the confirming run checks only what the sentinel runs found printed, so it does not recover these, and a plain value
whose letters TeX prints as other characters (a font's ligature glyph) would fail it; a label with an accent
(`R\'esum\'e :`, `\textbf{Mots-cl\'es :}`) is not read off the code (`label_item`), and a heading-style label before an
abstract the kernel's `\abstract` owns (`\begin{center}{\bf Abstract}\end{center}`, `{\bf Abstract.}`) is not this
mechanism's: both stay orphan paragraphs, as on base (SYNC_STATUS "Silent-loss inventory" #6a residual, now `perfect_kernel/SILENT_LOSS_INVENTORY.md`); a constructor
outside `VERBATIM_PRINTERS` that prints a verbatim argument (a binding's two-verbatim `\href`, jhep_cls.rs) does not
count it printed; a store the class prints only behind a label macro it defines at `\maketitle`
(bullsrsl.cls:747-765 `\BSRSL@CorrespIntro` "Correspondence to:", 2401.09121, 2410.19120) is a pubnote without that
label, a hover-only popup (SYNC_STATUS row "bullsrsl correspondence", now `perfect_kernel/SILENT_LOSS_INVENTORY.md`). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch77i::{offtable_stores_read_by_class_author_are_the_creators,
offtable_store_typeset_by_the_deposit_stays_there, offtable_store_the_class_title_hands_on_is_the_title,
offtable_store_the_title_page_does_not_print_is_not_handed_on, unset_store_reads_as_the_title_page_tests_it,
store_read_as_a_number_is_not_printed, store_in_an_image_path_or_link_target_is_not_printed,
cover_author_list_is_dropped_only_when_it_repeats_the_names, store_label_is_printed_text_not_a_link_target_or_key,
store_label_is_the_phrase_printed_before_it, labelled_role_store_naming_one_author_is_a_note,
store_tested_against_a_word_is_not_printed, store_values_typeset_with_quotes_are_printed,
store_label_with_an_apostrophe_names_the_entry}`, `perfect_kernel_batch77h::an_without_institute_keeps_the_title_block`,
`latexml_core` `suppress_log_output_guard_restores_on_drop_and_unwind`.
