### 772. The AISTATS styles' title-block setters are the frontmatter, one binding for every year (Perl: no binding)

Every AISTATS template — aistats2e.sty (2010-2011), its margin variant aistats2eM.sty, aistats2012.sty, aistats2014.sty
… aistats2027.sty — prints its title block in place inside the document's `\twocolumn[…]`: `\aistatstitle`,
`\aistatsauthor` and `\aistatsaddress` (aistats2027.sty:173/248/355, aistats2eM.sty:102/171/252, the same in every
year) typeset the title and centred author and address tables and never reach `\title`/`\author`. **Perl** has no
aistats binding: the shipped copy is read raw (or, without it, the three are undefined), and the document has no title
and no creators — the HTML head falls back to the first section heading. **Rust** had the same, through a stub
registered under `aistats2026` only (the versioned fallback strips `aistats2027` to `aistats`, which nothing answered).

Now one family binding, `latexml_contrib/src/aistats_sty.rs`, answers `aistats` (the years the versioned fallback
strips to it: aistats2012, aistats2014 … aistats2027), and by name `aistats2026`, `aistats2e` and `aistats2eM` (a letter
follows their digits, which the fallback does not strip), as Perl's icml.sty.ltxml answers the ICML years. It reads the
paper's copy raw (`fallback_request`), then, where the copy defines them:
- the first `\aistatstitle{T}` is the title (`\title`; it also keeps aistats2022.sty:172's `\gdef\@supplementtitle{#1}`
  for that copy's `\makesupplementtitle`, 1910.09056); a later one prints in place as the copy does (2610.11580's
  supplement "Supplementary Material" heading, which a second `\title` would drop);
- `\aistatsauthor{A₁ \And A₂}` with the `\aistatsaddress{a₁ \And a₂}` under it are authors: column by column
  `A₁ \\ a₁ \And A₂ \\ a₂` when the row has several columns and the address as many (`\And`, `\AND`, `\ANDD`), in as
  many rows (`\AND`), and the address is no key to marked names (two or more distinct marks in it: 2312.06786's two
  marked affiliations over a second row of e-mails go by mark; one mark is a note's, `$^*$equal contribution` or
  `Univ A$^*$` twice, and the columns still pair — 1905.11190, 2405.18281, 2011.03885, 2301.11862, 2410.15516), read as the kernel `\author` reads name, affiliation and e-mail lines (2610.11580,
  1002.4058) — the PDF prints column i under author i. The binding reads ahead from the row, brace-balanced, through what prints nothing (spaces, `~`,
  paragraph ends, vertical space, definitions, size and font declarations, the copy's `\runningauthor`/`\runningtitle`,
  groups) to the address, stopping at anything that may print, the next `\aistatsauthor` or the block's end; the
  material between runs first, then the pair (29 of 2,843 papers: `\runningauthor` 1804.04378, 2402.12508; `\vspace`
  2003.03080, 2305.16147; `\medskip` 2602.12181; `~` 1603.09584; `\newcommand` 1302.5348, 1902.01239, whose macro is
  then defined when the address is read). Otherwise — a row of one column, whose address the copy centres under every
  name (2510.09534's `Jeong$^\ast$ \quad Zhai$^\ast$ \quad Ro\v{c}kov\'{a}`), columns that do not match (1806.02924's
  four names over one address), or an address after printed material — the names are one author list rebuilt
  from their columns (`\ANDD` a column break, not an undefined command inside a name), and the address goes through the
  kernel's `\lx@add@affiliation@shared[annotate=run]`: marked, each `$^1$` line to the authors showing the mark
  (1910.09056: Wood gets UBC, MILA and CIFAR); unmarked, each column an affiliation of every author of the row (columns
  printed alike once), its e-mail lines the authors' e-mails placed as a marked list's are — one for each
  author in their order, else the block's (1806.02924's `\{asuggala, …\}@cs.cmu.edu`, 1311.1894's
  `\{honda,takemura\}@…`): the row is the authors queued after the last affiliation, as `annotate=run` attaches one
  (2006.04012's, 2310.19690's later row), else the last author list (2010.08573's second `\aistatsaddress` of e-mails
  under a paired row), and a list not one for each author is one block contact an address, not the raw line
  (1802.07182). A shared affiliation attached to every author it serves is the kernel convention (Perl's
  `annotate` the same); the PDF prints it once. Each row (`\lx@add@authors@list`) adds to the rows before;
- the setters' arguments are read where they stand: a macro without parameters whose meaning the paper made inside the
  `\twocolumn[…]` group (1302.5348's `\newcommand{\UMDAddress}{…}` between `\aistatsauthor` and `\aistatsaddress`; a
  global macro renewed there) is replaced by its expansion, as the queued frontmatter is digested after that group ends,
  where the meaning is gone (`state::meaning_is_group_local`); a column that assigns or tests a meaning
  (`\renewcommand{\Uni}{…}\Uni`, 2511.05163's `\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.0}`) is left as it is;
- a submission under review (`\statePaper` not 1: no `accepted` option, nor aistats2027's `preprint`) prints
  "Anonymous Author" and "Anonymous Institution" where the copy has that block (aistats2020.sty … aistats2027.sty; the
  2e, 2012, 2014 and 2019 copies print the names either way), and so does the conversion (user ruling 2026-10-06,
  display toggles as the PDF shows them).

The copy's running-head measurement inside `\aistatsauthor` is not run, so its
`\PackageError{Document}{Running heading author exceeds size limitations}` (aistats2026.sty:289-295) no longer needs
the former stub's placeholder `\@runningauthor`. `\runningtitle`/`\runningauthor` (page furniture) stay the copy's.
Witnesses 1002.4058, 1302.5134, 1302.5348, 1303.0449, 1103.0941 (2e), 1202.1568 (2eM), 1102.1492 (2012), 1311.1894
(2014), 1806.02924 (2019), 2604.21432 (2020), 1910.09056 (2022), 2405.15172 (2025), 2605.03921, 2510.09534 (2026),
2610.11580 (2027); 7 of 6,000 sampled papers, each with no title and no creators before. Repros
`class-bindings/aistats_{setters_are_the_frontmatter,one_column_names_share_the_address,unpaired_address_columns_split}`,
`class-bindings/aistats_{address_after_unprinted_material_is_paired,in_place_leaves_assignments_alone,shared_email_list_goes_to_its_row}`,
`class-bindings/aistats2e_template_reaches_the_binding`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch77o::aistats*`.

*Live rule: OD #460.*

### 775. aero.cls's `\ADsetup` title page is the frontmatter (Perl: no aero binding, `\ADsetup` undefined)

aero.cls (latexstudio.net's *Astrodynamics* template, v1.0 2022/01/04, shipped with the paper, not in TeX Live) keeps its
title page in l3keys variables `\l_ADkeys_<key>_tl` set by `\ADsetup{title=…, author=…, address=…, email=…,
abstract=…, keywords=…, name=…, url=…}` (aero.cls:97-118) and prints them only in its `\RenewDocumentCommand\maketitle`
(:128-148), which the kernel's locked `\maketitle` refuses: the replayed class body printed them as body paragraphs and
the document had no title, creator or abstract (2610.12827, arXiv html_feedback HF14; user ruling 2026-10-19 — a
reader-reported class gets a binding at any sample reach). The binding (latexml_contrib aero_cls.rs) loads the shipped
class raw, so its own keys run, and the kernel `\maketitle` (`\lx@maketitle@begin`) hands each variable the paper set —
one that differs from the class's `initial:n` value, the template's placeholder, kept as `\lx@aero@initial@<key>` when
the class loads — in the class's order: `\title`, `\author` (the article split), the address under every author
(`\lx@add@affiliation@marked[annotate=all]`, its `\sep` a line break as the class's hanging paragraphs, :137; marked
lines to the authors their marks name), the e-mail, `\lx@add@abstract`, and the keywords joined by the class's `~·\ \ `
(:145), a `\\` ending them dropped. A variable the paper never set is no frontmatter: 2509.08607 and 2511.17720 ship a
modified class whose `\maketitle` prints the kernel's `\@title`/`\@author` and set those, never calling `\ADsetup` —
handing the placeholders over had replaced their title and authors with "Paper title: Preparation of papers for
*Astrodynamics*" and "First A. Author" (77p r2 review); the kernel path keeps them. The class's corresponding mark
`\cor` (:92 `{\rm (\Letter)}`) after an author's name is a request for the e-mail, as elsarticle's `\corref` is for its
`\cortext` (`\lx@request@frontmatter@annotation[cor]{aero}`, the e-mail `\lx@add@email[label={cor:aero}]`), not name
text: 2609.23496's `allan.junior@uc.pt` goes to `A. K. de Almeida Jr$^{1,2}$\cor{}` (was a nameless creator, the "(🖂)"
in the personname); without a `\cor` the e-mail is placed by the name it spells (`\lx@add@contact@placed`; the class
prints it apart after `\Letter`, :139). The class's own `\maketitle` is not replayed (`\lx@dropped@maketitle` relaxed).
`name` and `url` print only in the running head (:120-126) and stay page furniture. Witnesses 2610.12827, 2609.23496,
2509.20748, 2603.14589, 2607.23790, 2609.00861 (`\ADsetup`), 2509.08607, 2511.17720 (the variant). 2509.20748's `author`
key ends in two legend lines (`\\ \textsuperscript{*}\textit{Equal contribution.}\\ \textsuperscript{$\dagger$}…`),
which the article split reads as for any `\author` (OD #52(o)): the `*` legend is no part of the last name since 77p r4,
but lands on that author as an affiliation, not on the starred authors (the symbol-mark SYNC_STATUS residual). Repros
`class-bindings/aero_setup_frontmatter.tex`, `class-bindings/aero_corresponding_mark_owns_the_email.tex` (with an
excerpt of the class, `class-bindings/aero.cls`), `class-bindings/aero_variant/aero_title_author_without_setup.tex` (with
the variant's excerpt); guards `perfect_kernel_batch77p::{aero_setup_is_the_frontmatter,
aero_corresponding_mark_owns_the_email, aero_variant_keeps_the_kernel_title_and_authors}`.

*Live rule: OD #460.*

### 790. entics.cls and entcs.cls are read raw with elsart's frontmatter interface

entics.cls (Electronic Notes in Theoretical Informatics and Computer Science) and its predecessor entcs.cls (ENTCS) are
shipped by the papers and generated from Elsevier's esl.dtx, as elsart.cls is: `\author[keys]{…}`, `\address[label]{…}`,
`\thanks[key]{…}` and `\thanksref{key}`, which is no command but a delimiter `\author` reads its argument by
(entics.cls:707-735, :860-930). Read raw, the kernel's `\thanksref` (a superscript of its key, sect05.rs) printed the key
in the name — 2212.08177 "Willem HeijltjesALL", 1812.00040 "Mauro LucciALLmyemail" — the `\thanks[key]` notes became
footnote texts of the document and the `\address` a paragraph of the body. Perl has no binding for either. Ours: an
entics binding for both names (latexml_contrib entics_cls.rs) reads the class raw and then elsart_support_core (the
elsart binding's frontmatter interface): `\thanksref{ALL}` requests the `\thanks[ALL]{…}` contact, the address is the
author's. Repro class-bindings/entics/entics_thanksref_names_its_note (a stand-in class written for it: entics.cls may
not be redistributed); guard `perfect_kernel_batch77t::entics_thanksref_names_its_note`.

### 791. A class-numbered `\institute` store goes to the authors by their numbers

A raw class carrying llncs's `\institutename` (llncs.cls:870-885; copied by preprint.cls:233-256) prints its
`\institute{A \and B}` list with each `\and` stepping the institute counter and printing the number before the next
entry, the first numbered 1. The K11 store path (`\lx@add@store@affiliations`, frontmatter_stores.rs) saw unmarked
entries and gave every author every entry (`annotate=all`): 2405.16615's two authors each held Imperial College and
Edinburgh. Ours: when the class numbers the store's entries, the store holds at least two `\and` entries and no mark,
and the queued authors' marks request numbers, the entries are led by their numbers as the title page prints them
(`class_numbered_institutes`, base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_api/affiliations.rs) and labelled by them, so `$^{1}$`/`$^2$` — or
the class's `\inst{1,2}`/`\inst2` (2512.08621) — pick one each. Whether the class numbers them is read from its own
output (batch 104b, census129 cluster 3): one speculative run of the whole title page with the store set to an `\and`
list of three letter sentinels (frontmatter_stores.rs `note_and_numbering`, at `\maketitle`, K11's store route and the
displaced route of #955), numbered when each sentinel printed right after its number in order
(`printed_after_their_numbers`; recorded as `lx_and_numbered_<store>`) — sab.cls:404-426's and edpsci.cls's, baaa.cls's
`\refstepcounter{inst}`, which the earlier reading of `\institutename`'s body (a `\def\and` with `\stepcounter`) missed
(2308.05831, 2308.05830, 2501.08874, 2206.02830; 2102.09010, 2504.01277; 1701.08962's my_NSP: every author held every
institute). That reading remains where no run is made (an in-place line, no store) and where the run's text does not
hold the sentinel entries, which says nothing of the numbering: raa.cls's title page is not typeset by the run, and
reading that as "not numbered" gave every raa, raa_rb, raa_twocolumn and cjaa author every institute (2003.13998,
2511.10805, 2511.06927, astro-ph0701846). The marks request numbers when each is a comma list of numbers beside which
only symbols stand (a legend's `$^{*}$`, `\textsuperscript{\dag}`; edpsci's empty `$^{,}$` piece), never a letter label
(`numbered_marks_requested`). Perl reads such a class raw (its `\institute` the class's). Repros
sectioning-frontmatter/class_numbered_institutes_go_by_the_authors_marks (with numinst.cls),
raw_class_refstepcounter_numbered_institutes_go_by_their_numbers, raw_class_unnumbered_and_institutes_stay_every_authors
(control), raw_class_numbered_institutes_the_run_does_not_print_keep_their_numbers; guards `perfect_kernel_batch77t::{class_numbered_institutes_go_by_the_authors_marks,
class_numbered_institutes_go_by_inst_marks}`, `perfect_kernel_batch104b::{a_refstepcounter_numbered_and_list_goes_by_the_authors_numbers,
an_unnumbered_and_list_stays_every_authors, a_numbered_and_list_the_run_does_not_print_keeps_its_numbers}`. Not read (RED catalog repros, SYNC_STATUS row "104b"): a numbered store

### 792. An llncs `\\` line reading as an affiliation is the affiliation of the names over it

The llncs binding splits `\author` at `\\` as at `\and` (a Rust improvement over Perl's llncs.cls.ltxml, which splits at
`\and` only: 2606.19939's `Hiuyi Cheng \\ Dezhi Peng`), so `\author{Ann Able\\University of Somewhere\\\email{…}}` made
a creator "University of Somewhere" holding the e-mail. llncs.cls:1019-1036 sets `\@author` as one centred paragraph,
its `\\` a line break: the line is printed under the name; and its `\and` is inline text (llncs.cls:1013-1018,
`\unskip,` or `\lastand` in `\@maketitle`), so the names it joins share the row. Ours (llncs_cls.rs `\lx@llncs@author`):
in an author list with no marks and no `\inst` marks, read across the whole `\author` body (its `\and`, `\And` and `\\`
pieces in order), a line after a `\\` that reads as an affiliation (`reads_as_affiliation`; a piece after the inline
`\and` is names, `Ann Able \and the ATLAS Collaboration`, the rev77t2 re-review's L6) goes into the author content of
each name since the last line under names — an affiliation line or an e-mail line (`line_is_email_list`), after which
the next names start a new row —, as an `\email` there does (so `\institute`'s clearing of the queued affiliations
leaves it): `Ann Able \and Bob Baker\\ University of Somewhere` both names' (2604.11038's Simon Fraser University on its
three authors), `Ann Able\\ University of X\\ Bob Baker\\ University of Y` one each. A list with marks is split as
before, since a contact digested with the authors would come before `\institute`'s entries in the count
`labelseq=affiliation` numbers them by. Residual: an address line with no institution word (`Stanford, CA 94305`) still
reads as names, creators "Stanford" and "CA 94305" (as before); in a list with `\inst` marks a line under the names
stays a creator of its own (`University of X`, as before; the rev77t2 re-review's L11); a `\texttt{ann@x.org,
bob@x.org}` line under the names makes two creators (as before; L8). Repros
sectioning-frontmatter/llncs_author_line_break_affiliation, llncs_author_line_break_affiliation_rows,
llncs_author_and_is_inline; guards `perfect_kernel_batch77t::{llncs_author_line_break_affiliation,
llncs_author_line_break_affiliation_rows, llncs_author_line_break_affiliation_per_name, llncs_author_and_is_inline,
llncs_author_e_mail_line_ends_a_row}`.

### 800. webofc.cls is read raw with the `\inst` frontmatter, its side caption a caption

webofc.cls (EDP Sciences' Web of Conferences: EPJ, MATEC, E3S, ITM, SHS, BIO; shipped by the papers, about 30 of the
30,000-paper sample) titles the A&A/Springer way: `\author{Ann Able\inst{1}\fnsep\thanks{\email{…}} \and …}` with an
`\institute{A \and B}` list its title page numbers (webofc.cls:217 `\fnsep`, :434-440 `\institute`, `\inst` =
`$^{#1}$`, `\email` = "e-mail: …"), and `\sidecaption` (:824-857) reads the float's body up to `\caption` to set it
beside the caption in a `\parbox`. Read raw (no binding; Perl has none and errs on `\sidecaption`, `\firstname`,
`\lastname`), the names kept their superscripts ("Andrea Shindler,1": 2301.07438), every author got every institute
(1411.7792), the e-mail was a thanks note's text, and a side caption was text in a parbox with no `<caption>` (the
html_feedback report on 2610.23498, the figure's label on its section). Ours (latexml_contrib webofc_cls.rs): the class
read raw (its packages as it loads them), then inst_support's `\institute`/`\inst` (as aa, llncs and the Springer
classes have them), its `\author` split at `\\` as well as at `\and` (as llncs's: the template's `\\The SND
Collaboration` line under the names, 1609.01040 and 2610.23498, a creator of its own, not part of the last name; the
break's `*` and `[…]` no text, #804), the e-mail the author's contact (`\lx@add@email`; a `\thanks` that held only the
e-mail leaves no note, #803: 2409.01693), `\sidecaption` layout only (as aa_support and sv_support), and the class's
`\@makecaption` label format, "**Figure 1.** …" with the period and the space after it in the bold (:786-812
`\@CaptionTitleFont #1\@FloatCounterEnd\@FloatCounterSep` in one group; `caption_sty::class_makecaption_label`, shared
with jinstpub, whose period is outside; caption, when the document loads it, replaces it). The kernel's frontmatter
`\fnmsep` rule (nothing before a `\thanks`/`\inst`/`\footnote` mark, `digest_frontmatter_item`) covers webofc's `\fnsep`
too. Repros class-bindings/webofc/{webofc_authors_take_their_institutes, webofc_sidecaption_keeps_its_caption,
webofc_author_line_break_options} (beside a minimal webofc.cls stand-in written for them: the shipped class states no
licence); guards `perfect_kernel_batch78e::{webofc_authors_take_their_institutes, webofc_sidecaption_keeps_its_caption,
webofc_author_line_break_options}`.

### 801. jinstpub.sty is jheppub's frontmatter with JINST's extras

jinstpub.sty (JINST's SISSA/IOP publication style, 2015/08/05 v1.0 and 2020/09/18 v1.1638; shipped by the papers, 23 of
the 30,000-paper sample, about 121 in 8 months) is jheppub.sty with JINST's journal name, an optional mark on `\note`
(:91-98), an optional placement on `\collaboration` (:145), newtx fonts, amsthm and wrapfig (:32-56), section-numbered
equations (:335), a bold caption label with a period (:362-378) and four reference shorthands (:384-387). Read raw
(neither Perl nor Rust had a binding), its `\maketitle` laid the stored frontmatter out as body text: the affiliations an
itemize, the e-mail and the keywords paragraphs, the author's `\note{Corresponding author.}` a footnote inside the
personname (2006.05543, 2303.10224). Ours (latexml_contrib jinstpub_sty.rs, as jcappub_sty.rs gives JCAP; both in
latexml_contrib, as Perl has neither): jheppub's binding, then jinstpub's packages, `\note[]{}`, `\collaboration[t]{}`
(with its "option b/c" warnings), `\numberwithin{equation}{section}`, the caption label format
(`caption_sty::class_makecaption_label`), `\erratum`/`\addendum`/`\ibid`/`\pos`. Its `\emailAdd` is jheppub's
binding's since 78f (#805): JINST's `\maketitle` prints every address on one shared "E-mail:" line under the
affiliations (:133-138, :219-224), so an address is the contact of the author whose name it spells, else of the n-th
author when the list is the authors' in order, else (the one address left) of the one author marked as the
corresponding author (#809), else of the group's only author or the author block (78e r2 placed
jinstpub's alone, `\lx@add@contact@placed`; with Perl jheppub's n-th rule 16 of 23 papers had an address on a wrong author:
2311.16063's bross@fnal.gov on Andrea Bersani, not Alan D. Bross; 2307.12991, 1910.06438, 2311.00870, 2605.30709);
an `\emailAdd{a, b}` list is an address each (2211.05026, 2409.03065, 2112.00370). For the spelling, the kernel's name
reading takes a macro whose arguments all go into a frontmatter annotation (`\lx@add@contact`, `\lx@add@note`,
`\lx@add@thanks`, `\lx@add@email`, `\lx@add@affiliation`) as a name annotation, as it takes a note macro
(`is_note_macro`, base_utilities/frontmatter/classify/notes.rs): the corresponding author's `\note{Corresponding author.}` — the template's required
shape — is no part of the name the address spells, where its last word had made "author" the surname (2406.08712's
zhouyi@ for Y. Zhou, 2603.01867's yuanzy@ for Zhiyang Yuan).
The "Prepared for submission to JINST" header line (:22, printed first, :180) is page furniture, not kept; a paper's own
header (its copy's `\gdef\@fpheader{…}`, or its preamble's) is author content, a pubnote (role preprint) at
`\begin{document}`: 2103.06391 "Prepared for submission to JINST (FERMILAB-PUB-21-079-ND-SCD)", 2205.10526, 2311.06155.
The table of contents its `\maketitle` ends with unless `\notoc` (:241-249) is dropped and `\notoc` is a no-op, as in
jheppub's binding (Perl jheppub.sty.ltxml:97), so the family keeps one rule (main session ruling 2026-10-21; whether
JHEP/JINST should print it is a SYNC_STATUS row awaiting a user ruling). The binding stands in for the paper's copy
(`author_files::AUTHOR_FILE_STAND_INS`), so the copy is read after it (OD #731), its own definitions of the binding's
names holding only inside it: its page geometry stays (`\textwidth .72\paperwidth`, the 442pt that `\linewidth`-sized
figures had read raw). Residual: a copy whose own `\maketitle` adds lines (2103.11983's "Published in JINST as DOI:
10.1088/1748-0221/16/07/P07016") loses them, the binding owning `\maketitle` (jheppub the same; SYNC_STATUS). The older
JINST class (`JINST.cls`) keeps its own binding (jinst_cls.rs). Repros package-bindings/jinstpub/{
jinstpub_frontmatter_is_jheppub_s, jinstpub_emails_go_to_the_authors_they_spell,
jinstpub_edited_header_is_a_preprint_note} (beside a modified, shortened jinstpub.sty that keeps the original's
copyright and LPPL 1.3 notice); guards `perfect_kernel_batch78e::{jinstpub_frontmatter_is_jheppub_s,
jinstpub_emails_go_to_the_authors_they_spell, jinstpub_edited_header_is_a_preprint_note}`.

### 802. vmsta's e-mails and addresses are their authors' contacts

vmsta.cls (Modern Stochastics: Theory and Applications, VTeX; shipped, about 71 papers) prints its e-mails and addresses
only from its title page: the 2014-2018 copies write each `\email` to the `.aux` for a later run (vmsta.cls:242-256
`\@email` → `\emailauthor`) and append each `\address[label]` to `\@@@address` (:381-390); the 2018+ copies
(iosart2x-based) take `\ead[label=…]{…}` inside the `\author` (:1263-1297, the title page's e-mail line) and keep an
`\address` list (:871-920). The vmsta binding (OD #789) read the class raw, so the e-mails were lost (1508.02842's
`myus@univ.kiev.ua` nowhere in the output) and the addresses were paragraphs of the deposited title page. Ours
(latexml_contrib vmsta_cls.rs): `\author[labels]{…}` replays the class's own `\author` for its counters and lists and
makes the creator with its labels as annotations (`\lx@add@authors@append`), an `\address[a]` is the affiliation of the
authors labelled `a` and an unlabelled one that of the authors before it with none (`annotate=run`), an `\email` the
contact of the author it follows and an `\ead` that of the author it is in; where the class's own code runs `\ead` (its
replayed `\author`, its deposited title page) it only counts the address for the class's "At least one email address is
required!" check (:550-565) and keeps the e-mail block's font for the history line after it. Perl has no vmsta binding.
Witnesses 1508.02842, 1801.00977, 1411.4499, 1506.02940, 1601.01109 (2014-2018), 1805.02511, 1810.09681, 2001.02487,
1912.07948 (2018+). Open: the 2018+ copies' `\thanksref{cor1}` key in the name (SYNC "quality inventory" row 17). Repros
class-bindings/vmsta/vmsta_emails_and_addresses_are_contacts_red, class-bindings/vmsta_2018/
vmsta_2018_emails_and_addresses_are_contacts_red (cut-down classes beside them); guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78e::{vmsta_emails_and_addresses_are_contacts, vmsta_2018_emails_and_addresses_are_contacts}`.
The names: the frontmatter observer's rehearsal read the author content without the author markup its digestion runs
(`\lx@author@markup@begin`), so vmsta's `\inits` was undefined there, its "Yu." printed, and the emitter wrote the names
from that reading, "Yu.Yuliya Mishura" with no Warning (since HG1; 1508.02842, 1411.4499, 1506.02940). The rehearsal now
reads each author block under `author_markup_begin` (observer/reading.rs; defs/frontmatter_fields.rs
`author_markup_begin`): the binding's class markup, OmniBus's, and the title code's definitions that read arguments (#941).
Repro class-bindings/vmsta/vmsta_title_page_name_parts (GREEN); guard
`perfect_kernel_batchlostf::lost_frontmatter_content_is_kept`.

### 803. A frontmatter note all of whose content became contacts is not emitted

An author's `\thanks{\email{…}}` — the A&A and Web of Conferences templates' `\fnmsep\thanks{\email{…}}` /
`\fnsep\thanks{\email{…}}` — digests the `\email` into the author's `email` contact (an annotation made while the note's
content is digested), which left the thanks note empty: `<note role="thanks"/>`, a visible mark opening a note with
nothing in it (2409.01693's "†" after Wolfgang Lucha holding only "thanks:"; 20 of 21 webofc papers of the rev78e
review). Ours (main session ruling 2026-10-21; `\lx@annotate@frontmatter@now`, base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_api.rs): a frontmatter
`ltx:note` whose digested content typesets nothing after one or more annotations were made while digesting it is
dropped, its pending stub removed — for every class whose `\email`, `\affiliation` or other contact setter runs inside a
`\thanks` (aa, webofc, …); the rule covers `ltx:note`s only, not contact-typed notes (elsarticle's `\fntext[f1]{\ead{…}}`
keeps an empty `<contact role="note"/>`, as before; synthetic, 0 corpus cases in the rev78e2 sample). Generalised by #916
(2026-10-30): every frontmatter note with no ink is dropped, an author's own empty `\thanks{}` too, by a structural
test (`leaves_no_ink`) in place of the count of annotations made while the note digested.
Residual: a note left holding only a separator or a lead word once its addresses became contacts — `\thanks{\email{a},
\email{b}}` a "," note, `\thanks{e-mail: \email{x}}` an "e-mail: " note (0902.3523's three "E-mail:" notes, 1610.04567's
","; as int45b) — is kept: no further rule (rev78e2). Perl (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml, `\lx@add@thanks` a `role=thanks` contact) emits
an empty thanks contact the same way. Repro class-bindings/aa_thanks_email_leaves_no_empty_note (and webofc's
webofc_authors_take_their_institutes); guards `perfect_kernel_batch78e::{aa_thanks_email_leaves_no_empty_note,
webofc_authors_take_their_institutes}`.

*Live rule: OD #981.*

### 804. `\lx@splitting` at `\\` drops the break's `*` and `[…]` from the next piece

`\lx@splitting{op}{delimiters}{tokens}` (Perl Base_Utility.pool.ltxml, `SplitTokens`) cuts at the delimiter tokens
only, so a split at `\\` left the line break's star and optional spacing at the start of the next piece. No Perl binding
splits at `\\`; two Rust ones do, an author list printed as a paragraph whose `\\` is a line break: webofc's `\author`
(#800) and llncs's `\inst`-marked `\author` (llncs_cls.rs `\lx@llncs@author@split`). There `B\inst{2}\\*[2mm] C\inst{1}`
made a creator "*[2mm] C" (the rev78e review's finding 6; synthetic, 0 of 158 webofc papers). Ours: a piece after a
`\\` delimiter loses a leading `*` and `[…]` (`strip_linebreak_options`, which the kernel's own author splitting and
llncs's unmarked list already apply). Repros class-bindings/webofc/webofc_author_line_break_options,
sectioning-frontmatter/llncs_author_line_break_options_with_inst_marks; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78e::{webofc_author_line_break_options, llncs_author_line_break_options_with_inst_marks}`.

*Live rule: OD #993.*

### 805. A class's e-mail list goes to the author an address spells, else in author order when the list is the authors'

jheppub.sty's `\emailAdd` (jheppub.sty:126-131; jcappub.sty and jinstpub.sty the same) stores the addresses for its
`\maketitle`, which prints them as one shared "E-mail:" line under the affiliations, attributing none. Perl's
jheppub.sty.ltxml:40-41 gives the n-th `\emailAdd` to the n-th author (`labelseq=author`), which names the wrong author
wherever the list is not in author order (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1030): in the 150 jheppub and 83 jcappub e-mail papers of
the sel78d 30k census, 7 and 15 addresses were on an author another name spells (2407.18115's Michael.Fucilla@ on
Renaud Boussarie and back, 2011.05971, 2212.09776; jcappub 1804.07528, 1806.05015, 2010.13504, 2310.18996, 2407.07862),
and an `\emailAdd{a, b}` listing two authors' addresses was one contact of the first (2406.03543, 2505.23122). Placing
each address by its spelling alone (jinstpub's 78e rule) puts the many addresses no name spells but the list's order
gives right (1303.3040's `zhl61@` for Zhen Liu, 2011.02499's `tpsg4@`/`tpsr@`, 2212.01400's `jss55@`: 40 in the jheppub
sample) on the author block. Ours (`\lx@add@contact@placed[owner=sequence]`, each class command call marked by
`\lx@sequence@call`; the flush's `sequenced_contact_labels`, base_utilities/frontmatter/place.rs), against all the authors of the same
frontmatter flush: an address goes (1) to the author it spells (`address_owners`); else (2) to the author at its place
when the list has one place for each author in their order — no address spells another author than the one at its
place (`addresses_in_order`'s reading of an author block's line), the place the address's, or else the call's (an
author's two addresses in one call, 1710.06069; `\emailAdd{divyeshsolanki98@…, srijuster@…}` for two authors read by
the address, 2308.02445); else (3) where `\lx@add@contact@placed` put it, the group's only author or the author block,
as the PDF's shared line leaves it (a list shorter than the authors orders nothing); and (4) the one address of the list
left on the block of a multi-author paper to the ONE author marked as the corresponding author, where there is one
(#809). Step (1) also
knows the owner a mark gives (iopart's `\ead` under its `\address`, #808: 2311.07087's second `\ead`, `sgess@`, under
`$^4$ SLAC`, is the fifth author's). Step (2) is the user's ruling of 2026-10-21: a list with exactly one address per
author that every spelled address agrees with is evidence of the order, so an unspelled address in it goes to the
author at its place (an inconsistent list sends its unspelled addresses on, to (3) and (4)); it is one function,
`author_order_step`, so a later ruling can switch it off in one change. A flush with no authors (the list after
`\maketitle`, 1903.05554) keeps Perl's rule. jheppub's binding (latexml_package jheppub_sty.rs) defines it, an
`\emailAdd{a, b}` an address each (`\lx@add@contact@list` = `\lx@sequence@call\lx@split@addresses`, which parts a
list at its commas and at an " and ", and writes out the addresses of a braced group of local parts before a shared
domain, `\{a, b\}@x`, in a list of plain text only: a list in markup, `\emailAdd{\mbox{a@x, b@y}}`, is one contact, its
markup kept; 2011.05971's bare `nikolay.bobev, anthony.charles, valentin.reys @kuleuven.be` is no address list, kept
whole); `\lx@add@contact@list` is a frontmatter call by its name, so an `\emailAdd` inside an `\author` stays that
author's one contact (`adds_to_frontmatter`, `is_note_macro`; an address-list contact digested inside another entry
is that entry's, placed by nothing of its own). jcappub and jinstpub (latexml_contrib) take it with the binding, so
the family has one rule (OD #801's jinstpub placement is this one's steps 1 and 4). A/B (int47a → 78f, release, `--preload=ar5iv.sty`; by the reviewer's
spelling test, `emailmatch.py`; E, F and W equal, 0 of 100 random controls changed): jheppub 150 papers (18 outputs
changed), addresses on their spelled author 360 → 386, on another spelled author 7 → 0, on the block 0 → 2 (1802.03677's gear8mike@, 2212.09776's inalecz@ for Ignacy Nałęcz, a `\l` the name
keys drop); jcappub 83 papers (17 changed), 174 → 196, 15 → 0, 0 → 8 (each a list shorter than its authors, none spelled: the n-th
rule's guess there, 1802.07622's `sma74@` likely right, 2407.07862's `hdel@` wrong, is no evidence); jinstpub 23 papers
unchanged. Residuals: a surname letter the name keys drop (`\l`, `ø`; 2212.09776) or a spelling they do not read
(`ue` for `ü`, 2211.05026; two-letter surnames, 2409.18288) leaves an address unspelled; an address that spells two
authors equally (1710.06069's `sjkim0305@` beside two Kims) goes by the order or to the block. Repros
sectioning-frontmatter/{jheppub_emailadd_in_author_order, jheppub_emailadd_one_call_lists_the_authors_red,
jheppub_emailadd_out_of_order_by_spelling}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch78f::{jheppub_emailadd_in_author_order,
jheppub_emailadd_one_call_lists_the_authors, jheppub_emailadd_out_of_order_by_spelling}`,
`perfect_kernel_batch78e::jinstpub_emails_go_to_the_authors_they_spell`.

**Amended (107f).** `\lx@split@addresses` reads a brace set in math as the brace it prints
(`\emailAdd{$\{$a, b$\}$@x}`, `frontmatter_fields::contacts::math_braces_as_printed`, #972), so such a list is an address each as the
text-brace list is.

### 808. iopart's `\ead` goes to the one author its `\address`'s mark names, and each iopart `\author` is a group

iopart.cls:363 `\def\ead#1{\vspace*{5pt}\address{E-mail: \mailto{#1}}}`: an `\ead` prints as an address block of its own
right after the `\address` before it (iopart.cls:246-248, "Use once for each address"), so in the PDF the address stands
inside that address's block, under its mark: 2407.14305's `rockfish3141@` under "¹ Graduate School … Waseda University",
Hidetomo Hoshino's alone (the PDF's reading; today ours sits on the block's nameless creator, as 1111.5264's `johnwc@` —
RED `iopart_ead_under_its_address_mark_red`, since int160a; revP5c). #806 placed it by the spelling or the author order only, so an address no name spells went to
the author block (78f r1) or, in Perl, to the last author (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1031). Ours: the binding's `\address`
records its block's mark (`\lx@address@mark@set`, base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_fields.rs: the operand of the block's one leading mark, none for
an unmarked block or one of several marked lines; the binding's `\author` clears it), and `\lx@iop@ead` passes it as the
contact's mark (`\lx@add@contact@placed[mark=address]`), a weak one: it places only an address that spells no one
(`placed_contact_owner(…, weak)`: 1111.5264's `johnwc@` under `$^6$`, which two authors request, is J W Conklin's `$^1$`,
and stays unplaced by it), on the one author requesting it (2311.07087's `sgess@` under `$^4$ SLAC`, Spencer
Gessner's), and only (a) where the list is no list in author order, which the flush still reads first
(`sequenced_contact_labels` step 2: 1902.07874's `\ead{…, b97202056@gmail.com, …}` of five authors after
`\address{$^9$ …}` is Che-Yu Chen's at place 3; 1710.02251's three `\mailto`s in one `\eads` after `$^{(2)}$` each the
author's at its place), and (b) in a document that writes an e-mail between its addresses, so places its e-mails by
address block (2407.14305, 2311.07087): IOP's guidelines ask for the `\ead` "after the postal address(es)", and an
`\ead` after the last `\address` of a document that writes them all so is under that address by position only — in the
A/B the mark named the wrong author in 3 of the 4 such papers (0910.0753's `wolfgang.muender@`, W Münder's, on C L
Henley; 1111.3344's `knarf@`, Frank Löffler's, on Gabrielle Allen; 1911.06133's `ledou@`, Pierre Le Doussal's, on
Thimothée Thiery; right only in 1209.0173, `jahan@` for Jahanfar Abouie), so there it places nothing
(`_unmarked`, the placement without the mark). A mark-placed address counts as placed for the corresponding-author step
(#809). An `\ead` digested inside an `\address{… \ead{x}}` is that address's, as before. Each iopart
`\author` now starts an author group (`\lx@frontmatter@group@start`, iopart.cls:225-231 typesets each call where it
stands): an `\ead` nothing else places is the group's only author's, a group of two leaves it to the block
(`\author{A. Bal and C. Cole}\address{KIT}\ead{zq1@…}\author{B. Maier}\address{ICL}\ead{yy2@…}`: yy2@ B. Maier's, where
78f r1 put both on the block; rev78f probe i03). A/B (78f r1 → r2, release, `--preload=ar5iv.sty`, all 278 iopart `\ead` papers of the census, E/F/W equal, 9
outputs changed): by the address mark rockfish3141@ and sgess@ placed, each its author's; the four documents whose

### 809. The one e-mail address left over goes to the one author marked as the corresponding author

A class's address list printed apart from the names (jheppub/jcappub/jinstpub `\emailAdd`, iopart `\ead`; #805, #806)
often lists only the corresponding author's address, which spells no name ("E-mail addresses: only for the
corresponding author", 2510.11030's template comment): #805 left it to the author block, Perl gave it to the first
author. User ruling 2026-10-21: the one address left on the block of a multi-author paper — after the spelling, the
list in author order and the group's only author — goes to the ONE author marked as the corresponding author, by a
"Corresponding author" note or a mark whose legend says so, else it stays the block's. Ours (`marked_corresponding_author`,
step 4 of `sequenced_contact_labels`): an author is marked (a) by a note in their own name that names correspondence
(`\note{Corresponding author.}`, jheppub's; `\thanks`, `\footnote`; a note given just after their `\author`, as it is
placed: 1909.06107), or (b) by a mark they carry whose legend names correspondence — an affiliation line's
(`\author[a,*]` under `\affiliation[*]{Corresponding author}`, 1304.1216's `\affiliation[f]{…Corresponding authors}`;
iopart's `$^{1,*}$` under `\address{$^*$ Author to whom any correspondence should be addressed.}`, 2504.15015) or a
note's: its own mark (jheppub.sty:84-89 `\note[*]{…}`, kept since this round, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1033) or, for a
jheppub-family `\note{…}`, which steps the footnote counter and prints its text under that number beside no name, the
n-th such note's number, written on the names it is about (`\author[a,1]`) — save where an affiliation is labelled
with that number too: there the number on a name is that name's request for the affiliation (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4), so
the note's counter number is no legend (`AuthorNote::numbered`; `\author[1]{Ann Able,\note{Corresponding author.}}`
`\author[1]{Bob Baker}` `\affiliation[1]{Univ A}`: Ann Able alone is marked, rev78f3 probe a6; the shape of 2005.05695,
2005.14143, 2405.09762, 1403.3797, 2101.00866), while a note's own mark (`\note[*]`) stays its legend. Exactly one marked author gets the
address; none, or two and more, leave it to the block (1802.03677: M.V. Smirnov's "Corresponding author." note is note
1, which J.J. Ling carries too; 2606.26596's `\note[*]{Corresponding authors.}` under two `*`s; a set: two noted authors
and a third under a "Corresponding author" legend are three). A legend or note that says something else ("Equal
contribution", 1510.03434's `\note[*]{Since October 1, 2015 at Karlsruhe …}`) marks no one, and a mark with no legend at
all says nothing of correspondence (2111.00753's two `$^{*}$`; 2602.07867's `\author[a,c,d,e,*]{Kun Zhang}`) — save
where the address itself names it the corresponding author's and exactly one candidate carries a `*` no legend explains
(2308.06532's `\emailAdd{zyxu@gzu.edu.cn(Corresponding author)}` and `\author[1,*]{Zhaoyi Xu}`). The candidates are the
authors the address may be of: its author group's, where the class marks groups (iopart's `\author`, #808; recorded on
the contact as `_group`), and of those the ones requesting the mark of the address it is printed under, where the
document places its e-mails by address block (`_marks`; rev78f2 probes i1, i2). A note names correspondence by a phrase
(`names_correspondence`, `CORRESPONDENCE_PHRASE`: "corresponding author(s)", "correspondence to/:/should…", "to whom
(any) correspondence…", "for correspondence" with no word between, so not "a test for the correspondence"; a note opening
with "Correspondence" only before ":" or "to", so not "Correspondence between …"), not by the word alone ("the AdS/CFT
correspondence"); English phrases only, as the census's frontmatter of this population (1,911 jheppub-family and iopart
papers) names correspondence in no other language. Witnesses 1901.08773 (`beril@`, A. Kopylov), 2510.11030
(`hjhspace223@`, J.-H. Ha), 2211.07892 (`yoomin@`, Y. M. Oh), 2308.06532 (`zyxu@`, Zhaoyi Xu); 1802.03677
(`gear8mike@`) and 2111.00753 (`lad@`) the block's. The 78e jinstpub guard's `info@lab.gov` goes to B. Baker, the
note in his `\author` and its number on no other name. A/B (78f r2 → r3 and int47a → r3, release, `--preload=ar5iv.sty`, 1,247 papers: the r2 A/B's 1,140, the review's 66
`\emailAdd` papers that name correspondence, and 41 more of the 1,911 whose frontmatter names it or writes `\note[`; no
"another TeX tree"): E 1,559, F 12, W 53,315 equal, 0 papers worse, 0 of the 100 controls changed; r2 → r3 4 outputs
changed, each right by its source: 1802.03677's `gear8mike@` the block's (the note's 1 on M.V. Smirnov and J.J.
Ling), and the `\note[*]` names whole — 2606.26596's Jia-Jun Wu, 1510.03434's José Zurita, 2404.00867's Paul J.
Steinhardt, who also gets back his affiliation b (#810) and the note; int47a → r3 221. Residual: a corresponding author named only in an
address or affiliation line of another class (1603.06724's svjour3 `G. Mazzarella [corresponding author]. \email{…}`) is
not read; the n-th note's number assumes the footnote counter starts the title page at 0; it counts only the `\note`s
written inside the names — a `\thanks` or `\footnote` there steps the same footnote counter but is not counted, and a
`\note` given apart from the names gets no number (rev78f3 probes a2 `\author[a,1]{Ann Able,}\note{Corresponding
author.}`, a4b `\note{Equal contribution.}` apart before `\author[a,2]{Bob Baker,\note{Corresponding author.}}`: the
later inner note's number is then one too low; 0 realised cases in the 1,247 A/B papers). A/B 78f r3 → r4:
1,251 papers (r3's 1,247 and 2005.05695, 2005.14143, 2405.09762, 2101.00866 — 1403.3797 among them —, release, `--preload=ar5iv.sty`): E 1,559, F 11, W 53,326 equal, 0 worse, 0 outputs changed (temp-dir paths masked; the five a6-shape papers place each address by its spelling, none left over; 1806.01746 times out on both). ### 837. The frontmatter observer records and lexes the author calls, in shadow mode

Beyond Perl, infrastructure only: Perl reads an author block as tokens (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:676-700, `@authorsplits`
and `positionOf`), and so does our analyser (`base_utilities/author_block/`). FM S2a.1 (frontmatter model M3 stage
S2a, KERNEL_CAPABILITIES K23 step 1; design `agent_reports/2026-10-21_fms2_design_refresh.md` §2, defaults 1, 2, 6 and
9 adopted by the user 2026-10-21) adds an observer that reads what TeX prints instead, beside the conversion, in
`base_utilities/frontmatter/observer/`. It runs only under the runtime environment variable `LATEXML_FM_SHADOW=1` (read
once per process; a test sets the thread's override, `set_fm_shadow_override`), which stays **unset on the fleet**
(`cortex_worker` writes no dump; the shadow census runs through the local CLI), and decides nothing: a conversion's XML
and its log are the same with and without it (guard `shadow_switch_leaves_the_xml_unchanged`, since DEL4
`the_rehearsal_leaves_nothing_behind`: the switch is gone, "Deleted (DEL4)" below; over the review's
adversarial shapes: an `\aftergroup`, a `\thanks` holding a `\label` with a `\ref` to it, a `\footnote`, a `\gdef` and a
`\stepcounter`, an unclosed `\begingroup`, an undefined command, an `\input` in the field).
- **Ledger** (`ledger.rs`): a block per `\author`-family call — `\lx@add@authors@adaptive` (the kernel `\author`,
  policy `kernel`), `\lx@add@authors`, `@append`, `@list`, `\lx@add@author@split`, `\lx@ijcai@names` — with its
  `replace`/`sectioned`/`cautious` options, keyvals, the frontmatter queue's length and queued authors at the call (and
  the `epoch`, the flushes before it: each flush empties the queue, so a position is one queue's), and its positions in
  the author field: the kernel block's are `\lx@field@mark`'s own (S1, #715; the mark confirms the block it is the
  stored copy of), a binding call's (and a kernel block's past the stamps' 16,383) are projected from where the field's
  stamps end, as the new argument stamper `\lx@field@stamp{<field>}{<tokens>}` (frontmatter_fields.rs; no call site yet,
  S2b stamps the calls) would give them: positions per call (F1), never after the blocks before, which no token of the
  document carries, in the author field's 15 bits (`token::AUTHOR_PROV_POS_MASK`, 32,767); one call past them is unstamped.
  With the emitter's switch off a block past the 14 bits the calls took together is out of positions as before
  (`Stamp::Overflow`, decided where stamping is, `ledger::out_of_positions`), so that path's output doesn't move. Per `\title` call the S1 stamp. Per
  queued creator, contact or note (`queue_front_matter`, gated on the switch before anything is built) an API call,
  `inside` when the latest block's own expansion made it: nothing the input held at the block's call has been read since
  (core `gullet::input_unread_since`: the mark keeps no copy of the pushback, but its length, a serial and its last 4
  tokens (`InputMark`, `Copy`), and each mouth's `PushbackWatch` keeps, per run of marks, the shortest the pushback has
  been since, told by every site that shortens it (the fast read pops only above the watch's floor, its emptiness test;
  the full read, `consume_pushback_to`, the raw-line readers and `flush_mouth` tell it); a slot read and refilled with an
  equal token reads as read, a peek or a `\futurelet` of at most 4 tokens put back as unread, a mark of a mouth since
  closed as read: IEEEtran's affiliation calls, made after the block's line-end space was read, were recorded as the
  block's own, 2401.11731, 1801.03314 — and the mouth position; no `unsafe` (Perl's own marker token was weighed and set
  aside: every Perl reader drops a marker it meets, but our raw-line readers, `Mouth::read_raw_line`, and the native l3fp
  readers do not, a parity gap of their own, SYNC leftovers (24)); 3,000 macro-held revtex authors peak at
  270 MB against MV1base's 261 MB, where a copy per mark took 3.7 GB; instructions −0.10 % to +0.09 % of MV1base on
  hello, b5_fill1000, 1507.02068, 2103.04797 off, +0.16 % and +0.19 % on the last two at `=2`). Nothing is recorded while
  the frontmatter is frozen (a replayed class setter, a speculative run, the rehearsal) or a stand-in copy reads its
  defaults. A block not rehearsed says why (`SkipReason`: out of positions, empty, no flush after the call, the
  rehearsal's own Fatal, not undone; one no journal could open for — the flush inside a speculative run — waits for the
  next flush, `Outcome::Deferred`, and reports `journal unavailable` if none rehearses it).
- **Rehearsal** (`rehearsal.rs`): at the flush (`digest_front_matter`) each block not yet rehearsed is digested from its
  stamped tokens in text mode, in a group of Layer-B event bindings (`\and`/`\And`/`\AND` a column, which one kept; `\\`,
  `\newline`, `\linebreak`, `\par` a row; `\thanks`, `\footnote`, `\footnotetext` a note reading its argument;
  `\footnotemark`, `\inst` marks; `\label` the note's label; `\lx@annotate@frontmatter` and the defined contact commands
  `\email`, `\url`, `\href`, `\orcidlink`, `\affil`, `\address`, … contacts; `\thefootnote` the title's footnote marks:
  the title's `\thefootnote` hook `\lx@title@thefootnote` when one is defined — the kernel's own, the one the printed
  title marks follow (78o r2, #851: rehearsal.rs `TITLE_FOOTNOTE_HOOK` is `latex_constructs::TITLE_THEFOOTNOTE`;
  article, report and book define it `\@fnsymbol\c@footnote`), else the kernel `\maketitle`'s `\@fnsymbol\c@footnote`
  — for a class numbering its title's marks otherwise: revtex4-2.cls:3040-3041 `\frontmatter@thefootnote` is
  `\@fnsymbol` by default and `\@alph` only under its `altaffilletter` option, :5978; guards
  `title_footnote_hook_overrides_fnsymbol`, `perfect_kernel_batch78o::declared_title_thefootnote_prints_the_marks_the_observer_labels`), through
  the speculative-run engine of #767 (assignments journalled and rolled back, diagnostics held and discarded, terminal
  output muted, the frontmatter frozen), with progress notes silenced (core `error::SilenceProgressNotesGuard`: an
  `\input` in the field reads its file again, and its `(Processing content …` note is not the conversion's) and with the
  field ledger put back after it (core `token::FieldLedgerScope`: the serials, the pending cover, the settled flag and
  the stamped gate as they were). The whole group — its opening, the digestion, its end — reads from a mouth of its own (`reading_from_mouth`,
  closed with whatever is left), under a current token of its own: what the group's end unreads (an `\aftergroup` of the
  block's, core `pop_stack_frame_with`) never reaches the document's input, and `egroup`'s template-brace check never
  sees the document's token. No counter is stepped: a bare `\footnotemark` prints `\thefootnote` with `\c@footnote` set
  only inside its mark, to the counter's value at the rehearsal's start plus the steps the block's `\thanks`,
  `\footnote` and bare marks made before it (`\footnotemark[<n>]` at <n>), as latex.ltx `\footnotemark`/`\@xfootnotemark`
  print. No `tabular[t]{c}`: a stray `&` digests as the `&` constructor's whatsit, which errs only when it is built into
  the document (tex_tables.rs) — never in the rehearsal, so nothing is held for it —, and the lexer reads it as a column
  separator. A Fatal of its own skips the block, a resource Fatal propagates.
- **Event lexer** (`events.rs`): the digested list into Name, Mark (its label; `symbol` when it prints only LaTeX's
  `\@fnsymbol` characters, whatever command printed it; its line's first ink), Sep (column with its command — `\and`,
  `\And`, `\AND`, or `column` `&` for an alignment tab —, comma — a mark printing only a comma, llncs's `\fnmsep`, is
  one —, the word "and" or a printed `\&`, a gap: ≥ 2 spacing items, one wider
  than an interword space, or one holding fill glue — `\hfil`/`\hfill`, tex_glue.rs `isFill`, always a separator —, with
  its item count, its natural width in em of the box's font from a spacing box's `width` property (`\hspace`, `\hskip`;
  fill glue 0) or the space characters printed, and `fill`), Break (the rehearsal's `\\` and also the kernel's
  `\lx@newline`, `\lx@parboxnewline` and `\@normalcr` whatsits: `\centering`/`\raggedright`/`\raggedleft` let `\\` be
  `\@normalcr`, a minipage `\lx@newline`, a parbox's body `\lx@parboxnewline`, past the rehearsal's binding; guard
  `breaks_survive_a_rebound_newline`), Contact, Note (label, inner contacts, `thanks` or `footnotetext`), Layout (a
  container, an alignment cell, a font change between runs) and, from the ledger, the API calls after the block; each
  with its span of the field's positions (`fieldProv`/`fieldSerial`, `gullet::field_cover_of`) and its ink. A
  container's content is the arguments it shows (util_text.rs `shown_arguments`, as `typesets_content` reads them) and
  its body: a placement keyword is none (the `[t]` of `\begin{tabular}[t]{c}` and `\parbox[t]`, the `[l]` of
  `\makebox[3cm][l]`, the `[b]` of `\begin{minipage}[b]`; an image, showing none of its arguments, is a Layout event of
its own, not its file name — 2503.08161's logos —; guard `placement_arguments_are_not_names`).
- **Dump**: the CLI writes `<dest>.fmshadow.json` (`write_fm_shadow`: the entries in call order and a summary) after the
  output; a failure to write it is a Warning, not the conversion's failure. `cortex_worker` writes none.
- **Core**: the status line's undefined macros and missing files are listed sorted (`error::get_status_message`): a hash
  map's order follows the symbols' interning history, which the rehearsal (or any new definition) changes; Perl
  State.pm:771 lists `keys %{$$status{undefined}}`, a random hash order, so either order is Perl's.

Departures from the design note §2 (for S2a.2): the per-block policy id is the hook's family (the policy table, keyed on
the binding owning the `\author` meaning and the hook, is S2a.2's); single-author API calls (`\lx@add@creator`,
authblk's unlabelled `\author`) are API calls, not blocks (the comparator's "no block" class); contacts are rebound only
where the document defines them (an undefined one errs, held, as in pdflatex); a Note carries no mark (only the optional
number given to it: the symbol its `\thanks` prints is not recorded); a font-change Layout event has no span; a gap's
em is its box's font's quad (10pt where it has no font); a font switched inside a run of ink is no event there: the
run stays one Name and the Layout event, which compares a run's first font with the previous run's, shows at the next
run (`Ann Able\begingroup\bfseries Bob \and Carl`: after the `\and`, before "Carl"; splitting the run at the switch
would split every name set with a small-caps surname — gretsi's `first \textsc{last}`, 2508.03934 — into two Names:
S2a.2's call; guard `font_switch_inside_a_run_keeps_the_name`); tokens an `\input` in the field reads come from the
file and carry no position, so their events have no span (guard `input_field_events_carry_no_span`); `\corref`, `\fnref`, `\thanksref` and `\ead` are not bound
(they digest as their binding defines them, read by what they print); a bare `\footnotemark`'s label is the kernel
`\maketitle`'s `\@fnsymbol` mark unless the title's own is declared through `\lx@title@thefootnote` (above; article,
report and book declare `\@fnsymbol`, a title-page class none — report and book print arabic there —, and revtex's
default is `\@fnsymbol` too, `\@alph` only under `altaffilletter`), and assumes the counter at
the flush is the one at `\maketitle`; a binding block's projected positions may coincide with positions a later real
stamp gives (spans are unique only within a block: key an event by (block index, span); once S2b stamps for real,
projected must equal stamped); an event ending its block stops short of a trailing delimiter (`\footnotemark[1]}`'s
`]`: core `gullet::field_cover_of` ends a cover at the field's next token, and there is none); a mark printing only a
`\ref` (A&A's `\inst{\ref{ipag}}`, 1809.08354) prints nothing at digestion — the reference resolves in post — and is
no mark (S2a.2: read the `\ref`'s label). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchfms2a1::*` (event lists of the design probes, the gretsi
repro, 2401.16957's `,\inst` shape and the SYNC rows 46-48, 53, 62, 64, 66 shapes; spans in two shapes, gap widths and
fill, footnotemark labels and `\and` commands, the `inside` flags; the stamper's provenance and base; XML and log
unchanged by the switch; the CLI dump only under it, 0 errors and 0 warnings; r3, review revfms2a1_2: placement
arguments, rebound line breaks, the `&` column, the title-footnote hook, a font switch inside a run, an `\input`'s
spans; engine unit test `reading::tests::deferred_block_reports_the_journal_not_the_flush`); repros `sectioning-frontmatter/observer_*`
(the four symbol-line and mark-macro ones RED for their output, the S2b targets: witness 2304.13998's shape and the
design probes; `observer_rehearsal_aftergroup_stays_inside` and `observer_fill_gap_and_footnotemark_labels` GREEN, the
review's probes), `class-bindings/gretsi_v13_shared_mark_affiliation` (2508.03934).

**S2a.2: the resolver, the policy table and the comparator, still shadow only** (fms2a2; design note §2 points 1-9, §3
S2a, §5 defaults 4, 5, 6, 8, 9; the main session's S2a.2 notes). Under the switch the dump gains `resolved`: the ledger's
blocks and the API calls made apart from them, read into the tuples `ab_audit`'s `front.rs` extracts — each creator's
name without its marks, its requests (the marks shown on it), its affiliations, contacts and notes, the author block's
own (the XML's trailing nameless creator, #159) — each association with the rule that decided it and its source keyed by
(ledger index, span) (spans are unique only within a block; S2b's assertion that a projected range is the stamped one,
`ledger::projected_is_stamped`, is in place and off, `ASSERT_PROJECTED_IS_STAMPED`). Nothing of it reaches the output
(guard `perfect_kernel_batchfms2a2::resolver_leaves_the_xml_unchanged`).
- **Resolver** (`resolver/`, Layer C, class-independent; split by stage in r4): rows from `Break`, columns from `Sep(And)`/alignment tabs
  (unless the policy reads `\and` as inline); a line's type from its first ink — a mark-led line is labelled (unless it
  is the block's first line and its entries read as names whose marks a later line answers: the prefix convention), a
  column's first line or one whose name pieces each read as a name (`name_count`, `reads_as_affiliation`,
  `is_name_qualifier`) is a names line, a line of one link printing a name that name, a line of contacts a contact
  line, any other unmarked; names split at the separators, a name run that only layout parts one name (revtex's
  `\firstname{…} \surname{…}`, 1303.6104; a font switch or box never separates, decision 6d — an image does: a logo,
  review revfms2a1_3), a run of initials not ended by a gap (`V.G.~ Kagramanova`, 0802.4349), a qualifier after a comma
  the name's (`Robert W. Heath, Jr.`, `…, Student Member, IEEE`), an institution among the names the affiliation of the
  name before (`Chen Jia, SI-TECH Information Technology`, 2406.02959), a lone placement letter beside a box flagged
  (`flag:placement-letter`); a mark between a separator and a name the one nearer in the source (`Ann,$^{1}$ Bob` the
  name before, 0705.3409; `Ann$^1$, $^{2}$Bob` the next), an `\inst` after a comma the name before under the policy;
  ruling 1 — a mark's labels split at commas and spaces, a symbol run glued to a label two (`*1`), the name its text
  alone, a labelled entry to every name requesting it, a `fuzzy:<name>` label (svjour's `\institute` entries) to the
  name it spells; ruling 2 — a symbol-led line to every carrier of the character, an uncarried one the block's; an
  unmarked line under names the row above's, each line one contact (as today's `\\` lines: 0707.1113, 1404.0431),
  while an unmarked line under a labelled entry continues it (0803.3589); a note opening with a requested label that
  label's legend (2311.16145); the owner chain — the address's own label, the spelled author (`NameKeys`,
  `spelled_owners`), a class list's author at its call's place (one place per author, every spelled address at its
  author's: `_sequence`, #805), the group's only author, elimination (the line's one unspelled address and the one
  author without an address), the one author a note names the corresponding author (`names_correspondence`), the block;
  one contact per printed address (a braced `{a,b}@x` written out); a note emptied into contacts dropped
  (`ruling4:emptied`), and so is a note nothing in which prints (`ruling4:inkless`, `\thanks{}`, `\thanks{~}`: the
  lexer's `Event::inkless`, the XML's `leaves_no_ink` read on the rehearsed note; user ruling 2026-10-30, #916,
  superseding the 2026-10-21 reading that kept `\thanks{}`). API calls: a creator; a labelled contact (`label=`, a `labelseq=` place — a `\and`-list entry numbered piece by
  piece, #791 —, its leading mark, a `\label` a `\ref` mark names) to its requesters, the block's when none; an
  unlabelled one by its `annotate=` (the last author; `all`; `new`; `run[:<cap>]`, a second contact before a new author
  the same run's), its `\email`s its owners' too; a title's note (its parent `ltx:title`) is no creator's.
- **Lexer and rehearsal additions** (the events change only here): a mark printing only a `\ref` is a Mark labelled
  `ref:<key>` (A&A's `\inst{\ref{ipag}}`, 1809.08354; open question (a)); `\lx@request@frontmatter@annotation[<p>]{<l>}`
  (elsarticle's `\corref`, `\fnref`) a Mark labelled `<p>:<l>` printing nothing; a `\footnotemark[<n>]` reads <n>
  with `\c@footnote` at the rehearsal's start plus the steps the block's notes made before it, local to the mark
  (`\footnotemark[\arabic{footnote}]` after a `\thanks` prints that note's symbol, 2201.11183, 2111.13260; review
  rev78o2 finding 3; guard `footnotemark_number_reads_the_stepped_counter`); each API call's content (the queued
  command's last argument, inside the affiliation wrappers) is rehearsed and lexed at the flush, and its attributes and
  parent recorded; the binding owning `\author` is recorded at the call — the compiled binding whose load changed the
  meaning (`note_binding_load`, the loader seams of latexml_package and latexml_contrib `dispatch`; a pool's load is the kernel's), else
  `kernel`/`document`/`raw`/`fallback` by its origin — and with the hook is the policy key (notes decision 2, "no keyval
  in the binding files", superseded at 87a: each binding declares its conventions, below). A bare `\footnotemark` prints the kernel title hook `\lx@title@thefootnote`
  (`TITLE_FOOTNOTE_HOOK` = `latex_constructs::TITLE_THEFOOTNOTE`, 78o) when defined; else the policy entry's
  `title_marks`: `Fnsymbol` (the kernel `\maketitle`'s `\@fnsymbol\c@footnote`) or `Body` (the class's own
  `\thefootnote`: report's and book's title page, arabic). (r2: the revtex entry's inert `\frontmatter@thefootnote`
  field is gone — revtex4-2.cls:3040-3043 is `\@fnsymbol` by default, :5976-5978 `\@booleanfalse\altaffilletter@sw`
  after :3043's default, checked with pdflatex; `\@alph` only under `altaffilletter`.) The policy key is the binding
  owning `\author`, or — when that is the kernel's — the document class's binding with an entry (`ledger::policy_binding`:
  the first binding the class's load loaded that has one; `jpconf.cls`, `report.cls`, `book.cls` — iopart_support owns
  its `\author` itself),
  never over a package owning `\author` (authblk); an API call runs under the policy of the block before it.
- **Policy table** (`policy.rs`, Layer B; first match on (binding, hook), else `kernel`; since 87a each binding's own
  declaration, "The conventions' home" below): `revtex`
  (revtex4_support.sty; `annotate=new` declared by the binding's call), `authblk` (`thenote`: authblk's `\AB@thenote`
  under ruling 1, below; `state_counter` `Maxaffil`), `report`, `book` (`title_marks: Body`), `llncs` (`\inst` after a comma, `\and`
  inline: #791, #792, #807), `aa`, `inst_support`, `svjour` (`\inst` after a comma, #807), `jheppub`, `jcappub`,
  `jinstpub` (e-mail by spelling else call order, #801, #805, #809), `iopart`, `jpconf` (the same, each call a group:
  #806, #808, #841); each entry cites what it reproduces (since 87a checked at the declaration and over the
  re-resolver's list, ab_audit `fmshadow::tests::a_declared_familys_dump_re_resolves_under_its_bindings_conventions`).
- **Comparator** (`ab_audit fmshadow ROOT [-o PREFIX] [--keys F] [--re-resolve]`, latexml_oxide/bin/ab_audit/fmshadow/):
  per paper the shadow's tuples against the XML's (names without their `ltx:sup` marks, texts by their letters and
  digits; contacts of role `note`/`thanks` read as notes on both sides), each disagreement a row — kind (`name-split`,
  `affiliation`, `contact-owner`, `contact`, `note`, `block`), family (the policy key's binding), the deciding rule —
  **classified** when that rule holds an adopted ruling's change tag (`CHANGE_TAGS`) or the disagreement falls in a
  PDF-confirmed XML-wrong class (`XML_WRONG`, by name with its witnesses; r2, below), unclassified otherwise; a paper with no rehearsed block is "no block" and one whose rehearsal held an
  error "held", both outside the gate's denominator (notes decisions 1, 3); the block-final `]` span shortfall is not
  compared (texts are). `--re-resolve` resolves the dump's events again with the binary's resolver. Output
  `<prefix>.tsv`, `<prefix>.disagree.tsv`, `<prefix>.shadow.jsonl`, `<prefix>.summary.txt` (the per-family table by
  reach with the gate number, the share of a family's counted papers with an unclassified disagreement).
Measured (the census numbers and the PDF checks are in SYNC_STATUS "FM S2a.2"): far from the K23 class guard (under 0.5 %
per family) on every family but the smallest; S2b waits for further resolver rounds. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batchfms2a2::*`; engine unit tests `policy::tests::*`, `resolver::tests::*`; ab_audit unit tests
`fmshadow::tests::*`.

**S2a.2 r2: the resolver by defect class, the comparator made honest** (review revfms2a2: of 40 sampled unclassified
disagreements 31 were the resolver's, 8 today's XML, 1 normalisation). Still shadow only (XML byte-identical with the
switch on and off and against int53a, SYNC "FM S2a.2").
- **Notes** keep their whole text (their contacts' texts too: a note's text is its events' printed text, the rehearsal's
  contact constructors printing nothing); what is left once the contacts are taken out decides only ruling 4's "emptied",
  and an emptied note goes to `Resolved.dropped` (rule `ruling4:emptied`) for the comparison (2401.17399, 1607.05792,
  2603.01292). A note's legend label is its body's leading Mark event (the lexer adds it to the note's `inner`), never
  the flattened text (`$^{1}$Unit` read "1Unit"; 1909.02288, 2608.06122, 1903.10543, 2407.19826); the "any word of three
  letters" reading is gone.
- **Labels**: a `fuzzy:<name>` label stays whole and is matched by the name's letters, a mark command's argument and a
  formula dropped (`Luca Passalacqua (\Envelope)`, 0807.3898, 2403.09642); a creator's own `author:N` is the N-th
  creator, matched exactly (relocate.rs:42-50; 1804.09680, astro-ph0611539); every other label by Perl's chain
  (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:891-900): the exact request, then past the request's prefix, the label's, both
  (elsarticle's `fn:label1` answers `\address[label1]`, 1712.00945).
- **Names lines by evidence** (finding 6): a later line of a column is names only after a blank line, continuing a
  names row that ended in a comma or "and" (1403.0130), under a row with its affiliation line already when set in a font
  of its own (1009.1429, 1108.3744) or after the row's labelled lines (SYNC row 46), with marks or notes on its names
  (1403.5246), or as two or more name pieces — and then each piece must read as a name; one name-like piece without
  evidence is an affiliation ("Capital Fund Management", "Google DeepMind": 2606.07382, 2307.02318, 2305.16559,
  2609.09054); a line of e-mail addresses alone is never names (2210.05991). An IEEE ordinal before a name
  (`1\textsuperscript{st} Sertac`) stays with it, as today's personname (2412.10792, 2202.06596).
- **Marks in lines**: punctuation before a mark does not lead the line (`($^1$)`, 1004.4809); a mark set off by a space
  (source positions between it and the ink before) opens an entry of its own (`$^1$Arizona State University $^2$Rider
  University`, 2601.20069); a symbol some name shows that the lexer read as ink at a line's start is a Mark (`$\sharp$ -
  CBCL`, 1209.1360); marks trailing their text, each shown on another line, label it (2507.05750; not a lone
  `Harvard University$^{*}$`, 2307.02318).
- **Lines under names**: unmarked lines under a row whose names show non-symbol marks are one affiliation of every name,
  as today's `\\`-joined contact (0903.2366, 2303.09899; a footnote symbol is no such mark, 0707.1113); a line under a
  labelled entry continues it unless it is addresses alone, which the owner chain places (2509.12185, 0801.3376,
  0810.3062).
- **API intake** takes only creators and creator annotations (`resolver::creator_call`): no MDPI `reftitle`, no
  author-contribution note (2608.12223). **Contact roles**: the call's declared role wins over a `mailto:` link inside
  it (2506.17875), a url printing one e-mail address is an e-mail (1409.0496); the rehearsal binds `\email`-type
  commands only when the document's take an argument (jmlr2e's `\email` is a font switch: 2412.18293, 2305.17297);
  acmart's address-part key is no ink (1907.07713). An annotation of the new authors (`annotate=new`/`run`/`<n>`)
  before any creator reaches none (revtex collaboration lists declaring every `\affiliation` first, 2103.04797,
  0704.1604); an unqualified one is the block's (0709.0811).
- **Today's placements reproduced**: the amsart contact grid (insert.rs `distribute_upfront_contacts`; 2205.02163); a
  replacing `\author` keeps the latest call's authors (`\lx@clear@frontmatter`; 2502.11323, 2509.11381).
- **authblk** (`thenote`, review answer 6b): an unlabelled author requests `\AB@thenote` (the `affil` counter, stepped at
  the first `\author` after an `\affil`), an unlabelled `\affil` is labelled by it — when the marks show (a label given,
  or the counter past `\c@Maxaffil`, recorded at the block's call); else (block mode) the run, as the binding declares
  (authblk.sty:114-118, 148-151; 2605.25017).
- **Comparator honesty** (findings 8, 9, 14): the block's items are compared as a multiset (kind `block`) and `rule_of`
  searches them; an XML item is explained by the shadow's items only when it is two or more of them joined (the word
  "and" between allowed), no looser overlap; ORCID links compare by their identifier (the XML's `ref` href, in a contact
  or the personname); `ruling3:one-per-print` classifies only a joined item, the owner its other tag's; elimination is
  **not** a change — today's output applies it (#52's e-mail lines, `owners_by_elimination`, under user ruling R10 2026-10-20, 77p r10), and
  FIDELITY_CHARTER §4's owner order is silent on it (flagged to the main session). The XML-wrong classes, each confirmed
  on its witnesses' pdflatex PDFs: names parted by a wide space merged into one personname (2312.06207, 2303.02369,
  2512.16241, 2511.18287), a list of names in one personname (1512.06985, 1610.06365, 2211.02638, 2411.11150), an ORCID
  logo's glyphs read as "ID" after the name (2501.15882, 2405.19400); a name class applies only when it explains every
  XML name. Guards `perfect_kernel_batchfms2a2::{notes_keep_their_whole_text, fuzzy_labels_stay_whole,
  author_sequence_labels_place_their_contacts, prefix_fallback_answers_a_mismatched_label,
  note_legends_by_their_leading_mark, institution_lines_are_not_names, contact_roles_follow_the_call_and_the_address,
  marks_mid_line_and_trailing_label_entries, authblk_unlabelled_affil_is_its_thenote, report_title_page_marks_are_arabic,
  a_replacing_author_call_keeps_the_latest, ams_contact_grid_is_distributed}` (each red on r1), the r1 guards pinned as
  whole sequences; unit tests `resolver::tests::*`, `fmshadow::tests::{block_items_and_joined_pieces,
  xml_wrong_name_classes_explain_every_name}`.

when they spell the owner or are its only link (no guessing, user ruling 2026-10-20 #4) — r6; a braced `{a,b,c}@x` group in
an `\institute`/`\affil` entry is written out and each address goes to the author it spells, an unspelled one to the block's
shared creator (#4/#8/#10) — r6; the corresponding-author fallback holds only for an address printed alone (user ruling
2026-10-21 #14). The resolver drops a replaced `\author` call's block items with its creators (`resolver/mod.rs`, 2510.26354);
its footnote-text pairing skips the replaced creators' marks since r6 (below).

  note's e-mail with no owner; the block's own items of the replaced call go with its creators (2510.26354's first
  `\author`, whose `firstname.lastname@h-its.org` the second call's addresses write out).
- **A resolved name is its printed text** (finding 2, the main session's decision): `new_creator` keeps a piece printing
  no letter or digit (r5's filter, review revfms2a2_4 finding 6, removed), its spaces collapsed, as the join paths keep
  it (1706.00234's "TIÊ ´N-SO . N PHẠM"); a zero-width character never reaches it (the lexer's `is_zero_width`).

  note's only link and the note's mark is shown on the owner, or when it spells the owner (an e-mail by the owner chain's
  spelling, a url by its letters after the scheme and `www.`, `link_letters`: `owner:spelled`); an e-mail spelling
  another author of the block is that author's, as before (1908.04020); any other stays in the note's text, no contact,
  and a note whose contacts are not all taken out is never emptied (ruling 4's drop). A class printing no note marks —

  (2504.08644) and four co-authors' ORCIDs (2602.13176) went to the last author. The comparator strips ORCID iDs from
  the notes it compares (`without_orcid_ids`: the XML's note prints an ORCID link's logo, the shadow's its iD).

  `\institute`/`\affil` entry holds that prints several addresses (`\{a,b,c\}@x`, or a list) is written out, each address
