- **Source order** (finding 1): a note `answer_note_links` keeps once every name is read came after the notes the source
  gives later (`\author{Ann Able\thanks{\url{ann@x.org}, \url{zed@y.org}}\thanks{Second note.} \and Bob Baker}` read
  `[Second note., ann@x.org, zed@y.org]`, int69b the source's order) — and a deferred link after the contacts of the lines
  under it. Once `resolve` ends each creator's notes and contacts, and the block's own, are in source order
  (`in_source_order`: ledger index, then span start; an item with no source keeps its place). The comparator sees note
  order now: the notes both sides hold, each side's in its order (`note_orders`), a `note-order` row when they differ,
  its rule the first out-of-place shadow note's (`order …`): unclassified unless a ruling placed that note — a legend
  ruling 1 places by its label is today's last, relocated, where the shadow keeps the source's order (2607.03557's
  `\textsuperscript{$\dagger$}Corresponding author` before its funding note).
- **An ownerless note's link** (finding 2, decision 4): `fallback` asks for an owner — a note no name holds (an address
  line's, a line's) gives its link to the author it spells or leaves it in its text, never to the block (the only link of
  `ann@x.org, bob@x.org\thanks{Code: \url{…}}` was a block url, and a sole author's by `sole_author_takes_the_block`).
- **A url is an author's only as the page it spells** (finding 3, decision 1): a url is spelled by its page
  (`link_page`: its last path segment, an `index.*` or `*.html` page after it aside, else its host), read from the link's
  target (an `\href`'s first argument) in all four placements — a co-author's, the note's owner's (`owner:spelled`), the
  only-link fallback, and so an ownerless one (the sole-author move sees none, above). A homepage
  (`sites.google.com/view/<name>`, `tu.berlin/disco/klimm`, `…/MarcinPitera`, `portal.research.lu.se/en/persons/<name>`,
  `insti.physics.sunysb.edu/~siegel/plan.html`, `www.pengxu.net/`: 2301.03638, 1409.7028, 2601.07017, 1603.02588,
  2001.02600; `academics.aut.ac.nz/robin.hankin` behind `\href{…}{work}`, 2210.15991) goes to the author it spells; a
  repository, a project or a file under an account stays in the note's text (`github.com/<user>/<repo>`,
  `…/resolution.git`, `<user>.github.io/<project>`, `…/<name>/accvideo.mp4`: 2008.12970, 2511.08416, 2103.05251,
  2503.02954, 2509.01952), and a page no name spells is no one's, the note's only link too (r2-r7's fallback made
  `\thanks{Code is available at \url{…}}` its owner's contact: 2409.18582, 2511.12997, 1607.05792, 1908.10122's doi,
  2509.14694's springer.com; 1401.0489's `people.cs.uchicago.edu/~laci`, a nickname, too). A link to an address
  (`\href{mailto:tsamak@clemson.edu}{tsamak}`, 2309.10007) or printing addresses (`\url{brunnerj, edemaine, dylanhen,
  wellman@mit.edu}`, 2010.09271, 1407.7882) is the address: read by its letters, the note's only link its owner's (r9:
  a `mailto:` link an e-mail read by the address it points to, every link contact carrying its target — below).
- **jpconf's note marks** (finding 4): jpconf prints them as the body's arabic `\thefootnote` set as a superscript
  (jpconf.cls:139, 153), its policy entry `TitleMarks::Body` — 1105.2659's `\footnote[3]{Speaker}` shows "3", as its PDF
  (the kernel's `\@fnsymbol\c@footnote` recursed through jpconf's `\@fnsymbol`); a bare `\footnotemark`'s print is read
  quietly as a note's (`note_mark_quietly` in `\lx@fm@obs@fnmark`): under a class whose `\@fnsymbol` reads `\thefootnote`
  with no policy entry it ran away and ended the block's rehearsal, the block unobserved.
- **A glued symbol run a line leads with is one mark** (decision 2): `glue_shown_runs` marks a mark's run of two or more
  different footnote symbols (`§†`) that a line of its block leads with and a name shows (`Event::glued`), read as one
  label (`event_labels`) as a run of one symbol (`††`) is — 0907.1243's `W.Y.~Ching$^{\S\dagger}$` has only the line
  `$^{\S\dagger}$…Missouri…`, `R.H.~French$^{\S}$` only DuPont's; a run no line leads with stays the marks it is written
  of (`R.~Podgornik$^{\dagger\star}$`).
- **Nits** (findings 5-8, decision 3): a mark `split_text_marks` parts from a line's text is a footnote symbol only when
  its characters are `\@fnsymbol`'s (`#`, a `★` set in text: marks of no such kind, their legend ruling 1's); an entry of
  no label is no legend (`.all()` of none); an API entry a symbol leads (`api:leading-mark`) whose text names the
  corresponding author or an equal contribution is that legend, a note of the names showing its mark (0812.1531's
  `$^\star${corresponding author, e-mail: …}` in revtex's `\affiliation` was Curtarolo's affiliation; 1902.02631,
  2205.09074, 2504.15015, 1412.0709, 2409.11440) — only those: the call declares an affiliation, an address change is
  one, and a funding word names an institution as often (`$^\dagger$Science \& Finance, Capital Fund Management, …`,
  0710.0802); the comparator's `part` is one line, or a run of lines, of the joined entry (`Resolved::continued`, the
  dump's `continued`, `is_line_run`; a dump made before r8, no lines, keeps r7's substring), today's one contact of an
  API call's affiliations and its legend is their sequence (`affiliation_rule_of`'s `pieces_rule`: 2409.11440, 2306.16240,
  2608.17299), and of two shadow items of one kind and text the rule kept is a ruling's change (ruling 3's second print,
  2509.23109: its order no longer decides it).
Not done (r8 residual): jpconf's `\footnote[<n>]` sets the counter (jpconf.cls:145-146) where the rehearsal's binding
does not, so a bare `\footnotemark` after it shows the kernel's count (`Cat Cole\footnotemark` after `\footnote[3]`: the
PDF's 4, the shadow's 1); a homepage spelled by no name's spelling (1401.0489's `~laci`) stays in the note; and, found by
r8's census unset vs set, pre-existing: the rehearsal leaves a box register an author block `\usebox`es changed (its
content then wrapped in an `ltx:text`: 2405.14627, 2603.26792) and, under siamart, algorithmic's `\AND` printing a plain
"and" (2409.10200) — the switch is not yet output-neutral there (SYNC row "FM shadow rehearsal leaks", RED repro
`sectioning-frontmatter/observer_rehearsal_leaves_a_used_box_unchanged.tex`). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batchfms2a2r8::*` (10; each red on r7 but the XML pin and the address-line positive control: the
convert shapes by r7's own shadow dump, the resolver-level unlabelled entry by its code), the re-pinned

**S2a.2 r9: the r8 landing review's findings, the rehearsal's isolation** (review revfms2a2_8 findings 1-7; the SYNC row
"FM shadow rehearsal leaks"). Shadow only, and now so with the switch set too: int65's 725 papers, the 992 sectioning-frontmatter repros
and the 26,323-paper census byte-identical int73a → r9 unset and r9 unset → set (but a clock paper, 2109.00764, and a
time-budgeted math parse, 1001.0023, whose reruns agree).
- **A link contact carries its target** (finding 1): `Assoc::target` (the dump's `target`), where the link points — an
  `\href`'s first argument, a `\url`'s text, a `mailto:` link's address (`link_target`, `mailto_address`: its scheme and a
  `?subject=` query aside) —, its `text` the anchor it prints: Hankin's `\href{https://academics.aut.ac.nz/robin.hankin}
  {work}` was a url contact "work", the url lost (2210.15991). A `mailto:` link is an e-mail (`contact_parts`), placed by
  the address — its note's link by `place_note_link`, a block's contact by the owner chain on the address
  (`contact_event` → `place_line_contacts`) —, not the anchor (2309.10007's `tsamak`, `csamak`, `vkrovi`). S2b has the
  target to write; the comparison still reads the anchor, today's note text.
- **The API legend reads the text** (finding 2): an API entry a symbol leads is a legend note (r8) only when no piece of it
  reads as an affiliation (`reads_as_affiliation` of each name and contact it prints — an address and its label read as
  none —, not of the joined text, where any address answers "no") or when it is one piece its marks split an entry into
  (`api:split-by-marks`); the role change carries its own tag, `api:legend` (a change tag; `affiliation_rule_of` explains
  today's affiliation by it, not by `api:leading-mark`). IEEEtran's `\IEEEauthorblockA{{*Equal Contribution} \\
  \IEEEauthorblockA{Tsinghua University} \IEEEauthorblockA{National Supercomputing Center in Wuxi} …}` was one legend
  note of the starred names, both institutions out of the affiliation role (1903.06934); it is their affiliation again,
  as r7 read it (the entry whole — today's has the nested calls apart: unclassified, residual). 0812.1531, 1902.02631 and
  the census's other API legends stay legends.
- **Comparator honesty** (finding 3): the notes a ruling placed (a change tag) are taken out of both sides' orders and
  the rest must agree (`compare`'s `note-order`): `[L, A, B]` against `[B, A, L]` was explained by the legend L, A and B
  swapped; now unclassified, its rule the first of the rest out of order. Every rule of a (kind, text) key is kept
  (`TCreator::all_rules`, `Tuples::block_all_rules`) and each copy the XML lacks takes one, the copies it holds taking the
  rules that reproduce today's first (`surplus_rules`): 1910.01401's second ORCID copy, placed by `owner:adjacent`, read
  as the ruling's `note:adjacent ruling4:inner-contact` — unclassified now (the shadow is right: the ORCID is printed
  beside the name and in the note, today's holds it in the block alone; residual).
- **Rehearsal isolation** (the SYNC leak row; 2405.14627, 2603.26792, 2409.10200): two kinds of state the rehearsal
  changed and nothing put back. (1) A box the stomach stamped with a field provenance (`fieldProv`/`fieldSerial`,
  `invoke_token`) is stamped only when it has none; `\copy`/`\usebox` hands back the register's box itself, so the
  rehearsal's print stamped the shared box with a serial its `FieldLedgerScope` then dropped, and the conversion's print,
  finding it stamped, did not stamp it again — its field ink then wrapped it in an `ltx:text` with an id. The scope now
  journals the boxes stamped while it is open (`token::field_stamp_noted`) and unstamps them when it closes
  (`Digested::try_remove_property`): a stamp on a box that had none is all the stomach writes. (2) A meaning's standing as
  a fallback guess, kernel stub or borrowed package's (`state::fallback_meanings`, which a `\newcommand` may replace,
  `is_definable_latex`) is changed by an assignment beside the meaning and put back by no group end: the rehearsal's
  group-local `\let\AND\lx@fm@obs@AND` cleared OmniBus's `\AND` (the siamart binding loads OmniBus), so
  algorithmic.sty:161's `\newcommand{\AND}{\algorithmicand{} }` was refused and `\AND` printed the separator's plain
  "and". An assignment journal now saves a meaning's standing with its bindings at its first assignment
  (`AssignmentJournal::fallback`) and its rollback restores it — every speculative run's, not the rehearsal's alone.
- **Nits** (findings 4-7): the dump's `continued` optional (`Resolved::continued: Option`; a missing key an old dump, "any
  part" — an r8 dump's empty list no longer); `link_page` reads a `*.html` page right under the host as the page that
  spells its owner (`host/jsmith.html` "jsmith"; one under a segment stays that segment's, `~siegel/plan.html`), and a
  url is "printing addresses" only when it holds one (`addresses_in`), not any `@` (`medium.com/@user` a page);
  `in_source_order` sorts a span-less item after its block's spanned ones; `is_symbol_char` is the lexer's
  `is_fnsymbol`.
Measured on the census (26,323 papers, switch set): 19,510 agree, 1,880 classified, 1,816 unclassified (7.8 %; r8 19,510 /
1,882 / 1,814); two papers moved, both classified → unclassified (1607.00911, 1910.01401: the honest readings above);
revtex4_support 23 of 5,639 unclassified (0.4 %), the same 23, its seeded 41-paper draw unchanged but for the `api:legend`
tag on three rows (0812.1531, 2605.28357, 2501.04244).

**S2b r1 (int79, 2026-10-24): the observer writes one family, under the switch.** For a family whose policy entry is
`written` — the pilot, revtex4_support's `revtex` — `observer::writer::write_observed_frontmatter` runs at the end of
`insert_frontmatter` with `LATEXML_FM_SHADOW=1`: the paper's creators are read back as the comparator reads them
(`emitter::dom`), compared with the resolver's reading, and written only when every difference is one of the writer's
operations (`emitter::plan`): an entry given to the names the reading gives it (owners by mark), one call's marked entries
cut apart at their marks (pieces mapped to the call's queued tokens by a stamped rehearsal, the mark kept as styled label
ink), a legend made a note of the names showing its mark, a url printing an address made an e-mail. Each operation is a
rule holding an adopted ruling's change tag (`resolver::CHANGE_TAGS`, shared with `ab_audit fmshadow`); any other
difference leaves the paper as today's, and what was written is read back against the reading (a Warning names the
writer's own defect). Unset, nothing of it runs. Measured: unset 367/367 byte-identical to int78c (300 census revtex
papers + controls); set, 23 of the 300 revtex papers written, controls unchanged, E/F equal, no distinct frontmatter word
lost or gained in any of the 23 and every byte after the frontmatter identical — the word count falls (−3,061) where a
whole marked affiliation list was every name's (1409.8253: one 7-institution block on 23 names, now each institution on
the names showing its mark) and a starred legend leaves the affiliations for a correspondence note (2602.16003: Romera's
mark 2 answers no affiliation in the PDF, today's gave Romera Torres's corresponding-author line). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batchfms2b::{footnote_marked_affiliations_go_to_their_names, a_marked_affiliation_is_cut_at_its_marks}`;
the shadow-neutral guards of batchfms2a2r7/r8 keep the families not switched. Next: the full 5,639-paper revtex census
switched off vs on with PDF checks on a seeded draw, then the switch on by default for revtex4_support; then the next
family by the per-family gate.

**The conventions' home (87a, 2026-10-28; user ruling "in each binding", the audit's §3a item 1).** A family's
conventions are declared by its binding at load, not looked up in a table keyed on binding file names in generic
code: `declare_frontmatter_conventions(&FRONTMATTER_CONVENTIONS)` is the first statement of the binding's load, its
`FmConventions` (`observer::policy::Policy`: every field the table carried — `inst_after_comma`, `and_inline`,
`label_sequence`, `email_owner`, `call_is_group`, `title_marks`, `thenote`, `state_counter`, `and_word`,
`unmarked_notes`, `written`, `cite` — completed from `FM_KERNEL_CONVENTIONS`) kept in the state globally under the
declaring binding's file name (`frontmatter_conventions:<binding>`, one declaration per hook, `*` any; the first
matching in declaration order applies, a re-declaration replaces in place). `policy_for` and `has_entry` read the
state; a family that declares none is `KERNEL`, as the table's fallback was (since 93a, OD #925: the kernel's own
blocks `KERNEL`, written; a binding owning `\author` that declares none `UNDECLARED`, the same reading unwritten);
`written` (revtex4_support, ams_support: the default build's S2b writer) is the binding's own flag. The key is the one the ledger already recorded at the call
(`ledger::author_binding`, `ledger::policy_binding`), as the table's lookup was: a declaration reaches a binding only
while that binding's `\author` at the call is still the declaring binding's — loading the declaring binding is not
enough. revtex4_support's reaches revtex4, revtex4-1, revtex4-2; ams_support's ams_core's amsart, amsproc, amsbook and
amsaddr; iopart_support's iopart.cls, because iopart_support's own locked `\author[]{}` owns the call (all 122 author
blocks of the 97 iopart census papers keyed `iopart_support.sty`); `policy_binding` — the class's declaring binding under
the kernel's `\author` — reaches jpconf.cls, report.cls and book.cls (the census's only blocks where owner and key
differ: 57, 36, 33). Not reached today: the
aastex classes load revtex4 and then `aas_support`, whose `\author` (aas_support_sty.rs) takes the ownership — kernel
conventions, keyed `aas_support.sty` (every aastex-family census paper: aastex 45, aastex631 24, aastex63 13,
aastex62 7, aastex6 3, aastex7 3; 1005.0770, 1910.05363, 2604.19097); lmcs's own `\author` (lmcs_cls.rs) calls
`\lx@add@author`, no `\lx@add@authors*`, so the observer records no author block and no conventions are read
(2306.08266, 2108.06944, 2402.09138: 0 blocks under `LATEXML_FM_SHADOW=1`); OmniBus (inst_support's conventions by
default, loaded eagerly) is reached by ams_support's only when its `\subjclass` autoload (omnibus_cls.rs:820) or the
ambient `\curraddr` autoload (tex.rs:314) loads ams_support before `\author` (the 87a r2 re-review's probes p2, p4; the
ambient one would also reach a kernel-`\author` class, a shape pdflatex does not compile); aa.cls's declaration
is unread, inst_support owning aa's `\author` (all 100 aa census papers keyed `inst_support.sty`, the same values).
Whether aastex should take revtex's conventions is an observer decision left open. The fifteen former
rows, each in its binding (latexml_package: revtex4_support, authblk, llncs, aa, inst_support, sv_support,
ams_support, IEEEtran, jheppub, iopart_support, report, book; latexml_contrib: jcappub, jinstpub, jpconf); no binding
file name is a key in `observer/`. Offline (`ab_audit fmshadow --re-resolve`) no binding loads, so the re-resolver holds
the bindings' declarations by reference (`fmshadow/conventions.rs` `DECLARED`, `resolver::resolve_with`) and fails a
paper loudly (`stale-conventions`) when a block's recorded conventions are not the ones the list gives its binding, or
it records none: a summary column of its own (`stale_conventions`), counted by the gate as unclassified, and a non-zero
exit. A drift guard scans the bindings' sources for the declaration and checks the list is exactly theirs, each
`binding:` its own registry entry's name and extension.
A pure refactor: the observer census (1,612 papers over every family that declares, `LATEXML_FM_SHADOW=1`) gives
byte-identical shadow records on both binaries, and the same XML (one display formula's parse varied under the census
load, 2002.02531, identical on solo reruns of both), and the A/B (5,309 papers: those families plus 2,000 of
popint110u; E 7,230 → 7,230, F 12 → 12) changes no paper (its four changed rows — math-ambiguity enumeration counts
under load, 2507.14058, 2411.02167, gr-qc9505014, and a 180 s timeout, 2203.01615 — identical on solo reruns of both).
Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch87a::a_bindings_declared_conventions_are_read_and_an_undeclared_family_is_the_kernels`, engine
unit test `policy::tests::a_declaration_is_read_and_an_undeclared_family_takes_the_kernel`, ab_audit
`fmshadow::tests::{a_declared_familys_dump_re_resolves_under_its_bindings_conventions,
the_declared_list_is_every_bindings_own_declaration,
stale_conventions_have_their_own_column_count_in_the_gate_and_fail_the_run}`.

### 840. A space a name sets before its own mark is the name's; spacing-only math, `\enskip` after a mark part names

OD #52(i) rewrites a horizontal space in an author block (`\hspace`, `\hfill`) to `\quad`, which with `\quad` and
`\qquad` is a separator of the author/affiliation split (Perl's `@authoraffilsplits`, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:681-682).
A name that sets a space before its own mark then lost its co-authors: `Oleg Lychkovskiy\thanks{…}\hspace*{2mm}$^{\rm
a,b}$, Sergei Blinnikov\hspace*{2mm}$^{\rm a,c}$` (0905.3658) split into the line "Oleg Lychkovskiy" and the mark-led
line "$^{\rm a,b}$, Sergei Blinnikov", an affiliation (one creator, a contact ", Sergei Blinnikov"); Perl, which never
rewrites `\hspace`, reads two creators — but splits a written `\quad` there the same way. Ours (78m, rows.rs
`space_before_own_mark`): at the block's top level, outside math, after a name letter, a run of horizontal space that
opens with `\hspace` (its `*` and length read with it), `\hfill`, `\hfil`, `\quad` or `\qquad` (more spacing and spaces
after it in the run) is dropped when a mark or a note of the name before it follows (`leading_marks_end`: `$^{…}$`,
`\textsuperscript{…}`, `\altaffilmark{…}`, `\thanks{…}`, `\footnote{…}`) and no entry text follows that — a comma, `;`,
the word "and", a line separator, a separating run of spacing (a separating space, an `\enskip` — a separator right
after a mark, below —, or two or more spacing commands as #52(o) counts them), `\par`, a closing brace or the end come
after it; one spacing command after the marks (a tie, a control space) and the spaces around it are passed over before
that test, being the next entry's. A mark that leads an entry keeps the space a separator: `$^1$Univ A\quad$^2$Univ B`
and `$^1$~Univ A\quad$^2$~Univ B` (78m r2; r1 read the tie as "more spacing", so Ann had "Univ A² Univ B" and Bob none)
are an affiliation line's two entries, as `\textsuperscript{2}\ Univ B` is. Two more spacings part names (78m): a math
group at the block's top level holding only spacing (`\quad`, `\qquad`, the spacing commands of #52(o), spaces) is that
spacing written outside math (`spacing_math_unwrapped`; 1602.04504's `Michael J. Wilber$^{1,2}$ $\qquad$ Vitaly
Shmatikov$^{1,2}$ $\qquad$ Serge Belongie$^{1,2}$` was one creator, in Perl too, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1069), and
latex.ltx's `\enskip` (`\hskip.5em\relax`) at the top level right after a mark or note is a space #52(i) rewrites to
`\quad`, as `\hspace` (1312.1414's five names parted by `Berry\thanks{…} \enskip \normalsize Andrew M.\ Childs`);
elsewhere it is one of #52(o)'s spacing commands (`is_spacing_command`), one of which stays inside a name (`J.\enskip
Smith$^{1}$`, `A.\enskip B. Smith`, which 78m r1, reading every top-level `\enskip` as a separator, parted) and a run of
two or more of which parts names. The labels of a mark lose a `\rm` glued to them as Perl's `s/\\rm//g`
(Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:365) strips it (`clean_frontmatter_labels`): `$^{\rm a,b}$` reads "\rma,b", the tokenizer
having skipped the space after `\rm`, which OD #34's `FONT_SWITCH` (a switch before a non-letter) left, so "\rma" was
requested and no `${\rm ^a}$` line answered it. Residual: in a block marked with labels, a name whose only mark is a
footnote symbol continues the line before it (`Bob Baker$^{2}$\quad Cat Cole$^{\S}$` is one name, the base too:
1312.1414's "Richard Cleve Robin Kothari Rolando D. Somma", flagged `merged_creators`; SYNC_STATUS 78m bullet). Repros
sectioning-frontmatter/{author_space_before_own_mark_is_the_name, author_spacing_math_between_names_separates,
author_tie_after_entry_mark_is_the_entry, author_enskip_in_name_and_after_note}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78m::{author_space_before_own_mark_is_the_name, author_spacing_math_between_names_separates,
author_tie_after_entry_mark_is_the_entry, author_enskip_in_name_and_after_note}`.

*Live rule: OD #993.*

### 841. jpconf.cls is read raw, then its address and e-mail blocks are the frontmatter

IOP's conference class (jpconf.cls 2004/05/04 v1.0, Journal of Physics: Conference Series; not in TeX Live, 58 census
papers ship it) copies iopart.cls's author block: `\address` (:108-110) and `\ead`/`\eads`/`\mailto` (:104-106) print
an `{indented}` list item where they stand. Perl has no binding (OmniBus: `\address` an address contact, `\ead` an empty
e-mail contact, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1068); under the raw-class lever (#444) the blocks were bullet lists after the
abstract and the authors had no contact (0705.0202, 1011.0523). Ours (78m, `latexml_contrib/src/jpconf_cls.rs`): the
paper's copy is read raw (`RawRead`, `shipped`), then iopart_support's address and e-mail definitions are made
(`iopart_support_sty::iop_address_and_email`, factored out of the iopart_support binding unchanged): each `\address` an
affiliation of the authors before it (`\lx@add@affiliation@marked`), each `\ead` an e-mail placed with its author
(#806, #808, #809). The class's other definitions stay its own; jpconf.cls is on `author_files::AUTHOR_FILES`. Repro
sectioning-frontmatter/jpconf_copy (a stand-in jpconf.cls written from scratch); guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78m::jpconf_address_and_email_are_frontmatter`.

*Live rule: OD #460.*

### 842. bmcart.cls is read raw, then its title, author and address printers are the frontmatter

BioMed Central's bmcart.cls (VTeX; not in TeX Live, 20 census papers ship it) lets `\title`, `\author`, `\address` and
`{fmbox}` to its printers in `{frontmatter}` (:966-984): `\title@fmt` typesets the title in the `{fmbox}` (:1034-1053),
`\author@fmt[keys]{name}` the name and the numbers of its `addressref` addresses (:1198-1255), `\address@fmt[id=…]`
stores the address (:1287-1296) for the "Author details" that `\thebibliography` prints (:1708-1712 `\printaddresses`),
which the kernel's bibliography constructor never runs. Read raw (#444) the document had no title, no creator and no
address (1711.01177: a `titlepage` of boxes, the marks "??"); Perl, with no binding, makes one creator "[" (OmniBus's
`\author` reads the bracket as the name) and 7 Errors (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1067). Ours (78m,
`latexml_contrib/src/bmcart_cls.rs`): the copy is read raw, then `\title@fmt` is `\lx@add@title`; `\author@fmt` a
`\lx@add@creator[role=author,annotations={…}]` requesting its `addressref` and `presentaddressref` ids, its name parts
as the printed name reads them (:1247-1249: `\inits` dropped, `\fnm`, `\snm`, `\particle`, `\suffix` as written), each
address of its `email` key (`email={a@x, b@y}`) an `\lx@add@email`; `\address@fmt` an affiliation
`\lx@add@contact[role=affiliation,label={id}]` (the class's `aff<n>` without an `id`), its parts as
`\address@definitions` prints them (:1298-1304); `\@bmcartnote[id=…]{text}`, an article note (`{artnotes}`'s
`\note[id=n1]{Corresponding author}`, :1371-1395), which the class stores by its `id` for `\printartnotes` to print
under the title block's rule (:999-1002 `\auto@set@thanksbox`, :1406-1409, :1440-1447), a note
`\lx@add@contact[role=note,label={note:id}]` as elsart_support_core's `\fntext[label]` is, and the author's `noteref`
ids (and `thanksref`'s, whose alias `noteref` is, :1131-1143) requests of `note:id` among its `annotations`; `{fmbox}`
only holds them, its "Full list of author information …" line (:1002) a print flourish. (78m r1 kept `{artnotes}` to the
class, whose printer the empty `\bmc@endfmbox` never ran, so the notes were dropped silently: 1507.06515's
"Corresponding author", 2007.00437's "Second corresponding author: kcsamir@gmail.com", 2112.10068's "Equal contributor"
of two authors, which the PDF prints.) The class's `corref` key (its "Correspondence:" line, :1463-1467) keeps the
class's own printing, the e-mail it names an `email` contact already. bmcart.cls is on `author_files::AUTHOR_FILES`.
Repro sectioning-frontmatter/bmcart_copy (a stand-in bmcart.cls written from scratch); guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78m::bmcart_frontmatter_is_frontmatter`.

### 881. A note written inside an author's mark is taken out after it

latex.ltx:17215 `\thanks` (and `\footnote`, `\footnotemark`) inside a superscript prints its own mark there and its text
as a footnote, so `Nataliia Babina\textsuperscript{\rm 1,\rm 2\thanks{Work done during internship at Integral AI.}}` is
"Nataliia Babina1,2∗" with a note (2512.05464). Perl's `\lx@author@withsup` (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:729-734) lets
`\textsuperscript` and `^` be the annotation request, which reads the whole operand as its label, so the label
`2\thanks{…}` answered nothing and printed nothing: the mark `2` and the note were lost, in Perl and ours alike
(KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1136). Ours (78u): `notes_out_of_marks` (author_block/preprocess.rs, first in
`add_authors_calls_sectioned`) takes every note command a mark's braced operand holds, at any depth (`^{\mathbf{1,
\thanks{…}}}`), with its arguments, out after the mark — `\textsuperscript{\rm 1,\rm 2}\thanks{…}` — so the mark's
labels are read as labels and the note is the author's, as one written after the mark; a macro of optional arguments
only whose expansion holds a note command is taken out with its `[…]` the same way (`split_mark_notes`, `makes_a_note`:
the AAAI stub `\equalcontrib`, 2603.17529; a document's `\newcommand*\samethanks[1][\value{footnote}]{\footnotemark[#1]}`,
2309.12862), while a macro of no arguments that prints a label beside a note (`\newcommand\fnA{2\footnotemark}`) is read
with its body in its place, the "2" a label (`prints_beside_a_note`, 78v) — only when its body holds no conditional and,
its notes out, only label-safe tokens (characters, font switches, spaces, a `\protect` right before a note command,
another such macro); any other falls back to being taken out whole, so what its body does beside the note stays TeX's
(`\fnD{\thanks{D note}\unskip}` "Di Delta3" and the note, `\fnE{\ifshow\footnotemark\fi}` under `\showfalse` "Ed Eps4"
and no mark, `\fnF[1][x]{6\footnotemark}`, whose "6" stays in the name text as before: 78v r2, review rev78v finding 1;
a `\relax` or another `\protect` beside the label, `{\relax 5\footnotemark}`, `{\protect 5\footnotemark}`, a
`\DeclareRobustCommand`'s `\protect\fnS␣`, which the label would keep and no list answers, and so one written after a
`\protect`, `\textsuperscript{\protect\fnA}`, its "5"/"2" in the name text as before: 78v r3, review rev78v2 finding 1),
and a `\protect` right before a note command goes out with it (`\textsuperscript{1\protect\thanks{…}}` kept the label
`1\protect`, 78v; guard `perfect_kernel_batch78v::author_protect_thanks_and_note_macro_inside_a_mark`); a mark holding nothing else goes
(`$^{\thanks{Topical Group Conveners}}$`, 2212.00809). The mark readers (`\lx@sup@request@affiliation`,
`\lx@sup@setlabel@affiliation`) read a note left in an operand after the mark all the same
(`frontmatter_sup_operand_and_notes`), for a binding that wraps a line in `\lx@author@withsup` itself. The note mark is
printed after the mark rather than inside it (the size of the mark only). Residual (order): a label no list answers is
shown by `show_unanswered_marks` at the end of the name, so a `\footnotemark` taken out of `$^{1 \footnotemark[1]}$`
precedes it ("Ann Alpha∗1", pdflatex "Ann Alpha1∗"; 2403.04164, 2203.10085); the same holds today for
`Ann$^{1}$\footnotemark[1]` written so (the census: 223 mark-then-`\footnotemark` adjacencies in 135 papers, 23 the
other way in 15). Census (`census/pops/pop78u_1.tsv`: every census paper with a note command, or a macro making one,
inside a name block's `\textsuperscript{…}`/`^{…}`; 32 papers): A/B release int59a vs 78u, XML changed in 28, every one
a regained note or mark (notes 76 → 110, words +332), E/F/W equal; the other 4 are a false hit (2503.05186's
`\corresponding` is a symbol), a block whose note was kept already (2604.18459, authblk), one with no creator either way
(2012.01602) and 2211.09622, whose main file the harness missed (its `main.tex` by hand: "corresponding author"
regained). PDF (arXiv) checked for 16: 2512.05464, 1911.03118, 1912.00833, 2306.17472, 2309.12862, 2403.04164,
2410.12564, 2502.15412, 2503.05905, 2402.13113, 1310.0294, 2211.09622, 2402.18447, 2501.01423, 2605.17958, 2603.17529 —
notes present, marks as printed; unchanged residuals there: a symbol inside a mark (`\textsuperscript{\rm 1,2,$^{*}$}`,

### 894. An author block's tabular juggle is the line break it prints (Perl: digested, a tabular left open)

LaTeX sets `\author` inside the title page's own tabular (article.cls `\@maketitle`, sig-alternate.cls), so a class or
template macro that closes it and opens another — the ACM SIG template's
`\def\sharedaffiliation{\end{tabular}\begin{tabular}{c}}`, set between the names and their shared affiliation; the
class's own `\alignauthor` juggles the same way — breaks the block into columns. LaTeXML digests the author outside any
tabular: the juggle closed a tabular nothing opened ("Attempt to close a group that switched to mode
restricted_horizontal") and left one open, whose lines — the affiliation — were lost, and the item's unclosed group
kept its `\label` binding for the rest of the document (every reference dangling; the group itself now closes with
the item, queue_digest.rs `digest_in_own_group`, a Rust-only fix as Perl's `egroup` runs after the item's errors).
Ours (frontmatter/fallback.rs `tabular_juggles_as_line_breaks`): a parameterless macro of the author block whose
expansion begins `\end{tabular}` is read as the `\\` it prints, so the names and the affiliation split as lines; the
author separators (`\alignauthor`) stay for the splitter. Witnesses 1704.03168, 1301.5612, 1401.6981, 0712.1016
(sig-alternate; 21 census papers write `\sharedaffiliation`). Repros sectioning-frontmatter/author_shared_affiliation_line,
sectioning-frontmatter/author_group_left_open_keeps_labels; guards `perfect_kernel_batch79l`.

*Live rule: OD #459.*

### 897. Names parted by horizontal space alone are separate creators (Perl: one author holds them)

pdflatex sets names apart that an author line separates only by horizontal space: a wide space (`\quad`, `\qquad`, a
group of them `{\quad}`, `\hspace{…}`, `\hskip`/`\kern` a length of 4pt or more, `\enspace`, `\enskip`, `\hfill`),
marked names or not, or a name's marks or notes followed by any space (` `, `\ `, `\:`, `\,`, `\;`, `~`, a line
ending in `\`). Perl's `SplitTokens` splits at commas and "and" only, so one creator held them all — or, where the
classifier read the run as a continuation, the names after the first were lost: 2207.06953 kept 2 of its 7 authors,
2411.14257 1 of 4, 2406.12338 1 of 5 (`\thanks{…} {Carla Schenker,}` — each note leads its name), 2604.17501 lost
Ruiyao Xu and Mihir Parmar. Ours: `space_parted_names` (author_block/space_parted.rs) writes each such space as the
comma the split reads, at the line's top level, outside `$…$` and `\(…\)` math, after a name letter, and only where
every piece then reads as a name or qualifies one and two or more read as names (`name_count`): `John Smith\quad Bell
Labs` and `Mc\kern1pt Donald` stay as written, a narrow space with no mark before it parts nothing (`Florian P.\
Busch`, 2212.12575; ecai's `Ann Able \ Bob Baker`, #52(o)'s 77n r2 negative), and a run of two or more narrow spaces
stays #52(o)'s. In a line whose marks lead its names, a space parts two names before the next name's marks
(`$^{1}$Ann Able \: $^{2}$Bob Baker`) or a wide space before a name. A brace group of spacing with a `\quad` in it is
that spacing (`spacing_math_unwrapped`: `Byeongjun Park$^{1}${\quad} Byung-Hoon Kim…`, 2609.03563); a names line
continued after a wide space on its first name's printed line is more names (`space_parts_names`: `\textbf{Ruiyao
Xu}$^{\star}$ \quad \textbf{Mihir Parmar}…`, 2604.17501; 2212.12575). Witnesses 2406.07115 (`\:`), 2609.32353
(`\thanks{…} \ `), 2310.15398 (`\textsuperscript{2} \,`), 2609.03563, 2212.12575, 1909.09562 (llncs `\kern1em`),
2312.06613 (inside `\normalsize{…}`), 2207.06953, 2102.12470, 2002.09131, 2411.14257, 2308.08563 (`$^{1,2,*}$ Defu
Lian`), 0811.3255 and 1311.0077 (aastex `\altaffilmark`), 0806.3855 (A&A `\inst{1}\fnmsep\thanks{…}`), 2406.12338,
1911.02873 (jfm `\ns`: before 84a one creator and an `Error:frontmatter:merged_creators`, now three creators and no
Error). Repros `sectioning-frontmatter/author_{mark_then_space_separates_names, wide_space_after_marked_name_separates,
braced_quad_separates_names, kern_separates_names, wide_space_inside_wrapper_separates,
aastex_mark_then_space_separates, prefix_marks_then_space_separate_names, prefix_notes_then_space_separate_names,
space_inside_a_name_stays}`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch84a::*`, `perfect_kernel_batch77d::
names_parted_only_by_marks_are_split`, `perfect_kernel_batchfms2b::a_mark_in_paren_math_is_cut_whole` (a mark's space
inside `\( ^{1} \)` parts nothing). A comma set in no width before a name's marks, `\rlap,`/`\llap,`, is written as
the comma it prints where the line is cut: kept, the marks the split moves before a glued comma became `\rlap`'s
argument (hep-ph0411288's ptptex `Tatsuo~{\sc Kobayashi}\rlap,${}^{1,}$\footnote{…}`: 6 math Errors in 84a r1; int111d
had given each author the next one's mark and note) — repro `author_lapped_comma_before_marks`, guard
`perfect_kernel_batch84a::author_lapped_comma_before_marks`. A group holding only marks is the name's marks
(`Jia-Bin Huang{$^{2}$} ~ David W. Jacobs{$^{2}$}`, 2406.09417; repro and guard
`author_grouped_marks_then_space_separate_names`).

**107b (census138 row 3, MERGED): wrappers are transparent, one rule per separator; the detector reads lines.**
Perl's `SplitTokens` passes over groups, and our splitters stopped at a wrapper's edge in the ways below; each such
block was one creator holding every name (Perl the same, silently). Each rule is general, no class named:
- *A wrapper around the block's lines is each line's* (`wrapper_over_lines_as_lines`, author_block/separators.rs, in
  `add_authors_calls`' `lines_prepared` after the alignment unwrapping): a text font command, a group or an
  environment of declarations, or a `\parbox` (its declarations kept on each line, its paragraph layout and the box
  dropped, as `names_in_wrapper` reads a box around names), opening and ending its line and holding a top-level `\\`
  or a `center`/`flushleft`/`flushright` paragraph (its own line), is written as one wrapper per line joined by `\\`;
  a wrapper inside a wrapped line is unwrapped too, its style added; a line of spacing only is dropped. Witnesses
  2311.03613 (mnras `\parbox{\textwidth}{\Large A,$^{1,2}$ … \begin{center} (DES Collaboration) \end{center}}
  \vspace{0.4cm}\\ \parbox{…}{$^{1}$…\\…}`: 1 → 55 creators), 1202.2048 (elsarticle `\begin{small} names \\ (BESIII
  Collaboration)\\ {\it $^{1}$ … \\ …}\end{small}`: 1 → 340 creators, round 2), 2306.04870
  (aastex `\textsc{A$^{1,2}$⏎B$^{3}$, … \\ (The KMTNet Collaboration)\\}`: 1 → 20), 2306.04988 (a `\parbox` of
  `\quad`-parted names over a `\\`: "Botian Shi <break/>Chiyu Wang" parted). An article `\author{Ann Able \\
  University of Alpha}` and its `\parbox` form stay one author and her affiliation (R12). A font command around both
  lines (`\textbf{A \\ Univ}`) is invalid in article's tabular `\@author` (pdflatex errs) but reads the same.
  **107g:** only over lines of names or marked entries (`wrapper_holds_names_or_marks`): under the block's first line a
  wrapper is transparent where it holds a mark or a line of names horizontal space parts; over plain lines it stays one
  entry, as the base read it (`{\small Department of Mathematics,\\ Central University,\\ …}`: 2404.17162, 2405.20895,
  2106.11727, astro-ph0412305, 0902.2761, 2509.02924, 2608.04869, and 2010.09850's two institutes in one `\parbox`, the same
  shape, words equal, one affiliation as on base). The wrapper opening the block keeps 107b's reading. The cost of the
  unwrapped reading (`Dept,\\ Univ,\\ City` cut at each line, the base's too) stays. Guards
  `perfect_kernel_batch107g::a_wrapper_over_plain_lines_stays_one_entry` (repros `author_wrapper_over_plain_lines_stays_one_entry`,
  `author_group_over_plain_lines_stays_one_entry`, `author_group_legend_line_is_a_note_as_unwrapped`: a `{*Corresponding
  author}` in a group a note, as unwrapped, once the wrapper beside it is one entry).
- *A wrapper whose name ends in its marks ends where they do* (`space_parted_names`, `wrapped_name_marks_end`):
  `\textbf{Youngho Cho\textsuperscript{1}} \⏎\textbf{Junho Kim\textsuperscript{1}}` parts as the marks and space
  after a bare name do (2608.29120: 5 → 9 creators; "Dan Dee Eve Eden Fay Fox" one creator and the last name lost
  before).
- *IEEE's dotless grades qualify the name before them* (`NAME_GRADE_ABBREVIATIONS`: `SM`, `M`, `F`, `LM`, `LSM`,
  `LF`, `GSM`, `S` glued to a society, `SMIEEE`, `FIEEE`): 1906.01719's `\IEEEauthorblockN{Krishan K. Tiwari$^1$,
  \textit{SMIEEE}, Eckhard Grass$^{1,2}$, …}` reads as four names, each grade its author's membership contact (#967).
- *A surname that is an institution's word after an initial is a marked name* (`marked_names`,
  `surname_after_initial`): `Gary P. Centers,$^{1}$` in revtex4-1's one-call list (1901.10843: 1 → 12 creators);
  only in a list by its marks, the last word after a capital initial, no other institution word (`W. M. Keck
  Observatory` stays an institution; `St.`/`Mt.`/`Ft.` are no initials).
- *authblk's "and" test sees through a group or font command around the whole list* (authblk_sty.rs
  `has_top_level_and_word`): `{A\textsuperscript{a}\thanks{…} ~and B\textsuperscript{a}}` (2506.23337: 1 → 2).
- *A sole `\input{file}` argument is read as the file's content* (`expand_sole_author_macro`'s `sole_input_file`, a
  file mouth, as `\input` reads it), unless the file changes how it is read (`\catcode`, `\makeatletter`,
  `\endinput`, a further `\input`/`\include`): 2609.38746 `\author{\input{author_grid.tex}}` 1 → 7.
- *The detector reads each printed line alone* (`flag_merged_creators`, name_text.rs `personname_text`'s
  `PERSONNAME_LINE_BREAK` at a `<ltx:break/>` and a paragraph's or box's edge): a line of two or more names is a
  merge, and so are two or more lines each of names and nothing else, none a mixed-case line holding an acronym
  (`holds_mixed_case_acronym`: `Vage Egiazarian <break/>IST Austria`, 2504.20039, is a name over its institution); a
  line naming no one (a collaboration's, the affiliations') no longer hides the names beside it. The 3 silent census witnesses (2311.03613, 2609.38746,
  2306.04988) and 2401.12049 read so; a block kept whole in a tabular or a minipage (the Perl fallback,
  Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:693) is still not read. A `\shortstack{Ann Able\\ Bob Baker}` is flagged, and so is a
  refused `\input` file's names line.

**107b round 2 (review rev107b).**
- *A line of names horizontal space alone parts is a names line, never an affiliation of the name above it*
  (`space_parted_rows_joined`, author_block/space_parted.rs, at the head of the unmarked reader; `space_parted_name_line`
  reads the line at its top level or inside one wrapper over the whole line, a font command or a group): the unmarked
  reader parts a block's groups at `\and` and `\quad` before its lines, so `Ann Able \quad Bob Baker\\ Cat Cole \quad
  Dan Dee` gave Bob Baker the affiliation "Cat Cole" (pre-existing at the top level; introduced in a `\parbox` by the
  wrapper reading above). Such a line's line break is written as the space between two names (`\quad`) after the
  names line — the block's first line, one an `\and` opens, or such a line — and as an `\and` after a line under the
  names, the next group's names (1203.0321: `F. Inti Pelupessy\hspace{0.5cm}Simon Portegies Zwart` and `Michael
  Kliphuis\hspace{0.5cm}Henk A. Dijkstra` under the rows' institutions had been welded into them, 7 → 9 creators,
  each its institution and e-mail). A comma list stays the comma rules' (`names_continue`: 1901.10843's lines keep their
  printed commas), and a line holding an institution word parts nothing, so R12's unmarked line under one name stays
  its affiliation (a name-shaped institution row, `Carnegie Mellon \quad Johns Hopkins`, still parts: RED
  `author_row_of_name_shaped_institutions_red`, review rev107b2 F1, synthetic only — base already made its second
  piece a creator). The marked reader takes such a line under a names line as more names (2507.19054's `\\ \textbf{Ludwig
  Schmidt \quad Serena Yeung-Levy} \\`: 4 → 6 creators, the merge Error gone).
- *A space before a tie is a tie* (the observer's lexer, `Lexer::ties_the_gap`; the walk's `Atom::Space` carries the
  one word-space or tie character it prints): an interword space and a tie beside it are one word space of a name,
  not a gap of two. 1202.2048's `Lei~Li$^{1}$, N.~B. ~Li$^{22}$` read "N. B." as initials after "Lei Li," and the two
  one name written surname first, so the writer declined the whole block and its sub-lettered marks with it
  (`$^{18a}$`: the sub-lettered names had no institute 18). **107g:** only inside one name (`Lexer::run_awaits_its_name`:
  one word so far, or words ending in an initial); after a whole name a tie and a space are a gap of two, the gap between
  two names (1805.06045's `Alexander Gasnikov~\IEEEmembership{}⏎ Nikolay Malkovsky~…` one creator on int139a; `Ann Able
  ~Bob Baker`). Guard `perfect_kernel_batch107g::a_tie_and_a_space_are_one_word_space_only_inside_a_name`. **Known residual:** a sub-lettered mark the writer answers
  stays shown on the name (`E. Boger18a`; 2007.02542's `D. Four 23A`), against FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 "a name's label is
  the name alone" (rank 93) and the other names of the same block, whose answered marks are not shown — pinned as is by
  `besiii_creators` and batch98e until fixed (review rev107b2 F3).
- *A legend line never becomes a personname* (`marker_leads` reads through every wrapper that opens the line and
  holds a mark): `{\small{\it \vspace{0.2cm} $^{a}$ also at …}}`, a legend line once `wrapper_over_lines_as_lines`
  gives each line its wrappers, read past one wrapper only, had the spacing's letters before its mark and was an
  author. And a creator whose name reads as a line under the names — lower case first (no particle, no article: `the
  ATLAS Collaboration` is an author), an institution word, no address, no name, no group's name (SBX1: a collaboration
  or a team named in lower case, `sPHENIX Collaboration` 2606.17184, `openJiuwen Team` 2605.10052, by
  `reads_as_collaboration`; whom the authors speak for, `for the PAROS Clinical Research Network` 2605.24212: a
  `SPEAKS_FOR` prefix, then a group's name the same reading does not flag — `for correspondence: Physics Department` is
  flagged) — is a `frontmatter:creator_not_a_name` Error (`flag_merged_creators`), never silent (1309.4007's
  creator "e-mail").
  1202.2048: 342 → 340 creators, every one named, each sub-lettered name its institute and its legend.
- `perfect_kernel_batch94a::an_entry_of_several_pieces_is_written_whole` re-pinned: `and~ Bob Baker` is parted by the
  word "and" (`sep:word`), its tie and space one word space, no longer a gap (`sep:gap`); the XML is the same.
- The merge Error counted by a personname's lines, each one name, says so: "holds N lines that each read as a name:
  "Bob Baker / Carnegie Mellon"; the names a line break parts, or a name and the line under it (its affiliation),
  were not told apart" (a name welded to an unmarked line no institution word marks).
- `sole_input_file` decodes the file as a mouth does (`mouth::decode_input_bytes`: a Latin-1 line as its bytes) and
  matches its refusing commands whole (`\inputencoding`, `\includegraphics` are none of them).

### 898. eptcs.cls: `\institute` and `\email` inside `\author` are each a line under the names (Perl: no binding)

eptcs.cls (Electronic Proceedings in Theoretical Computer Science; v1.5-v1.7, shipped with each paper, not in TeX Live)
sets `\@author` in a centred `tabular` (eptcs.cls:160-180, `\and` the article class's), and defines `\institute{#1}`
as `\\` and a one-column `tabular` of #1 and `\email{#1}` as `\\{\footnotesize\tt #1}` (:186-191), written inside
`\author` after the names. Read raw as the kernel's author line, the institute and the e-mail stayed in the name
("Ilaria De Crescenzo Università degli Studi di Salerno Dipartimento di Informatica", 1408.5969): the frontmatter
scorer found every one of its 6 sample papers wrong, and 18 of the census's 73 eptcs papers change. Ours: a contrib
binding (`latexml_contrib/src/eptcs_cls.rs`) reads the shipped class raw and reads `\author` as the class prints it —
each `\and` cell a row of names (`Tobias Grubenmann and Jens Lehmann`, 2109.08295), every institute under the row
each name's affiliation (FIDELITY_CHARTER R12), an e-mail line the author it spells, else, a list of one address per
name, the name at its place, else the row's only author, else the block's (§4; since Z18k the reading places each line,
the binding writing the block as printed to `\lx@add@author@split`: #991). A cell that opens with a `tabular` of names (1407.7928) or with an environment of the
paper's own that opens one (2409.15014's `{authors}{5}`) is read by its columns: a column's names its cell, a full
row's cell a line under its column, any other line every name's. A block with no `\institute`, `\email` or leading
table is the kernel's. Open: an institute or e-mail block labelled by marks (`$^{1}$ Quantinuum … \\ $^{2}$
Informatics Institute …`, `\email{$^{a, b}$ \{…\}@quantinuum.com, $^{c}$ …}`, 2304.02524) goes whole to every
name, not by its labels. Repros `class-bindings/eptcs/eptcs_{institute_email_cells, row_of_names, author_tabular,
author_environment_columns}` (beside a stand-in `eptcs.cls` written from scratch); guards `perfect_kernel_batch84b::*`.

### 899. lmcs.cls: an author's letters request the addresses they label; `\lmcsorcid` is the author's ORCID (Perl: no binding)

lmcs.cls (Logical Methods in Computer Science; shipped with each paper, not in TeX Live; the contrib binding
`latexml_contrib/src/lmcs_cls.rs` loads amsart under it) prints `\author[short]{Name}[a,b]` with the letters raised
after the name and the addresses as one list after all names, each led by the next letter, a, b, c, … (2306.08266's
v0.92 copy, lmcs.cls:391-450); the earlier classes' papers write the letters themselves, `Name\rsuper a` and
`\address{{\lsuper a}Univ}` (1103.0510's LMCS.cls v0.8, cs0701140, 1202.6352). The binding read neither: every address
went to the last author, the letters were left as a paragraph of their own, an ORCID was "ORCID:0000-…" inside the name
(the frontmatter scorer's 2 of 2 lmcs sample papers), and `\lmcsheading` read four of its seven arguments, leaving the
submission and publication dates in the first paragraph. Ours: a name's letters (`[a,b]`, `\rsuper{a,b}`) are `\inst`
requests, llncs's; an address is labelled by the letters written before it, else, in a paper whose names carry
letters, by its place in the list, and an address with several letters (`{\lsuper{b,c}}`, 1202.6352) is each one's;
an address of spacing alone (`\address{\vskip-6 pt}`) is none; a paper whose names carry no letters keeps amsart's
reading, an address the run of authors' it follows (2108.06944, 2402.11987); each address of an `\email` list goes to
the author it spells, else the one its address's letter names, else the group's author (2402.09138's one `\email`
of three addresses); `\lmcsorcid` in a name is the author's ORCID contact; `\lmcsheading`'s fifth and sixth
arguments are the paper's submitted and published dates; `\subjclass` is named as the paper's class names it (2012
ACM CCS, the earlier classes' 1998 ACM Subject Classification). Shared change: `sequenced_contact_labels`
(frontmatter/place.rs) counts an `address` contact as it counts an `affiliation`, so an e-mail under a lettered
`\address` is placed by its letter. Repros `class-bindings/lmcs_{lettered_addresses, unlettered_addresses,
written_letters}`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch84c::*`.

### 900. An unmarked author block's next name line under the lines of the name above starts the next author (Perl: the first author holds every line)

A hand-formatted `\author{…}` in the article class often lists its authors as blocks of lines: a name line, its
address lines, then the next name line (`\author{Laura Rebollo-Neira\\ Mathematics Department\\ Aston University\\ B3
7ET, Birmingham, UK\\ \vspace{0.1cm}\\ A. Plastino\\ IFLP-CCT-Conicet\\ …}`, 1702.01413), which pdflatex prints as one
centred column of author blocks. Perl's no-marker branch reads the first `\\` piece of each `@authorsplits` part as
the names and the rest as their affiliations (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:720-725; its parts are cut at every comma and
"and" too, so the column falls into creators named by address fragments, "Birmingham", "UK"), and ours kept the
first-line rule, so every later name was an affiliation contact of the first author — silently: the frontmatter
scorer's largest missing-author shape (9 of the 18 missing authors on int114a). Ours (`opens_next_author`,
author_block/name_text.rs, a rule of `name_groups`): after the lines under a name, a line that reads as a name and
nothing else (`reads_as_name_alone`: every part a name, `name_count`, a trailing address aside, `\name … \email …`; no
word of a title-case common-noun phrase, `NON_PERSON_WORDS` — roles, titles, fields of study, facilities, documents:
`Chief Scientist`, `Associate Dean`, `Mathematical Sciences`, `James Clerk Maxwell Building`, `Technical Report`; no
note, no leading mark, no e-mail or link line), not going on with the line above (that line ending in a connective,
`School of Physical and \\ Mathematical Sciences`, or the line opening with one), starts the next author when
- a line that prints nothing stands before it (`\\ \vspace{0.1cm}\\`, `\\ \\`, `$ $\\`; the dispatch hands
  `name_groups` a gap flag per line), or a positive `\\[len]` does — pdflatex prints the same gap, so
  `strip_linebreak_options_keeping_gaps` writes it `\\ \\` at the block's top level, outside environments, but not
  after a row of names (`\\[0.2em]` rows, 2605.24414), nor in the whole-block tabular/minipage fallback, whose
  content keeps its line breaks as written (1901.06146); a gap before every line under the names line, the first line
  break's included, or before every line from the second under it on, or at every line break of the block down to the
  candidate, is the block's spacing, no gap (`Ann Able \\[2pt] University of X \\[2pt] Hong Kong`; `\\ University of X \\[2pt]
  Santa Barbara \\[2pt] California`; `\\[3pt] University of X \\[3pt] Santa Barbara \\ California`; lengths are not
  compared, so a wider gap among narrower ones parts no authors, nor does a name set as that place is: RED
  `author_block_uniform_gaps_hide_a_wider_gap`); and a gap-opened last line of the block needs a person's cue (`\\
  \\ Hong Kong`, `\\[12pt] Hong Kong` stay lines);
- it is styled as the names over it in markup of its own the line above is not (`{\bf Anne Schilling}` under `{\em
  …}`, 1509.03383; `\name Mohammad Rostami` under `\addr …`, 2408.11742), or, with a line under it, plain as they
  are under a line set in a style group of its own (`Eddie Monroe` under `{\it Institute of Noetic Sciences …}`,
  1709.07791; not a closing `\textit{University of X} \\ Costa Rica`);
- the line under it is an e-mail address its names spell, a line styled as the block's styled affiliation lines
  (`David Hanson \\ {\it Hanson Robotics}`, 1709.07791), or an institution of its own under a person's name
  (`person_over_institution`): an institution that does not go on with the line (`continues_the_line`: a connective
  opening it, every word of the line again, or its words before the first comma one generic institution noun and the
  adjectives before it, `INSTITUTION_ADJECTIVES` — `Johns Hopkins \\ University, Baltimore`, `Los Alamos \\ National
  Laboratory`, `San Diego \\ State University`), under a name carrying a person's cue, an initial or a particle
  (`Palash B. Pal \\ Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics`, gr-qc9906006; `James M. Robins \\ Department of …`,
  1908.10448). Two capitalized words alone over an institution are as often a place, an institution's name or a role
  (`Santa Barbara \\ Kavli Institute …`, `Max Planck \\ Institute for …`, `Associate Dean \\ School of Medicine`), so
  with no gap and no styling a cue-less name stays a line.
With no gap, a name styled as the line above it that itself reads as a name is a stacked run of names, whose lines
below are the run's: its last name does not take them alone by position (1702.07694's `\name Stephen N. Pallone
\email … \\ \name Peter I. Frazier \email … \\ \name Shane G. Henderson \email … \\\\ \addr …`). After a gap, no
line opens the next author when every line between the names line and it reads as names — a name, or a row of them
(each piece of `split_author_line` a name) — however styled: the gap parts rows of names from the lines they share
(`Ann A. Able \\ Bob B. Baker \\[6pt] Cat C. Cole \\ Institute of Y, Z`; `\textbf{6 names} \\ \textbf{5
names\thanks{…}} \\ \\ CUHK MMLab \\ \texttt{…}`, 2604.18394, the lab no creator); otherwise a gap parts the
authors whatever the line above reads as (`Comunidad de Palo Blanco, Salamanca Gto. México.\\ \\ V.I. Tkach`,
0801.1297). A line that opens the next author — by this rule or by #52's alternation, note or "and" rules — is a names
line: a row of names on it parted by a run of spacing is parted as the block's first names line is (#52(o), then
`space_parted_names`: `\\ \\ Bob Baker~~~~Cat Cole \\ Univ B`, two creators). A name-shaped line with none of these
stays a line (`Hanson Robotics` over a name, `Hong Kong` over `The Hong Kong University …`, a closing `Costa Rica`),
as does a name directly under names (Perl's reading). The "and"-led opening of #52's math-ph0303018 rule skips a field
of study the same way (`\\and Computer Engineering`, 2510.15190). And a block a line break opens after names only
horizontal space parts it from (the JASA template's `Name\thanks{…}\hspace{.2cm}\\`), names with no lines of their
own, is those names' lines when its first line is an institution: the names line and the block's lines are one
group's, which `name_groups` parts as any — its first group's lines are the names', its later groups the next
authors' (an "and" line opening one and dropped, a gap, the names' styling, a note, an institution under a person's
name: `Assaf P. Oron\hspace{.2cm}\\ Children's Core …\\ and \\ Nancy Flournoy \\ …`, 1701.05964; 2004.03971's Han
Lin Shang; 2503.11250's `\\[5pt]` gaps; 1504.05438's "and" line; `Lin Liu \hspace{.2cm} \\ Institute of Natural
Sciences, School of Mathematical Sciences, MOE-LSC \\ …`, 1908.10448: before, three creators named by the
institution's parts). Residuals, each a RED repro: a cue-less person's name over an institution with no gap or
styling stays a line (1908.10448's `Zach Shahn \\ IBM Research,`; `article_plain_name_line_between_affiliations`), and
so does a row of names (`author_block_row_of_names_with_no_signal`, SYNC row 121); the names of a stacked run stay
lines of its first name (1702.07694; deferred; `author_block_stacked_names_each_a_creator`); an eponym or a place with
a particle over an institution reads as a person (`L.D. Landau \\ Institute for Theoretical Physics`, `Rio de Janeiro
\\ Centro …`; `author_block_eponym_or_place_over_institution`); a cued name under a place that reads as a name, or
over an institution whose head noun leads it (`Bob B. Baker \\ Imperial College, London`), stays a line
(`author_block_next_name_under_a_place_or_whole_institution`); a wider gap among uniform ones parts no authors
(`author_block_uniform_gaps_hide_a_wider_gap`); a name line carrying a note or an address after a wide space stays a
line (`author_block_name_line_with_trailing_text`, int114a's reading); an organisation's name after a gap, with a
line under it, opens an author as a name does (`University of X \\ \\ Google DeepMind \\ London, UK`; only words
tell them apart; `author_block_organisation_after_a_gap`). (A block opening with a line that prints only `\ ` read
it as an empty names line, and `coalesce_empty_creators` appended its lines after the next creator's own —
solv-int9710025, `author_block_leading_spacer_line` — GREEN since 98b, #949.) Witnesses 1702.01413, 0801.1297, 1608.08479,
2201.06821, 1509.03383, 1709.07791, 1908.10448, 2408.11742, gr-qc9906006 (its repro red since 64w), 1702.07694,
1701.05964, 2004.03971, 2503.11250, 1504.05438, 2604.18394, 1901.06146. Repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/author_block_{next_name_after_a_spacer_line, next_name_under_its_institution,
next_name_styled_as_the_names, name_and_address_lines_styled_alike, lines_that_read_as_names_stay_lines,
stacked_names_keep_their_lines, row_of_names_opens_the_next_author, lines_after_spaced_names}` (GREEN, guarded; the
two stacked-run guards assert a name under names only where today's reading and the right one agree); catalog repros
without a guard, near-duplicates of a guarded path: `article_author_block_second_author_after_spaced_break`
(gr-qc9906006: its gap and its cue are guarded apart), `author_block_{institution_split_across_lines,
places_and_roles_under_an_institution, next_name_after_a_gap_under_a_place, linebreak_length_gaps, marked_block_gaps,
rows_of_names_share_their_lines}`; and the RED ones above; guards `perfect_kernel_batch85a::*`,
`author_split_tests::{institution_head_continues_the_line_above, person_over_institution_needs_a_persons_cue,
linebreak_option_gap_kept_between_lines}`.

*Live rule: OD #459.*

### 901. llncs's one `\institute` is every author's, its e-mail lines by their owners (Perl: on the first author)

llncs.cls:868-886 prints a sole institute (no `\and` in `\institute`, `\c@@inst=1`) unnumbered under the whole author
row; `\inst{n}` (:894) numbers each author's when there are several. Perl numbers the sole institute `affiliation:1`
(llncs.cls.ltxml:46-49), which no author requests without `\inst{1}`, and its prefix-stripped fallback strands it on
the first author (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1195); #159 had kept it once on a nameless creator under the names, so no author
had an affiliation (20 of the frontmatter scorer's 56 llncs sample papers). Ours: the binding queues the sole
institute with `_share=authors` (`\lx@llncs@institute@sole`), and the frontmatter's reading (`Resolver::share_unpicked`,
`answer_shared_emails`, written by the emitter with or without an author block; until P27b the old row split,
`share_row_contacts` in `frontmatter/shared_row.rs`, shaped the queue before digestion) makes it every author's unless it is picked:
only the class's own request picks it, a command requesting a labelled annotation (`\inst{1}`) with a number; a
hand-typed `$^{1}$` (2607.02596), a paper's mark macro (`\affmark{1}`, `\printfnsymbol{1}`: 1804.05870, 2007.07423,
2102.12877, 2403.11865) and llncs's `\fnmsep` are answered by no one and pick nothing (`\inst{*}`, 2207.04574, and an
empty `\inst{}`, 2604.20229, neither). Not shared, as before: an institute holding marks of its own (a superscript, or
a paper macro raising its argument bare, `\textsuperscript{#1}`: 2608.21425's `\affmark{1} City University … \quad
\affmark{2} …`), a shown mark numbering another institute than the first (`Ann Able$^{1,2}$` over `{1} Univ A \\ {2}
Univ B`: several institutes numbered by hand, astro-ph0305539's shape), an empty `\institute{}` (none, 2407.13764).
Shared, the old split had each author's content request `row:shared`, which the contact set as its own label, so it was
digested once and placed on every author as an `\inst`-picked one is.

(The row split this paragraph describes was deleted in P27b, below: `row_email_calls` and `holds_raw_address` are gone,
these lines the reading's and the emitter's entry cut's, `classify/entry_emails.rs`.) Its e-mail lines are lines under the row, taken out of the contact and each decided on its own (`row_email_calls`); the contact's lines are its `\\`/`\newline`/`\par` parts. With several authors, a line
holding an `@` outside the class's `\email` calls — at any depth, a note's too, or in what a command of the paper's
own on it prints (a parameterless macro's body; a `\urldef`'d command's text, which `\urldef` keeps beside it,
url_sty.rs) — is an e-mail line (`holds_raw_address`): `{\tt \{joxan,navas,andrews\}@…}` (1103.2027), `\texttt{…}`,
`\url{{farazi, pallgeuer}@…}` (1809.11127), `\href{mailto:…}{…}` (2408.03209), `\mailsa` (1307.8067; 1408.0384's
`\mailk, \mailt`). The address reader (`email_addresses`) reads it after an `Email:` label (the contact's own name)
or a label of its own (`Corresponding author:`, its first word a contact's, which keeps the line whole), each address
its owner's as a call's are;
a line of a shared institute the reader cannot read is the block's, as written, an affiliation (1708.06860's brace
list cut across two `\urldef`s; `Department of CS: {\tt able@x.edu}`, no label of its own); when that line is the
institute's own first line (`… Hamburg, Germany \mailsa`, 1706.02124; an address in the institute's `\thanks`), the
whole institute is the block's, as written (int114a's placement). Each `\email` call: each address the reader takes goes to the author it spells; else, a list of one address per author that every
spelled address agrees with — an address several names spell agreeing only when the name at its place is one of them
(`lee@` at Cid Cole's place under Ann Lee and Bob Lee is no order), a list of local parts the reader cannot part never
— to the author at its place; else, with one author, to that author; else, the one address left of several authors,
to the one marked as the corresponding author (`marked_corresponding_author`) who owns no other address of the line
(2510.12629's `kgwo0528@` stays the block's beside Jinwoo Kim's `jinwookim@`), unless it is a template's
(`{firstname.lastname}@`, `first.last@`: no one's); else, in a shared institute, to the author
block (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4, `row_address_owners`, the reading of eptcs's rows, #898). A brace list of local parts is each address apart
(`\{saad,saia\}@cs.unm.edu`, 1405.1167); split so, a list no one owns keeps its printed braces
(`{stomforde|bsick}@uni-kassel.de`, 1701.08125). One address in printed braces is that address, set as written
(`\email{\{fatima.iribu@gmail.com\}}` ×3, 2410.04091: one per author, each the author's at its place). A call the
reader cannot part (`{a,b}@x` without printed braces, 2206.10050; 1809.06205, 2607.18577), or parts into pieces no
whole address (`[a@insa-, b@insa-]rouen.fr`, 2609.24668), is the call as written, the block's (user ruling R10), one
author's when there is one; when another call or line is not read, no list is one per author and the others go by
spelling alone. A label of the call's own the rule recognises goes with it, in its piece, the call then unparted
(`call_label`): before the call, one to four words of letters and hyphens ending in a colon, read as printed
(through a font's group, a `~`, a spacing command: `\textit{Corresponding author:}`, `Corresponding~author:`,
`\hspace{1cm}Contact:`), the first a contact's (`names_a_contact`, one vocabulary with the `Email:` label reader
`split_email_label`: corresponding, correspondence, contact, author, e-mail, mail, address), from a later line's start
or after a `,` or `;`, the spacing before it aside (`Corresponding author:`, 2410.06985, 2609.00838; `Contact:`,
2509.05139; `Correspondence to:`, the r4 re-review's q03, q23); after it, a parenthetical of words
(`(Corresponding author)`, 2608.24697). Other text on the call's line stays the institute's, every author's: `… Rouen,
France. \email{…}` (2609.24668), `\hspace{0.5cm}` (2310.06847), text that only ends in a colon (`Department of
Computer Science:`, `Dept. of CS:`, `Lab of A. B. Smith:`: the r3 re-review's n09, n10, n35) — and a label of a form
the rule does not recognise, a residual (prose without a colon, `Corresponding author email \email{…}`; a label word
the rule does not know, `Reach me at: \email{…}`, kept off the block so that n09/n10's department stays the
institute's; a label after a `.` or after other text on its line, `Univ X. Corresponding author: \email{…}`). A
connective between two calls (`\email{a} and \email{b}`, `\&`, `or`: the r4 re-review's q08, q28) is no call
separator and stays the institute's, every author's — a residual. A shared contact's `\email` inside its `\thanks` (no other `@` in it) stays in the
note, given its owner's label in place; as int114a, the address leaves the note's sentence. Every address goes through
`\lx@row@email{label}{address}` (llncs's sets its `\emailname`). An e-mail digested inside a shared contact all the
same (a paper's own `\email` macro) never inherited `row:shared` (the old split's `SHARED_ROW_LABEL` in
`\lx@annotate@frontmatter@now`, deleted at P27b with the only writer of `row:shared`; 2410.04091 byte-identical). So in a shared institute an address the rule reads, and a
label it recognises, is one author's or the block's, never every author's; a shared contact every line of which is
taken is none. An `\inst{1}`-picked institute is its picked authors' as the marks decide, and the block is the
shared path's fail-safe only: a piece leaves it only when it is an address the reader reads and an owner is found for
(the rules above), with the label the rule recognises; everything else stays in it, as written, its picked authors'
(int114a's placement): a line the reader cannot read, first or later (`\institute{Univ X, able@x.edu}`, `Univ X\\
Twitter: @univx`; the r3 re-review's n31-n33, the r4 re-review's q01, q25), the calls on it each read apart
(`\email{able@x.edu}, Twitter: @univx`, q31), a line holding a note (q02), `Department of CS: {\tt able@x.edu}` (q19),
a call or line no address of which an owner is found for (2109.05583's template, 2307.04136, 2609.24668), and the
text between — save decision 3 of 2026-10-22: of a call or line parted by owner (a group written out), an address no
one is found for is the block's, as in a shared institute (2510.12629's `\email{kgwo0528@gmail.com,
jinwookim@kw.ac.kr}`: `jinwookim@` Jinwoo Kim's, `kgwo0528@` the block's); a picked contact every line of which is
taken stays, empty, answering its authors' `\inst{1}` marks. Two residuals of the picked path (the r5 re-review):
the corresponding-author step is not limited to the picked authors, so a "Corresponding author" note on an author with
no mark takes an unspelled address out of the picked institute (s17, RED below); and one address no one spells, alone
in its call under two or more picked authors, stays every picked author's (s01, s16, s19; int114a's placement, while
the same address in a call parted by owner is the block's) — FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 sends an unspelled address to the
block, so it waits on a ruling. A shared institute's line holding a note with an `@` reads the line's own word as the
spelled author's address (`Univ X\\ Visit\footnote{able@x.edu}`: "Visit" Ann's e-mail, s23, RED below; the picked
path keeps the line, q02, v03). Left in the contact, an e-mail would
have inherited the institute's label (Perl Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:497-500): every author's, or with `\inst{1}` every
`\inst{1}` author's (2608.11332's brace list whole on both, arXiv/html_feedback#6881's witness, now each address its
owner's).

The binding also takes an `\institute` written inside `\author` out of the last name (1609.01220): it is the class's
store, run when `\@maketitle` sets the names, before `\institutename` prints it, so it wins over an outer
`\institute` before or after it (`\lx@llncs@inner@institute`; a later `\author` without one gives the store back).
Unchanged: `\inst`-numbered institutes, several institutes without marks (the block's, or Perl's numeric pairing when
as many as the authors; 2207.06953's hand-typed `$^1$` marks still read by no one), the lazy superscript block.
Witnesses 1002.2793, 1307.8067, 1405.1167, 1509.00818, 1609.01220, 1809.11127, 1910.11599, 2011.00616, 2101.06781,
2106.04289, 2205.06740, 2207.04574, 2207.11464, 2306.03360, 2405.11276, 2502.08785, 2511.12796, 2603.26486,
2604.20229, 2402.19043 (#159's); 1804.05870, 2607.02596, 2007.07423, 2102.12877, 2403.11865 (marks no one answers);
2410.04091, 2206.10050, 1701.08125 (e-mail calls); 0712.2737, 1103.2027, 1307.8067, 1405.0417, 1408.0384,
1503.02007, 1504.01099, 1511.00725, 1705.06516, 1706.02124, 1708.06860, 1805.11291, 1809.11127, 2103.08389,
2207.07506, 2407.18381, 2408.03209, 2411.00887, 2504.06600 (address lines outside the calls); 2410.06985,
2609.00838, 2608.24697, 2509.05139 (a call's own label); 2609.24668, 1812.09276, 2310.06847 (the institute's text on
a call's line). Repros `class-bindings/llncs_{sole_institute_is_every_authors,
sole_institute_before_the_authors, institute_inside_author, inst_marks_pick_the_sole_institute,
several_institutes_without_marks_stay_the_blocks, institute_marked_by_a_paper_macro_is_not_shared,
empty_institute_keeps_the_inst_marks, each_email_call_is_decided_alone, single_address_braces_are_each_owners,
address_in_institute_note_is_never_shared, hand_marks_pick_nothing, paper_mark_macro_picks_nothing,
fnmsep_note_in_institute_is_shared, inner_institute_wins, ambiguous_spelling_is_no_place,
listed_local_parts_keep_their_braces, corresponding_author_takes_the_left_address,
inst_picked_brace_list_is_each_owners, email_line_by_place, address_line_is_each_owners,
urldef_address_line_is_each_owners, email_label_goes_with_the_call}` (the r1 review's probe shapes p01-p25, q01-q03,
r01-r05, the r2 re-review's s01-s30;
one guard per distinct path, near-duplicates repros without a guard); RED, not handled: `class-bindings/llncs_hand_marks_with_several_institutes`
(hand-typed marks over `\and`-parted institutes, 2207.06953, deferred) and `llncs_author_line_brace_list_email` (an
author-line `\email{\{a,b\}@x}` split inside its braces, 1609.01220, the author-block e-mail reader) and
`llncs_marked_block_ambiguous_spelling_is_no_place` (the general reader's `addresses_in_order` places an address
several names spell by its place, SYNC_STATUS) and `llncs_unknown_email_label_stays_the_institutes`,
`llncs_connective_between_email_calls` (the two label/connective residuals above) and
`llncs_corresponding_note_does_not_override_inst_marks`, `llncs_shared_note_line_word_is_no_email` (the r5
re-review's s17, s23 above); guards `perfect_kernel_batch85b::*`,
`frontmatter_llncs_institute_shared_email`; the 77t llncs guards carry the `\institute{Inst A}` on every author.

Batch 104d (census129 Bundle 2b): cas-sc/cas-dc declare the same sharing for an unlabelled `\affiliation`/`\address`
under no marked author (cas_dc_cls.rs `cas_labelled_entry`), with a run as well: `_share=authors,annotate=run`.
cas-common.sty prints its entry list under the whole row of names, so the PDF decides one entry and cannot decide
several. **One** such entry in the queue is every author's, before it and after it:
`\author{Ann}\affiliation{organization={Univ A}}\author{Bob}\author{Cat}` prints "Ann, Bob and Cat / Univ A"
(2201.00009, 2511.22218, 2106.02306, 2606.24054; it had been the author's before it, and an entry above every author a
nameless creator's). **Two or more** are each its run's, the authors since the entry before it, read by authoring
order as elsarticle reads an unlabelled `\address` (`annotate=run`, `\lx@els@shared`; main-session decision, review
rev104d B1): the reading counts them across the queue (`Resolver::sole_shared_run`; the old split's
`share_row_contacts` dropped `_share` from every row contact declaring `annotate=run`) when there are several, so `\author{Liu}\address{RC}\author{Sun}\author{Zhang}\address{UCAS}` is Liu's RC, Sun's and Zhang's UCAS
(2202.06096; round 1 had given every author both) and the interleaved `Ann; X; Bob; Y` each author the entry after
it. llncs's and aa's `_share` entries declare no run and are unchanged. Once an `\author[…]` is marked, the marks link
the labelled entries and an unlabelled one stays the author's before it (R1), as elsarticle's own does. Under runs an
author after the last entry has none (`Ann; X; Bob; Y; Cat`: Cat none), and an entry above every author is the
block's, as elsarticle's. On a row's line a space factor's `\@` is a call separator (`is_call_separator`), so `…,
USA;\@ Email: \email{\{alopez3,jmuirhead,cpinciroli\}@wpi.edu}` (2602.18622) is an e-mail line parted by owner, no
longer the block's whole with its label; the e-mail label a row's call or line prints before its addresses (`Email:`,
`E-mails:`, `email_label_before`, `split_email_label`) names each contact made of it, whole or parted
(`\lx@row@email@named`, `name={<label>~}` as `named_email_calls` names an e-mail line's), over the class's own e-mail
name (llncs's never-printed "E-mail "), as the take-out's label word names a cut entry's contacts (OD #944,
`plan::holder_label`; round 1 had named each part "E-mail ", the printed "Email:" lost). And one local part in printed
braces is no list (`links::lists_local_parts`, both engines' spelled step): `\{raffaele.perego\}@isti.cnr.it` spells
Raffaele Perego under an institute three authors carry (2403.13468; it had been the block's). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch104d::{a_cas_unlabelled_affiliation_is_every_authors, cas_unlabelled_affiliations_are_their_runs,
an_llncs_labelled_email_list_on_the_institute_line_is_spelled, an_llncs_lone_braced_address_is_its_spellers}`;
