### 920. A binding's `\author` replaces or stacks as its class's does where the binding owns it; inst_support's keeps stacking (Perl: inst_support's clears on every call; no ptephy or webofc binding)

User 2026-10-30 (review rev92a_r5): every .cls defines `\author` its own way — some stack one call per author, others
take the whole list in one call that a later call replaces — and the frontmatter API serves that diversity through the
binding, each binding's `\author` saying it with the API's primitives (`\lx@clear@creators[role=author]` for a
replacing class, none for a stacking one); never a flag, a convention key, the spelling of the call or `[marks]`.

- **ptephy** (`ptephy_cls.rs`, one binding for the three versions, read off `\@currname`): ptephy.cls:427 replaces
  (`\def\author#1{\gdef\@author{#1}}`, 1412.6580): its kernel author clears; ptephy_v1.cls:485 and ptephy_v2.cls:485
  load authblk-TI, whose `\author` (authblk-TI.sty:70) appends each call: they stack (2311.07297, 1606.03167; ptephy_v2's
  2511.03250, the census's one paper, whose six `\author[1]{R.~Miyata}` calls a test for `ptephy_v1` alone had cut to
  the last — review rev92b_r1 S1). All had stacked through inst_support's `\author`.
- **webofc** (`webofc_cls.rs`): its own `\author` (the `\\` line split) clears: webofc.cls defines none, its
  `\@parseauthor` reads the kernel's `\@author` (:431-466; 1609.01040).
- **inst_support's own `\author` keeps stacking (OD #53), an open question.** Perl's per-call clear
  (inst_support.sty.ltxml:33-35) is right for aa (aa.cls defines no `\author`; pdflatex prints only the last call's
  names — the rev92a_r5 probe `s1_aa_cleared_current` keeps Ann Able) and l-aa, but inst_support's `\author` is also
  OmniBus's, which about 40 class bindings load and every unknown class falls back to. Restoring the clear changed
  162 of 1,305 OmniBus papers with two or more `\author` calls in the 92b A/B: achemso 69 (achemso.cls:336 stacks,
  `\acs@author@cnt`), autart 20, pasj00 12, oup-authoring-template 9, gtpart 7, lipics 5+, ifacconf 4, the AMS `-l`
  classes (conm-p-l, memo-l, tran-l, pspum-l, crmp-l: amsart's stacking `\author`), aomart (stacks, aomart.cls:267),
  ieeetj (ieeetj.cls:4857 stacks); and a `\documentclass{subfiles}` subfile (1210.5518, 2307.07324) or a subfile
  loaded mid-document (1502.05436), whose main class (revtex) stacks, guessed OmniBus. Each binding saying its class's
  `\author`, and aa's binding its replacing one (which moves aa's policy key from `inst_support.sty` to `aa.cls`, the
  gate study's piece 8: landed, OD #922), is the decision this leaves.
- The 16 aa census papers with two `\author` calls in source change nothing either way (their second calls sit in
  comments or conditionals).
- Repros sectioning-frontmatter/`ptephy_author_given_twice_keeps_the_last_red`, `ptephy_v2_author_calls_stack`; class-bindings/
  `webofc_author_given_twice_keeps_the_last` (catalog only: its raw-read class leaves a conditional open, a pre-existing
  Warning), `aa_author_given_twice_keeps_the_last` and `ieeetj_author_calls_stack` (catalog: the open question's
  shapes); guard `perfect_kernel_batch92b::each_class_author_replaces_or_stacks_as_its_class`.

### 922. aa's binding owns a replacing `\author`; a binding's own redefinition after a nested binding's owns the meaning (Perl: inst_support's `\author` clears for aa; no ownership notion)

aa.cls defines no `\author`, so the kernel's `\gdef\@author{#1}` prints only the last call's names. `aa_cls.rs` now
defines its own `\author[]{}` after `aa_support` loads inst_support: `\lx@clear@creators[role=author]`, then
inst_support's split (its `[marks]`, `\and`/`\And`, OD #53) — the class's `\author` said with the API's primitives
(OD #920's rule). inst_support's own `\author` keeps stacking for the classes reaching it through OmniBus.

- **Ownership** (`ledger::note_binding_load`): a load that changed a tracked command (`\author`, `\email`,
  `\emailAdd`) owns it when no binding it loaded did, or when its own code redefined it after one did (the meaning now
  is not the nested owner's and its origin is `Binding`; a raw file's redefinition stays no binding's). aa's blocks
  are keyed `aa.cls` and read by aa's conventions (`email_in_place`, `inst_after_comma`), no longer
  `inst_support.sty`'s, which OmniBus shares (the stage-6 gate study's piece 8).
- Repro class-bindings/`aa_author_given_twice_keeps_the_last` (rev92a_r5 probe `s1_aa_cleared_current`; pdflatex
  with 1707.06238's aa.cls prints "Bob Baker1 and Cid Cole2"; Perl too); guard
  `perfect_kernel_batch92c::aa_author_replaces_and_keys_aa_blocks`. The 16 aa census papers with two `\author` calls
  (pop92b6) change nothing: their second calls sit in comments or conditionals.

### 923. aa and llncs are written by the frontmatter observer (FM stage 7); the writer writes an address group out, an empty call holds nothing back (Perl: the old reader's output, no observer)

`aa_cls.rs` and `llncs_cls.rs` declare `written: true` (their `FRONTMATTER_CONVENTIONS`, as revtex4_support and
ams_support): by default the flush rehearses a paper whose every author block is a written family's, and the writer
(`observer::writer`) rewrites today's creators where they differ from the reading by its operations alone; any other
difference leaves today's output (the fail-safe, unchanged). Three writer changes the two families needed:

- **write out** (`plan::Op::WriteOut`): an e-mail call printing several addresses (`\institute{Univ X\\
  \email{\{a,b,c\}@x.org}}`) that the reading writes out (`ruling3:written-out`, decision 3 of 2026-10-22), today's one
  contact on every carrier of the entry — each address a copy of today's contact printing only it (its text leaf, a
  contact holding only `ltx:text`; one holding a link or a formula is declined), given to its owner, today's removed.
  Witnesses 1811.05243, 1812.02463, 2403.14668, 2501.11467 (95 llncs and 25 aa census papers were held back by it).
  Only a contact printing its addresses alone is written out (`plan::addresses_alone`: with the braced groups taken
  out, every word between `,` `;` and spaces an address): beside a remark or a label (`\{ann,bob\}@a.org
  (corresponding)`, `Emails: \{ann,bob\}@a.org`) the words were lost; such a contact stays today's and the paper is
  declined (review rev92c B2). A domain printed after the group's brace is the group's (`\{bob@mails,
  cid@mail\}.b.edu`, 2407.18899: `.b.edu` had read as a word beside the group, the paper declined and Zijia Lin's
  `linzijia07@` stayed on another carrier; review rev92c r2 B-3). An address of the group its owners hold already from
  another print is not written again.
- an author block skipped as empty (`Outcome::Skipped(Empty)`: llncs's `\and\\`, the empty piece of its split) holds
  no paper back (2409.09478).
- a later placement pass that finds the document reading as the reading keeps the earlier pass's outcome
  (`--streaming` places the frontmatter again at the document's end: it reported `same` after `written`).
- **one item per owner and text** (`plan::wanted`, `owners`): the reading's identical items of one creator (or of the
  block) are one, and so are today's in the comparison — the writer never adds a second copy of an item its owner holds
  (0906.2451's S. K. Mathew had `shibu@prl.res.in` from institute 1 and from `\offprints`, written twice; review rev92c
  S2); a removal takes every copy today's gives an owner the reading does not.
- **print order** (`apply::place`, `prints_after`, `plan::Place`): the items of every owner an operation touches are in
  the reading's order — an item before the first of its owner's items the reading prints after it: a note's item after
  the author block's (`plan::prints_in_note`: a publication note's call, a footnote's text, an `ltx:note` call, a
  contact inside a `\thanks` or `\footnote` — the page prints them below the author block, whatever the call's place:
  aa's `\offprints{O. Kochukhov, \email{oleg@…}}` is called before `\institute`, and ordered by the calls the address
  had gone above the institute on 9 aa papers, 0903.3512, 0902.0930, 1205.5105, 1411.3255, astro-ph0203288,
  astro-ph0509342, astro-ph0512559, astro-ph0608284, astro-ph0702605, and 2212.07438's `\thanks{\email{…}}`; review
  rev92c r2 B-1; a note itself stays at its call's place), then its block or API call's ledger index, then within one its span's start, or, neither spanned, an
  entry's own text before the contacts it holds; a spanned and an unspanned item of one call are not ordered — not
  today's order with the added items at the
  creator's end in the order of their texts (2207.06953's Sangyoun Lee$^{1,2}$ had KIST before Yonsei; 2608.05923's
  S. Mangla and O. M. Smirnov; 1812.02463's Ilyass Haloui his Airbus address after ISAE; 2603.23924's Yuan Gao;
  2603.13900's Claudio Di Ciccio his address before his institute; amsart's address now before the e-mail, as printed;
  review rev92c S1). The order is the institute list's, as today's places `\inst{2,1}` (institute 1, then 2). Notes
  stay where they are and a made legend last: the row's e-mail lines are queued after the entry they print inside, so
  the calls' order does not place a note line among them (residual: an entry line printed after a row-parted address
  line, on an owner holding both, is placed before it). An item the reading places nowhere stays where it is.

Scorer (the 3,000-paper sample, structurally decided creators exactly right; int122w → 92c): aa 81.23 % → 100.00 %

### 925. The kernel's own `\author` is written by the frontmatter observer (FM stage 7: `article` and every class whose bindings declare no conventions); a binding owning `\author` that declares none stays unwritten (Perl: the old reader's output, no observer)

`observer::policy::KERNEL` is `written: true`: a block of the kernel's `\author` (`ledger::meaning_owner` "kernel",
under a class whose bindings declare no conventions — `article`, `report`, `book`, and every class with no binding of
its own) is read and written as revtex's, ams's, aa's and llncs's are: by default the flush rehearses a paper whose
every author block is a written family's, and the writer applies the reading where its operations explain a
difference, each item it declines left as today's output holds it (#942). A binding that owns the `\author` meaning and declares no conventions (JHEP.cls,
aas_support.sty, elsart_support_core.sty, …; acmart.cls and mn2e_support.sty declare their own since 95b, OD #942; or a
meaning no binding owns: the document's own, a raw file's, the fallback class's) takes `policy::UNDECLARED`, the
kernel's reading unwritten, until its family passes its own gate
(`policy::undeclared`, `conventions_among`); every declaration completing `..KERNEL` states its own `written`.

- The writer's comparison skips a reading item of no letter or digit, a creator's as the block's, as it already
  skipped today's (`plan::wanted`): a note printing only a superscript or a box (`\thanks{\textsuperscript{}}`, the
  observer's note of ink in doubt, OD #916) held the paper back.
- An entry the reading leaves to the block because no name requests its label (`label:unrequested owner:block`,
  `ruling2:uncarried owner:block`) is no ruling's owner decision: the writer keeps today's placement (`emitter::writes`;
  as a line of a block-line cut whose other lines a ruling decided it is cut too, once for the block: #947 round 3)
  — espcrc's `\address[ETHZ]{…}` after each name inside `\author` (hep-lat0409072), a numbered line under names
  printing no mark (1205.5573's shape).
- The writer declines a copy of an e-mail address onto a creator while today's holds it on the creator it spells
  (`plan::plan`, `resolver::spelled_name`: "an address added beside the creator it spells") — a reading that copies a
  spelled address is a defect, never printed (review rev93a B1: `$^\dagger$\texttt{\{ann, cat\}@x.org}` was written
  onto both carriers, 2409.11430, 2506.19548).
- Census mode and the default write alike, and a paper the writer holds back keeps today's XML: the guards'
  `*_leave_the_xml_unchanged` compare the census switch with the default mode and, but for a written shape, with the
  observer off (`batchfms2a2r7` GLYPHS and SEPARATORS, `r8` GLUED are written, their XML pinned whole in their own
  guards; review rev93a S3: against the default alone the check was a tautology for a written kernel shape).

### 928. The writer re-parts today's names from the reading where the reading refines them (Perl: the old reader's parting, no observer)

`emitter::repart` (FM stage 7, "name parting last"): where the resolver's reading parts the names and today's old reader
parted them otherwise — no creator pairs by name, so no item-wise operation applies (`declined: the creators' names`)
— today's creators are written again from the reading, every written family alike (kernel, aa, llncs, revtex, ams).
Each named reading creator is one `ltx:creator` (the attributes and font of today's creator whose name printed it)
whose `ltx:personname` is the run of today's digested personname its words are (`repart::slice_name`: today's name
cloned and cut to the run — its fonts and a note set in it such as a `\footnotemark` kept, its ids given back; its
marks out; a layout's cells, rows and boxes unwrapped and their geometry dropped; a request no entry answers shown as
`show_unanswered_marks` shows it, unless a kept note prints it) —, then its affiliations, contacts and notes, one per
kind and text (the one a ruling decided kept, as `plan::wanted` reads them), placed by the writer's own print-order
pass (`apply::place` over `plan::reading_order`, rev92c S1), the author block's own on a nameless creator after them.
A name is never the reading's text set as a string, nor its tokens digested again: the string took the font current
at the document's end, where the writer runs (`\small` after `\maketitle`: `fontsize="90%"` on every name, 1607.00911;
smallcaps dropped, 2304.09381) and lost the name's markup (1909.05311's `\footnotemark[1]`); a Name's span may carry
the cover of the command or environment its ink came through (`\begin{tabular}{c}A …` opened an alignment). An item is
today's own, copied (its ids given back once today's is taken), where today's holds one of its kind and text anywhere
among the creators; else an affiliation, or a block line the reading takes for a legend (never a name's
`\thanks`/`\footnote`), made from its entry's tokens — read on from the entry's first Name through the events after it
until their ink is the entry's text (`entry_span`: an entry of several pieces, the word "and" inside one, the lines an
unmarked line continued), digested in the font of today's name, its leading line breaks taken (asme2e's in-name
`\affiliation{…}` printing `\\` first, 2107.11510). A made affiliation carries no entry mark, as today's copies hold
none (`block_span_tokens` without the mark, `drop_leading_marks`); a legend keeps its mark's ink (the label-text
ruling). The writer's block-line cut reads its lines so too: a mark's formula cut from a group the entry closes
(`{\small $~^2$ Univ Y}`) was no balanced run, so the cut declined and 2308.11662's two institutes stayed one contact.

Only where the reading refines today's names, across a boundary the digested structure shows (`repart::plan`, else
declined): every reading name is printed as a run of words inside one of today's names, in order (none is made of an
item of today's — a url column, an institution row, `Google DeepMind` under symbol lines: 77p, 77y); every name of
today's that reads as names (`reads_as_names`) keeps one (a prefix-marked `$^2$Bob Baker` the reading made an
affiliation: 61); a one-word name parted from a shared name at a comma is the given name of a name written surname
first (`Smith, Jr., John`: 61's ACM shape); an item the reading gives more authors than today's held it is a ruling's
change (`emitter::writes`: a role or note line under a row given to every name, 77t's rank 15); a creator of today's
becomes an item of another only on structural evidence — the reading's item answers a mark or is a labelled line or
row (its label), or came from an API call (`repart::structural`; round 4) — and no item read from its words alone is

superscript its text opens with where that prints it (`\textsuperscript{*}`'s `*`, `$^*$`'s `∗`), and the owner's name

between the mark and its ink with the groups it takes is its own — its switches (`$^1$\it`, `\small`, `\color{red}`,

a box —, but a line break or an alignment token; a letter outside a group, a break, an alignment token between, or no
balanced run so, and it starts at its ink as before.

### 932. aa's sole `\institute` is every author's unless the class's `\inst{n}` picks it, as llncs's (Perl: inst_support's `affiliation:1`, which no author requests; the first author's by the prefix-stripped fallback)

aa.cls:736-757 counts an `\institute`'s pieces at its top-level `\and`s (`\aa@nbinstitutes`) and `\aainstitutename`
(:886-899) prints a sole one unnumbered under the whole author row (`\ifnum\aa@nbinstitutes=1 \noindent`), as llncs.cls
does. aa's binding now owns `\institute` (`aa_cls.rs` `\lx@aa@institute@dispatch`): a sole non-empty institute is
`\lx@add@contact[role=affiliation,labelseq=affiliation,_share=authors]`, the convention llncs's binding declares
(`\lx@llncs@institute@sole`, OD #901) — every author's in today's output and the reading unless an author's `\inst{n}`
picks it, its e-mail lines each the author they spell; several institutes split as inst_support's (OD #53). Hand
marks over numbered lines (`{1} Univ A \\ {2} Univ B` under `$^{1,2}$`, astro-ph0305539) leave it the block's; unmarked
names share it (2210.16066: base on a nameless creator, its address on the first author). The Perl defect is
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1195's (inst_support.sty.ltxml:36-37 for aa). Repros class-bindings/
`aa_sole_institute_numbered_lines_is_the_blocks`, `aa_sole_institute_is_every_authors`,
`aa_sole_institute_address_line_is_the_rows`; guard `perfect_kernel_batch92c::aa_sole_institute_is_the_rows`.

The shared row reads aa's sole institute as llncs's (`shared_row::row_email_calls`; review rev92c r2 B-2):
- aa_support's `\email` is the kernel's `\lx@add@email{\lx@address@urlfont{#1}}` — Perl's `\lx@add@contact[role=email]
  {#1}` (aa_support.sty.ltxml:109), the same contact as `\lx@add@email` (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:655) —, so it is a
  class e-mail call (`is_email_command`): `\institute{Univ A, City A, \email{ann@a.org}}` gives the address to the
  author it spells and the institute, its comma before the call a separator, to every author (1312.1871, 2310.16880:
  both had been the block's, the row finding no e-mail call and an address on the institute's first line). The
  institute's content stays aa's (no `\lx@affiliation@withinst`, whose `\inst{n}` sets the entry's label: aa's `\inst`
  there is a request, `\institute{\inst{1} Univ X\\ \inst{2} Univ Y}` cut at its marks, 1003.3020).
- A note's text is no line of the institute (`holds_raw_address`, aa and llncs): `\institute{Univ A, City A\thanks{email:
  ann@a.org}}` prints its address in the footer, so the institute is every author's, the note a publication note
  (0705.1240; it had been the block's).
- A later line the address reader does not part, opened by an e-mail label (`e-mail: gil@astrax.fis.ucm.es (AGdP)`,
  astro-ph0007270), is an e-mail of the block under that label, not a nameless `role="affiliation"` (review rev92c r2
  S-3); the reading keeps it in the institute's text, so the writer declines and today's stands.

Repros class-bindings/`aa_sole_institute_inline_email_is_its_authors`, `aa_sole_institute_thanks_stays_shared`,
`aa_sole_institute_email_line_is_an_email`; guard `perfect_kernel_batch92c::aa_sole_institute_reads_as_llncss`.

### 936. A raw file's in-place contact setter is the Frontmatter API's: `\address`, `\affil`, `\affiliation`, `\institute`, `\email` that print a title-page line become contacts (Perl: the shipped file is not read; OmniBus's setters feed the API)

A paper's own class or style read raw (beyond Perl, which ignores the shipped file and gives the paper
OmniBus.cls.ltxml:77-94's setters) that defines a contact setter as typesetting kept the line out of the frontmatter:
the author's `$^1$` mark had no entry to answer it, and the line landed in a titlepage block (1303.3004,
ae100prg.cls:188 `\begin{indented}\item[]\normalsize #1\end{indented}`), as body text after the names (hep-ph0312288,
11lomcon.sty:17; cond-mat0611585, jetpl.cls:302) or glued into the last personname (1602.05576, 2405.08158,
ar-1col.cls:341 `\affil` written inside `\author{}`). `frontmatter_stores.rs` `reroute_in_place_contact_setters` runs
after a raw class is read (`\lx@class@loaded@raw`, after K11's store reroute) and after a raw package is read
(`\lx@package@loaded@raw`, a hook `input_definitions` now fires for a `.sty` read raw); each of the five that is still
the file's own definition (`store_setters::defined_by_a_raw_file`: not a binding's, nor one K11 rerouted as a store) is
the API's when the file's code says it sets a title-page line (`in_place_contact_setter`), as the kernel's locked
`\author` stays the kernel's against the file's own: (a) a macro of one argument, or of `[opt]{arg}`, whose executed
code (`executed_code`: what its definitions store left out) prints the argument where it is called — at its top level,
in a plain group, or in an argument a face, a box or a link prints, or that a macro the raw file defined prints, a few
levels down (`prints_argument`, `command_arguments`; ae100prg's `\email` = `\vspace*{5pt}\address{E-mail: \mailto{#1}}`)
— beside a line break (`LINE_BREAKS`: `\par`, `\\`, `\vskip`, `\item`, …; one that prints it as text with none, a
run-in setter, is the API's only where its call stands as a line of its own, OD #955); or (b) one that appends the argument to a
store the class's own `\author` — the definition the lock refused, `\lx@dropped@author`, and the raw macros it calls —
writes too (`class_author_stores`: 11lomcon's `\@aabuffer`, jetpl's `\@authoraddress`; amsart copies' `\addresses`,
nyjm.cls, smfart.cls, birkart.cls, whose `\enddoc@text` prints the list) — not the kernel's own `\@author`, whose
appended rows are its authors' already (`\lx@author@flush`, 59d: cjs-rcs-article.cls's `\g@addto@macro\@author{\\#1}`).
The API call (`IN_PLACE_CONTACT_SETTERS`): `\lx@add@address[annotate=run]`, `\lx@add@affiliation[annotate=run]` for
`\affil`, `\affiliation`, `\institute` — a line printed under the names printed above it, the authors new since the last
such entry, or those its marks request — and `\lx@split@addresses{\lx@add@email}`, each address of a listed line placed
by the API's evidence (1303.3004's `\email{rnarayan@…, jmcclintock@…, atchekho@…}` one address of each author); an
`[opt]{arg}` setter's optional argument is read by the API's convention, Perl's own bindings' (`optional_contact`;
jheppub.sty.ltxml:35-37 `\affiliation[a]{…}` → `label={a}`, ams_support.sty.ltxml:115 `\address[]{}` →
`\lx@add@address[name={#1}]{#2}`): empty, dropped (OmniBus.cls.ltxml:92); a printed mark (a superscript,
`\textsuperscript`, `\inst`: w-art.cls's `\address[\inst{1}]{…}`, 0910.5837, 1105.1753, quant-ph0606237) leads the line,
an address read for its marks as an affiliation is (`\lx@affiliation@withinst`); a key an `\author[key]` gave its
authors (the kernel's `\author` records each call's optional argument and the author creators it made,
`\lx@author@keys`) labels the line for each of them, `author:N` (a jheppub copy's `\affiliation[b]` Joydeep
Chakravarty's alone, 2303.16316; stacs.cls's `\address[uniroma]`, 0902.1737) — the resolver reads a creator's own

two words or more no creator requests are its caption, `name=` (amsart copies' `\address[Current address]{…}`: smfart,
nyjm, birkmult, birkart, ECACRM); anything else — a lone word no one requests, which reads as a key as often as a
caption, or other markup — is in doubt: an in-place setter's call stays the class's, a stored one's drops it (a generic
`name={#1}`, review rev94b B2, wrote "\hbox{\@textsuperscript{1}}" and "a" as contact names). An in-place call in doubt
runs the class's definition and prints its line in the body where it stands: its words kept, its contact markup lost
(main-session ruling 2026-10-31: content over markup). The
observer reads such an affiliation as the API attaches it (94a r6): the rehearsal binds a rerouted in-place setter
(`\lx@class@contact@<name>` defined) to `\lx@fm@obs@affil@run`, a Contact event of `annotate=run`, which a names line
gives every name of the run before it back to the block's contact of its role before it, labelled or not
(`Resolver::record_run` within the line, `Resolver::ends_a_run`, rule `owner:annotate:run`; OD #928 round 7), not the
name beside it alone — ci2018's `JORGE RAMIREZ and EVGENY KRIVOSHEEV \affil{University of Trento} MARCOS BAEZ and …`

`perfect_kernel_batch94a::an_affil_after_a_run_of_names_is_the_runs`.

*Live rule: OD #767.*

### 937. An in-block affiliation that opens with marks is the entry they label in the observer's reading (Perl: no observer)

An `\affil`, `\address`, `\affiliation` or `\institute` written inside `\author{}` with no label argument is one Contact
event (`\lx@fm@obs@affil`); its text was its whole ink, the leading mark's included ("1Max Planck …"), and it went to
the name beside it (`owner:adjacent`): ar-1col's `\affil{$^1$…}` lines both on the last author, the writer declining
(1602.05576, 2405.08158). The event now reads its digested content's leading marks as its label — the run
`events::leading_marks` finds, the one an API entry's leading-mark reading takes (`resolver/api.rs`, which now calls the
same function) — its text as the rest of its events (`events_text`, moved beside the lexer), and its span as its
content's from the marks on: a labelled entry, which the names showing the mark request (`ruling1:request`), never a
character stripped from the text, and which the writer's re-part (OD #928) makes from its own tokens
(`plan::block_span_tokens`, `<sup>1</sup>Department …`), not from the call, whose typesetting is no part of it. The
witnesses' reading is today's XML (`writer: same`); 94a's fail-safe repro
`author_names_reparted_declined_mark_in_contact` (the paper's own `\newcommand{\affil}[1]{\\{\footnotesize #1}}`, which
no reroute touches) is now written, each line on the name showing its mark
(`perfect_kernel_batch94a::an_affil_in_the_author_led_by_its_mark_is_reparted`, renamed from
`a_repart_that_does_not_read_as_the_reading_is_taken_back`). Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch94b::an_affil_inside_the_author_is_labelled_by_its_leading_mark`.
Round 2 (review rev94b B1): a contact of several marked entries (`\affil{$^1$Univ A, Town\\ $^2$Univ B, City}`, after a
line break, a `\par`, a `\newline`, a comma or a gap) is one Contact event per entry (`events::labelled_entries`), cut
as the API reading cuts a call (`mark_led_pieces`, moved beside `leading_marks` with `inked`; jetpl's
`\address{$^1$…\\ $^2$…}`, cond-mat0611585), each labelled by its own leading marks: it was one entry under the first
mark, on every name showing it, the `2` dropped from its text. An entry that holds a mark past its leading run
(`$^1$Univ A$^2$`), which its text would drop, keeps the call one entry (round 3, below). Each entry's
span is its own ink past its marks, the writer's entry made without the mark, as a made affiliation carries none
(`plan::block_span_tokens`, which holds an in-block labelled contact's span at its own ink: the marks' closing `$` before
it is theirs); the writer cuts today's one contact into the entries (`plan::cut_block_lines`). Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch94b::an_affil_inside_the_author_of_several_marked_entries_is_cut_by_its_marks`.
Round 3 (review rev94b r2 B1, N4): entries the writer could not cut left today's one contact on a nameless creator.

an entry leads with no labelled mark or holds a mark past its leading run, has no text (`$^1$\\ $^2$Univ B`), the
entries' texts joined are not the content's (`Town and $^2$Univ B`: the word between them no entry's), or a span is no
balanced run the writer's cut reads as its text — checked at the reading with the writer's own function
(`plan::span_tokens`, on the block being rehearsed, `events::with_block_content`) —, and when an entry's marks are no
name's (`$^3$Lab C` under names showing 1 and 2: the writer makes no entry of the block's own; `lex_events`). An entry's
cut keeps the group and the switches its line opens before its mark (`{\itshape $^1$Univ A}`) or after it
(`$^2${\itshape Univ B}`, `$^2$\textbf{Univ B}`: `span_tokens` reads them back to the mark's closing shift), and the
punctuation it prints at its line's end (`Town;\\`, `events::mark_led_pieces_keeping`; a comma between two entries of
one line still parts them). Repros sectioning-frontmatter/`raw_class_affil_cut_keeps_its_font`,
`raw_class_affil_uncut_noline_stays_one_contact`, `raw_class_affil_uncut_midword_stays_one_contact`,

Round 4 (review rev94b r3 B1): a cut entry lost the font open from before its line — a switch at the content's head
(`\itshape $^1$…\\ $^2$…`, `\footnotesize`, `\bfseries`, `\color{red}`), a group or a font command's argument

every entry after the first was plain. Each entry now carries the font in effect where its cut starts, read from the
rehearsal's digested ink, not from the tokens' shapes (`events/fonts.rs` `entry_font`): the font of the first text
character from there on with nothing between but spaces, math shifts (`\(`, `\)`), scripts, braces and what a mark, a
break or a separator prints; else of the last one before it, a group closed before it passed whole; else, nothing of
another kind before it, the call's own — each character read at its own token's position, never the cover of the
expansion that made it (`\textbf{Lab C}`'s letters are covered from `\textbf`). The changes against the call's font
(family, series, shape, size, colours) are registered and the entry's tokens open with `\lx@fm@entry@font{n}`
(`plan::entry_font_tokens`, `frontmatter_stores.rs`), which merges them: the made entry is digested in the call's font,
the switches of a group it sits in no longer copied (an `\em` toggled twice). An in-block cut whose font the boxes
cannot tell (a command between: `\itshape $^1$\textbf{Univ A}`), or one whose entries' ink a container other than a
group holds (`\underline{…}`, `\emph{…}`, `\href`), was no cut — today's one contact on the first name (corrected in
round 5, below: the base cut these, attribution beats typography); an API call's piece whose font cannot be told is cut as before (`$^2$\mbox{…}` after `\mbox{Univ A}`,
`perfect_kernel_batchfms2b`). The API call's cut (`plan::cut`) reads its pieces' fonts from its own rehearsal. The
rehearsal's `\lx@fm@obs@affil` and `@run` are bounded, a group of their own as the API digests each entry (a switch in
one affiliation was the next one's font, its `\textit` read as no change). Repros
sectioning-frontmatter/`raw_class_affil_cut_keeps_the_font_open_before_it`,
`raw_class_address_cut_keeps_the_font_open_before_it`, `raw_class_affil_crossed_container_stays_one_contact`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch94b::a_cut_entry_keeps_the_font_open_before_it`, `an_api_piece_keeps_the_font_open_before_it`,
`entries_inside_one_container_stay_one_contact` (renamed in round 5).
Round 5 (review rev94b r4 B1; main-session rule: a font the reading cannot tell never undoes a cut the base made): no
early exit of the cut turns it into one contact any more — the audited exits, each with its fallback: no font or span
of the call (`scope` none: every entry cut without a font), a container holding two entries (wrapped again, else cut
without one), a cut start out of the content (`labelled_start`: the writer's `span_tokens` fails there too — no cut, as
94a r7), a font the boxes cannot tell (`entry_font` none: cut without one, the switches opening the group it sits in its
own, `span_tokens`' `own_font` false), and in `plan::cut` no call font (`lookup_font` none: pieces without one) and a
container (as in-block); what stays one contact is only what 94a r7 kept one (entries of no text, a mark past the
leading run, texts that do not join to the content's, no balanced run, a mark no name shows). `entry_font` reads a line
break's own box (`InkFonts`' whatsit fonts, at the break token's position): the font in effect where the next entry
starts when nothing between switches (`$^1$\textbf{Univ A}\\ $^2$…`, `\textit{Town}\\`, `Town~\\`), and its backward
scan stops at the content's first token by position (`FontScope::start` is a position, the block's `base` subtracted:
a second block's scan had stopped short). A container spanning entries (`InkFonts::holders`: `\emph{…\\…}`,
`\underline{…\\…}`; pdflatex prints both lines in it) wraps each entry again (`plan::entry_forms`,
`plan::container_wrap`, the event's `wrap`): its opening tokens — the command, its `[…]` and braced arguments up to the
one holding the entry, switches between nested containers — before the entry, one end-group after, the entry's font
then the one where the outermost starts; exact only when the container's entries read one font and nothing switches
between the innermost container's argument's start and its first entry (`events::switch_free`; an outer container's
argument holds nothing but font declarations and spaces before the next container, round 7), else cut without either
(`\emph{\bfseries $^5$…\\ $^6$…}`: the bold the first entry's switches carry, the second plain). Probes `p/f` (46):
none attributes worse than 94a r7; od4, mac7, mac4 back to 94a r7; od1 the second entry italic (94a r7: plain); emph,
und each entry its name's with the markup (94a r7: cut, markup lost). Residual: the API path's `\affiliation{\emph{$^1$…\\
$^2$…}}` (revtex) stays one contact, as 94a r7 — the reading's first piece spans the container (`piece_span` of the
`\emph`'s events), no balanced run. Repros sectioning-frontmatter/`raw_class_affil_uncertain_font_still_cuts`,
`raw_class_affil_container_wraps_each_entry` (was `raw_class_affil_crossed_container_stays_one_contact`); guards
`perfect_kernel_batch94b::an_uncertain_font_never_undoes_a_cut`, `entries_inside_one_container_are_each_wrapped_again`
(re-baselined from `entries_inside_one_container_stay_one_contact`: each entry its name's).
Round 6 (review rev94b r5 BL3): a container's wrap needs the font where the outermost container starts; when the boxes
cannot tell it (`\itshape\emph{…\\…}`, `\textcolor{red}{\emph{…}}`, `\small\emph{…}`) the entries get neither font
nor wrap — the base's cut, plain (`plan::entry_forms`; round 5 wrapped each in `\emph` alone: italic where pdflatex
prints upright, the red and the size lost). Nested containers (`\emph{\underline{…\\…}}`) wrap each entry in both:
the switch-free test runs on the innermost container's argument only, the tokens before an inner container read as the
switches between the two (`plan::container_wrap`; round 5 read `\underline` as a switch, every entry plain). Repro
sectioning-frontmatter/`raw_class_affil_container_outer_font_unknown`; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch94b::a_container_whose_font_is_unknown_is_cut_plain`.
Round 7 (review rev94b r6 B2, S1): B2 round 6 copied whatever stood between two nested containers into every entry's
wrap — `\emph{\newline\underline{…\\…}}` a `<break/>` in each contact, `\emph{\quad\underline{…}}` (and a space) a
leading space in each. Between them now stand only font declarations (`events::font_declaration`: the head of
`frontmatter_stores::LAYOUT` up to `\selectfont` — `\bfseries`, `\small`, `\em`), copied into the wrap since every
entry prints under them as every line does in pdflatex, and spaces, left out; anything else prints or acts once, so
the entries get the base's cut. S1 a kernel text font command whose argument opens with the outermost container
(`\textbf{\emph{…\\…}}`: latex.ltx:14213-14226 `\DeclareTextFontCommand`, a macro `\bgroup\bfseries #1\egroup`, no
whatsit holding the ink — `events::text_font_command`) wraps each entry too, nested ones each
(`\textrm{\textbf{\emph{…}}}`), the entry's font then the one where the outermost command starts: round 6 cut them
plain (the font where `\emph` starts unknown), 94a r9 wrapped each in the `\emph` alone (pdflatex: bold italic). Any
other command round a container (`\textcolor{red}{\emph{…}}`) keeps the unknown font and the plain cut. Residual, as
round 5: the API path's container round the marks (`\address{\textbf{\emph{$^1$…\\ $^2$…}}}` after `\author`) stays one
contact on every author (all rounds and the tip alike). Repros
sectioning-frontmatter/`raw_class_affil_nested_containers_only_font_declarations_between`,
`raw_class_affil_text_font_command_round_a_container`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch94b::nested_containers_wrap_each_entry_only_across_font_declarations`,
`a_text_font_command_round_a_container_wraps_each_entry`.

### 938. An e-mail address printed inside an affiliation entry is an e-mail contact of the author it spells; one `\email` of several addresses is decided address by address (Perl: the address stays in the affiliation's text, copied onto every carrier; the call's text one contact)

**Defect.** An address printed in an affiliation entry's text — `$^1$ Dipartimento…, Italy
(saro,borgani,tornator@oats.inaf.it)` (0810.2791), `…, France - e-mail: julien@obs-besancon.fr` (aa `\institute`,
1909.06145), revtex's `\affiliation{…, email: rlake@ee.ucr.edu, …}` (cond-mat0607219), llncs's `\institute{…, UK,
\{n.camgoz, s.hadfield, r.bowden\}@surrey.ac.uk, \and …}` (2009.00299) — or on an e-mail line the block sets under an
entry, which the reading continues the entry with (`$^2$ 3Dwe.ai\\ {\tt hyunjun.jung, p.ruhkamp, b.busam@tum.de}`,
2308.10621; a `\{…\}@umontreal.ca` group broken over two lines, 2311.18002, 2603.12826), stayed inside the affiliation
contact, copied onto every carrier, so each carrier held its co-authors' addresses (the scorer's `email_of_other`, 91
creators in 41 papers of the 3,000 sample). A mark-led address line (`$^1$\{cherian, …\}@merl.com \quad
$^2$goncalo.pais@…`, 2108.13865) the reading read as e-mails since 93a r2, but today's old reader had made it an
affiliation and the writer had no operation to take it back. One `\email` printing several addresses (G3: revtex
`\email{seracre, hanaki, jimliu, pszepiet@umich.edu}` after the last author, 0812.3572; `\email{tuhin@…;rajib@…;…}`,
0901.1641; `\email{julioleite,tmariz@fis.ufal.br}` after each author, 1110.2127; `\email{cpotts@…, jdavis@…}`, 2104.11218)
was one contact of the call's author. And `insert::respell_emails` moved elsarticle's `\author{Javier
Martínez-López}\ead{javier.martinez@ugr.es}` onto Carlos Javier Navarro, whom it also spells (G6, 2410.00275).

**Fix (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4's chain, the reading's own lexer).** `resolver::address_runs` reads the address runs of a
printed text — a braced group (the forms `addresses_in` reads; spaces before its `@` the group's, 2311.14729), a list of
lowercase local parts sharing the domain (without spaces always, the main session's ruling for 1110.2127; with spaces
when each part spells an author or the list opens the text, a parenthesis or a label — `Univ Tübingen, Germany,
wilhelm.kley@…` is one address; a part holds a letter, so a digit run glued before an address — `Tel:5551234,info@x.org`,
`ORCID 0000-…,ann@x.org` — is no local part), a plain address —, each with the label word printed before it
("E-mail:", "Emails", "e-mail addresses:"; a label only with a colon after it or opening its line:
`\texttt{mail ann@x.org now}` keeps its "mail") and the parentheses round it. A run comes out only at a list boundary
(`at_list_boundary`): on one side at least the text's or a line's end, `,` `;`, a bracket (an opening one or a closing
one before it, a closing one after it), before it its label word, after it a period ending the text or line; and no
parenthesised tag after it — so prose with a plain word on both sides (`write to info@x.org or data@x.org for data`)
and a tagged run (`ann@y.org (Ann)`, 0811.1419's `zhanghuamaths@163.com(H. Zhang)`) stay as printed (review rev95c
B2), while `Correspondence: {…}@westlake.edu.cn` (2601.07312) and `SPAIN. {…}@upc.edu` (2509.12185) come out. `address_cuts` takes the separators a cut strands, each within its line (a run ending its
line those before it, the break kept: cond-mat0607219's `FAX: 951-827-2425; email: rlake@…` leaves `FAX:
951-827-2425`), and keeps one space of two. After every name is read, `Resolver::take_out_entry_addresses` gives each address of an affiliation entry
its owner: the author it spells (`owner:spelled`, any live author); else the entry's only carrier, when no other of its
addresses spells that carrier (`owner:only-carrier`); else, on a symbol-led line, every carrier (`owner:carriers`, the
2026-10-30 ruling); else, within one run,
one address per carrier that every spelled one of the run agrees with, by place (`owner:order`; an address another run
prints is no place of the order: `Dept X, Univ Y, ann@x.org, Phone 123, office@x.org` under two authors leaves
`office@` the block's). A run
holding an address the chain cannot attribute (it would be the block's) stays in the entry as today's prints it — the
fail-safe, now of this text reading only (OD #956): a line or note of addresses the author block kinds at the API goes to
the block once (ruling E, main session 2026-11-02, TENTATIVE: FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 step 4 wins — astro-ph0512555's
`Email:dzg@,xywang@,hyf@`), and the chain is the one both engines run (`email_owners::entry_address_owners`), its carriers
every holder of a print of the entry's text. The entry keeps the rest of its words (`ruling3:address-out`; an entry of addresses alone is gone); each
e-mail is one per print and owner (`owner:entry-address`, a change tag). The writer cuts today's item by the same lexer
over its printed segments (`dom::address_cut`, marks a space, a line break a line's end — the reading reads an API
entry's lines too, `events_lined_text`; only the runs the reading holds as e-mails), in place (`plan::Op::CutAddresses`;
an item cut to nothing is taken; a font wrapper or a link left printing nothing is removed), before the re-assignment
that copies it, and makes each e-mail contact from that item (`Op::Address`: role `email`, the address in the outermost
`ltx:text`/`ltx:ref` the cut takes whole — `\href{mailto:…}{…}` keeps its link, 2111.14566, 1804.04123 — else the font
wrapper it printed in), in print order. The re-part (OD #928) reads the reading with every take-out given back; the plan then takes out
those today's can cut (`writer::take_out_again`), an entry today's holds no item of given back (the cut never declines a
paper). G3: an `\email` call printing several addresses alone (`resolver::listed_addresses`; a label word beside them
keeps it whole, as the group write-out does) is placed once every name is read (`Resolver::answer_listed_emails`), each
address the author's it spells, else its call's own authors' (`owner:call`); the writer's group write-out reads the
same lists. G6: the reading's `Resolver::respell_emails` (the DOM pass `insert::respell_emails`, alike, deleted at P6e; an e-mail
the reading does not place, a flush with no author block or a document's note, is respelled on the queue by
`place::shared_block_email_labels` only after a run of two or more names, P6e2) picks the author an address moves to
by the names as printed and keeps an address on the
holder it spells by base letters (`resolver::base_letters`, as the reading does since 92c): `javier.martinez@` stays on
Javier Martínez-López, whom it spells by base letters (as printed it spells Carlos Javier Navarro alone), and Anna
Smith's own `\email{muller-group@x.de}` stays hers though by base letters it spells Jörg Müller (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4
#420's example; review rev95c B1 — targets picked by base letters had moved it). Measured on real papers (brief 95c
r3, the user's ruling "answered by our natural examples data"): the rival rule, FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 #420 read literally
(an author's own one-name call holding one address never respelled; otherwise spelling decides, base letters allowed),
differs from this one on 24 papers of a 347-paper respell population (amsart, elsarticle, revtex4*, aastex*, article,
≥2 `\author` calls, an address spelling another author) and none of the 2,270-paper census; on 22 of them it is wrong —
the corresponding author's address set after the last `\author` or after `\correspondingauthor`, which the class
prints on the call's author (revtex 2011.01984, 1303.5460, 1304.4972, 1503.07733, 1608.00809, 2303.00383; aastex
1102.0339, 2004.06253, 2005.06651, 2103.16254, 2105.05931, 2110.15275; amsart 1511.04148, 2408.09634) —, right on 0711.3633
and 0809.3090 (`\author{Santos Bravo Yuste}\email{santos@unex.es}`: the holder's given name, today's moves it to Andrés
Santos), and, outside that population, right on 2112.10604 (`\author{Dario Mathi\"a and Ulrich Thiel}`, `mathiae@` on
Thiel; a several-name call, base letters alone) and on the ASCII twin `\author{Anna Smith}…\email{mueller-group@x.de}`
beside `\author{Jorg Mueller}` (moved here, as by every binary before; FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 #420 amended to this measurement, user
2026-10-31). This rule stays; the rival's witnesses are RED
repros `amsart_email_of_a_two_name_call_spelling_an_accented_name`, `revtex_email_spelling_its_holders_given_name` (SYNC).

**Label words** travel as an e-mail line's do (`author_block::labelled_emails`): an e-mail label word goes with the
address and names its contact as printed (`E-mail: `, 1911.11406; `email: `, cond-mat0607219), the class's "Email: "
only without one (review rev95c B5); any other word stays the entry's (`Univ B Correspondence: bbaker@…` leaves `Univ
B Correspondence`; `* Contact: \{…\}@x.edu` leaves `* Contact`) — the open question on contact labels decides more.
The e-mail words are the e-mail line's, `author_block::is_email_label`: "E-mail", "Email", "E-mails", "Emails" (any
case, a hyphen or none), alone or before "address"/"addresses"; "mail" is none (`Univ X, please mail ann@x.org` stays
prose; review rev95c_r2 N1).

**Round 3** (review rev95c_r2). The wrapper an address prints in (`dom::Wrap`): any inline element wrapping text alone
(`dom::wraps_text`: its children text and such elements — `ltx:emph` too, not only `ltx:text`/`ltx:ref`) is taken whole
when every piece under it is text inside the cut (0808.1112's `\small Email: \emph{duan@iit.edu}`: the e-mail keeps its
italic and its size, the emptied `ltx:emph` leaves the affiliation; F1); a link is kept whole only when it prints that
one address or its `mailto:` target is it (one `\href{mailto:able@x.org}{\{able,baker\}@x.org}` gives `baker@` no
link; F3); otherwise only the font of the innermost inline element is carried (a link's an `ltx:text` in its font), and
an icon in the link (`\includegraphics`, `\rule`, a formula) stays once, with its link, where it printed (F2). The
writer's address layout reads an element of no content as an icon (`dom::segments_of`, U+FFFC), so the cut's separator
trim stops at it and at any piece no text (`Univ X, \href{…}{$\boxtimes$\,ann@x.org}` keeps `Univ X, ⊠`; F6). One
boundary side is enough only when the other side is no lowercase word without a colon (`Univ X, see also data@x.org`,
`Univ W, see sales@w.org, City W`, `write to a@z.org.` stay; F5), and a bare e-mail word with no colon after a
separator or a period is the label when its run ends a list's item (`Univ X, E-mail ann@x.org` is "Univ X" and an
"E-mail " contact; `\texttt{mail ann@x.org now}` stays; F4). G3's write-out reads today's contact across a line
break (`apply::text_leaf`, `leaf_text`): `\email{mhamed.ghiati@…;\\ mohammed.mouniane@…}` (2212.08940) is written out
address by address, where the writer had declined the paper and so dropped the rest of its work (Mohammed Mouniane's
`$^{*1}$` address, which the base's writer gave him); the same write-out reaches every `\email{a\\ b}` call (read against
their sources, final review rev95c_r3: 1010.2311, 1705.06212, 2307.07287, 1110.1356, 1610.09150, 2108.11087, 2109.13668,
2301.05042 — each address to the author it spells, else its call's author, only the `;`/`,` and the break dropped).
Census against round 2 (2,270 papers): two changed, 0808.1112 (the font) and 2606.13944 (a space kept before an icon).
Open, RED `entry_address_after_a_non_email_colon_word_keeps_the_colon` (review rev95c_r3 S1): a run after a colon word
that is no e-mail label (`Mail:`, `Contact:`) comes out one-sided and the separator trim takes the colon ("Univ X, Mail";
2601.07312's `Correspondence:` likewise). Repros `entry_address_in_emph_keeps_its_font`,
`entry_address_link_with_an_icon_keeps_it_once`, `entry_address_group_in_one_link_keeps_its_target`,
`entry_address_after_a_bare_label_word`, `entry_address_in_one_sided_prose_stays`,
`amsart_email_call_of_addresses_over_a_line_break`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch95c` (round 3, six).
**95e** (bundle int124b's A/B). G3's write-out left the name re-part (OD #928) nothing to write a call's e-mails from:
today's holds the call as one contact on its author, the reading one contact per address, so a names call the reading
parts and today's does not stayed one creator (2109.07363's `\author{Jinsong Liu\textsuperscript{1,2} $\&$ Fei
Tao\textsuperscript{1,2} $\&$ Huaying Wei\textsuperscript{3}}` with `\email{liujsong@…,\:ferrytau@…,\:hywei@…}`: one
creator and `merged_creators`, where int123a wrote three). The resolver keeps each such call as today's holds it
(`Resolved::listed`, `resolver::Listed`, both deleted by DEL5b as never read: the contact whole, the rule of the call's own placement — `api:annotate:last` —,
the authors it gives it), and the re-part reads it so (`writer::give_back_listed`, beside the entries'
`give_back_addresses`); the plan writes the addresses out after it, as the take-outs (`take_out_again`: only when the
re-part's reading is the whole reading). Fail-safe: where the plan declines with the calls written out, it plans again
with each call one contact on its authors (`write_observed_frontmatter`) — today's, which the re-part wrote — so an
e-mail split never declines a paper's names or the rest of its writing (no one text leaf to write an address from: an
`\href` around one address, 1412.1769; a separator printed in its own run of text, `\xand` 1411.1443, `{\rm and }`
2307.05703, `{\rm ,}` 2603.10734). Where keeping the calls whole leaves today's as it was, the ledger still reads
`declined: …` (the write-out the reading wanted, declined — not `same`, rev95e S2), as before 95e; those four papers'
XML is today's. A reading a conceded creator changed keeps every call one contact, as today's. Repros
`amsart_names_call_with_a_several_address_email` (RED → GREEN), `amsart_names_call_of_three_with_a_several_address_email`,
`amsart_names_call_with_a_several_address_email_kept_whole`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch95e` (2). Census against
int125a (the 95c populations, 2,686 papers, and 192 papers of amsart, elsarticle, revtex4*, aastex*, article with an
`\author` call naming several people and a several-address `\email`/`\ead`): creators changed in 2109.07363 alone; the
3,000 scorer sample unchanged. Residual, RED `amsart_dollar_numbered_addresses_under_shared_marks`: 2109.07363's
`\address{$1.$ …}` labels are not read, so its names' marks stay unanswered and the upfront grid — which fires only
because the call is no longer in the reading's pile (`answer_listed_emails` runs after `distribute_upfront`) — gives

**Residual.** Unwritten families (mn2e 0810.2791, authblk 2511.07020, 2008.07734, 2110.01283, 2008.13643, elsarticle
2308.13695, IEEEtran 2405.16358, 2311.14729, 2202.02533, 2401.16729, 1303.4266, acmart 2311.10779, 2010.12245) read right
under `LATEXML_FM_SHADOW=1`, today's output unchanged; a symbol line set after a numbered one today's old reader joins

sectioning-frontmatter/`entry_address_inside_an_entry_is_its_speller_email`,
`entry_address_line_continuing_an_entry_is_email`, `entry_address_unspelled_by_the_chain`,
`entry_address_mark_led_line_today_an_affiliation`, `revtex_affiliation_address_is_its_speller_email`,

`revtex_email_list_after_each_author_by_spelling`, `elsarticle_ead_spelling_its_accented_holder_stays`; round 2:
`amsart_email_spelling_an_accented_coauthor_stays`, `elsarticle_ead_spelling_an_accented_coauthor_stays`,
`entry_address_in_prose_stays`, `entry_address_after_a_digit_run`, `entry_address_mailto_link_moves_whole`,

### 939. A raw class's token register that only its title page's page style prints is the frontmatter's note; `\fancypagestyle` stores the style (Perl: `\fancypagestyle` a no-op, the register undefined — an Error, its value a body paragraph)

googlecloud.cls:80 `\newtoks\correspondingauthor` (cmu.cls:113, nv.cls:180, deepseek.cls:112 and 20 more shipped
classes: googledeepmind, nvidiatechreport, berkeley, instadeep, hku, ds, dm, dmml, …) is filled by the document's
`\correspondingauthor{…}` and printed only in the foot of `\fancypagestyle{firststyle}` (:103-114), which its
`\maketitle` selects with `\thispagestyle{firststyle}`: page furniture LaTeXML does not set, so the note was lost with 0
errors (2607.06973, 2608.26053, 2604.13010). Two parts. fancyhdr_sty.rs ports fancyhdr.sty:691-711:
`\fancypagestyle[*]{name}[base]{defs}` defines `\ps@name` as the base style then the definitions (Perl
fancyhdr.sty.ltxml:56 makes it a no-op); `\fancyfoot` and the other fields stay no-ops, and the starred reset and the
base style's checks are not modelled. The style is there to be read, not run: `\ps@name` wraps its code in
`\lx@fancyhdr@style`, which drops it, so `\pagestyle{name}` (sect05.rs runs a class's own `\ps@…`) selects nothing, as
Perl's no-op `\fancypagestyle` and `\pagestyle` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:997) — its fields set no head or foot here,
and its code may test what a binding does not model: popets.sty:189-279's `standardpagestyle` under the acmart binding
reads acmart.cls's `\if@ACM@printfolios`/`\if@ACM@timestamp` (acmart.cls:147-153), 9 Errors each on 2408.16304,
2602.20222, 2606.05273 while the style ran (95d; pdflatex 0). schooldocs.sty:312-315's `exam` style, which makes
`\subtitle` a store, therefore never replaces schooldocs_sty.rs's `\lx@add@subtitle` hoist (schooldocs-examples.tex
:227-230). fancyhdr.sty's other user commands a style or field calls are defined: `\fancycenter[][]{}{}{}` (:378) and
`\fancyfootalign{}` (:429) no-ops, `\fancyhdrsettoheight{len}{field}` (:438) a zero length, `\fancypagestyleassign`
(:753) as fancyhdr's, `\ps@fancydefault` (:767). And K11 (frontmatter_stores.rs
`toks_store`) takes a table name (`STORE_SETTERS`, now with `correspondingauthor` → `\lx@add@frontmatter{ltx:note}
[role=corresponding]{#1}`) that a raw file made a token register, when every macro reading it is printed code
(`ClassReaders::printed`) or a fancyhdr page style, and one of them prints its value — a `\the\X` that is no conditional's operand
(`\if\relax\the\X\relax` only tests it: nvidiatechreport's copy in 2507.09850 prints "* Equal contribution."
instead) — in a macro the title page reaches or a page style the title page selects (`selected_page_styles`:
`\thispagestyle{…}`/`\pagestyle{…}` in the refused `\maketitle`, `\@maketitle` or a printed macro). At `\maketitle`
(`harvest_stores`) a non-blank value is the table's call, led by the text the class prints right before it in its line
(`printed_text_before`: "Corresponding author(s): " of googlecloud.cls:114, the "*" of deepseek.cls:170; none when a
test's operand ends it). A fancyhdr style is not printed code otherwise (`page_style_name`): its fields are page
furniture, and a store's class default read only there is not the frontmatter's (nbdt-article.cls:292-325's foot prints
its `\@jname` default only under a `\@paperreceived` the paper leaves empty, 2211.12591). The deepseek.cls binding (deepseek_cls.rs, which added this note for one class name) is
retired into this path; 2401.14196's note is unchanged. Not covered: a page style the class selects only at its top
level or in `\AtBeginDocument`, fields set outside `\fancypagestyle` (`\fancyfoot[L]{\the\X}` under `\pagestyle{fancy}`),
the class's other footer registers (`\paperurl`, `\reportnumber`), and a macro store a `\ps@` style prints under another
name (`\def\correspondingauthor#1{\gdef\@corr{#1}}`). Repro sectioning-frontmatter/
`toks_store_printed_in_a_fancy_page_style_is_a_note`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch95d::toks_store_printed_in_a_selected_page_style_is_a_corresponding_note`,
`perfect_kernel_batch74b::deepseek_corresponding_author_note_is_kept`; package-bindings/
`fancy_page_style_a_package_gives_a_binding_class_selects_nothing`, guard
`perfect_kernel_batch95d::a_fancy_page_style_a_package_gives_a_binding_class_selects_nothing`.

### 940. A raw package's table stores are rerouted as a raw class's; a date's printed label names it; two dates of different roles are two (Perl: the shipped style is not read; elsarticle's binding keeps received and accepted, `\finalform` and `\availableonline` are undefined)

medima.sty:300-312 (2307.16262, under elsarticle) redefines `\received`, `\accepted` and adds `\finalform`,
`\availableonline`, `\communicated` as pure stores (`\def\received#1{\gdef\@received{#1}}`) that only its own
`\maketitle` reads, which the kernel refuses; K11 ran after a raw class only, so the five "Article history" lines were
lost (jcomp, prletters, ycviu, yjvci, cag, jasr and imsart.sty copies ship the shape under elsarticle: 17 census papers).
`\lx@package@loaded@raw` now runs `reroute_raw_package_stores` (frontmatter_stores.rs) — the table setters the package
defined itself (`store_setters::defined_by_a_raw_file`), rerouted as a class's, not its keywords environments, kernel
field setters or off-table stores — unless a raw class is being read (`store_setters::in_a_raw_class_read`, counted
around a `.cls` read raw in content.rs), whose end reroutes them with its title page known. The table gains
`finalform` → `\lx@add@date[role=revised]` and `availableonline` → `[role=published]` (the roles revtex4_support and
aipproc give them; received, accepted, communicated as before). Two siblings: a date store's label is read as a
classification's (`labelled_api`): `Received~\@received\par` names the date "Received" and the deposit takes the label
out with the store, where a lone "Received" paragraph stayed (a raw package under article, and a raw class) — not a
label that opens a parenthesis the store's line closes (jpsj2.cls's and ptptex.cls's `(Received \@recdate)`: the date
keeps the role's name, the deposit its "(Received )"); and a
replaceable entry is replaced only by one of the same role too (`frontmatter_clear_same_name`, as its seal key has it):
the unnamed `published` date was replaced by the unnamed `communicated` one. A label starts at a branch's `\else`/`\or`
too (`line_label_before`): medima.sty:322-347 prints each date in the `\else` branch of its emptiness test,
`\ifx\@finalform\@empty\relax\else \finalformhead~\@finalform\\ \fi`, and the head macro the file defined is read as
its text ("Received in final form", "Available online"; `\maketitle`'s run of the title page still checks it prints
there, `verify_title_page_labels`); when that branch holds no label before the store, the label is the one before
the whole test, which leaves the title page with it, `\fi` included (`Received: \ifx\@received\@empty--\else
\@received\fi` is "Received:", no "Received: –" left; `enclosing_conditional`). A label phrase ends at a `;` or a `,`
as at a sentence's end, and the separator leaves with its clause: pazha2.cls:166-167's `Received \@submitted; revised
\@revised; accepted \@accepted` names the dates "revised" and "accepted" (2408.01858, 2607.07582); a store right after
a separator has no label of its own (iaus.cls's `Proceedings IAU Symposium No. \@volume, \@pubyear`, 0707.3527: no
"\@volume," label read). A date's or
classification's label is read in any code the title page reaches (`ClassReaders::printed`), not only the code grown
into it: jasr.sty:449-466's `\elsarthistorybox` is printed by `\MaketitleBox`, which its uncalled `\pprintMaketitle`
calls too (:507), so it never grows (2311.02753, "Received"). Where no label is read, the role's default name
(`\lx@date@<role>@name`, `\lx@classification@name`) stands only when its word is the text a raw file's macro prints
right before the store (`ClassReaders::prints_default_name_before`, `text_right_before`: case and a trailing colon
aside, a parameterless macro read as its characters) — wiley2sp.cls:296-302's `\receivedname\ignorespaces\@received`,
`\def\receivedname{{\normalfont Received:}\ }` (1211.4450, 1306.2559: "Received "), zaa.cls:513-515's
`\AtEndDocument` hook `Received \rm\@received` (1902.07328), rose_v01.cls:259-260's `\text{Received}\hspace{1.5mm}
\@received` and `\text{revised}\hspace{1.5mm}\@revised` (0907.2032; a layout command's braced arguments print nothing)
—; otherwise the date or
classification has no name (`name={}`), never a role's default the class does not print (FIDELITY_CHARTER
2026-10-30): 95d named medima's final-form date "Revised " (2104.10903, 2307.16262); ujp.sty's `\pacs` (1906.11531,
under revtex4), printed as `\udkpacs~\udkpacsnum` ("PACS" through a macro that reads the store), is unnamed, not
"Classification: ". The bindings' own calls keep their defaults (revtex4_support, aipproc). A raw package's setter's own `\@<name>` is rerouted only when code that never runs here reads it, or no macro does
(`store_setter_body`, `ClassReaders::read_where_nothing_runs`): a macro reached from the title page's roots, a refused
definition (`\lx@dropped@<name>`) or a page style. rlj.sty:73's `\@keywords`, read only by the `\makeCover` 2605.31044
comments out, was invented as keywords (ycviu.sty's history dates too, read only by an `\articleinfobox` its title page
never calls, 2009.01540), and a store only a `\printkeywords` the document calls, a body `\printhistory` or an
`\AtEndDocument` hook prints was printed twice, frontmatter and body (csagh.sty 2305.10014, rlj.sty 2605.26012).
Reached, not grown (any reader, not every reader): cesj.sty's alternative title page `\cejpmaketitle` reads
`\@institute` as the refused `\cesjmaketitle` does (physics0510010), and requiring every reader to be title-page code
lost its affiliations. A raw class's own store — and a package's its read loads — is rerouted as before: the test lost
real class stores whose readers the survey does not follow (bfhlayout.sty:743-752's `\@titlefooterleft`, printed by a
scrlayer layer of bfhthesis.cls's title page, reads `\@department`/`\@institute`: DEMO-BFHThesis,
`perfect_kernel_batch61::bfh_thesis_stores_stay_affiliations`; dmtcs.cls's `\@keywords`, 0905.1102), so a class's
uncalled cover macro's store stays an item (RED `raw_class_store_only_an_uncalled_macro_reads_is_no_item`, rev95d p9).
A store no macro reads is still rerouted (astlb.cls:361-372 prints `\@shorttitle` only in a running head its top level
sets, 1202.2889's `<toctitle>`); rule (a)'s other store keeps its title-page-only test. Repros sectioning-frontmatter/
`raw_package_history_dates_are_the_frontmatter_dates` (medima's shape),
`raw_package_store_a_document_macro_prints_stays_in_the_body`, `raw_package_dates_printed_in_the_body_stay_there`,
`raw_class_dates_in_one_line_are_named_by_their_clauses`, `raw_package_history_box_a_shared_title_macro_prints_is_named`,
`raw_class_date_labelled_before_its_emptiness_test_is_named`, RED `raw_package_store_no_macro_reads_is_no_item` (a
package's store nothing reads is still an invented item, review rev95d-r2 probe qn); guards
`perfect_kernel_batch95d::raw_package_date_stores_are_the_frontmatter_dates` (elsarticle, an unlabelled date, article),
`perfect_kernel_batch95d::raw_package_store_other_code_prints_stays_where_it_prints`,
`perfect_kernel_batch95d::{raw_class_dates_in_one_line_are_named_by_their_clauses,
raw_package_history_box_a_shared_title_macro_prints_is_named, a_date_labelled_before_its_emptiness_test_is_named,
a_date_with_no_label_read_keeps_its_default_only_where_printed}`.

### 941. A table setter that prints a mark before its pure store is a store; the mark still prints (Perl: OmniBus's `\email`, the class unread)

astlb.cls:78 `\def\email#1{\textsuperscript{*}\gdef\@email{#1}}` (1202.2889; 10 of the 11 pazh/astl census papers:
astlb, pazhb, pazhb_eng, pazha2, pazhastl) is read only by `\endabstract`'s `\maketitle` (:176), which the kernel's
locked `{abstract}` never runs; K11's `pure_stores` refused the setter because the mark typesets, so the e-mail was lost
with 0 errors. `table_setter_stores` (frontmatter_stores.rs) also takes a table setter whose body is a printed mark of
the forms a marked line leads with (`leading_mark`, the extent-reporting form of `leading_mark_operand`:
`\textsuperscript{…}`, `\@textsuperscript{…}`, `\inst{…}`, `$^{…}$`) that does not use the argument, then a pure
store; the rerouted setter keeps the whole body, so the mark prints where it is called (inside `\author{…}`, at the
name) and the store goes to the table's call (`\lx@add@email`, read at `\maketitle` or the frontmatter's flush). Only
table setters; an off-table setter (`survey_off_table_stores`) still needs a pure store. Repro sectioning-frontmatter/
`mark_then_store_email_read_by_a_refused_abstract_red` (RED since DEL1, post-merge: the observer reads the rerouted
setter as the class's own e-mail command, `EmailMeaning::Own`, so the emitter writes the call `\email{…}` as an e-mail
item — its mark a contact "*" of its own, not the name's).

**The title code's marks in the rehearsal (LOSTF).** The pazh/astl title code defines `\address` and `\addresstext` only
in `\@maketitle`, where `\@author` expands (astlb.cls:117-118, pazhastl.cls:112: `\def\address##1{\textsuperscript{##1}}`,
`\def\addresstext##1##2{\footnotetext[##1]{\itshape ##2}}`). The digestion of the author content runs them (#983), but the
observer's rehearsal read the content without them: undefined, their arguments printed as text, and the reading took "1,"
and the institutes for names and affiliations — 1206.0451's S.Yu. Sazonov merged into an affiliation, "2 1Space Research
Institute" an affiliation of 1202.2889 and 1108.4222. Rule: the rehearsal reads the author content under the author
markup its digestion runs, a title-code definition among it where it reads arguments (`author_markup_begin`;
`title_code::reads_arguments`); a parameterless one stays undefined there, its held Error a piece's to take (#983's
aaai2026 `\co`: run in the rehearsal it moved 2508.08170 to a counter decline). PC3's exclusion of such definees from
`content::Field::held_undefined_at` is deleted: no Error is held at them. Still wrong (post-merge): the institutes notes go
to the block's last name, not by their marks. Repro `sectioning-frontmatter/astlb_title_code_address_marks_keep_the_names`;
guard `perfect_kernel_batchlostf::lost_frontmatter_content_is_kept`.

### 942. The observer writes IEEEtran, acmart, authblk and the MNRAS family, each behind its own gate; an entry's take-out e-mail is a change tag; the comparator reads the take-out (Perl: the old reader's output, no observer)

**What.** `written: true` for IEEEtran (`ieeetran_cls.rs`), authblk (`authblk_sty.rs`), and two new declarations in
the files whose `\author` they own: acmart (`acmart_cls.rs`, its comma-list `\author`, acmart.cls:1620-1621) and the
MNRAS family (`mn2e_support_sty.rs`, mn2e/mnras/mn; mnras.cls:1072-1079) — both the kernel's reading, no longer
`UNDECLARED`. elsarticle stays unwritten (its `\author` is elsart_support_core.sty's, which elsart_support shares with
OmniBus; its one wrong sample creator, 2308.13695, the reading gets wrong too). The writer declines per item, each
declined item left as today's output holds it (`writer` module docs): an entry whose address take-out today's does not
print so is given back whole (2102.08148's Hongyun Yu keeps today's entry while the other authors' are cut), and a plan
difference no operation explains (the ledger's `declined: …`) leaves every item of the plan as today's. No item an
unwritten family's call made is written: the call's setter, not the author block, decides (95b r3, below).

**Mechanisms.**
- `owner:entry-address` is a change tag (`resolver::CHANGE_TAGS`), as #938 names it: the writer writes every owner the
  take-out's chain decides — the entry's only carrier (`owner:only-carrier`) too, not only a spelled owner
  (0707.1008's `\IEEEauthorblockA{ETH Zurich\\ … Email: lapidoth@isi.ee.ethz.ch}`; 36 IEEEtran census papers).
- The comparator (`ab_audit fmshadow`) reads the take-out: today's affiliation whose printed addresses, read by the
  reading's own reader (`resolver::address_take_out`, `address_runs` + `strip_address_runs`), are all shadow e-mails
  tagged `owner:entry-address`, the rest the shadow's cut entry (or nothing), is one classified row (`compare::
  taken_out_rule`); an unbraced list sharing a domain (`\email{vsiyer, rajaln, …@uw.edu}`, 1812.09419, 1802.08365) is
  written out by the same reader (`written_out_rule`). IEEEtran unclassified 362 → 90 papers, acmart 21 → 2.
- A call's label as its source spells it (authblk's `\author[…]` keyval holding a backslash) is what it spells before
  its first command (`labels::parted_label`): `\author[3\authfn{2}]{Raul Ramos-Pollán}` is `3` (2405.16051: parted
  whole, its command's letters were labels and its argument's `2` a request of `\affil[1,2,4]`), `\author[1\thanks{…}]`
  `1` (2202.05736, 2410.10922). Never parting such a label lost those `1`s (95b r1, measured on the census).
- The writer never takes an item that prints, after its first ink, a mark its creator requests (`plan::later_marks`,
  `dom::later_marks`: an `ltx:sup` or a formula that is a mark): the reading labels an entry by its leading mark alone
  where a later symbol is glued to the word before it (`City$^\ddagger$Lab Y`), and taking the entry lost that name's
  own affiliation (2311.10290's Hongyang Chen, 2405.00230's Maximilian Schiffer under an unlabelled authblk `\affil`
  printing `\textsuperscript{2}`): declined, today's.
- The take-out's holders are remapped when `resolve` deletes a replaced `\author` call's creators (`resolver::resolve`):
  an anonymous-review `\author{Author Names Omitted…}` before the real one (2602.12633) left the last holder past the
  end — the writer's give-back panicked (Fatal `panic:caught`) — and every other holder named the creator after its own.
- The re-part (OD #928) is taken back when a written creator holds an element beside its name that today's creator did
  not (`repart::apply`): a name inside an ORCID link holding its logo (`\href{https://orcid.org/…}{\usebox{\orcid}
  \hspace{1mm}Patricia~Paskov}`, 2603.11001) was sliced into the personname and its link left beside it as well — the
  name printed twice, an `ltx:ref` child of `ltx:creator` the schema refuses (the off/on census's one schema-invalid
  paper). No guard of its own: the witness's trigger, a nested `\author\href{…}`, errs in our conversion (a
  `readBalanced` Error pdflatex does not raise), so no clean fixture reaches the re-part there.
- An entry's number is parted into digits only under single-digit numbering (`Resolver::part_glued_labels`, the entry
  side, the mirror of the names' side guard of 1501.05343): every other numbered entry label one digit, and every
  numbered mark the names show. 2207.06713 (mnras) prints `$^{15}$The Inter-University Institute … (IDIA)` under names
  marked up to 18, none 15: read as `1` + `5`, IDIA went to the 9 authors marked 1 or 5 (95b r1, review rev95b B1); it
  stays in the block, as int124b and the print have it. Symbol compounds part as before (2602.19190's
  `$^{\dagger\ddagger}$`, 1505.06831's `∗∗`). The kernel's and revtex's `$^{15}$` entry under names marked 1 and 5 (wrong
  in int124b too) now stays in the block as well.
- The comparator's take-out reading (`compare::taken_out_rule`) explains the block's rows as a creator's: today's
  block entry cut by the reading, with the shadow's cut entry it leaves, is one classified row (2106.15893's
  `\affil[$\star$]{… corresponding author: michaela.benz@…}`, written, was unclassified).
- An unwritten family's call is not written (95b r3). The writer required every author block's family `written`, not
  every API call's: 2609.05466 (svjour3 with authblk loaded) holds authblk's `\author` and svjour3's
  `\institute{N. Cuellar \and A. Pereira \and I. F. M. Menezes \at Pontifical Catholic University … \and A. Cunha~Jr
  \at National Laboratory …}`, which the reading, under authblk's conventions, numbers as entry 1 before `\at`
  (`api:labelseq ruling1:thenote`), and 95b wrote "N. Cuellar" onto all four authors. Each API call now records the
  binding of the frontmatter setter whose expansion made it (`ledger::ApiCall::binding`). The setters are `\email`,
  `\emailAdd`, `\institute`, `\address`, `\affil`, `\affiliation` and the stores' contact setters `\ead`,
  `\emailaddr`, `\affaddr`, `\department`, `\institution` (`ledger::FRONTMATTER_SETTERS`; not `\inst`, a mark
  request, whose inst_support.sty would watch every aa paper). A call is noted once its arguments are read
  (`Expandable::invoke`): the innermost setter whose expansion is still being read, by `gullet::input_unread_since`
  (`state::open_frontmatter_setter`), a robust setter's `\cs␣` too. The binding is the setter's owner as
  `note_binding_load` records it (OD #922), when that owner declared conventions (authblk's `\affil`, also under the raw
  pnas-new.cls that loads it, 1706.06282 and 2212.01357; sv_support.sty's `\institute`; aa.cls's own `\institute`).
  It is the class's family (`ledger::class_family`) when the owner is the kernel, a raw file's setter rerouted in place
  (OD #936, the kernel's gate, OD #925: 94b's `a_raw_class_in_place_address_is_the_api`) or a class binding declaring
  none (revtex4-2.cls's). That family is the first class binding to declare conventions, else the class's own `\author`
  binding (elsarticle's elsart_support_core.sty), else the kernel's. Another binding declaring none takes the family of
  the first binding its load loaded that declares (`ledger::LOADED`: `\documentstyle{revtex}`'s revtex3_support.sty,
  loaded by revtex.sty after the article class, is REVTeX's under the revtex4_support.sty it loads — cond-mat0505458,
  cond-mat9803141, hep-ph9909393, cond-mat0209515, hep-th0503100, hep-th9507063, nlin0207050 lost their written
  addresses on the scorer run without it). Any other owner keys a block's way: undeclared, not written. Each item of a call whose family is not written (`policy::family_written`) stays as today's holds it
  (`writer::keep_as_today`): its take-out and write-out are given back, and each item of its text is owned as today's
  owns it, none where today's holds none. The paper's other items are written: `iopart_address_with_authblk_kept_as_today`,
  authblk's take-out written beside iopart's `\address`. The whole paper is declined where a written item would depend
  on the unwritten reading: the names do not pair with today's (the re-part writes every item), or the call made a
  creator. The ledger says `declined: an unwritten family's items kept as today's` where the reading wanted them
  otherwise.
  The watch costs every macro call, so it starts only at a written family's block that finds an unwritten family's
  setter defined (`ledger::watch_unwritten_setters`); calls made before then are `unobserved`, not written. Unwatched,
  the expansion path costs +0.02-0.05 % instructions (1106.2670, 1103.4425; base noise ±0.03 %). Deleted in DEL5: once
  `Policy::written` went (DEL4) no family was unwritten, so the watch never started; the core's `FRONTMATTER_WATCH`,
  `state::open_frontmatter_setter` and `frontmatter_setter_calls`, `ApiCall::binding`, `AuthorBlock::setters_before`,
  `setter_binding`, `class_family`, `CLASS_AUTHOR`, `LOADED` and the nine setters' owner tracking went with it (output
  byte-identical).
  Not observed, so written under a written block as before: a binding's other commands (`\thanks`,
  `\IEEEauthorblockA`, elsarticle's `\cortext`), and a raw class's stores handed on at `\maketitle`
  (`frontmatter_stores::harvest_stores`, where no setter's expansion is open; SYNC row "unobserved frontmatter calls").
  Census (default mode; the five populations above, 3,697 papers, and the 419 authblk papers under other classes):
  against the int125a build the one byte-changed paper is 2609.05466 (creators now int124b's); no paper 95b r2 wrote is
  left as today's. Guard `perfect_kernel_batch95b::an_unwritten_familys_call_is_kept_as_today` (repros
  class-bindings/`svjour3_institute_names_at_with_authblk`, RED in 95b r2, and `iopart_address_with_authblk_kept_as_today`).
- Considered and dropped: an entry the call labels with a footnote symbol (`\affil[*]{Equal contribution}`) as a legend
  note like a symbol-led one (`api:legend`): seven sample papers' `\affil[*]{Corresponding author, …}` lost their
  affiliation and e-mail (2206.08826, 2403.17178, 2409.13995, 2503.00537, 2603.05201, 2608.03927, 2106.04144); such an
  entry stays the starred names' affiliation (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 ruling 2, "affiliation or legend alike").

**Gate (OD #837 S2b; shadow census over seeded populations, `census/who_uses.py --sample all --cap 1000 --seed 95`).**
Unclassified, with the comparator reading the take-out: IEEEtran 90 of 973 papers (9.3 %), acmart 2 of 72 with a block
(2.8 %; 774 of 873 make each author one API call, no block), authblk 58 of 814 (7.1 %), MNRAS mn2e 9 of 363 (2.5 %),
mnras 30 of 458 (6.6 %); elsarticle 23 of 881 (2.6 %, not written). Above the 0.5 % rule, as aa (3.2 %), llncs
(5.4 %) and the kernel (19.4 %) were when written (#922, #925). An unclassified row marks an item the writer may
decline, not the paper: on the review's sample (rev95b) 24 of authblk's 59 unclassified papers were written in their
other items, IEEEtran 18 of 94, mn2e 3 of 9, acmart 2 of 7, each read and improved. After 95b r2 (the comparator
reading the block's take-out rows, over the same census dumps): unclassified IEEEtran 89 of 973 (9.2 %), acmart 2 of 72
(2.8 %), authblk 47 of 814 (5.8 %; 58 before, the block cuts now classified), mn2e 9 of 363 (2.5 %), mnras 30 of 458
(6.6 %); re-resolved with the entry digit guard, IEEEtran and authblk the same (acmart and the MNRAS family cannot be
re-resolved: their dumps predate their declarations, `stale_conventions`).
