### 943. A per-author class's marked names line is a list by its marks; a line its marks do not cover stays whole and its marked names are a reported merge (Perl: the binding's `\author` kept whole, its kernel marked branch splits at every comma)

**What.** The per-author bindings' cautious split (`split_author_line_cautious`, author_block/names_split.rs: aastex,
amsart, revtex, an IEEE block, a labelled authblk `\author`) splits a names line where it reads as two or more names
(`name_count`, 63e) or, now, where each of its two or more pieces (`split_author_line`) carries its own mark after the
name (`marked_after_name`) and none reads as an affiliation (`reads_as_affiliation`): `marked_names`. A wrapper or a
whole-line group holding the names reads the same way (`reads_as_name_list`, the gate of `names_in_wrapper` and of the
whole-line group's descent). `name_count` needs every comma part `name_shaped`, so one name of a shape it does not know
(`N.~in der Wiesche`: `in` is no `NAME_PARTICLES` word; `P. v. Brentano`, `Benjamin Rouillé d'Orfeuil`, `J.J.M. in 't
Zand`) made a whole marked list one creator, silently — 2410.11607's 672 BESIII names (dev), the holdout's
`name:unmatched` shape (52 papers, 2,189 creators on int123a). Perl 0.8.8 keeps the revtex `\author` whole
(revtex4_support.sty.ltxml:46), so the merge is PERL-ORIGIN; Perl's own kernel marked branch splits a marked names line
at every comma (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:708, `SplitTokens($line, T_OTHER(','))`), which this reads as cautiously as the
marks allow. The resolver already reads it so (`joined_single_name` joins no names with marks between them).

**The merge report.** A line the marks do not cover — a piece without its mark (`A.~Able$^{1}$, B.~in der Baker,
C.~Cole$^{1}$`; reversed names `Surname, I.\altaffilmark{1}`, 1903.10014), or one reading as an affiliation (`and the
XYZ Team`; `M.~Huertas-Company\altaffilmark{1}`, 1212.4143, whose "Company" is a `NON_NAME_WORDS` word) — stays one
creator as before; when two or more of its pieces are marked names (counted inside a whole-line group too) the line
carries their count (Rust-only `\lx@author@merged@names{N}`, author_macros.rs, setting `_mergednames` on the creator)
and `flag_merged_creators` raises `Error:frontmatter:merged_creators` ("One author holds N names", N the marked names,
a lower bound). A creator the observer's writer makes again from its reading carries no count (`creator_attributes`
copies no `_` attribute): a line it re-parts raises nothing.

**Census** (95b r3 → 97a, `--preload=ar5iv.sty --nocomments`; the populations hold no holdout id): revtex marked
one-`\author` papers (`who_uses.py --class 'revtex*' --glob --feature author_marks --and --nauthor 1`, 771 converted):
759 byte-identical, 12 changed, E 527 → 527, F 2 → 2, no word lost — 2003.03705 2 → 492 creators, 2307.12736 2 → 625,
2401.13225 2 → 650 (BESIII), nucl-ex0410037 1 → 14, hep-ph9710228 1 → 3, and seven whose writer re-part gave way to the
kernel split their name-shaped siblings take (0903.4816, 1104.4729, 1309.6958, 2210.16528, cond-mat0007048: the same
creators with the marks shown as printed and `before`; 1310.0383, 1809.06333: `before` and ids only). aastex marked
papers (294): 291 identical, 1010.1733 1 → 59, 1706.03320 1 → 11, astro-ph0408436 1 → 13, and two new
`merged_creators` Errors, both real merges kept as before (1212.4143, 1903.10014). amsart marked papers (235): all
byte-identical. IEEE blocks with marks (`--term cs:IEEEauthorblockN --feature author_marks`, 674): 668 identical,
2201.10426 1 → 4 creators (each its affiliation and e-mail), 2204.09839 1 → 6, three the kernel split their name-shaped
siblings take (2509.10689 shows its `1\textsuperscript{st}` ordinal and marks as printed; 1509.06333, 1712.07369,
1901.07422 `before`), and two new reported merges kept as before: 1012.4815 (an `\IEEEauthorblockN` left open over its
`\IEEEauthorblockA`s, the last piece reading as an institution), 2508.04092 (two names without a mark). Where today's
token split replaces the writer's re-part, the marks a name prints stay shown on it (the kernel's convention for the
name-shaped list too) — the writer's re-part hides them. Dev witnesses: 2410.11607 1 named creator → 672 (30 sampled against pdflatex: each name and the
affiliations its answered marks name), hep-ex9611002 1 → 70 (REVTeX 3, `E.~M.~Aitala,$^9$`); of the 17 dev revtex
papers with ≥ 20 marks in one `\author`, the other 15 (1903.04164, 1706.04100, hep-ex0312016, 1311.5347,
nucl-ex9903010, 0708.2014, …) byte-identical. Frontmatter scorer (the whole 3,000 sample, `fm_scorer/run_97a` against
the base binary): three papers' output changed — 1311.0586 (aastex, 1 → 7 creators), 2604.10787 (IEEEtran, the marked
`1\textsuperscript{st} … $^\dagger$` block 1 → 3 creators; its block with an unmarked name stays one), 2311.14729
(`before` only); D3 98.18 % → 98.18 % (6,044 of 6,156), lost-words papers 0 → 0.

**Left.** In 2410.11607: the `75A,75C` marks (institute 75's `(A)…; (B)…` parts) unanswered, their institutes one
nameless creator; the collaboration line welded into the last name (OPEN_ROWS.md:810 ruling); a mark-covered list with a
`NON_NAME_WORDS` word in a surname stays whole (F3, the word lists). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch97a` (three; since HG1/HG1b four rows of
`perfect_kernel_batchhg1::hollow_guards_restored_read_as_printed`, the module removed); repros
sectioning-frontmatter/`author_marked_list_lowercase_particle_merges` (the merge GREEN; its separators RED,
`author_marked_list_keeps_its_printed_separators_red`),
`author_marked_list_with_an_unmarked_name_is_a_reported_merge`, `author_marked_names_beside_a_team_move_their_and_red`.

### 944. A take-out removes what it read and nothing else TeX prints: aa's `\mail` labelled as its copy prints it, an emptied entry's label kept, a store's label read before its printed occurrence, a marked split's separators kept (Perl: `\mail` always "Correspondence to " as an address; no take-out, no K11, no marked split)

**What** (brief 97b; the int125b A/B's `fm_checks.py` losses against int123a). One principle over four mechanisms: a
take-out keeps every printed word of what it removes that is neither the item's value nor the label it took — as the
item's label, or left in place.

- **aa `\mail`** (aa_support_sty.rs). Perl labels it `\lx@add@address[name={\mailname}]` under every copy
  (aa_support.sty.ltxml:118-119). The copy the paper ships decides, read off its code: a copy naming `\mailname` (aa.cls
  v4.03-v7.0, `\footnotetext[0]{\kern-\bibindent\mailname\ \ignorespaces\@mail}`, 1005.3784 :272, :466-468) keeps the
  label; one without it (v8 on, `\newcommand*\mail[1]{\renewcommand*\aa@mail{#1}}`, read by nothing: 2007.14739
  :965-966) prints neither the address nor a label, and the item has none (`name={}`, FIDELITY_CHARTER §4). No copy
  shipped: Perl's label. `\mailname`'s `\it` is in a group, as aa.cls's `{\it Correspondence to\/}`: Perl's unbraced
  `\it` set every frontmatter item after `\mail` in italic (2012.11607's names and affiliations, the date). Its text is
  aa.cls's own `\def\mailname{{\it Correspondence to\/}:}` (the one definition of every copy that has it, 129 of the 434
  `\mail` papers: 0705.1240, 1005.3784, 0805.1001), not Perl's colonless `\it Correspondence to \/`, with no copy shipped
  too (1209.2606: no TL aa.cls, the class the paper was written for prints the colon); the space after it is the print
  code's (`\mailname\ \ignorespaces\@mail`), so `\mail`'s name is `{\mailname\ }`: "Correspondence to: " (MB2, review
  revMB1 P2; the join's space, #992).
- **The writer's take-out of an entry it empties** (observer/emitter/plan.rs `cut_entry_addresses`, `holder_label`).
  95c cut an affiliation-kind entry printing only addresses and named each e-mail contact by the label word the cut took,
  else the class default, so the `\mail` holder's "Correspondence to " was printed nowhere (1005.3784, 0805.1001, …).
  The emptied entry's own `name` now goes to its contacts, before the cut's label word (0805.1001's
  `\mail{e-mail: …}`: "Correspondence to e-mail: "), unless it is its role's default (`get_frontmatter_name`:
  1506.05709's "Affiliation: " is no printed label). Where no contact would carry it — every address of the entry
  already an e-mail contact of its owner, from another print (1005.3784's `\institute{… \email{x}}`, astro-ph0107243's
  `email: x` beside `\mail{x}`) — the entry is given back whole (writer/mod.rs `give_back_entries`), as int123a held it.
- **A K11 store's label** (frontmatter_stores.rs). The label reader (`ClassReaders::label_in`, `line_label_before`)
  skips an occurrence of the store inside an argument TeX does not typeset (`in_unprinted_argument`, `argument_of`, by
  the `PRINTED_ARGUMENTS` / `UNPRINTED_ARGUMENTS` tables: `\href`'s target) and walks back through
  the commands that print the store alone (`\href`'s text, `\textcolor`'s, now in `PRINTED_ARGUMENTS`), so
  acl2023.sty:186's `Correspondence: \href{mailto:\@corremail}{\textcolor{black}{\@corremail}}` reads "Correspondence:"
  (2506.10896). The same walk passes a `\parbox`'s printed argument (its width, a `[t]` before it, unprinted), so
  jpsj2.cls:789-818's `KEYWORDS:\hskip.5em\parbox[t]{330\p@}{\@kword}` names the keywords "KEYWORDS:", the class's
  printed label, where they had the role's default "Keywords: " (416 of the int125a bundle population's papers,
  0704.0082, 0809.3084, cond-mat0605318; FIDELITY_CHARTER §4), and an off-table store printed as `G:\href{mailto:\@vg}{\@vg}`
  is named "G:" (guard `perfect_kernel_batch77i::store_label_is_printed_text_not_a_link_target_or_key`, unnamed before). A note store's label (`\lx@add@frontmatter{ltx:note}`: `corremail`, `corraddress`, `fundinginfo`,
  `authornote`) now leads the note's text, as a token register's note's does (`toks_store`): the schema's `ltx:note`
  has no `name` (LaTeXML-meta.rnc:27-35). It is checked by `verify_title_page_labels` as a date's is. Before, a labelled
  note store was handed on unlabelled and its emptiness test (`\ifx\@corremail\empty\else … \fi`) left the title page
  with it, taking the label.
- **The marked-list split** (author_block/names_split.rs `with_printed_separators`). 97a's split of a per-author
  class's names line by its marks gave each creator the binding's `before` (revtex: the kernel's space), so
  hep-ph9710228's `de Melo$^a$ , Naus$^b$ and Frederico$^c$` printed "and" nowhere. Each piece after the first now
  carries the separator printed before it (`\lx@author@printed@before`, author_macros.rs, `_printedbefore`), which
  place.rs's creator punctuation takes over `\lx@author@sep`/`\lx@author@conj`; a separator that is no plain text
  (`\and`, a macro) leaves the binding's. A piece that is an address and no name is no marked name (`marked_names`,
  `only_addresses`: review rev97a S1), so `A.~Able$^{1}$, B.~in der Baker$^{2}$, b.baker@two.edu$^{*}$` is one creator
  and a reported merge; a name with its e-mail command beside it (imsart's `\snm{Dalmasso}\textsuperscript{1,}\ead{…}`,
  2107.03920; emulateapj's `\authoremail{…}`, astro-ph9812176) is still one.

**Left.** A line the names' shape splits (63e) keeps the binding's `before` (`\author{Ann Able, Bob Baker and Cat Cole}`
under revtex4: before="  ", as int123a); the writer's re-part writes no `before`. Two prints of one address with two
labels — `\institute{… email: x}` and `\mail{x}`, the institute's run cut first by key order — keep one contact and one
label (95c's order). A store-affiliation e-mail legend after empty-math spacing lines is one affiliation of the last name
(2508.08560, RED `store_affiliation_email_legend_after_spacing_lines`). A label part the deposit takes out of the first
place its tokens stand: jpsj2.cls prints its keywords line in five option branches, the first (two-column) not the one
run, so the printed "KEYWORDS:" stays in the body beside the name (int125b the same, beside "Keywords: "). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch97b` (five; two since HG1 the REDs below, their counts and right parts rows of
`perfect_kernel_batchhg1::reds_keep_their_counts_and_right_parts`); changed, to the printed label or separator: 97a's
`marked_list_with_an_unknown_name_shape_is_a_list` (deleted in HG1; its revtex, grouped and amsart cases are rows of
`perfect_kernel_batchhg1::hollow_guards_restored_read_as_printed`, which pin today's lost separators — before="  " for
", ", amsart's " and " for ", and" — citing RED `author_marked_list_keeps_its_printed_separators_red` and
`author_marked_list_amsart_comma_and_keeps_its_comma_red`),
`raw_class_stores_reroute_to_frontmatter::jpsj2_stores_become_frontmatter` ("KEYWORDS:"),
`perfect_kernel_batch77i::store_label_is_printed_text_not_a_link_target_or_key` ("G:");
repros sectioning-frontmatter/`aa_mail_printing_copy_keeps_its_label`, `aa_mail_storing_copy_has_no_label`,
`aa_mail_repeated_address_stays_labelled`, `raw_package_note_label_before_a_link_names_it`,
`author_marked_list_keeps_its_printed_separators_red` (RED → GREEN 97b → RED int160a, HG1),
`author_marked_email_piece_is_no_person_red` (RED → GREEN 97b → RED int160a, HG1).

### 945. An affiliation the reading already has reaches its author: a block entry is cut by its whole span, llncs's one institute cut at its marks stays every author's, svproc's `\institute` is sv_support's (Perl: no observer, the names line split at its "and"; llncs's whole institute on the first author; svproc's per author through OmniBus's inst_support)

**What** (brief 97c; the dev20k census of `own:aff_missing`, 364 creators in 119 papers). Three mechanisms in which the
reading or the binding was already right and a span, a share rule or an override discarded it.

- **A block entry's span** (observer/resolver/blocks.rs `labelled_entries`). A mark-led entry of a names block whose
  words an inner `and` or comma parts into several events took its first event's span alone, so the writer's cut
  (emitter/plan.rs `span_tokens`: the span's letters must be the entry's key) failed — "a block line does not cut" — and
  the whole line stayed the first mark's name's: `\author{Ann Able$^{1}$ Bob Baker$^{3}$\\ $^{1}$Univ of Science and
  Technology~~~~$^{3}$Univ C}` gave Ann "Univ of Science and Technology 3Univ C", Bob nothing. The span is now its first
  event's start to its last ink's end, as a joined name's (`joined_single_name`). Witnesses 2111.07950, 1503.06795,
  2504.05692 (its nameless extra creator gone), 2008.02300, 2404.01856; 2212.01433, 2608.06741 (W1b, the same cause).
  The cut now acts where the reading parted an entry wrongly and the decline had hidden it: a digit mark glued inside a
  word (`$^1$NLP$^2$CT Lab, Univ X`, 2603.20851) is the word's in the reading too (events/lexer.rs `glue_in_word_marks`,
  as today's `rewrite_in_word_superscripts`), so the paper is declined as before (its key keeps the 2, today's not) —
  only when the source glues it (`glued_in_source`: nothing but the mark's math shifts between it and the names), so a
  mark after a `\break` still opens the next entry (`\address{{$^1$… Russia\break $^2$Nuclear …}}`, hep-ph9809222,
  whose three addresses the first reading made one of every author; its article twin, both entries one of Ann in 97b, is
  now each name's).
- **llncs's one `\institute` cut at its marks** (llncs_cls.rs `\lx@llncs@institute@sup`, shape (c): no `\and`, a
  superscript in it). Its split (defs/frontmatter_api/affiliations.rs `affiliation_calls`) labels every entry by its mark and
  dropped the call's `labelseq`, so the line no mark labels (`\institute{Univ A, Town \\ \textsuperscript{*}Equal
  contribution}`) was an unlabelled affiliation of the last author, where llncs.cls:868-886 prints it unnumbered under
  every name. The call now passes `labelseq=affiliation,_share=authors,_markpiece=true` for an entry with no mark and no
  footnote symbol leading it (`unmarked_attr`), which `\lx@llncs@institute@sole`'s rule shares (`share_row_contacts`,
  OD #901; the reading's `api:share:authors`). `_markpiece`: a number an author shows by hand other than 1 does not make
  such a piece "several institutes" (`marks_pick`, `share_unpicked`) — it labels a sibling piece (`\institute{Skoltech,
  Moscow, Russia\\ $^1$Aeronet, $^2$ADASE\\ \mailsc}`, 1905.07852, whose shared line had been Ann's today and the block's
  in the reading, the writer then declining and its e-mails lost). Perl puts the whole institute, legend included, on
  the first author (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1195's fallback). Witnesses 2603.18089, 2608.22772 (its e-mails moved from a
  nameless creator to their authors), 2207.13038, 2609.31726, 1905.07852.
- **svproc** (latexml_contrib svproc_cls.rs). The contrib binding defined `\institute` as a document `<note
  role=institute>` (since the 2026-05-21 parity import, no witness), overriding sv_support's split, so no author held an
  affiliation. It no longer does: sv_support's `\institute` stands, split at `\and`, each piece answered by `\inst{n}`,
  as Perl's (no svproc binding: OmniBus's inst_support, inst_support.sty.ltxml:36-38). On sv_support's split alone an
  `\email` in a piece inherits its label, as svjour3's and Perl's (2409.01900's address list on every `\inst{1}`
  author) — against FIDELITY_CHARTER §4, which gives an address to the author it spells (review rev97cd C1: 2101.04527,
  2206.03859, 1911.11805, 2102.01452, 2404.15833, 2505.18180, 2507.18248 each had an address on a non-owner on 97c
  alone). It lands only with OD #948 (sv_support observer-written), whose writer places each address by its spelling:
  on 97c + 97e none of the seven shares an address and each gains its affiliations (base: none). Witnesses 2101.04527,
  2504.04157, 2206.03859, 1911.11805, 2409.01900.

**Measured** (97b → 97c). Bundle population int125a, 28,354 papers: 70 changed (50 in the frontmatter), Errors and
Fatals equal once the timeouts are rerun alone, no creator merged or lost, no frontmatter word lost (`fm_checks.py`: the
marks' digits and letters left the names, 13 papers); llncs with `\institute` 686 papers, 1 changed (1910.10296); svproc
17 of 17 changed (21 with the `styles/svproc` copies): 16 gain their authors' affiliations. Scorer, the 3,000 sample:
archival 98.18 → 98.36 %, lost-words papers 0 → 0, R2 papers 7 → 5. The dev census's 146 `aff_missing` papers: 81
creators right that were not (18 papers), none the other way.

**Left.** (a) Two group-wrapped entry lines do not cut: `\author{Ann Able$^{1}$ \quad Bob Baker$^{2}$ \quad Cy
Cole$^{3}$ \\ \textnormal{$^{1}$Univ A \quad $^{2}$Univ B} \\ \textnormal{$^{3}$Univ C}}` gives Ann "Univ A 2Univ B" (one
such line cuts; 2609.38081, W1b's third witness). (b) llncs's legend line before the institute: `\institute{
\textsuperscript{*}Equal contribution \\ Univ A, Town}` — the unmarked line continues the legend entry, Ann's
"Equal contributionUniv A, Town", Bob none (97b the same). (c) svproc's sole institute (no `\and`) is sv_support's
unlabelled piece, the block's (OD #159), with an `\email` in it: `\author{Ann Able \and Bob Baker}\institute{Univ A,

of its five addresses lost or moved off their authors. (d) The in-word digit's paper is still declined (its key). (e) A

### 946. A collaboration or team named in the author line is a `contact role="collaboration"` on the names it covers, no creator and no part of a name (Perl: a piece of the names, welded into the last name, or a creator; aastex's `\collaboration` alone a contact)

**What** (brief 97d; FIDELITY_CHARTER §4, user ruling 2026-11-01). An author call's collaboration is read out of its
names and becomes the contact Perl's aastex binding makes of `\collaboration{n}{name}`
(aas_support.sty.ltxml:126, `\lx@add@contact[role=collaboration,annotate=new]`), on the names it covers
(author_block/collaborations.rs, wired into `add_authors_calls_sectioned`, dispatch.rs).

- **Recognition** (`reads_as_collaboration`, from the piece's words, by the existing `NON_NAME_WORDS` machinery): its
  name ends with a collaboration word (`COLLABORATION_WORDS`: collaboration(s), consortium/consortia) or with a team word
  (`TEAM_WORDS`: team(s), group(s), experiment(s)) the line frames — "the", "for", "on behalf of", "representing",
  brackets, dashes (`Framing`) — or a names line lists with "and" (`… and LHD experimental group$^{2}$`, 1711.07097); on
  a line of its own a team word only by more than a bare "the" (`collaboration_line_framing`: `The Robotics Group`, `the
  Applied Mathematics Group` under a name are its institution's); an unframed one whose address goes on under it is an
  employer's line, an affiliation (`collaboration_line_before`: 2501.13770's `\textit{WIDE Consortium}\\ \.Zabbar\\
  Malta`, as the next column's `\textit{ACURRAENT UG}\\ Frankfurt (Oder)`); a line ending in "and" or "&" and the line
  under it that together name one are one line (`joined_collaboration`: 1210.5341's `the \textit{Fermi} Pulsar Search
  Consortium and \\ the \textit{Fermi} Pulsar Timing Consortium` one contact); no word before it names an
  institution (`The ATLAS Collaboration Office, CERN`, `Theory Group, Department of …` stay affiliations; an unframed
  `Machine Learning Group` line too, 2205.00756); a lowercase word only right before the collaboration word (no sentence,
  and no name the text runs into: 0907.0548's `Monica Brigida\\on behalf of the \emph{Fermi}-LAT Collaboration`).
  Brackets holding a name opening with "The" and no institution word are one too (`(The Nearby Supernova Factory)`,
  1511.01102). A name the collaboration follows is a name and its remark (`name_and_remark`: `J.~Zapatero$^{5}$ (The
  MAGIC Collaboration)`, 0910.4381; `Bob Baker for the ATLAS Collaboration`), the name's annotations the remark holds
  moved onto the name (`name_takes_annotations`: 1408.0414's `(for the ALICE\fnref{col1} Collaboration)`, whose
  `\fnref` in the contact asked for a label no creator answers); a heading before a colon is one too
  (`heading_and_name`: `Euclid Collaboration: Y.~Fu…`). The pieces the names split parted are put together first
  (`names_and_collaborations`: `for the XYZ` + `ABC Collaborations`; `ATLAS`, `CDF`, `CMS` and `D0 Collaborations`,
  1311.7305). A piece the commas alone part from the names is none (`reads_as_listed_collaboration`: framed or listed
  with "and"; revtex's `\collaboration{Fermilab Lattice, HPQCD, and MILC Collaborations}`, 2412.18491, stays one
  creator, as Perl's `\author{#1}` makes it; nor is an unframed collaboration listed with "and" after unmarked names,
  which may be the whole line's one name: `\collaboration{Fermilab Lattice and MILC Collaborations}`, 1211.0751,
  1411.1651), and beside a collaboration piece every other piece must read as one name (`Content \& Services Team`,
  2109.03031). The plural and `experiment` forms are added to `NON_NAME_WORDS`.
- **Where.** A piece of a names line (`collaboration_split`, before the cautious and the kernel split; the piece carried
  as `\lx@author@collaboration{…}`, defined as its text for a reader that does not know it); a line of the block under
  the names (`collaboration_line`, at the weld site of the marked block — Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:700-701 welded it into
  the last name — and among an unmarked block's lines); an unmarked line of the marked block where an author stands, or
  an `\and` group that is only a collaboration, before names of the call (a heading). A per-author class's line is read
  so only when every other piece reads as one name, by its shape or its mark (97a's list by its marks); a call naming
  only a collaboration keeps it the author it is (`\author{The ATLAS Collaboration}`).
- **Coverage** (`Collaborations`; `annotate=N`, the names counted where it is read): one after names covers the names of
  its `\and` group made since the group's last collaboration (the names before a bracketed remark, not those after it:
  0910.4381's 144 MAGIC names, not the six of other teams — Perl's `annotate=new`, the authors before it that carry
  none, kept to the call); a heading every name after it in the call, once when the same collaboration closes them
  (2212.06489's `\center BESIII Collaboration\\~\\ … J.~Zu$^{68,55}$ (BESIII Collaboration)`), as does one ending in a
  colon (`Tam\'as Cs\"org\H{o}$^{4}$, for the TOTEM Collaboration:\\ G.~Antchev …`, 1204.5689); one right after
  another, no name between, covers the same names (`… I.C. Luhmann$^7$, the ASDEX Upgrade Team and the EUROfusion MST1
  Team$^*$`, 1603.09150), within one `\and` group (`close_group` forgets the last: a collaboration opening the next
  group heads its own names); a trailing `\and` group naming only a collaboration, marked or not, covers every name before
  it that carries none (`annotate=new`, `Collaborations::finish`). The contact's text is
  the piece as written, without the layout around it and the affiliation marks on it (a footnote symbol it shows
  stays).
- **Order.** Each contact is made where its collaboration prints among the creator's other contacts (they render in
  document order, LaTeXML-structure-xhtml.xsl:795): a line under the names in the last name's content at its line's
  place (0910.2149's `On Behalf Of The ATLAS Collaboration \\ University of Wisconsin` the collaboration, then the
  institution; hep-ex0011032), a names-line piece after the name before it, a heading's in each name's content
  (`annotate=1`) after the name's words and before the notes it carries (`heading_place`: 1204.5689's
  `G.~Antchev\footnote{INRNE-BAS…}` under `for the TOTEM Collaboration:`), after the whole name when the name makes its
  creator itself. The kernel's `\lx@add@contact` in a creator's content is no name text (`visible_name_text`): its words
  ran into the name's last ("WestXYZ") and iopart's `\ead{awest@…}`, placed by the names' words, went to a nameless
  creator (1612.09318).
- **A name making its creator itself** (PoS's `\speaker`, `\lx@add@creator[role=speaker]`) takes the marks after it into
  that creator's content (`marks_into_own_creator`), and as the call's one name its e-mail lines by a label of its own
  (`placed_label`), in print order: 1508.03930's `\speaker{Lukas Nellen}$^a$ for the HAWC collaboration$^b$` gives the
  speaker his affiliation and e-mail (97b: the pseudo-creator "for the HAWC collaboration"; Perl a nameless author), the
  `$^b$` line no author's mark answers the block's; 1708.04166's and 1211.0751's speakers their affiliations.
- **The observer's reading agrees** (resolver/lines.rs `names_line_events`, resolver/mod.rs `attach`), so the writer
  compares like with like: a names-line piece or a name's remark reading as a collaboration is a `collaboration` contact
  on the line's names since its last one, its mark no name's; an unlabelled line of the block reading as one is the
  owners' collaboration — not a class's affiliation command holding one (revtex's `\affiliation{(WA98 Collaboration)}`,
  0708.2630, an affiliation of today's and the reading's alike). Probes 97b → 97d writer outcomes: the team piece, the bracketed remark, the speaks-for tail, the
  line under marked names `same`; the heading shapes, `for the XYZ` + `ABC Collaborations` and a remark line under one
  name (resolver/blocks.rs, batch 97c's) and a colon heading `declined: the creators' names`, today's XML kept — the
  reading does not split `JLQCD Collaboration: S.~Aoki$^1$` (hep-lat0212039: today's names keep revtex's visible marks
  where the writer had re-parted them), as it cannot tell it from one inside a box today's keeps whole
  (`\parbox{\textwidth}{\Large{ MAGIC Collaboration: K.~Abe$^{1}$, …}}`, 2601.03873, which the writer re-parts). The
  reader's colon is the line's own, outside every group (`MeerKLASS Collaboration\thanks{Corresponding authors:}:
  Matilde …`, 2407.21626: cut inside the note, the pieces' braces did not close — a Fatal the A/B found).

**Why.** Perl keeps the piece in the names: one creator for 1708.04166's 15 names `… and the GAPS Team`, the line
welded into the last name for 2410.11607's `\\ (BESIII Collaboration)\\`, `Bob Baker for the XYZABC Collaborations` for
`Bob Baker$^{2}$ for the XYZ and ABC Collaborations`; 97a's list by its marks read the piece as an affiliation and kept
the whole line one creator with `Error:frontmatter:merged_creators` (2212.06489, 582 names). Dev witnesses 97b → 97d:
2212.06489 3 creators + 1 Error → 582 named (+ the 97a nameless one), each with the BESIII contact, 0 Errors;
1708.04166 2 → 16; 1711.07097 1 (+1 Error) → 11; 1311.7305 1 → 2; 1905.11825 and hep-ph0502212 the line out of the
last name; 0910.4381 1 (149 names) → 150, its six unseparated non-MAGIC names one reported merge; 1511.01102 the line
every name's affiliation → their collaboration.

**Left.** aa's own `\and` split (`\lx@splitting`, aa_cls.rs) reads no `\and` piece that is only a collaboration (`\small
H.E.S.S. Collaboration \and …`, 1912.05868), nor a heading over the pieces after its own (llncs `\author{XYZ
Collaboration: Ann Able\inst{1} \and Bob Baker\inst{2}}`: Bob Baker carries none) — since 103b each piece's own
collaboration is read (`split_author_calls`, below) —; the IEEE block reader reads none
(`\IEEEauthorblockN{J.K. de Jong\IEEEauthorrefmark{2}for the MINOS collaboration.}`, 1111.2718); a lone `\author{The ATLAS and CMS Collaborations}` under svjour3 stays two creators (RED
`author_collaboration_name_with_and_stays_one`); the reading's heading over later lines and its line under one name
(resolver/blocks.rs). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch97d` (nine); changed, to the contact: `perfect_kernel_batch94a` (five:
`what_a_name_held_is_written_where_the_reading_puts_it`, `a_bracket_holds_its_and`, `a_bracket_after_a_mark_is_the_names`,
`a_name_speaking_for_a_collaboration_is_a_name`, `an_institution_stops_at_a_person`), `perfect_kernel_batch97a` (three
then; `marked_names_beside_an_affiliation_are_a_reported_merge` now `marked_names_beside_a_team_are_a_list_and_its_collaboration`,

pinning B. in der Baker's moved " and ", RED `author_marked_names_beside_a_team_move_their_and_red`), `perfect_kernel_batchfms2a2` (two readings: `address_lists_in_author_order_and_collaborations`,
`an_unmarked_line_under_a_run_of_names_rows_is_every_names`), `perfect_kernel_batch77t::
role_and_note_lines_are_no_unmarked_institution` (its "for the ATLAS Collaboration" line). Repros

**Round 2** (review rev97cd). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch97d` (seven more: `collaboration_line_is_made_where_it_prints`,

### 947. The declarations around an author block's alignment environment go with it, and spacing after its close is no part of the block; AASTeX's `\affiliation` is REVTeX's (Perl: one creator per `\author`, the block kept whole; aastex's affiliation the last author's)

**What** (brief 97f; dev giant-list census M1, M3). Two author-block readings.

- **The wrapper around a whole-block alignment environment** (`unwrap_alignment_environment`, author_block/
  separators.rs). The environment that wraps a whole author block or an `\and` group (`center`, `flushleft`,
  `flushright`, already read through) is now found through the declarations around it: a declaration environment
  (`\begin{small}`, latex.ltx `\begingroup\small`; any font or size switch of `NAME_TEXT_COMMANDS` that takes no
  argument, and `\centering`/`\raggedright`/`\raggedleft`/`\noindent`/`\par`: `is_wrapping_declaration`), a group
  opening with them (`{\small …}`), bare ones before it (`\small\bfseries\begin{center}…`), and leading spacing
  (`leading_spacing_end`). After the wrapper's `\end{…}` only spacing may follow (`only_spacing`:
  `\end{center}\vspace{0.4cm}`); the same holds for an environment set under the names
  (`trailing_alignment_environment_as_lines`: `… Bob Baker \begin{center}Department of Physics\end{center}\vspace{2mm}`).
  Not `prints_nothing`, which passes an `\end{…}` closing what opened before the names: 2012.14750's
  `\author{\author{Author list} \begin{small}\begin{center}…\end{center}\vspace{0.6cm}\end{small}}` then left its
  `\begin{small}` open in a names line (two Errors; it stays as in 97d).
  The declarations are peeled only on the way to an alignment environment: a declaration wrapper with none inside keeps
  its declarations on the names as before (`\author{\begin{small}Ann Able$^{1}$ \\ $^{1}$Univ A\end{small}}`, each
  name `fontsize="90%"`), and a command that prints (`\lead\begin{center}…`) is no declaration. The size or font such a
  wrapper set is dropped with it — a cosmetic loss (the names and their contacts are the content; `90%` on a
  personname is no semantic markup), against one creator holding an `<inline-block>` of the whole list.
- **AASTeX's `\affiliation`** (aas_support_sty.rs, also `\affil` and, through revtex's `\replace@command`, `\address`)
  is REVTeX's call (`group_or_marked_affiliation`, factored out of revtex4_support_sty.rs's `\affiliation`, unchanged
  there): a mark-led line no group shares goes to the names showing its mark (`\lx@add@affiliation@marked`), any other
  to the group before it with `annotate=run` — every `\affiliation` after a run of `\author` calls, before the next
  `\author`, is each one's (aastex62.cls:278-292 loads revtex4-1, whose `\move@AU\move@AF` file the run). It was
  `annotate=new`, which gave a run's second line to its last author only. Under marks (user rulings R1 and R2, 2026-11-01: a
  convention never gives a line to an author whose own marks request that role, and never outranks a mark; a
  hand-printed leading number is a label wherever the names request numbers), aas_support_sty.rs's `\affiliation`
  reads the call's line and declares the result at the call, so the frontmatter observer reads the same attributes:
  - a line's leading label — a superscript (`$^{1}$`, `\textsuperscript{1}`) or a hand-printed number (`1 Univ A`,
    `2) Univ B`, `3. Univ C`, behind the font switches it is set in; `relocate::leading_line_label`) — that a queued
    `\altaffilmark{N}` requests (`relocate::queued_name_marks`) labels the line `altaffil:N`
    (`\lx@add@affiliation[label={altaffil:N}]`, the label off the line), so it goes to the names requesting it: AASTeX
    5's `\altaffilmark` names over `\affil{$^{N}$…}` or `\affil{N …}` lines, whose two label spaces never met; one
    `\affil` holding a block of `\\` lines is read entry by entry (a labelled line opens one, an unlabelled line
    continues it: 1610.06611, astro-ph0108212), an entry holding only an e-mail is an e-mail (below), and an `\email`
    set in an entry is the spelled author's, not each holder's (`take_placed_line_emails`, 1503.02933; since Z18l the API's
  Link step's, #992);
  - a hand-printed number a queued `$^{N}$` requests is that mark (`$^{N}$` written for it), and the line goes by
    REVTeX's marked-line rule;
  - an unlabelled line goes by REVTeX's group rule (`annotate=run`) unless the run's names request affiliations by
    `$^{N}$` marks (`relocate::run_names_show_a_mark`: no footnote symbol alone, no `\altaffilmark`, which asks for an
    `\altaffiltext`), when the call declares `annotate=new` (97d's result: each line every author's still without one,
    the later ones the last author's) — no group sharing every line. That is a stopgap: R1 gives such a line to no
    marked author, which the observer's one placement order ("marks before convention", the next refactor stage)
    decides.
  AASTeX 7 is unaffected in practice: aastex701.cls:7370 `\affil@error` stops on an author without an affiliation, so
  its authors never share a run.
- **REVTeX's own call** (`group_or_marked_affiliation`, both bindings): a line led by a macro standing for a mark
  (`\edef\MSU{$^{1}$ }`, `\address{\MSU Moscow …}`: `relocate::leading_macro_mark`) under names carrying such macros
  (`relocate::run_names_macro_marks`) is no group's (R1): labelled by its mark (`label={affiliation:1}`, the macro off
  the line), or, where a mark leads a name — written after the comma (`M.~Osipenko,\MSU$^,$\INFNGE\ G.~Ricco,…`), so
  the comma split put each on the next name — the block's, once (`label={addresses:block}`). hep-ph0301204 (CLAS, 213
  names, 38 addresses): every author all 38 (8,094 affiliations; base all 38 on the last author; Perl one merged
  creator) → the 38 once on the block.
- **An AASTeX `\affil` holding only an e-mail** (`\affil{e-mail: kangx@shao.ac.cn}`, a labelled or bare address, no
  e-mail command; `\affil{$^*$ Email: x@y}` too, its mark kept for the placement) is no affiliation:
  `placed_email_line_calls` (author_block/email_block_calls.rs) makes each address `\lx@add@contact@placed[role=email]`,
  the label its `name` — placed as a class's e-mails apart from the names are (`placed_contact_owner`: the author
  requesting the mark, the author the address spells, the only author of the group, else the block's shared creator,
  #159). Perl: an affiliation of the last author (aas_support.sty.ltxml:118). (Superseded by #992, Z18l: the line goes as
  the affiliation it is, the API's Kind and Link steps place its addresses; the reader is deleted.)

**Why.** Perl (revtex4_support.sty.ltxml:46) makes one creator of each `\author` call: the 2015 BESIII template
(`\author{\begin{small}\begin{center} names \\ \vspace{0.2cm} (BESIII Collaboration)\\ {\it $^{1}$ aff\\ …}
\end{center}\vspace{0.4cm}\end{small}}`) is one creator in Perl and was one in 97d — 758 of the 861 wrong creators of
the twelve dev papers with more than 50 scored creators. The names split as their marks say (97a, OD #943), the
collaboration line their contact (97d, OD #946). Perl's aastex `\affiliation{#1}` (aas_support.sty.ltxml:118) is the
last author's; pdflatex with aastex631 prints "K. Ieki 1, 46" for `\author{K. Ieki}\author{…}\affiliation{U1}
\affiliation{U2}` (2403.06760).

**Witnesses** 97d → 97f: 1507.02068 1 → 419 creators (418 names and the nameless one below), 1512.08197 1 → 413,
2201.02056 1 → 520, 0 Errors each; every name whose marks are plain numbers or letters holds the affiliations its marks
name (381 of 418, 374 of 412; the rest are the sub-labels below and two repeated names); scored 0 → 382 of 385, 375 of

**Round 3 (98e; bundle int126a's A/B blocker, review revab126): a block the marks cannot split lands once.**
- **A one-argument line wrapper is a line** (`relocate::wrapped_lines_as_lines`, called at the head of
  `group_or_marked_affiliation` and of aas_support_sty.rs's `\affiliation`, before either reads a leading label): a
  block line set as `\centerline{…}`, `\leftline{…}` or `\rightline{…}` (latex.ltx:16403-16406, each a box as wide as
  the line) is a line of its own, and an `\mbox{…}`/`\hbox{…}` is one when it is the whole line between `\\` — or,
  side by side, where marks lead the first box and another (a box no mark leads goes on with the entry before it, a
  space between) — written as `\\` lines, each then read by its own label as the same block typed with `\\` is. Only
  where a wrapped line leads with a mark (`\address{\centerline{Univ A}}` keeps its wrapper); the wrapper's alignment
  is dropped with it. The D0 lists (`\address{\centerline{$^{1}$Universidad de Buenos Aires…}\centerline{$^{2}$…}…}`
  under ~600 `V.M.~Abazov,$^{33}$` names): 98a every creator the whole 75-institute block (hep-ex0409040 6,379 →
  377,251 words, 9.45 MB of XML; hep-ex0612013 7,895 → 428,795), 97b the block once on the last author; now each
  author its own institute (607 of 607 and 576 of 576 creators one affiliation each, 75 and 82 distinct; 10,085 and
  11,807 words). Also 1412.5812 (`\mbox{$^{1}$…}\mbox{$^{2}$…}…\mbox{Russian Academy…}`), 0911.2853
  (`\mbox{$^a$…}\\ \mbox{Blegdamsvej…}\\ …`).
- **The group rule's fail-safe** (FRONTMATTER_SINGLE_ENGINE_PLAN "The structure model" step 4): a block holding more
  than one label the names request (`relocate::requested_marks_held`) that no mark this reader sees leads
  (`leads_with_mark`), under names requesting affiliations by marks (`run_names_show_a_mark`), is no one entry a group
  shares: it lands once at the block (`label={addresses:block}`, #159), never `annotate=run`'s copy on each author.
  The call declares `_unsplit=true`, and the observer reads such a block's lines by their own marks all the same
  (`resolver::api`, the mark split of an entry of several marked entries), so the writer cuts it where it can
  (`\affiliation{\( ^{1} \)Univ A, City\\ \({}^{2}\)Univ B, Town}`: each author its line, as before). Where neither
  reader parts it, it stays once on the block: 0807.4407 (`\mbox{${\ }^{1}$} Department …`), 2208.09667 and
  2308.02280 (`\affiliation{&&${^1}$ Department …\nonumber\\$^{2}$ …}`), each author the whole block before.
- **A cut block line no name requests goes to the block** (emitter/plan.rs `cut_block_lines`): an entry the reading
  leaves to the block for a label no name requests (`label:unrequested owner:block`, `ruling2:uncarried
  owner:block`) is a piece of a block-line cut whose other lines a ruling decided, made once for the block — a
  labelled item nobody answers goes to step 4 of the placement order, never to the holders of the joined item; a run
  of such lines alone keeps today's placement (`emitter::writes`, #925). Such a piece is the block's by that order, not
  by doubt: `Op::Make`'s `unanswered` takes it out of the nameless-creator invariant (`writes_a_nameless_creator`,
  rev94b r3 B2). 2007.02542 (BESIII, 491 names over one `{\it $^{1}$ …\\ … $^{l}$ …\\}` group, labels 23, 24, 51 and
  63 requested by no name — the names ask `23A`, `63A,63C`): the writer had declined the whole paper, the holders of
  mark 1 (143) each the whole numbered list as one contact and 347 authors none; now every author the lines its marks
  name (714 affiliations, 80 distinct; 114,629 → 19,006 words), the four unrequested lines once on the block. Such a
  line keeps its printed label (`b Also at …`, the mark's `<sup>` kept as a legend's is: label text is markup, never
  dropped — review rev98e S1, ruling tentative, the user away).
- **A sub-lettered mark goes by its number** (review rev98e B1; resolver/labels.rs `parted_label`, post.rs
  `part_glued_labels`): a run of digits is one number, cut into its digits only under single-digit numbering (every
  number the other side holds one digit, as the names' side already read an all-digit mark: 2103.10685's `12` under
  entries 1-4), so BESIII's `23A` under institutes numbered 1 to 70 is `23` and `A`, never `2`, `3` and `A`; and an
  entry's own leading printed number is never parted (`$^{23}$ (A)INFN Laboratori Nazionali di Frascati …; (B)INFN
  Sezione di Perugia …` is no line of the names marked 2 or 3; 2207.06713's `$^{15}$` stays the block's as before). The
  name gets the whole numbered line; its `(A)` part stays a sub-entry of it (R6, tentative: sub-items at Stage 4a), and
  the unanswered `A` stays in the name. 98e's writer cut had applied the wrong reading: 2007.02542's 36 sub-lettered
  authors each two wrong institutes (R. Baldini Ferroli `23A` → Beihang and Beijing Petrochemical; S. A. Cetin `51B` →
  IHEP and Carnegie Mellon) where 98a gave them none; 1507.02068's `48A` read `4`, `8` on 98a too.
- **The fail-safe fires only for a block of labelled lines** (review rev98e S2; `relocate::requested_mark_lines`): two
  or more lines — the block's own and those of the boxes, groups and environments it sets them in, split at every
  `\\` — led by labels the names request, past spaces, font switches, `\noindent`/`\nonumber`, box openers and an
  environment's opener with its own arguments (`\begin{tabular}{c}`: 0911.3234 once on the block — since 104c a
  one-column tabular's rows are read as lines, each author its row, OD #964), a mark the binding
  does not cut included. Marks inside one line's text are no such block: `\affiliation{Joint Institute,
  \textsuperscript{1}Univ A and \textsuperscript{2}Univ B, City}`, printed once under both names, is the group's entry,
  a copy on each (FIDELITY_CHARTER; 97b, 98a), where 98e r1 had made it a nameless block. **A mark spelled
  otherwise is the mark it prints**, read by one shared reader of a line's leading printed label
  (`relocate::spaced_mark_at`, used by `notes::leads_with_mark`, `leading_line_label` — so REVTeX's, AASTeX's, sv's and
  IEEEtran's token readers alike — and by `requested_mark_lines`): a superscript on a spacing nucleus (`${\,\!}^{1}$`,
  `${}^1$`, `${\ }^{1}$`, `$~^{1}$`), the script braced whole (`${^1}$`), one in `\( … \)` (`\( ^{1} \)`), and a box holding only a mark
  (`\mbox{${\ }^{1}$}`). Where such a mark leads a REVTeX/AASTeX block, `spaced_marks_as_marks` (at the head of
  `group_or_marked_affiliation`, after the line wrappers) writes each such mark of a label the names request as
  `$^{1}$`, so the binding's marked list cuts the block by its marks as a `$^{1}$` block's; such a mark in a block none
  leads stays as written (`${}^{3}$He`). 2112.13115 (`${\,\!}^1$Department of Applied Mathematics and Statistics\\ and
  ${\,\!}^2$Department of Physics \& Astronomy, \\ The Johns Hopkins University…`): 98a both departments one contact on
  each author, 98e r1 none (the block's) — now Eyink both departments and Jafari Applied Mathematics (the second line's
  printed `and` stays at its head, as the marked list keeps a line's text before its mark); 0807.4407, 1211.5032 each
  author its lines; `\( ^{1} \)` lines go by their marks with the marks off their text, as `$^{1}$` lines (they had
  gone to the observer's cut of the fail-safe's `_unsplit` block, the marks kept). The observer reads a digested
  formula's marks from its own structure (`observer::marks`); a nucleus formula is no Mark event there (98e r1's
  `_unsplit` cut never fired on 2112.13115 or 0807.4407) — open, SYNC_STATUS row "int126a review".

  4 → 4. 2311.05131 (841 warnings) and 1111.1264 (an allocation failure under the 8 GB cap) vary run to run on either
  binary (a wall-clock Fatal, E 20/23), noise.

**Scorer** (the 3,000 sample, `fm_scorer/run_97e` against `run_97c` rescored with the same `score_tiers.py`): D3
6,054 → 6,059 of 6,156 structurally decided creators exactly right (98.34 % → 98.42 %; per paper 98.01 %), 5 better
(1701.05122's three, 1902.02872, 2007.07422), 0 worse; papers with lost words 0 → 0; R2 papers 5 → 6, the sixth
2105.09506 (Minglang Yin parted from George Em Karniadakis, whose unparted entries `1 … 2 … 3 …` now he alone holds,
as the merged creator did).

**Mechanisms the flip exposed, fixed in the writer and the reading:**
- *A block line's letters are read as printed* (`emitter::plan::span_tokens`): the source span's letters against the
  reading's key, accents folded on both sides (`resolver::base_letters`); an accent command adds none, a text symbol
  its own — latex.ltx's glyph for the current encoding (core `mouth::text_symbol_char`, now public; OT1's are
  `\chardef`s, decoded through the encoding's font map, `font_decode`), else a primitive printing it (`\i`, `\ss`,
  `\o`; Perl plain_base.pool.ltxml:108, 531). Before, `Ca\~nada` gave "Canada" against the key's "cañada" and the cut
  declined: 1009.1371 (73 creators, every one wrong), 2401.03603 (`H\"ugel`, `Astrof\'{\i}sica`).
- *A re-parted entry keeps today's role* (`writer::repart::item_source`): a made affiliation takes the role every
  affiliation of today's holds when they agree — appolb's and the ws-procs classes' `\address` lines are `address`
  contacts — else the reading's (1501.05548, 0710.5369, 0809.3340, cond-mat0311409 had theirs made `affiliation`s).
- *A letter-spaced name's word space is no gap* (`events::lexer::letter_spaced_word_space`): one spacing item
  narrower than a quad after two or more single letters, the run's last word one letter, is the name's word space —
  jfm's `\ls` (`\kern.15em`) and `\ns` (`\kern.5em`, jfm.cls:1024-1025): 1510.04254, 1403.3574, astro-ph0406083, each
  name read as two or three and re-parted. Initials (`A. B. C.`) carry periods and are no letter-spaced run.
- *An e-mail's corresponding owner is one of the authors it is printed for* (`resolver::post::answer_sequence`): the
  corresponding step of a class's address list looks within the call's group (iopart's `\ead` belongs to the `\author`
  group it follows, iopart.cls:225-231) and, an address set among the entries, among the requesters of the entry just
  before it (`Resolver::entry_printed_before`; iopart.cls:363) — `perfect_kernel_batch78f`'s r2 rulings, which the
  reading had not kept (2311.17496, 2407.14305, 2311.07087); jheppub's `\emailAdd` list, after every entry, keeps the
  paper-wide step (1901.08773).
- *A name read as an entry is never written onto an author* (`emitter::plan::{writes_the_name, prints_the_name}`): an
  affiliation the reading gives an author declines the paper, today's kept, when it writes one of the paper's names
  and nothing else (initials or words of the name in order, its last word the name's: svjour3's `\institute{A. Able
  \and B. Baker \at Univ X}`, whose name-only piece the `\and`-list numbers as entry 1, 2609.05466), or, given by the
  name it prints (`fuzzy:surname`, svjour3's `\at`), prints the name of an author it is not given to (words parted at a
  capital glued to a small letter, `Y. XuInstitute`: the `\\`-parted `\at` pieces read as one entry, 1506.02396,
  1908.03628, 2007.09912). A name in any other entry is no evidence: IEEE's `S. Sharma, Y. Kulkarni … are with the
  Walker Department` (2405.17600) names its own owners, `5720 S Ellis Ave` (1201.0008) is a street beside an author S.
  Ellis, `Johns Hopkins University` (0807.2295) an institution — each a false decline of an earlier, wider rule. The faithful link stays RED
  `svjour3_name_only_piece_shares_the_next_institute`; since sv_support is written, `keep_as_today` no longer covers
  these calls.

**Review rev97e (r2): two holes of the flip, fixed.**
- *An elsarticle key is answered by keys alone, and its title's marks are arabic* (B1): elsart_support_core.sty
  declares conventions of its own (`elsart_support_core_sty.rs` `FRONTMATTER_CONVENTIONS`, "elsart": the kernel's
  reading, written) for elsarticle, elsart and the classes keeping its `\author` (entics, arxbj; not autart, which
  loads OmniBus and its own `\address`, `autart_cls.rs`, and only this binding's keyword markup).
  `title_marks: Body` — elsarticle's `\maketitle` sets no `\@fnsymbol` (elsarticle.cls:819, :836
  `\gdef\thefootnote{\arabic{footnote}}`; elsart.cls v2.18 :1107-1108 `\xarabic`), so a `\footnotemark[1]` reads
  "1", not the kernel's "∗". `keyed_labels` (a new `Policy` field) — the key of `\address[key]`/`\affiliation[key]` is
  never printed (the class prints the entry's place: `\theaffn`, elsarticle.cls:656-662; `\theaddress`, elsart.cls
  :1135-1164), so an entry it labels (`api:label`) answers no footnote's mark, a symbol's neither — the symbol-line
  route of ruling 2 is closed to it (`resolver::post::answer_pending`, `keyed`; FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 R1). The authors'
  keys (`annotations=`) answer it, and so does a mark typed by hand: keys in order spell the places the class prints
  (`Denes Molnar$^{a,b}$` under `\address[a]{…}\address[b]{…}` prints "a,b" over "a …", "b …", 0907.5014; a first
  version answering keys alone left it, 1101.5562 and 2609.03753 unwritten). Not handled (rare): old elsart's proofing switch prints the key itself
  (`\if@Elproofing \def\@eltag{#4}`, elsart.cls v2.12 :1026; v2.19 :1178), where `keyed_labels` is wrong. 1108.0201's `\address[*]{current address}`, which pdflatex prints "bb current address"
  and no `\author[*]` requests, had gone to `M.~Pesce-Rollins\footnotemark[1]` (her `[6]` requests her affiliation):
  now the block's, as in 97c. The cost of the arabic marks: a `\footnotetext[n]` after `\maketitle` now pairs with the
  name's "n", as pdflatex prints it, and today's holds that note only after the writer runs, so the paper is declined
  whole — 1108.0201 itself, and 0909.2782, whose e-mails r1 had split onto their authors (pre-existing in every family:
  `article` under `\renewcommand\thefootnote{\fnsymbol{footnote}}` declines alike; SYNC row "97e r2 residuals"). Of the other bindings labelling an
  entry by a key (`label={#1}`): cas-dc rewrites its keys to the letters cas prints (`cas_labelled_entry`), so a mark
  matches the print; the rest own their `\author` and stay `UNDECLARED` (imsart, ecai, ceurart, icml, sn-jnl, bmcart,
  beilstein, interspeech, vmsta, quantumarticle; not audited for printed keys — SYNC).
- *A name the re-part would make that names no person declines* (S1; `emitter::repart::plan`,
  `resolver::names_no_person`): a reading's name not one of today's whole names that is a remark on a name (a bracket,
  what a name speaks for — `for`, `on behalf of`, `representing` —, whatever follows) or a collaboration's name (`the …
  team`, one ending in "collaboration(s)" or "consortium") leaves today's: svjour's and elsart's own `\and` pieces
  never reach the author block's collaboration reader (OD #946), so `(BES Collaboration)\\ \\ M.~Ablikim\inst{1}`
  (0710.5369, hep-ex0605103), `{The WASA-at-COSY Collaboration}\\[2ex]P.~Adlarson` (1805.08173) and webofc's `Eleni
  Petrakou\inst{1}\fnsep\thanks{…} for CAPP/IBS` (1702.03664) had made the phrase a creator of its own once the
  person's name was parted. Each paper as 97c: the phrase in the first name; hep-ex0605103's names keep their marks
  again (`M. Ablikim$^{1}$`), as in 97c. A collaboration's name declines only when the line alone parts it: a
  separator the names line prints before it or after it (the next name's) makes it an entry of the list, as the old
  reader and Perl read it — `\author{GRAVITY+ Collaboration\thanks{…}: R.~Abuter\inst{8} \and …}` (aa, 2206.00684),
  the first piece, has none before it and its colon after it; read by the separator before alone, int126a declined it
  and wrote "GRAVITY+ Collaboration: R. Abuter" as one name (review rev126a B1, 98a; guard
  `perfect_kernel_batch98a::a_collaboration_heading_a_separator_parts_is_a_contact_the_writer_declines` (since 103b the
  heading Ann Able's collaboration contact, the writer declining), with svjour's `{The XYZ Collaboration}\\[2ex]Ann
  Able`, which still declines).

### 949. A line before an author block's first that prints nothing is no names line, and a nameless creator's lines are the block's when no named author is left to take them (Perl: the spacer line an empty name, every line under it an affiliation)

**What** (brief 98b; dev lost-words census mechanism B). Two readings, one per stage, and a later block's.

- **The unmarked branch of the author-block reader** (author_block/dispatch.rs, `spacer_line`, the one predicate for
  every line of the block, in any position, and for whether a line break opens it): a `\\`-piece that prints nothing —
  empty, spacing alone, a tie, a control space, an empty group, a size or font switch alone, its line-break option
  (`{}~\\[0mm]~\\ \large Ann Able\\ …`; `prints_nothing`), but no environment's `\begin`/`\end` — is the block's
  spacing (a gap between lines), not a line; before the first printing line, not its names line. It had been read as a names line whose name printed
  nothing, every printing line under it that nameless creator's.
- **`coalesce_empty_creators`** (frontmatter/insert.rs) moves a nameless creator's contacts and notes to the named
  author before it, else the first after it. When none is left (a block of affiliation lines alone; a name written
  inside `\IEEEmembership{…}`), the first nameless creator carrying any keeps them all — the block's own creator
  (#159), `<ltx:personname/>` over the lines, as Perl. It had removed it with them: no creator and no Warning. A
  removed creator's other printing child is reported (`Warning:unexpected:frontmatter`); none is known to occur.
- **A later block a line break opens** — after an author separator, its first line printing nothing as above or empty
  (`\author{Ann Able \and ~\\ University of X}`, `… \and \\ University of X`) — whose first line is an institution
  (`reads_as_institution`) has no names: an empty names line over its lines, which `coalesce_empty_creators` keeps on
  the names before it, as Perl and int126a read the tie (round 2: the leading-spacer reading made it a creator named
  "University of X", the rev98b review's pb1; pb6's empty piece had been read so before). Round 2 also reads a
  spacer line after the first printing line by `spacer_line` (it had been a line only when empty or spacing alone).

**Why.** FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 "No printed frontmatter word is lost": the census's 8 papers whose whole author block was
dropped. Perl 0.8.8 keeps the lines but names no one (`<personname/>` and every line an affiliation, "Ann Able"
among them); ours names the author.

**Witnesses** (int126a: no creator → the author and its lines): 0812.2273, 0901.1754, 1706.10067 (`\IEEEauthorblockN{~\\
[-0.4ex]\large …}`: three authors), hep-lat0105010, hep-lat9207028, math0306336; solv-int9710025 (the `\ ` spacer of
#900's RED `author_block_leading_spacer_line`: Ann Able's lines no longer after Bob Baker's); the nameless holder:
1804.00021 (`\authorblockA{…}` with its names commented out), 2203.14581 (`~\IEEEmembership{Shasha Mei}`, with #950).

**Left:** an affiliation-only `\IEEEauthorblockA{Center X, University of X\\ …}` is kept but parted into contacts at the
commas of its first line (the names-line split reads into the command's group); the words are all kept.

**Guards** `perfect_kernel_batch98b::{leading_spacer_lines_are_no_names_line, nameless_block_keeps_its_lines,
institution_after_and_and_a_break_is_no_name}`; repros
sectioning-frontmatter/`author_block_leading_spacer_lines_are_no_names_line` (RED → GREEN),
`author_block_institution_after_and_spacer_line`, `author_block_institution_after_and_line_break` (RED → GREEN, round 2),
`author_block_leading_spacer_line` (RED since 85a r3 → GREEN), class-bindings/
`ieeetran_affiliation_block_without_names_is_the_blocks` (RED → GREEN).

*Live rule: OD #459.*

### 950. IEEEtran's grades are read under authblk's `\author` too, a line holding only the last name's grade is that name's, and `\IEEEpeerreviewmaketitle` is `\relax` outside the peer-review modes (Perl: every grade dropped; `\IEEEpeerreviewmaketitle` is `\maketitle` in every mode)

**What** (brief 98b; census mechanism C). ieeetran_cls.rs.

- **authblk** (a document's `\usepackage{authblk}`; the IEEEtaes and IEEEoj stubs load it) replaces the binding's
  `\author`, so each grade reached the binding's drop (`\lx@IEEE@membership@drop`, deleted by P5a). IEEEtran's binding now hooks authblk's load
  (`\AddToHook{package/authblk/after}`): authblk's `\author` is kept as `\lx@IEEE@AB@author`, and `\author` reads the
  grades of its names as the binding's own does (since P5a the reading's: `\lx@IEEE@grade`, OD #1016; only while
  `\IEEEmembership` is the class's) before handing the names to authblk's (a body of `\IEEEauthorblockN` blocks is read as the class's: #987), the optional label exactly as written (an
  empty `\author[]{…}` is no unlabelled `\author`: dropped, 2005.04149's, 2105.12254's and 2312.15778's addresses were
  welded into the affiliation). Conference mode
  still swallows them (`\lx@IEEE@membership`; pdflatex errs on an `\IEEEmembership` in authblk's `\author` there, an
  invalid probe).
- **A grade alone on the line after its name** (`and~Jussi Haapola,\\~\IEEEmembership{Member,~IEEE,}\thanks{…}`,
  2202.10869): `grade_only_line` — one `\IEEEmembership{…}`, else only spacing and notes — keeps the names line open
  across that `\\`, so the grade is the last name's, as any other; read as a line of the block it was dropped.
- **`\IEEEpeerreviewmaketitle`**: IEEEtran.cls:4920-4932, the peer-review modes' repeated title page, `\relax` in every
  other mode. Perl IEEEtran.cls.ltxml:135 lets it to `\maketitle` in every mode, so a call before `\title` (1909.01874)
  flushed the frontmatter without its title.

**Why.** FIDELITY_CHARTER §4: pdflatex prints every grade with its name (6 census papers); Perl drops them all
(IEEEtran.cls.ltxml:143, "nothing for now").

**Witnesses** (int126a → 98b): 1803.04687, 2208.04191, 2307.05035 (`\author[1]{Hani Saleh,~\IEEEmembership{Senior
Member,~IEEE,}}`), 2505.19506 (IEEEtaes), 2506.05637 (IEEEoj), 2202.10869 (`\IEEEoverridecommandlockouts` in
conference mode): each author its grade as `contact role="membership"`; 1909.01874: the title and both authors (the
title had been "I. Nomenclature", no creator).

**Guards** `perfect_kernel_batch98b::{authblk_author_reads_ieee_grades, authblk_labelled_author_reads_its_grade,
peerreviewmaketitle_outside_peerreview_is_relax}`; repros class-bindings/`ieeetran_authblk_membership_grades`,
`ieeetran_authblk_labelled_author_grade`, `ieeetran_peerreviewmaketitle_outside_peerreview_is_relax` (RED → GREEN),
`ieeetran_authblk_empty_label_authors_share_the_lines` (GREEN; RED on the batch's first build).

*Live rule: OD #459.*

### 954. A contact holding two or more marked entries is cut at its marks in the frontmatter API, for every binding (Perl: one contact, the marks printed in it)

**What** (batch 99a; FRONTMATTER_SINGLE_ENGINE_PLAN "The target model", placement step 0: "one item per printed
entry; marked lists cut at their marks"). `\lx@annotate@frontmatter` (defs/frontmatter_api.rs), through which
`\lx@add@affiliation`, `\lx@add@address`, `\lx@add@altaffiliation` and `\lx@add@contact` queue, reads an affiliation,
alternate affiliation or address contact before it is queued (`defs/frontmatter_api/cut.rs` `cut_marked_contact`):
content holding two or more entries, its first printed line led by a mark, whose marks a queued name requests (two or
more distinct labels, `requesting_authors`) is read again as one call per entry — the cutter the author blocks use
(`affiliation_calls`, now `entry_calls` with the call that held the list as its emitter: lines at `\\`, `\quad` and the
`\and` family, a line at each mark after spacing, a wrapper repeated on each piece, an address line placed as the list's),
each entry labelled by its mark (`\lx@affiliation@withsup`) and showing it (`_markshown`: the mark, and any later
superscript in the entry, read again as the plain superscript, so `$^{1}$Lab $\frac{a}{b^{1}}$ Lab` keeps its fraction's
script; read again braced as it was written — the Cut's reader of a mark on a spacing nucleus keeps a script's braces
as written too (`relocate::spaced_marks_written`: `${}^1$` as `$^1$`, hep-ph0007234) — so a shown mark renders as the
uncut contact rendered it — `$^*$`, `$^1$` upright, `$^o$` italic, a braced `$^{1}$` as the shared float-script rewrite renders a braced script, `tex_math.rs`
`FLOATSUPERSCRIPT` → `<sup><text font="italic">1</text></sup>`; review rev99a2 S-c: round 2 had re-read every mark
braced, so 2209.09217's `$^*$` turned italic; names' marks are left as they render, SYNC_STATUS row 99a "math→sup mark
font"). Being re-read before `queue_front_matter`, the entries are what the frontmatter observer's ledger
records too, so the two engines read the same items (the writer, which cut such calls itself for its written families,
finds `same` where it wrote before). Left as they were: any other role; a call whose binding placed it (`label=`,
`_unsplit`, REVTeX's fail-safe); a list already cut (`\lx@affiliation@withsup`, every binding's own `affiliation_calls`
path: authblk, IEEEtran, REVTeX, llncs); fewer than two requested labels (`Joint Institute,
\textsuperscript{1}Univ A and \textsuperscript{2}Univ B` is one entry). The entries drop the call's `labelseq` and
`_share` (the marks are their labels: R1, R3) and keep its `annotate=`, which an answered label overrides; an entry no
name requests lands once at the block (OD #159).

**Every spelling, the shared readers.** Before the cut a list's marks are written as the marks they print: lines in
one-argument line wrappers (`relocate::wrapped_lines_as_lines`; since 104c also a one-column tabular's rows and
commands set side by side, OD #964), a superscript on a spacing nucleus, in `\( … \)` or a
box of its own (`relocate::spaced_marks_as_marks` over `spaced_mark_at`, now past a one-argument wrapper the list opens
with: acmart's `\institution{${}^a$…}`), a class's `\inst{n}` as the `\textsuperscript{n}` it prints (aa.cls:759,
mem.cls:318) — by its meaning, `line_marks::inst_prints_its_mark` (the inst convention's, or a one-argument definition
raising its argument), so a document's `\newcommand{\inst}{Institute}` stays its word (review rev99a S2); a list wholly in one group is its content, and the declarations it opens with (`\itshape`, `{\bfseries …}`)
open every entry, as the observer writer's cut keeps them (review rev94b r3 B1). A name's marks are read on the queue
by `email_lines::mark_operands` (`${}^{a}$`, `$^{~a,b}$`) and on the DOM by `observer::marks::read_formula`
(`relocate::shown_marks`): the Cut needs the token reading, since it runs before anything is digested. A number range
is each number of it in one reader, the observer's `spelled_ranges` (now `queue_digest.rs`), which
`clean_frontmatter_labels` (a name's request, the Cut's `requesting_authors`) and `relocate::printed_marks` now apply
too: `Bauer$^{1-4}$` over `$^3$… and $^4$…` (2012.15817; the first A/B of this batch had sent both entries to the
block).

**The cutter's boundaries** (`notes::split_marked_pieces`, shared by every caller): a mark after spacing (`\quad`,
`~`, `\;`), not only a space, parts two entries (2506.18881's `\institution{\textsuperscript{1}…\quad
\textsuperscript{2}…}`); a mark that heads no entry is its entry's text — glued to the word before it (a plain space
between, no separator), a number or letter mark no queued name requests (`$^1$Laboratory for $^3$He Studies`), or a
requested one whose label also heads an entry after a separator (one list labels each entry once: `$^1$Inst.\ for
$^{2}$H Research \quad $^2$Univ B`) or that breaks the list's running sequence before it goes on (`$^1$Lab for $^3$He
Studies \quad $^2$Univ B`); anywhere, a mark no name requests that only spacing or a separator follows before the next
mark (`$^1$Univ A $^\dagger$ \quad $^2$Univ B`, a symbol too); undecided, the mark parts the entries (review rev99a S1,
S5); `trim_trailing_separator` drops the spacing, a trailing line
break and the conjunction joining a run's last two entries (`and`, `\&`) with the separator (a `\;` once left
"Univ A ", 2012.15817 "Department of Molecular Biology, and"); in a list the Cut makes, an address line behind an
e-mail label (`email: agupta@…, orion@…`) is the list's address run, each contact named by the printed label
(`email_line_calls`), not text of the entry above it (astro-ph0405186) — a binding's own list keeps such a line in the
entry, which the observer's writer reads (IEEEtran 2308.05546: made a run there, the writer declined the paper and the
old reader's symbol-labelled entries stayed on the block).

**Placement, two steps the Cut exposes** (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 "One placement order"): an address line of a marked list
no author's place claims goes to the author it spells before the block (`place_address_runs`, step 2 before step 4:
aa's `\institute{$^{1}$…\\ $^{2}$…\\ \email{ann.able@y.org}}`, 1507.05963; IEEEtran's `tufo@`/`svy@` under two
marks; aistats' `{gil,hal}@g.edu` under a row of three); and a relocated entry takes the place its call had in the queue
(R8, print order): `\lx@annotate@frontmatter@now` records each annotation's ordinal as the queue is digested
(`_queued`), offset by its print zone (`relocate::NAMES_ZONE` 0, `BLOCK_ZONE` 2^40, the default, `FOOTER_ZONE` 2^41):
a contact inside a name's note is the footer's (`Ann Able$^{1}$\thanks{\email{…}}` prints the address after every
entry of the block, 2212.07438, webofc 2409.01693), and a binding declares the zone of a contact its class prints apart
from the block (`_zone=names`: elsarticle's unlabelled `\address`, printed into `\elsauthors` with the names,
elsarticle.cls:665, 1710.03753; `_zone=footer`: REVTeX's `\email`, a front-matter footnote, 2312.02779, and aa's
`\mail`) — the API names no class. An annotation `relocate_annotations` appends by its label, or gives to the authors
its orphan label names, goes before the first of its creator's annotations in a later zone or queued after it in its
own (`relocate::at_queue_position`; `Resolver::respell_emails` does not call it, an address moved to its speller is
appended); a contact attached when digested keeps the queue's order (REVTeX's `\email` before an unmarked
`\affiliation` stays first) — the Cut's entries of amsart's
`\address{${}^{1}$…\\ ${}^{2}$…}` before the `\email` after it (2509.03485), acmart's before its `\email` (2112.12060,
2209.09217), a binding's own label-relocated list too (REVTeX 3's institute, hep-th9805210; authblk's `\affil[1]`
before an unlabelled `\affil`); 99a's first round appended them after every contact attached when digested.

**Parts after the wrapper** (`frontmatter_api::cut::shared_closing_parts`, the Cut's): a list held in a wrapper and followed by
parts of their own (`\institution{$^1$A \quad $^2$B}\country{X}`; pdflatex prints "X" on a line under both entries)
gives each entry the address parts, repeated as the opening declarations are — a reading of a part the entries
share, which the PDF prints once under all of them (`\institution{$^1$Univ A, Paris \quad $^2$Univ B,
Berlin}\country{Germany}` gives "Univ A, Paris, Germany", text pdflatex never prints: RED
`cut_acmart_closing_part_composes_unprinted_text_red`, review rev99a2 S-d) —, a part holding a link or an address
(`\country{Project page: \href{…}{…}}`, 2506.18881) once to the block (`label=addresses:block`), and a part whose
argument is spacing alone (a space, a tie, `\relax`, a spacing command: `\country{~}`, 2605.18872) to none; a part a
macro prints (`\city{\cty}`) is shared (review rev99a2 S-a: round 2 tested for letters only and dropped "Germany").
99a's first round gave every part to the last entry alone (int126b: every author). A separator closing an unwrapped list's last entry is trimmed
(`…Paris,⏎}`, 2009.04283; review rev99a N1).

**One printed list, one Cut** (review rev99a2 B1; 2312.02779's five identical REVTeX `\affiliation{{$^1$}…Belfast…\\
{$^2$}…Trinity…}`, one after each name). The Cut decides when the call is queued, from the names queued so far, so the
early copies of a list repeated after each name were left whole (one requested mark) and a later copy cut: its entries
reach every requester by label, and the early names held the whole list and their entry. Now each cut entry names its
list (`_cutlist`, a key of the role and the list as the Cut reads it, `affiliations::cut_list_key`), as a binding's own
cut of a marked list does (`\lx@add@affiliation@marked`, `binding_cut_list_attr`: REVTeX's binding cuts the copy after
the first name itself); a copy queued after the list is cut adds no entries (`cut_list_queued`); and when the list is
cut, each earlier uncut copy of it gives way (`place_uncut_copies`) when every name it reaches — its run, the names
queued since the last contact of its role, or every name for `annotate=all` — requests one of the list's marks: it
leaves the queue (and the observer's ledger, `ledger::record_cut_copy`), and a stand-in records its place for those
names (`\lx@cut@copy@place`), which the entry each takes keeps (`relocate::at_queue_position`, R8). A copy reaching a
name that requests none of the marks stays as it is.

**The decision, one predicate**: `affiliations::holds_requested_marked_entries` (public), the list's marks read as the
Cut reads them, is the one test a reader of a store's marked entries asks (batch 99b's `requested_marks_held` at
integration). Since Option C P4b2 the decision and the copy rule below read one digested fact,
`argument_marks::requested_entry_labels`: the list's entries as the observer cuts an API call
(`events::mark_led_pieces`, after the queued names' marks are read), each leading mark's label (`set_label`'s first)
with its requesters — a mark a document macro prints or a math-active `^` spells counts (`api_cut_macro_marks_list`,
`api_cut_math_active_marks_list`). A list whose first token, read through parameterless macros' bodies (and on past a body
printing nothing, `\newcommand\affilfont{}`), is a letter or digit is not rehearsed (`may_open_with_mark`:
2103.04797's 1,161 `\affiliation{\Amsterdam}`, −0.3 % instructions against P4b); the bindings' per-call reader `leads_with_label` (REVTeX's and AASTeX's `\affiliation`, sv's `\institute`, jfm, ws_procl, interspeech, IEEEtran) asks the same gate (CST1: 2103.04797 −10.5 %, 1901.01540 −2.6 % against int164a, byte-identical). The marks queries' own gate before their rehearsal (`may_mark`, in `mark_events`: `marks_as_printed`, `argument_marks`, the names' `queued_author_marks`) reads a whole argument so — a command through its parameterless body, the tie, `\relax`, an accent and a primitive or `\chardef` printing no mark character read past, a body's character a mark as the lexer reads one (`is_mark_char`), a command the rehearsal binds (`rehearsal::rebinds`) or any other a possible mark — so 2103.04797's `\affiliation{\Amsterdam}` and 1901.01540's tied, accented names (`M.~Soares-Santos`) are not rehearsed (CST2: rehearsals 3,297 → 2,156 and 4,155 → 2,646; instructions −9.7 % and −4.7 % against int165a, byte-identical). The gate reads no character typed straight into the argument as a mark: the earlier gate rehearsed any argument holding a command, so a `*` typed beside a tie or an accent (`\author{A.~Smith*}`, `Jos\'e Smith*`) was read as a mark, and REVTeX's names stood bare beside a nameless creator holding the block; now both authors hold both lines, as for the untied `A. Smith*` and as the PDF reads ("A. Smith* and B. Jones / 1Uni One, Town / 2Uni Two, Town"), and IEEEtran's tied names read as its untied twin's (no paper of the A/B changed; revCST2; guard row `revtex_typed_star_after_tie_or_accent_is_name_text`). A `*` a macro body or a `\chardef` prints, a `\relax`- or `\protect`-led body and a body past the gate's 8 levels stay rehearsed (rows `revtex_macro_and_chardef_printed_stars_are_marks`, `revtex_relax_protect_led_and_deep_mark_macros_are_marks`). An argument rehearsed for another command (`A. Smith\,*`, `B.\ Jones*`) still has its typed `*` read as a mark by the rehearsal, the block nameless (RED `revtex_typed_star_beside_thin_or_control_space_nameless_red`, post-merge). Unread (a rehearsal left a group open), none: the list stays whole for the observer, counted
(`--debug=frontmatter_marks`). The cutter (`entry_calls`, the Cut's and every binding list's) reads the same reading
(Option C P4b4a, `argument_marks::list_marks`: the starts `events::entry_heads` gives, the same cut of a list of one
entry or one led by unmarked text, and where each mark the list prints at its level stands): a line printing no mark
(nor a note opening with one) continues the entry above it; a line is cut at its later starts, inside a wrapper too (the
wrapper repeated with its declarations; a box the whole line is set in, `\parbox{\linewidth}{$^1$Univ A\\ $^2$Univ B}`,
`\mbox`, `\hbox`, dropped: what pdflatex prints are its lines, each piece led by the font, size and colour declarations
the body or line opens with (`notes::list_lead_declarations`, the Cut's own), read by meaning (`notes::sets_font`:
`\ifx`'s test against LaTeX's declarations, a `\let` copy too; the whole set, `\tt` and `\LARGE` too, the list
`frontmatter_stores::FONT_DECLARATIONS` the emitter's `font_declaration` reads: 2508.08560, P4b4f), never a macro
printing text (`\mydept`, `\ldots`: printed once, on the first piece; revP4b4a2 B1), and no piece, the first included, with an alignment (`\centering`,
`\raggedright`, `\raggedleft`, ragged2e's: `notes::aligns`), the dropped box's or the paragraph's (2608.21425's
`\centering\scriptsize`: every entry at 70 %, no mark a `<sup class="ltx_centering">`; revP4b4a2 B2; REVTeX's and
llncs's `\parbox` lists, `perfect_kernel_batchhg1::marked_blocks_restored_read_as_printed`) and inside a formula at a
mark on a base (closed and opened again); a mark on no base starts where its formula does (`classify::entry_starts`).
A start whose span opens in the delimiter before its line (`contribution \quad\authorrefmark{2}…`, the spacing its
reading looked past) starts that line (2601.03607); a line printing only addresses (P6d: its reading's text,
`resolver::prints_only_addresses`, the blocks' one reader; formerly `line_addresses` on its tokens) is read by its tokens, its
marks labelling addresses and a start possibly inside one (`$\{${\it\IEEEauthorrefmark{1}a, \IEEEauthorrefmark{3}b}$\}$@x`,
1506.02349); a cut line's last piece has its separator trimmed inside the groups it closes, as the wrapped token cut
did (`\institution{… ~$^{5}$Peking University \\ }`, 2511.20671). The starts read a name's mark as the Link step
does: a request no mark of the list prints, its marks written together (`$^{12}$` under `$^1$A Univ, $^2$B Lab`),
requests each (`events::names_requested` through `resolver::glued_request_parts`, `part_glued_labels`'s; 2409.11440,
2511.20671). P4b4f (CL166: int166a's four P4b4a regressions, each paper back to int165a's output).
No line break or cut stands inside an environment the list opens (P4b4a3, revP4b4a B1): the lines it spans are one. A
start after its line's first inside one leaves the whole list to its tokens, as the base read it, the cutter and
llncs's choice of shape (c) alike (`entry_starts::starts_inside_environment`; revP4b4a2 B3): on
`\institute{\begin{minipage}{…}\affmark{1} Univ A, \affmark{2} Univ B\end{minipage}}` the minipage once, on a nameless
creator (the base's output, owners post-merge); on 2506.05954's `\begin{footnotesize} ${}^a…\\ ${}^b…`, each name its
line, as the base had them (P4b4a's cut gave 2 Errors). Of closing and reopening the environment (its arguments' count is
its definition's, not the tokens') and leaving the list uncut, the simpler. A `tabular`'s `\affmark` rows keep the
base's owners, Ann Able all three lines (RED `llncs_institute_macro_marks_tabular_rows_red`, post-merge); the list's
opening declarations end at its first start (`\ua` printing `\textsuperscript{1}` is none); a line whose marks lead its
notes is cut inside the note by its tokens (the `\thanks` idiom); and llncs's shape (c) is read from the marks the
institute prints (`list_marks`). Unread, the
tokens (`author_mark_position`, `marker_leads`), counted. A list whose requested entries the cutter parts fewer than two
of still stays whole (`cut_list`'s fail-safe); the uncut copies give way only once the list is cut. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batchc1::queued_marks_read_as_digested` (P4b4a rows), `perfect_kernel_batchz18g::llncs_institute_hand_marks_cut`
(2608.21425), `perfect_kernel_batchhg1::marked_blocks_restored_read_as_printed` (P4b4f rows). Read before the queue's marks, the pieces
part at stale requests (`names_requested`): P4b part 1's port gave the unrequested `3 Univ C` to the mark-1 names.

**jfm** (latexml_contrib jfm_cls.rs): `\affiliation{…}` led by marks the names show is `\lx@add@affiliation[annotate=all]`,
so the Cut gives each name its entries (physics0607157, 1302.1594); unmarked it stays the `<note role="affiliation">`
it was.

store holding `$^1$A $^2$B` was copied onto every author or left at the block, in every binding that did not cut it
itself. Perl queues the call whole (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml `\lx@add@affiliation`; the marks printed in it).
