**Batch 107e: a marked run cut whatever parts it** (census138 row 2, MARKRUN; brief 107e). The cutter's boundaries
(`notes::split_marked_pieces`, the author block's and the API Cut's alike) also part a run at: a mark in a group of its
own (`{$^2$} ETH Zurich`, cvpr 2203.16586) and a mark opening one entry's own wrapper — a text font command's argument
or a group past its declarations (`\textit{$^2$CSIRO Data61}`, IEEEtran 2508.07190) — read at the top level by
`notes::wrapped_mark_at`; a mark right after a comma or semicolon with no space (`Lisbon,\IEEEauthorrefmark{2}…`,
2411.03010). A separator glyph between two entries after a space — a formula of `|`, `\vert`, `\mid`, `\cdot`,
`\bullet`, `\diamond` alone, or `|`, `\textbar`, `\textbullet`, `\textperiodcentered` — is no entry's text
(`notes::separator_glyph_len` in `trim_trailing_separator`). A space before `^` in math is no nucleus, as TeX skips it
(tex.web §1045): `$ ^1$` is `$^1$` (`relocate::spaced_mark_at`; revtex 0902.3613's `\affiliation{$ ^1$…; \ $ ^2$…;
$ ^3$…}`). A mark opening a line that prints no label (`$^{\;}$`, `\textsuperscript{\,}`) is no mark: the line continues
the entry above it (`affiliations::blank_line_marks_dropped`, in the block reader and in `entry_calls`; mnras
2303.08793). REVTeX's `\affiliation` whose first entry is unmarked over top-level lines marks lead
(`revtex4_support_sty::unmarked_head_over_marked_lines`) is no longer the fail-safe's when the names request exactly one
mark no line prints (`relocate::requested_marks_unprinted`): the head is labelled by it — superscriptaddress numbers it
and prints the number once, after the call's last name — and the lines are cut (2109.01501, 1903.07834: the block had
gone to a nameless creator); otherwise the fail-safe stands. The `;` control: `\affiliation{Dept. A; Univ B}` with no
mark after its `;` stays one entry. And authblk prints no note without an `\affil` (authblk.sty:168
`\ifx\AB@affillist\AB@empty\AB@author`), so under `\setcounter{Maxaffil}{0}` with the marks written on the `\author`
lines no author requests the thenote's 1 (`Resolver::thenote_finish`; 2510.24320, 2608.24199, 2609.35561, 2503.04130,
2512.05325, 2605.21951: the mark-2 holders had entry 1 too). A/B `pop107e.tsv` (1,162: the 12 census witnesses, 650 dev20k/dev3
papers with a multi-mark affiliation contact or a mark-led line of two marks in the source, authblk + `Maxaffil` 0,
`$ ^`, a blank mark; 500 controls) vs int139a2: 22 changed (0 controls), E 738 = 738, F 2 = 2, every one better or
neutral against its PDF; `fm_checks.py` 1-7 clean. **Residuals:** an entry led by two marks
(`\IEEEauthorrefmark{1}\IEEEauthorrefmark{3}Univ A`) is labelled by its first, the second printed as its text (owners
right through the cut; pinned in `a_mark_after_a_comma_parts_the_run`); the unmarked name revtex prints the head's

(1509.01480) are not read. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch107e::*` (6); repros sectioning-frontmatter/`cut_run_*`,
`cut_revtex_*`, `cut_lines_*` (7 RED → GREEN, 4 GREEN controls).

**Batch 107e round 2** (review rev107e). (1) A legend line under a run whose entries sit in font commands their marks
open (`\textbf{$^1$A}  \textbf{$^2$B}\\ $^*$ Equal Contribution, …`) is read by the observer's writer as under a plain
run: the observer's Mark event of a mark digested inside a wrapper is the wrapper's box, so its span covered the entry
and the writer's line cut (`block_span_tokens`) found no mark before it and declined; `emitter::plan::wrapped_entry_mark`
takes the mark's own formula before the entry's ink and opens the wrapper again round the entry made (its font kept),
when the wrapper closes where the entry ends; a legend in a wrapper of its own is cut with its mark (2609.38081's
`\textnormal{$^{*}$Co-senior authors}`, 2601.12823's `{\small\texttt{$^{\star}$Corresponding author: …}}`: the legend
had been the last entry's affiliation text). The kernel alone welds such a legend into the last entry, after a plain
run as after a wrapped one (the author block reader's "a note continues the affiliation above", batch 64k): a paper the
writer declines keeps it so — 2605.25195, declined over its `{\url{…}}` line (the reading gives it the last names row,
`line:contact R12:row-above`; the kernel, the block). (2) REVTeX's head over marked lines is read only where every
top-level line of the tail, a blank one aside, opens with a mark and no group or environment holds one
(`revtex4_support_sty::marks_lead_every_line`); else the whole call is the 98e fail-safe's (`$^{2}$Univ B\\
\parbox{…}{$^{3}$Inst C\\ $^{4}$Lab D}` under the head: the block creator's, as before 107e). (3) A wrapper is an entry's
own (`notes::wrapped_mark_at`) only where nothing but a separator (`trim_trailing_separator`; an unprinted lead such as
`\hfill` aside) follows it up to the next mark, line break or paragraph end (2603.19086's last entry before a blank
line): `Univ A, \textit{$^{2}$H} Lab, Rome $^{2}$Univ B` and `Lab for \textit{$^{3}$He} Studies` keep the isotope in
the entry; and a group that is a name annotation's argument (`\thanks{$^1$…}`, `is_name_annotation`) is no
wrapper. Not fixed, as before 107e: the plain `$^{1}$Lab for $^{3}$He Studies, $^{2}$Univ B, $^{3}$Inst C` and
`$^{1}$Univ A, $^{2}$H Lab, Rome $^{2}$Univ B` are cut at the isotope. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch107e::{a_legend_after_a_wrapped_run_is_its_carriers_notes,
an_unmarked_head_over_an_unreadable_tail_is_the_blocks, a_wrapped_isotope_is_entry_text}`.

*Live rule: OD #954.*

### 955. A raw class's affiliation or address that its own title page prints into the body is the creators' contact: a setter that stores it among code of its own, by what its call recorded; a setter that prints it with no line break of its own, where its call stands as a line (Perl: the shipped class is not read; OmniBus's setters feed the API)
**What** (brief 99b; census127 dev20k cluster 4 and the long tail's Coverage clusters; FIDELITY_CHARTER §4, displaced
text moves). Two shapes of a raw file's own frontmatter setter neither K11 (`pure_stores`: a pure store of the argument
in a `\@name` store) nor the in-place reroute (OD #936: a line break in the setter's own code) took, so the kernel's
`\maketitle` deposit or the call itself printed the line into the body below the names, every author with no contact.
- **A displaced store** (frontmatter_stores.rs `reroute_displaced_setters`, after K11's and the in-place reroutes of a raw
  class, or of a raw package read outside a raw class's read — one inside it is the class's, K11 taking its setters first
  at the class's end: apa6.cls's pure-store `\affiliation` after ftnright.sty, 1710.02566, 1902.06122): a table setter of an affiliation or address (`STORE_SETTERS`' `\lx@add@store@affiliations`,
  `\lx@add@address` names, `displaced_api`) the file defined, of one argument, whose executed code does not print the
  argument where it is called and whose body writes it into a definition (`written_stores`, a `\csname`-named one too),
  its last command reading nothing past the call (`tail_reads_ahead`): rstransa.cls:1154 `\gdef\@address{#1\ifaffbreak
  \relax\end{splitaddress}\fi}` (2607.20672), eph.cls:325 `\def\epl@institute{\epl@institute@makeup{#1}}`
  (nlin0310001), iau.cls:1515 `\expandafter\protected@xdef\csname affil\the\affilcount\endcsname{#1}` (2510.16758,
  2607.25849), alta.cls:58's pure store in a store not named `\@…` (2609.39929). The setter runs as the file's own
  (`\lx@class@displaced@<name>`) under a meaning recorder (`\lx@displaced@begin`/`\lx@displaced@end`; state.rs
  `begin_meaning_recorder` — no assignment journal, which does not nest: the setter's own code may open one, the
  speculative read of a mark it prints, utarticle.cls:125's `\address` → `\@makeadmark{\@tempb}`, 1209.6020, whose
  names lost their printed marks under the journal, review rev99b B4; kept in the state, so a document that stops inside
  a call leaves none open to the next one a worker converts, S1), which records, of each macro the call changed, the
  part that holds the argument (sect05.rs `assigned_parts_holding`, the
  replay records' reader, compared by its characters: `\protected@xdef` expands our accents, `\`` to `\lxaccentgrave`;
  an argument of fewer than two letters is no record) — the class's own record of the value, its provenance. At
  `\maketitle` (`\lx@store@defaults`, before K11's stores — an editor store makes its creator after the authors'
  contacts — and before the deposit; `route_and_hand_displaced`), of the records whose part still stands in its macro
  (a later call that replaced it leaves none), those whose macro the class's whole title page prints in its
  speculative sentinel runs (`sentinel_runs` of `title_page_print_tokens`, the confirming run for a plain value) are
  routed — unless K11's own rules for a store leave it to the class, its pure-store body test aside
  (`displaced_store_stays_the_classs`: a raw macro that is no title-page code reads it, `ClassReaders::read_by_other_code`,
  a class's `\signature` printing `\@where`; or the title page prints it glued to the class's text or in one line with
  another value the frontmatter does not carry, `ClassReaders::store_lines` with the document's values, uiucthesis.cls:177
  `for the degree of \@degree\ in \@dept\\`; the guards `perfect_kernel_batch68u::a_raw_class_store_another_macro_reads_stays_the_classs`,
  `perfect_kernel_batch79a::a_store_in_one_line_with_class_text_stays_the_class_line`,
  `perfect_kernel_batch61::uiucthesis_title_page_is_replayed` pin it) —: the deposit and the replay take each part out of
  its macro (`lx_replay_records`, `\lx@replay@records`), never by its text, and each call's argument is the creators'
  contacts through the API of its kind (`\lx@add@affiliation`, `\lx@add@address`), one entry per line led by a printed
  label (`displaced_entries`: `relocate::split_top_level_lines`, `relocate::leading_line_label`, the shared reader; the
  unlabelled lines before the first label one entry; no labelled line, the whole argument one entry), its `\label`s
  taken out (`without_labels`). An `\and` list the class's title page numbers (caosp.sty:519-527's `\institutename`,
  astro-ph9805069; as its speculative run shows, `note_and_numbering`, #791) is cut at its `\and`s, entry n led by n (`class_numbered_institutes`, the shared reader K11's
  store route uses). Each entry is placed by its leading label (`contact_line_call`, below). A record whose entry
  leads with a mark no author requests (`displaced_in_doubt`, `queue_digest.rs` `placed_authors_requesting`) stays the
  class's text, as an in-place line in doubt does, and so does a call holding the class's own entry separators
  (`displaced_argument_in_doubt`): an `\and` its title page does not number — the kernel prints it " and ", which gave
  astro-ph9805069's four institutes as one contact of every author with "and" written in three times, review rev99b B2;
  sifrev.cls's own `\split@rg`, 1704.03333 — or a `\\` or `\par` a title-page macro reading the store defines anew to
  number or mark the entry after it (`ClassReaders::separators_redefined`, `numbers_or_marks`: `\def\\{\par
  \stepcounter{adr}$^{\theadr}$}`; one still a line break, `\def\\{, }`, separates the lines as the kernel's does). One
  the title page does not print (a running head, a switch that is off) moves nowhere; without a speculative run nothing
  moves. The unclaimed-text net (#953) takes no macro a displaced call wrote.
- **A line's place** (`contact_line_call`; the displaced and run-in routes, and #936's in-place and stored setters'
  calls of one entry, `by_its_label`): a line led by a printed label a name requests (`names_request_label`: a queued
  author's mark read as `\lx@sup@request@affiliation` reads it, or one of the flush, or one a `\maketitle` placed) is
  that label's (`label={affiliation:<key>}`, the mark keyed by its printed text as `\lx@sup@setlabel@affiliation` keys
  it, `line_mark_label`; a hand-printed number, `affiliation:<n>`; the label's characters taken as text, so a symbol
  mark's `#` is no parameter token, 0807.3896), and the kernel pairs it with the names requesting it, later ones too
  (2608.19687's interleaved `\author`/`\affil` lines: `Anshu Gupta $^{1,2}$` after lines 1 and 2); any other line — led
  by no label, by a hand-printed number no name requests (user ruling R2), or by a mark no name requests by its label (a
  glued symbol run, `$^{*+}$`, requests `*` and `+` only by the frontmatter observer's parting, 0807.3896) — goes under
  the names of its run (`annotate=run`), capped at its own run where a labelled line stands in the kernel's
  (`run_cap_past_labels`: a labelled contact waits for its label and ends no run, so 2608.19687's `\affil{$^10$…}` —
  `$^10$`, no mark a line reader reads — reached every author since line 2). An
  in-place or stored call holding several labelled entries (jetpl.cls's stored `\address{$^{\#}$… \\ $^*$… \\ $^+$…}`,
  0807.3896) goes under its run as it is (review rev94b r3 B1), where batch 99a's Cut (`cut_marked_contact`, #954)
  cuts it at the marks the names request; a call the Cut declines is the observer's, the font open before each entry
  kept (`\lx@fm@entry@font`), or whole. A
  stub that requests the label it already carries is that one label (insert.rs `add_annotation_labels`: pasa.cls's
  `\affil{$^1$…}` inside `\author{…}`, digested under the author markup, read `affiliation:1,affiliation:1` and went to the
  nameless block creator, 2005.09266). Under `annotate=run` alone every author of the run held every
  line whenever the frontmatter observer declined to re-part them (review rev99b B1: 2512.20289's lettered lines under
  `$^{1,a}$`, `$^{2,b}$`, `$^{3,a}$`, the observer declining over the ORCID links; 2609.15125's `\affil{$^1$…}` …
  `\affil{$^3$…}` all Sarazin's; 2607.25849's affiliation 2 Ercolino's too; 1603.07668; 1704.03333; the in-place route's
  lines the same in the base). Marks win (FIDELITY_CHARTER "One placement order", R1). A line holding several entries
  led by marks the names request (`affiliations::holds_requested_marked_entries`, the Cut's own decision, its one
  reader) is the API call bare — no `label`, no run —, which batch 99a's Cut (#954) cuts once into an entry per mark,
  each its requesters', one no name requests the block's: never the whole list copied onto each author (1812.07638's 64
  run-in institutes under 200 names, which the run gave every author: 220,900 → 802,017 words), and, where the
  frontmatter observer declines (ORCID links in the names), no longer one nameless creator's whole list (batch 100a,
  SYNC row "99b" (e): in bundle int127a the `_unsplit` route took the line before the Cut, undoing 99a's cut of
  asp2006's `\affil` store, 1002.4968, and moriond.sty's `\address`, hep-ex0106079 — each a nameless creator holding the
  whole list again; restored, 1002.4968's D3 0/9 → 9/9 creators). A line holding several requested marks the Cut cannot cut (set in a box or an environment, or
  not led by a mark: `relocate::requested_marks_held`) lands once at the block (`label={addresses:block},_unsplit=true`,
  the REVTeX binding's fail-safe, FRONTMATTER_SINGLE_ENGINE_PLAN "The structure model" step 4), which the observer
  reads by its marks. A line keeps its printed mark, as the class prints it; the names no longer show a mark a line
  answers (`hide_answered_marks`). A labelled line that is a legend — a footnote-symbol mark and a correspondence,
  contribution, deceased or address-change text (queue_digest.rs `legend_note_kind`, `classify_thanks`: `$^*$Author to
  whom any correspondence should be addressed.`; `$^\dagger$Deceased`, an annotation on the author of the same kind as
  "Corresponding author", FIDELITY_CHARTER §4, user ruling 2026-11-02 — the observer's `is_legend_text` and its
  `api:leading-mark` legend read the kind too, so a block line or a binding's symbol-led entry is its carriers' note,
  `ltx_thanks_deceased`: 0708.2630's three `$^*$Deceased` authors, 1003.2628's `\addrdagger` line — an address twice on
  Stoneham before —, 1510.03948's `$^\dagger$deceased`) — is a note of the names carrying the symbol (`ltx:note role=thanks`, its mark
  the symbol), as the observer writes it when it re-parts the names: as an affiliation it was 2609.15125's every author's
  contact, and with labels 2602.03759's, 2604.08878's and 2607.12158's carriers' affiliation.
- **A run-in setter** (`run_in_contact_setter`): one of #936's names, of one argument, that the file defined to print
  its argument where it is called as text with no line break of its own — iopjournal.cls:108 `\newcommand{\affil}[1]
  {{\fontsize{8}{10}\selectfont \raggedright \if@anonymous \phantom{#1} \else #1 \fi}}`, a paragraph by the blank lines
  the document puts around each call (2608.28486, 2512.15449, 2602.03759, 2606.14342, 2609.32125) —, none of math, a
  superscript, a note or a raised box in its executed code (`MARK_OR_NOTE`: agujournal2019.cls's `\def\affil#1{$^{#1}$
  \ignorespaces}` is a mark), reading nothing past the call. Its call is the API's (`\lx@class@contact@runin`,
  `class_contact_run_in`) only as a line of its own in the title block — between paragraphs at the body's own level,
  the authors set and not placed (`title_block_line`), led by no mark no author requests —, never inside a creator's
  own content (a call there is part of the name's text), and not a line holding several marks the names request
  (`relocate::requested_marks_held`): else the class's line where it stands. The API's Cut would cut such a line
  (`contact_line_call`), but routing a run-in line of several marks changes which lines leave the body, its own
  population to measure: deferred.
- **Where a rerouted setter decides** (review rev99b B3): the rerouted contact setters (#936's, the run-in ones), the
  displaced setters and their deciders (`\lx@class@contact`, `@stored`, `@runin`, `@optional`) are protected, so a call
  inside a class's `\protected@xdef` store stays in the store as written and decides where it is digested — iau.cls:1516's
  numbered `\affiliation` store around 2607.25849's inline `\email` (iau.cls:4107) had the decider expand at store
  time, bake its API call into `\affil0` and fire it at the deposit, giving the address to the editors' creator and
  leaving "email: " in the body. An in-place, stored or run-in call holding an `\and` list its class does not number is
  the class's line too (`unnumbered_and_list`: sifrev.cls's `\institute`, 1704.03333). A call digested in the title page's deposit (`lx_depositing_frontmatter_fields`) — one
  a store the displaced route left the class's kept as written — is the class's line (`in_the_title_page_deposit`).

**Why.** FIDELITY_CHARTER §4: the text is displaced, not lost — the class prints it on its title page under the
names, which the deposit put in the body — so it moves to its owners, once (the body copy taken out by provenance,
never duplicated, never dropped). Beyond Perl, which does not read the shipped class and gives the paper OmniBus's
`\address`/`\affiliation` (OmniBus.cls.ltxml:77-94).
**Not reached** (counter-example triage). (a) Missing generality, deferred: a setter of `[opt]{arg}` storing through a
class list macro (xiaomiev.cls:137 `\addtolist[#1]{#2}{\affiliationlist}…`, 2604.26839: the mark is the optional
argument); a dispatcher (ifacconf.cls:1196 `\address` = `\@ifstar{…}{\@ifnextchar[…}`, elsart-style keys `\author[First]`
/ `\address[First]`, 1111.1311 and 25 hidden long-tail papers: it prints in place through `\address@optarg[#1]#2`, which
neither reroute reads; a dispatcher-following reader or an ifacconf binding declaration); a title page set in a
`tcolorbox`, whose text the speculative run's ink reader does not reach (alta.cls:86-99, 2609.39929); a setter the
document defines (1804.02826's `\long\def\address#1{…}`). A call holding the class's own entry markup — a frontmatter setter
of its own (2607.25849's `\affiliation{email: \email{…}\\ $^1$…}`) or a raw macro with parameters other than a mark
(cta-author.cls's `\address{\add{1}{…}\add{2}{…}\email{…}}`, 2307.11112, whose three authors were read as one when it
was routed whole), or lines led by `\footnotemark[n]` (simauth.cls:190's `\address`, 1603.07668: the marks only the names'
own `\footnotemark[n]` pair, which no line reader reads) — is in doubt and stays the class's text
(`displaced_argument_in_doubt`), as does an `\and` list a
class numbers with code of its own (sifrev.cls's `\split@rg`, 1704.03333: the numbers its title page prints are lost
in the base too). (b) A legend's mark: a labelled legend line is its carrier's note (`legend_note_kind`, below), but a name
that shows the symbol in a superscript of its own (`\lx@frontmatter@keepsup`, `Zhixin Lu$^{1*}$`, 2602.03759) keeps it
beside the note's mark — the frontmatter observer's `show_legend_mark` takes it out of the name, the kernel's line route
does not. (c) A displaced
call's entries are cut at its lines, so a font switch opening the call (`\address{\itshape $^1$… \\ $^2$…}`) reaches the
first entry only — the in-place route's observer Cut carries it (`\lx@fm@entry@font`), the displaced route does not. (d)
Order (R8): the relocation places a labelled contact after the creator's directly attached ones, so a run-in or in-place
`\email` line comes before the labelled affiliations printed above it (2412.06969, 2503.13373; RED repro
`run_in_lines_a_run_places_keep_their_order`); the run would keep the order but cannot tell at the call whether a later
`\author` requests the label (2608.19687) — the relocation's placement, batch 99a's relocate.rs. Fixed in bundle
int127a by 99a's `relocate::at_queue_position` (a relocated affiliation takes its call's queue place): on the integrated
binary the papers rev99b2 found (2412.06969, 2503.13373, 2512.20289, 2603.07344, 2607.12158, 2609.01336, 2609.32125)
and 2608.28486 print their affiliations before the e-mail, as pdflatex does. (e)
A label the class's own code prints outside the store, before it (`\noindent$^{1}$\enspace\@institute`), stays in the body
without its entry (repro `displaced_class_numbered_and_institutes_go_by_their_numbers`; caosp's `\llap` label prints none).
(f) Fixed in batch 100a: a line led by a control-sequence footnote symbol that no name requests
(`\affil{$^\dagger$Deceased}`) went to every author of the run on the run-in, in-place, displaced and observer-declined
routes, since `leads_with_unrequested_mark` and `displaced_in_doubt` counted letter/other tokens only (review rev99b2 F2;
probes `rev99b2/probes/q4c`, `q4d`, `q4g`, `q4h`; synthetic). Both now read a mark by `is_a_mark` — what the operand
prints, the printed-text reading of `line_mark_label` (queue_digest.rs `prints_a_mark`; its spelling where no printed text
is read): a letter, a digit, any other character, or whatever symbol a command prints, so `\bigstar`, `\natural`, `\flat`,
the suits (affiliation labels as digits are, 2601.05633) and `\textdagger` are marks too (review rev100a S1: read by a
list of footnote symbols they were none, and `\affil{$^\bigstar$Deceased}` went to every author) — and a mark is
requested by its printed text as well as by its operand (`requested_as_printed`: `line_mark_label`,
`names_request_label`, the reading `contact_line_call` places the line by), so `\textsuperscript{\dag}Deceased` under
`Ann Able$^{1,\dagger}$` stays her note. One key for both sides (review rev100a B1; user ruling 2026-11-02: "all
asterisks are the same key, they are visually identical to readers", FIDELITY_CHARTER §4): the names' requests
(`frontmatter_label_request`) and the line's label (`line_mark_label`) go through `clean_frontmatter_labels`, which keys
every asterisk one way — written `*`, `\ast` or `\textasteriskcentered`, printed `*`, `∗` (U+2217), `⁎` (U+204E), `✱`
(U+2731) or `＊` (U+FF0A) (`one_asterisk`, `ASTERISK_FORMS`) — the line's printed `∗` had been keyed apart from the
name's plain `*`, so `$^\ast$Deceased` under `Ann Able$^{1,*}$` was in doubt (the class's text; a displaced store lost
every affiliation) and `$^*$` under `$^{1,\ast}$` too; a legend note's `mark=` stays the glyph its line prints
(`line_mark`), and a legend is read by that printed glyph as well as by its operand (`legend_note_kind`:
`\textsuperscript{\textasteriskcentered}Deceased` is a note as `$^*$Deceased` is), and a requested asterisk no line
answers still shows on the name as its operand prints it (`prints_another_asterisk`: icrc2009's `\IEEEauthorrefmark{1}`
sets the math `∗` though read in text, 0909.3754, 0912.0896, 2609.25589). The frontmatter observer reads printed
glyphs by the same forms (`one_asterisk` in its writer's `show_legend_mark`, `hide_answered_marks`, `repeated_symbols` and
re-part; `ASTERISK_FORMS` in `resolver::mark_labels` and `lines.rs`'s `mark_text_symbols`); `insert.rs`'s and
`affiliations.rs`'s `∗`→`*` glyph maps (batch 100b's files) still read U+2217 only. "Deceased" is a legend only where the text does not read as an affiliation (`reads_as_affiliation`) or opens with
the word (`opens_with_deceased`), on the kernel's line route (`legend_note_kind`) and in the observer (`is_legend_text`)
alike (review rev100a S2: `$^\dagger$Department of Deceased Estates, Univ C` an affiliation, as REVTeX's binding read it;
`$^\dagger$Deceased 3 March 2021; formerly at Univ C` a note).

**Batch 100a guards** `perfect_kernel_batch100a::{a_deceased_legend_is_a_note_of_its_carriers,
a_run_in_or_in_place_line_led_by_an_unrequested_symbol_stays_the_classs,
a_displaced_line_led_by_an_unrequested_symbol_stays_the_classs, a_routed_line_of_several_requested_entries_is_cut_by_the_api,
run_in_lines_keep_their_print_order}` (repros `run_in_deceased_legend_is_a_note_of_its_carrier`,
`author_block_deceased_legend_is_a_note_of_its_carrier`, `binding_symbol_led_deceased_entry_is_a_note_of_its_carrier`,
`run_in_line_led_by_an_unrequested_symbol_stays_the_classs`, `in_place_line_led_by_an_unrequested_symbol_stays_the_classs`,
`run_in_symbol_line_spelled_otherwise_is_its_carriers_note`, `displaced_line_led_by_an_unrequested_symbol_stays_the_classs`,
`displaced_line_of_several_requested_entries_is_cut_by_the_api`, `in_place_line_of_several_requested_entries_is_cut_by_the_api`,
and (d)'s `run_in_lines_a_run_places_keep_their_order`, GREEN since int127a); round 2 (review rev100a)
`{an_asterisk_keys_alike_written_or_printed, a_line_led_by_a_printed_symbol_no_name_requests_stays_the_classs,
deceased_naming_an_institution_is_an_affiliation}` (repros `run_in_asterisk_legend_under_a_math_asterisk_mark_is_its_carriers_note`,
`run_in_text_asterisk_legend_under_an_asterisk_mark_is_its_carriers_note`,
`run_in_math_asterisk_legend_under_an_asterisk_mark_is_its_carriers_note`,
`displaced_math_asterisk_line_under_an_asterisk_mark_is_its_carriers`,
`in_place_math_asterisk_legend_under_an_asterisk_mark_is_its_carriers_note`,
`run_in_lines_led_by_unrequested_printed_symbols_stay_the_classs`, `run_in_deceased_named_institution_is_an_affiliation`,
`run_in_deceased_legend_naming_an_institution_is_a_note`); unit
`author_split_tests::{classify_thanks_reads_deceased_as_a_word, clean_frontmatter_labels_keys_an_asterisk_one_way,
opens_with_deceased_reads_the_first_word}`. Residual of the Cut the handover reaches (99a's own
output, restored): a list's trailing hand-labelled note lines (`a) also at UCEH …` … `g) …`, `b)` onward mid-line) join
its last entry, so hep-ex0106079's five `$^{12}$` authors hold them, and an unmarked trailing note line (`Both authors
contributed equally.`) joins the last entry's text (RED repros
`displaced_hand_lettered_notes_after_the_marked_entries_go_to_their_requesters`,
`displaced_unmarked_trailing_note_line_is_the_blocks`; SYNC row "100a").

**Guards** `perfect_kernel_batch99b::{a_marked_address_store_the_class_title_page_prints_is_each_authors_line,
a_numbered_affiliation_store_is_its_sole_authors, a_run_in_affiliation_setter_line_is_its_marked_authors}`; repros

### 956. An e-mail address printed inside an affiliation-kind entry is the entry's e-mail in both engines: its lines and notes of addresses are kinded once at the API, and one Link chain places every e-mail of an entry (Perl: the address stays in the affiliation's text, copied onto every carrier; an `\email` inside an entry one contact on its label's owners; a note in an `\affiliation` a document `<pubnote>`)

**Defect** (census127 cluster 1, the address family: 191 dev20k papers copy an address-bearing affiliation to 2+
holders). The old reader kinded no address inside an affiliation, alternate affiliation or address entry: authblk's
`\affil{Univ \\ Town \\ \{a,…\}@x}` gave every author the brace list as affiliation text (2502.01754),
`\affil[ ]{\texttt{\{a,b,c\}@x}}` made it the last author's affiliation (2602.21641, 2307.02047), the kernel's mark-led
`{\tt $^1$\{…\}@x}` lines were affiliations of the mark's carriers when a link line closed the block (1901.09107),
llncs's `\email{\{ivan|carolin\}@x}` and `\email{robert.holland15|e.chotzoglou16|b.kainz@x}` were one contact on a
nameless creator (0902.3918, 1909.00276), aaspp4's `$^3$…;\\ Email:dzg@, xywang@, hyf@` was welded into the entry on
every carrier (astro-ph0512555; `place_address_runs` spliced the run back), and REVTeX's
`\affiliation{…\footnote{Electronic address: x}}` / revtex 3's `\address{…\thanks{Corresponding authors e-mail: x}}`
were document `<pubnote>`s (1002.3223, cond-mat0202268; Perl-origin, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:331). The frontmatter
observer read some of them (`take_out_entry_addresses`, OD #938), but its writer never runs on API-only papers.

**Fix (the structure model's Kind and Link, one call site, one chain).**
- **Kind**, `frontmatter_api::kind::kind_entry_addresses`, at `\lx@annotate@frontmatter` right after the Cut (OD #954; each cut
  piece passes once): an affiliation-kind contact's lines (`author_affil_splits`) read by the author block's reader of an
  address line (`line_addresses`: a list, a brace group, one behind an e-mail label) — or, on a marked entry's first
  line, the rest behind the mark (`mark_led_addresses`) — and its notes (`\footnote`, `\thanks`) printing a labelled
  address alone (`note_addresses`: a label of at most four words ending in e-mail words, "Electronic address" now one,
  the label the contacts' name) leave the entry and are e-mail calls digested at its end (`AddressPlacement::Inner`,
  `email_line_calls`), each written-out address in the font the line printed it in — the declarations and wrappers
  round every `@` of the line, when they are one (`email_lines::in_line_font`: `{\tt \{…\}@x}`, 1804.05417;
  `$^\ddag$\tt\{…\}@x`, 2311.01166; `\texttt{\{…\}@x}, \texttt{…@y}`, 2410.24095; a line whose `@`s print in
  different fonts keeps its addresses plain — and so, wrongly, does a line one of whose `@`s is in `\href`'s URL
  argument, which prints nothing: `\href{mailto:a@x}{\texttt{a@x}}, \texttt{\{b, c\}@y}` gives plain `b@`, `c@` and
  drops `a@`'s `\texttt`, where base kept all three typewriter; RED repro
  `address_family_href_url_at_is_no_printed_font`, review rev100b3, SYNC_STATUS row 100b). An entry of addresses alone stays, empty, as their carrier and is dropped at the flush; the
  class's own name for it (`\mail`'s "Correspondence to", `\altaffiliation[E-mail address: ]`) names its e-mails (not a
  role default, not an empty one). Left as they are: an e-mail command's line (`\email{…}`: the class's label kept,
  llncs's "E-mail"), a template or a list the reader cannot part, an entry a class shares among every author
  (`_share=authors`, llncs's one `\institute`: the shared row's own reading, OD #901; 1103.2027), and a line holding any
  command but the url, link, font, size and spacing ones an address line prints with (`prints_addresses_only`): an
  ORCID, a note or a symbol glued to it prints more than its addresses (2308.02269's
  `\url{{arim,sue}@ist.hokudai.ac.jp}\orcidID{…}` had read the ORCID's digits into the domain and lost the ORCID). Lines
  only: an address inside a line of other words is the observer's text reading's alone (residual, SYNC 100b).
- **Entry key**: `\lx@annotate@frontmatter@now` gives every affiliation-kind contact a key (`_entry`) and whether a
  footnote symbol leads it (`_entrysymbol`); every e-mail digested while its content is digested (`ENTRY_DIGESTING`)
  takes them — an `\email` the author wrote there as well as the Kind step's calls.
- **Link**, `email_owners::entry_address_owners`, the one chain both engines run (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4): the author an
  address spells (any live author; names read by their base letters, `joze.rozanec@` Jože M. Rožanec's, 2105.01929) →
  the entry's only carrier, when it is the entry's one address no one spells, no other address of the entry spells that
  carrier and the carrier holds no address of its own — any address of a one-author document is its author's
  (1806.11431) — (2403.17706's `1022041122@, 1223045440@, hhp@` under Haiping Huang's second institute are three
  people's, 2411.17073's `bull@` is not Awais Naeem's beside his `awais.naeem@`) → every carrier of a symbol-led entry —
  a printed symbol or a symbol its call's label is, authblk's `\affil[*]{…}` — that no other address of the entry
  spells, as the only-carrier step excludes them (1907.01388's `* chinarentao@, zhutou@` under Tao Ren* and Tao Zhou*:
  `zhutou@` Zhou's alone) (before the order, the charter's "every symbol carrier") → one per carrier in order, every spelled one agreeing → the block, once (ruling E,
  TENTATIVE, main session 2026-11-02; surname-first initials, `dzg` for Z. G. Dai, are not read). Today's runs it at the
  flush (`insert::link_entry_addresses`, after `relocate_annotations`, before `respell_emails`): an entry's carriers are
  the authors holding a copy of its printed text (the same affiliation set after each name is one entry, 2212.12876; an
  entry of addresses alone is its address list, 2208.10784), else those holding its e-mails; an e-mail printing
  addresses alone is written out (`resolver::addresses_in`, in the font it printed in), a labelled group or one beside
  words left whole, and one printing more than text — an ORCID's link, math — never (`insert::prints_text_only`); an address an author already holds is not put on the block too; an e-mail command the author wrote
  inside the entry holding one address keeps the one author its own call placed it on unless it spells another
  (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 #420; jmlr's `\Name{…} \Email{costis@…}` under a misread `\AND`, 2002.00057, 1504.01446,
  2509.23923); each placed e-mail follows the entry on its owner (R8). Where the observer's writer copies an address
  onto an owner today's chain left it off, the copies of one span go by their place in the reading, not by their texts
  (`writer::plan::reading_order`, `apply::prints_after`: 2311.01166's `sjwang3@` had come before `ycwang12@`). The observer runs it in `answer_inner_emails` —
  every e-mail inside an entry, labelled or not (`api.rs` defers an unlabelled entry's, which it had copied onto every
  owner and so into the upfront grid, 2307.02047; an entry of addresses alone still holds its role for a later
  `annotate=new` run, as today's empty contact does, 2003.10933), entries printing the same addresses together — and in
  `take_out_entry_addresses` over the carriers of every print of a text; there a run the chain would give the block
  stays in the entry (the text reading's fail-safe: the writer declines a paper whose re-part needs a block creator for
  it, 2401.08092's names re-part lost).
- `place_address_runs` gives every run under an affiliation back to its entry — but one address under an affiliation one
  author requests, still made that author's contact there (a raw class's store's `\email` prints nowhere left in the
  entry, astro-ph0701846): the Kind step takes it out.
- **Readers, one separator set**: `|` parts a group's local parts like `,` and `;` (`ADDRESS_GROUP_SEPARATORS`, both
  readers; `$\mid$`, `\vert` print one, 2110.02026), an unbraced `a|b@x` or `a/b@x` too (`UNBRACED_LIST_SEPARATORS`,
  hep-ph9906243's `deleo/walrod/vaz@…`; `email_addresses`, the observer's `plain_addresses`/`address_runs`), and a
  comma list of local parts written without spaces, `a,b,c@x`, inside a `;`- or `,`-parted line, each part at the
  domain by the one function both readers call (`write_out_unspaced_lists`, `is_listed_local_part`: lowercase, a
  letter, no space after the comma — `address_runs`' list rule —, never a word naming a contact, `email,ann@x.org`,
  nor one letter, an initial, which ends no list either, `smith,j@x.org`: `ends_a_listed_run` (a list written with
  spaces keeps `address_runs`' word test alone, `E-mail: ann, b@x.org`, review rev103a2 — a mixed list with one spaced
  comma too, `ann, bob,c@x.org`, review rev103a3 n6); 2112.00969's `ann@a.edu;
  dzyang,ashishbshah@fb.com`, whose `dzyang` the flush's write-out had dropped while the take-out cut it, batch 103a);
  a run glued by its comma to a word before it that is no local part is no list, the word left whole as on base
  (`M.R.Pestalozzi,a.chrysostomou,j.l.collett@herts.ac.uk`: written out, `M.R.Pestalozzi` was cut off, the readings
  disagreed and the label copied the whole word onto all three carriers; a contact's word before it, `email,ann,bob@`,
  is a label), and at the flush a list written without spaces whose every part spells one author, each its own, is
  written out with its capitals as printed (`spelled_unspaced_list`, `insert::link_entry_addresses`: each of the three
  on its author; astro-ph0612088, int131fix, guard
  `perfect_kernel_batch131fix::unspaced_list_whose_every_part_spells_an_author_is_written_out`);
  the flush writes an e-mail out only where its two readings (`addresses_in`, `address_take_out`) agree, else it stays
  whole where its call put it (a spaced list not opening the line, `ann@a.edu; dzyang, ashishbshah@fb.com`); an e-mail
  label glued to an address (`Email:aable@a.edu`, `(E-mail:bogdan@…`, astro-ph0404330) is no part of it, and names
  the line's contacts as a spaced label does (`email_line_label` splits it off where the whole line reads the same
  addresses as the rest behind it: `\address{Univ A, Town\\ Email:zz@x.org}` gives `<contact name="Email: "
  role="email">zz@x.org</contact>`, not the label in the content and a `mailto:Email:zz@x.org` — GL1; hep-ph9606235,
  astro-ph0001190, hep-ph0411269, 2206.00543; guards `perfect_kernel_batchgl1::{glued_label_names_an_address_line_contact,
  glued_label_names_a_mailto_link_contact, glued_label_names_an_entry_note_contact}`; a glued label behind a first,
  spaced one, or behind a note's label, joins the name that label made, every printed label word kept in printed order:
  `E-mail: Email:zz@x.org` is `zz@x.org` named "E-mail: Email: ", as the spaced form gives, `\footnote{Corresponding
  author e-mail: Email:zz@x.org}` the note "Corresponding author" and the name "e-mail: Email: " — `joined_line_label`,
  review revGL1 B1; guards `perfect_kernel_batchgl1::{second_glued_label_joins_the_line_label,
  second_glued_label_joins_the_note_label}`), and any other colon before the `@` makes no address; a two-letter surname spells a local part of its letters alone
  (`NameKeys::short_surnames`: `an107@` Weili An's, not Anusuya Nallathambi's initials, 2608.22602) — not a name
  particle another word of the name follows (`de`, `la`, `da`, `le`, `di`, `du`: Ana de Souza spells no `de@`, Thanh
  Le's `le@` is his), nor two letters that are a word of the address's own entry, its mailbox (`ai@` under "AI Lab" and
  Wei Ai: `email_owners::is_entry_word_mailbox`, read in both engines; the observer's labelled-entry e-mails carry it as
  the `api:entry-mailbox` tag) — a state code after a comma is no such word ("Cambridge, MA 02138", Jun Ma's `ma@`).

**Beyond Perl** in all of it; F (a note in an affiliation) mirrors the class's own `\email`, which prints the same note.

**Guards** `perfect_kernel_batch100b::{an_address_line_of_an_entry_is_its_authors_emails,
an_entry_of_addresses_alone_is_no_affiliation, mark_led_address_lines_are_their_marks_emails,

### 958. A boxed author block's re-part writes the e-mails the reading spells out of its rows, and a `\resizebox`'s sizes print no name (Perl: one creator holding the whole `tabular`)

**What** (batch 100c; census127 cluster 3, SYNC_STATUS M1/M5). The frontmatter observer's writer re-parts a boxed
author block (a `tabular`, `minipage`, `\parbox` or `\resizebox` in `\author`, which the old reader keeps whole in one
`personname`) by the reading (OD #928). An e-mail the reading gives a creator that today's prints in no item of its own
is now made (`observer/emitter/plan.rs` `Made::Email`, `repart.rs` `item_source`, `apply.rs` `make`): an `ltx:contact
role=email` named as `\lx@add@email` names one (`get_frontmatter_name(None, "ltx:contact", "email")`, as
`email_contact`), its content the reading's address — one written out of a brace list, `\{ann,cat\}@a.edu`'s
`cat@a.edu` — in the fonts it prints in in the block (`plan::block_address_tokens`: each group holding it that a text
font command opens or a font declaration starts, and the declarations before it in its group; in an alignment, those of
its cell and those before the alignment). The re-part's word check counts a domain word the print shows once as printed
however many written-out addresses repeat it (`Repart::domains`). An e-mail of an API call is never made here (the
plan's write-out has it). `\Gscale@@box` (graphics_sty.rs, `\resizebox`'s box) joins the lexer's `KEYED_CONSTRUCTORS`
(observer/events/mod.rs): its height type and sizes are no ink. A fail-safe comes with it: the re-part declines a name
the reading joined across an alignment's cells (`repart.rs` `joined_across_cells`, over the resolver's
`name:layout-joined`): `K.~Ashwin Kumar& \mbox{\ \ } & Amol Deshpande & …` (1302.4168) read as one name, written
one person once its e-mails could be made; today's creator stays (RED repro `boxed_block_names_in_two_columns`: the
resolver's `joins_previous` joins across a cell boundary, SYNC_STATUS row 100c). A second fail-safe: the re-part
declines a made item whose text joins two or more of the block's Name events (from the one its source span starts at,
each one's words running on the item's, others' between passed over; `repart.rs` `joined_rows`) when one of them that
is a whole row — a line, a cell or a spaced-apart piece, no comma, word or other ink beside it (`whole_row`) — may on
its own name a person (`may_name_a_person`), save the first row of an item a mark labels, the line the mark makes the
entry (`$^{\#}$\,Hellebore Capital Management\\ 63 Avenue …` is the `#` affiliation: 1507.08137, four authors one
creator and a `merged_creators` Error until batch 101c; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch101c::a_marked_entrys_first_row_that_reads_as_a_name_stays_the_entry`). Rows, never runs of words
inside one (`Carnegie Mellon University` is no person), and never a comma's piece (`University of California, San
Diego`, 2103.14969; `Nanjing University, Nanjing, China`, 2609.21619). 2609.37429's `\FormatAuthor{Alessandro Chiesa}{…}{EPFL} \FormatAuthor{Zihan Hu}{…}{EPFL}` (two nested
`tabular`s in one cell) was read as one name whose institution row runs on over the second person's rows and written
Chiesa holding the affiliation "EPFL Zihan Hu zihan.hu@epfl.ch EPFL"; today's one creator now stays (review rev100c B1;
RED repro `boxed_block_two_people_in_one_cell`: two creators are right).

**Why.** The reading had every address right and `item_source` made only affiliations and legends, so the re-part
declined ("an item with nothing to write it from: (Contact("email"), …)") and the whole block stayed one creator, a
`tabular` inside its name; a `\resizebox` printed "0pt" into the names to the lexer. Witnesses 2609.39183,
2507.07465, 2107.12423 (`\resizebox`), 2603.10436 (`\parbox`), 2608.20401: each author now its own creator with its
affiliations and its e-mail. **Not done (3B, deferred):** an e-mail no name spells (`lab@a.edu`) is the block's, a
block-level contact that invents no nameless creator (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4, 2026-11-01); the writer has no such form but
OD #159's nameless creator, so the re-part declines on it ("a block e-mail no name spells") and today's one creator
stays (2605.09461, 2609.36484; RED repro `boxed_block_emails_no_name_spells`).

**Guards** `perfect_kernel_batch100c::{a_boxed_blocks_emails_are_their_names_contacts,
names_joined_across_cells_are_never_one_written_person, a_person_in_a_row_an_item_joins_is_never_a_contact,
a_resizebox_round_a_boxed_block_prints_no_size}`; repros sectioning-frontmatter/`boxed_block_emails_written_out_of_a_brace_list`,
`boxed_block_email_in_a_grouped_font`, `boxed_block_email_in_a_cell_font`, `boxed_block_resizebox_sizes_print_nothing`.
Updated: `perfect_kernel_batch97b::marked_address_piece_is_no_person` (revtex `A.~Able$^{1}$, B.~in der
Baker$^{2}$, b.baker@two.edu$^{*}$`) now reads two creators, the address B. in der Baker's by its spelling, 0 errors —
its one creator with a `merged_creators` Error was the fail-safe while the re-part could make no e-mail item. Its name
reads `<sup>2,∗</sup>`: the reading gave the `∗` printed after the address to the name (`mark:after-comma`), which
needs the made e-mail item to carry a mark (RED repro `author_marked_email_piece_mark_moves_to_the_name`, SYNC_STATUS
row 100c).

### 961. An affiliation whose whole text is a legend is its carriers' note, read once where every route meets (Perl: an affiliation contact, as the binding or block reader made it)

**Defect** (census129 cluster 6, mechanism 4; dev20k: 87 papers by markup, 15 in the D3 wrong set). A legend line —
"Corresponding author", "Equal contribution", "These authors contributed equally", "Joint first authors", "Work done
during an internship", "Project lead" — was written out as `<contact role="affiliation">` on the names its label marks
wherever it reached the frontmatter by a route other than a symbol-led displaced or run-in line
(`queue_digest::legend_note_kind`, #955) or the observer's own legend reading (`is_legend_text`): authblk's labelled
`\affil[*]{Corresponding author: x@y}` (wlscirep, googledeepmind, osajnl, uai, berkeley through authblk's binding; 45 of
the 87), an author block's line (`$^\ast$ Corresponding author.`, `$\dagger$Project lead`; 10), IEEEtran's
`\IEEEauthorblockA{\IEEEauthorrefmark{4}These authors contributed equally}` (6), a `\thanks` abusing marks (4), icml's
`\icmlaffiliation` (2), an llncs/svjour `\institute` entry (2: 2608.22772's "†" holders had "Joint first authors." as an
affiliation beside the "*" legend already a note), and 18 others.

**Fix (the Kind step for a legend).** `insert::kind_legend_contacts`, at the frontmatter flush after the placement, the
Link step and the observer's writing — the one place every route that makes an affiliation meets: a creator's
`ltx:contact role="affiliation"` carrying the role's default name whose printed text is a legend
(`notes::entry_legend_kind`) and that prints a mark is renamed in place to `ltx:note role="thanks"`, `ltx_note_frontmatter ltx_thanks_<kind>`, its
carriers and its e-mails as they were (the addresses its line printed were already taken out where a route takes them:
2409.05386's `ago@` stays Ororbia's e-mail contact; one left in its text stays there). The reader: the text without its
addresses and their e-mail labels, parted at marks, brackets, commas, colons, semicolons and line breaks (a nested note,
`\footnotemark`'s, is not read); every piece a legend that names no institution (`reads_as_affiliation`; "Deceased"
opening the text a legend whatever follows, #955), a name one of its carriers' personnames spells (`spells_a_carrier`;
a nameless creator, an author block's own, carries for every author: 2609.08556's "corresponding author(s): Xiaofan Xu,
Hua Zhu"), initials, or no letters, and one piece a legend. So a mixed line stays an affiliation ("DeepAuto.ai († :
Equal advising)", 2609.34327; "ByteDance *equal contribution", 2404.02132; "Facebook (work done while at JHU/APL)",
1702.02684; "Corresponding author \\ Proceedings of a workshop"; "Equal contribution, Google DeepMind", a company's name
shaped as a person's that no carrier has, review rev103c S2), and so do an address change and funding (an institution
is named for its funder as often). The note's `mark` is a mark that prints: the superscript its text opens with, else
a key of the label it was placed by, whole (2602.19190's `$^{*\dag}$Project lead: Yi Yang` `*†`), that a printed mark
gave or that prints — an `affiliation:K` label read off a printed superscript (the marks path, the Cut, the observer's
writer: 2609.03342, 2503.10710), a key a carrier's name shows or requests by its superscript (`Tayal<sup>4</sup>`,
2410.12184; `Bridgeford$^{1,\dagger}$`), or a label its binding prints before the line (`_labelprints`,
`frontmatter_api::LABEL_PRINTS`, a declared `Frontmatter` key: authblk's `\affil[*]`, authblk.sty:142 `\AB@affilnote`;
jheppub's and jcappub's `\affiliation[*]`, `\item[$^{#1}$]`, 2204.11919; cas's letter, `cas_labelled_entry`, 2303.06763)
— the carrier's own among several (`\affil[1,2]{These authors contributed equally}`: Ann's "1", Bob's "2", 2301.13111).
**A legend that prints no mark stays the affiliation it was**, whatever its route (main-session ruling 2026-11-04,
review rev103c B1, rev103c2 B-A): a note shows its text only behind its mark (`ltx_note_mark` holds the mark,
`ltx_note_outer` is `display:none` until hovered, LaTeXML.css:513,525), so an empty mark leaves nothing to reach it by
and a mark the page never prints names nothing on it — an unlabelled `\affil[ ]{Corresponding author: …}` (2412.14916,
2305.02090, 2609.07982), an author block's unmarked line (2004.11569, 2607.01136), a symbol printed as text and not as
the label (2011.02402's "∗ Equally contributed", 2410.12405, 2602.22712) — 18 papers of the A/B — and a binding's key
or an entry's place: icml's `\icmlaffiliation{intern}{Work done during an internship}` (a key; icml prints the
affiliation's number, "3": 2106.09776), svjour's `\institute{… \and A. King (corresponding author, …) \and …}`
(`affiliation:2` by its place, `labelseq`, recorded as `_seqlabel`, `affiliations::SEQUENCE_LABEL`; svjour_blank
prints no number and no name a mark: 1507.04774). IEEEtran prints `\IEEEauthorrefmark{n}` as the n-th footnote symbol
(`*` for 1), and so does the binding since #968: a label it placed shows the symbol its carriers' names print (`‡` for
`\IEEEauthorrefmark{3}`; 2205.00125, 2410.12184, 2504.18719, 2507.23474, 2603.14786).
`classify_thanks` (#156) reads an author's part in the work as a contribution: a project role as whole words ("project
lead/leader", "joint/co-first author(s)", "core contribution/contributor(s)", "senior author(s)/authorship") and the
work's circumstances opening the note ("Work done during/while/as …") — only where every piece of the text, read as it
prints (`printed_words`: a caller's `$^{\dagger}$`, `\textsuperscript` out), is a legend (`entry_legend_kind` with no
carriers); else the text reads as it would without them. That one gate serves every reader of the kind — the kernel's
line route (`queue_digest::legend_note_kind`), the observer's legend reading (`is_legend_text`), the line readers'
`classify_thanks(..) == "note"` tests, a `\thanks`'s CSS kind — so an institution named with a role's words
("$^{\dagger}$Project Lead Institute, Univ D", "$^{\ddagger}$Core Contributor Network, Paris") is an affiliation on
every route, as on base (review rev103c S1; the Kind step reads its pieces with the readings ungated, `thanks_kind`).
"Project lead: Yi Yang" names its author, so it is the Kind step's, which knows its carriers. The observer's writer
writes "†Project lead" and "Joint first authors." as legends (show_legend_mark hides the name's mark the note shows),
and a creator `\thanks{Work done during an internship}` is `ltx_thanks_contribution` (was `ltx_thanks_note`).

**Beyond Perl**: Perl keeps every legend an affiliation contact (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4: author annotations are notes).
Measured (A/B 103c r1 vs int130a, 1,881 papers: the 87, the witnesses, 800 phrase-bearing and 1,000 control papers of
int125a_s10k): 129 papers held a legend as an affiliation; 125 papers changed, E 1,883 = 1,883, F 5 = 5. After the
review's fixes (re-A/B of the 125 changed papers + 2602.19190 vs int130a): 107 papers change, 104 of them a legend now a
marked note, none with an empty mark (the 18 unmarked legends back to base); E 11 = 11, F 0 = 0, words +6; `fm_checks`
0 creators merged or lost, 0 e-mails moved, 0 word types lost — no printed word lost in the XML and the rendered page.
The gate returns two `\thanks{Work done during an internship at Microsoft Research Asia.}` CSS kinds to `ltx_thanks_note`
(2110.15064, 2410.24211: an institution named after the circumstances).

**Guards** `perfect_kernel_batch103c::{an_affiliation_that_is_a_legend_is_its_carriers_note,
a_project_role_or_joint_first_authorship_is_a_contribution_note, institutions_named_with_legend_words_stay_affiliations,
a_legend_whose_label_prints_no_mark_stays_an_affiliation}` (repros `legend_kind_icml_keyed_legend_stays`,
`legend_kind_svjour_institute_sequence_stays`, `legend_kind_authblk_multilabel_legend_marks_each_carrier`: review

unit `author_split_tests::classify_thanks_reads_project_roles_and_the_works_circumstances`; repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/legend_kind_*` (the controls `legend_kind_institutions_named_with_role_words_stay` and

`perfect_kernel_batch77y::mark_led_line_under_symbol_lines_is_no_names`,
`perfect_kernel_batch78f::{jheppub_emailadd_corresponding_author_star_legend, jheppub_emailadd_note_owners_are_a_set,
jheppub_emailadd_two_marked_authors_stay_the_blocks}`, `perfect_kernel_batch78u::author_thanks_inside_a_mark_keeps_the_mark_and_the_note`,
`perfect_kernel_batch92b::spacing_parts_a_marks_labels` and `perfect_kernel_batch95b::a_label_spelled_with_a_command_is_read_to_it`

done before joining Google DeepMind" (2603.23994), funding legends (1604.05657), a
legend sentence holding commas (1703.07724's "The authors wish it to be known that, in their opinion, the first two
authors should be regarded as Joint First Authors.": a comma parts a piece, which keeps "Entity, legend" lines

**Amended (107c; census138 LEGEND).** `classify_thanks` reads three more role phrases, each in the words the note prints
(`printed_words`: the observer's writer classifies a legend's untexed tokens, `\textsuperscript{$\star$}Work …`): "joint

(`\textsuperscript{*}First author`, 2609.03429; "The first author is supported by …" stays funding), and "work performed

carriers). An institution named after the circumstances keeps the gate's reading (the Kind step's piece is no legend

address: …", "Supported by NSF grant 123" —, an affiliation), which stays where it was; its lines' breaks are one each

but its carriers' note (`ltx_thanks_note`), as "Deceased" is: the frontmatter observer reads a dedication behind a

legend's mark reading) or a line whose leading mark a name answers to this Kind step (`$^2$Dedicated to the memory of

an unmarked one is the paper's, a marked one its carriers'. A one-line mixed text (`In memory of Professor Cole, and
supported by NSF grant 123`) stays one dedication, every word kept. The notes the observer's writer makes keep the print

### 962. An IEEE `\IEEEauthorblockA` shared by a names line goes on every name, whatever layout or notes stand before it; a refmark-led address line is its marks' (Perl: one creator holding the whole block)

**Perl behavior**: IEEEtran.cls.ltxml maps `\IEEEauthorblockN{…}` and `\IEEEauthorblockA{…}` to their text, so
`\author{\IEEEauthorblockN{Ann Able, Bob Baker and Cy Cole}⏎⏎\IEEEauthorblockA{University of X, City\\ Email:
\{ann, bob, cy\}@x.edu}}` is one creator holding names, affiliation and addresses. **Rust before**: the binding reads
each block (`\lx@add@authors@append`, `\lx@add@affiliation@marked[annotate=new]`; OD #128 "Bare text between blocks")
and wrapped every bare top-level run between blocks in `\IEEEauthorblockA{…}` (`wrap_bare_author_block_text`,
ieeetran_cls.rs). A run printing nothing — a blank line (1401.2118, 1705.03529), a `\vspace`, a `\\[2mm]` — or holding
only a `\thanks` (1508.00691) became an affiliation printing nothing that took the names before it (`annotate=new`),
so the real block reached the last name only: every other author lost the affiliation, with 0 Errors (dev20k: 10
papers, also 1708.09492, 1909.04111, 2105.14731, 2304.07909, 2404.12786, 2510.06250, 2608.23934). Printed text ending
in `\\` under each `\and` column's name (`\IEEEauthorblockN{Ann Able} \textit{School X}\\ \IEEEauthorblockA{…}`,
2605.15804) made a regular `\and`×`\\` grid, which `transpose_ieee_author_grid` read as row-major: the
`\IEEEauthorblockA` row went to the last author. And an `\IEEEauthorrefmark{1}`-led address line
(`\IEEEauthorrefmark{1}\{ms1801, bob\}@x.edu`, 2301.03018, 2510.06608) stayed an affiliation of every mark-1 author:
`relocate.rs` `leading_line_label` compared the first token with `\textsuperscript` literally, so the Kind step
(`defs/frontmatter_api/kind.rs` `kind_entry_addresses`, OD #956) never took its addresses out.

**Rust behavior**: a bare run that prints nothing once its line breaks (`\\` with its `*` and `[…]`, `\newline`) are
left out (`prints_nothing`, email_owners.rs, now `pub`) passes through as its spaces and braces (a group it opens
around a block stays balanced: `{\small \authorblockA{…}}`, cs0507001); a run of notes only before an
`\IEEEauthorblockA` is the document's notes, as in a block (`document_notes`, notes.rs: `\thanks` the
`\lx@add@pubnote@thanks`), and one no block follows is wrapped as before, so the block reader still reads it (the
e-mails of `\thanks{E-mail: \{lins, shahmohm, helgamal\}@ece.osu.edu.}` after the names, 0710.2705; a note a name's
mark requests, 1504.01072); printed text is wrapped without the line breaks and spaces it
ends with. A grid transposes only when every cell that prints something
names an author (`\IEEEauthorblockN`/`\authorblockN`); a column's rows of blocks or text are its author's, as printed.
`leading_line_label` reads a mark command or an alias of one (`is_mark_command`, marks.rs) as `\textsuperscript`, so
the mark-led address line is its marks' e-mails: bob@x.edu Bob's, ms1801@x.edu (no name spells it, three names carry
its mark) the block's, as the Kind step's "else the block". The kernel's "a contact printing nothing claims its
authors" stays (revtex `\noaffiliation`, aastex `\nocollaboration`). A run of notes and parts printing nothing
(`\thanks{…}\vspace{2mm}`) is notes too: `document_notes` leaves the rest out once it prints nothing. A names line
the kernel does not split (`\IEEEauthorblockN{Daniel (Yue) Zhang*, Yang Zhang*\thanks{…}, Dong Wang}`, 1909.04111;
`name_count`) is re-parted by the observer's writer, each name holding the shared block: the re-part gate
(`emitter/repart.rs`, "an item given more authors by no ruling") accepts an item the API's `annotate=new` or `run` run
gives every name (`api:annotate:new`, `api:annotate:run`) as it does the block reader's `owner:annotate:run`, when at
most one of today's creators held it and no name of today's prints a mark before its first word — in every class, not
IEEE's alone (1911.01005 acmart; revtex `\author{Ann (Al) Able*, Bob Baker*}\affiliation{…}`, review rev104a2) — a re-part takes a name's
marks out, as the reading has them, so the IEEE ordinal template (`1\textsuperscript{st} Milin Patel`) would print
"1 Milin Patel" (2503.04159, 1806.11431, 2406.04658 stay as today's; `ordinal_names` the control). An `\and`
at the top level of an `\IEEEauthorblockA`/`\authorblockA` argument that a block macro follows starts the next author,
as pdflatex prints two columns (a brace missing after the first author's block, `\authorblockA{…\\ \and
\authorblockN{Hadas Kress-Gazit}\authorblockA{…}}}`, 2105.06537): the binding closes the argument before the `\and`,
reads the rest as top-level blocks and drops the argument's own closing brace (the first top-level `}` no bare run
opened); before, the second author's blocks were the first's too (the base kept them apart only while the `\thanks`
before Wil Thomason's block was wrapped into an empty block). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch104a` (9); repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/ieee_shared_block/`. **Not reached** (RED repros, SYNC_STATUS row 104a): an explicit
`\IEEEauthorblockA{}` before the shared block (`explicit_empty_block`), and an "Email:" line with a refmark before each
address, still one entry labelled by its first mark (`email_line_marked_addresses`; 2209.10056, 2109.15322); a grid
with a cell naming no author, left in its columns, gives its creators column-major (`mixed_grid_column_major`: Ann,
Cy, Bob against pdflatex's Ann, Bob, Cy; owners right); an IEEE ordinal names line the kernel does not split
(`2\textsuperscript{nd} Marzana Khatun {3\textsuperscript{rd} Rolf Jung}`, 2503.04159; 1806.11431) stays one creator,
the writer's re-part reading the ordinals as marks.

### 963. AASTeX 6's `\email` after `\correspondingauthor{X}` before any `\author` is X's (Perl: dropped)

**Perl behavior**: aas_support.sty.ltxml:122 `\email` is `\lx@add@email`, the contact of the author before it, for
every AASTeX version; `\correspondingauthor{X}` (:115) is a `role=correspondent` contact labelled `fuzzy:X`. An
`\email` before the first `\author` (`\correspondingauthor{Ann Able}\email{ann.able@a.edu}\author{Ann Able}…`, census129
Repro A) has no author and is dropped. **Rust before**: the address on a nameless creator (95 dev20k aastex6x papers
with an e-mail there; 2601.19870, 2408.08166, 2206.11167, 2010.09756).

**Rust behavior**: aastex631.cls:6917-6931 prints the address in the footnote right after "Corresponding author: X"
(pdflatex: "Corresponding author: Ann Able / ann.able@a.edu"), as aastex701.cls:13341-13353 does, so the `\email`
after `\correspondingauthor{X}` names X: aas_support_sty.rs's `\email` is `\lx@add@aas@email`, AASTeX 7's dispatch
made every 6+ version's — the flag `\iflx@aas@correspauthor` is the next `\email`'s and an `\author` ends it
(aastex701.cls:12678). The address takes the correspondent's `fuzzy:X` label (placed by the name it spells,
`named_creators`) when it is one address, X one name, and, in AASTeX 6, no `\author` precedes it; otherwise it is read
as any `\email` (`\lx@aas@email@list`, the plain `\lx@add@email`): after an author, the author's before it, an
address spelling another author moving to that one (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4, OD #938) — the label would have taken it off
its author where X names no author whole (`\author{Yukun Huang (黄宇坤)}…\correspondingauthor{Yukun Huang}\email{…}`,
2511.16056) —; a list of several addresses (`\correspondingauthor{Lile Wang, Shenzhen Xu}\email{lilew@pku.edu.cn,
xushenzhen@pku.edu.cn}`, 2511.09481; 1803.06255, 2602.01373) each by the name it spells; a correspondent of several
names (`\correspondingauthor{Jiacheng Meng \& Cheng Li}`, 2008.13733) labels no single address. AASTeX 7, whose other
`\email`s print nothing, labels it wherever it stands (`\lx@aas@corresp@anywhere`; 2608.02190, 2608.00173). AASTeX 5.x
and emulateapj keep their own `\email`. So one address under a correspondent of one name, before any author, is that
name's; several addresses, or several names, are each read by spelling. Open (RED repro class-bindings/
`aastex631_correspondingauthor_after_authors_email_is_the_named_authors`, review rev104d P1): after every `\author`,
`\correspondingauthor{Ann Able}\email{xq1@a.edu}` stays the last author's (Bob Baker's) where the PDF names Ann Able;
fix sketch: take the label when it matches an author's name whole. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch104d::{an_aastex6_email_after_correspondingauthor_is_the_correspondents,
an_aastex7_correspondent_address_list_is_spelled}`; repros class-bindings/`aastex631_correspondingauthor_email_is_the_correspondents`,
`aastex7_correspondingauthor_address_list_is_spelled` (RED → GREEN).

### 964. The marked-list readers read a one-column tabular's rows, commands set side by side, a control return and a number in math as the lines, spacing and marks pdflatex prints (Perl: one contact, the marks printed in it)

**What** (batch 104c; census129 cluster 4, "marked runs 99a's Cut leaves whole"). The readers the frontmatter API's Cut
(OD #954, `cut_marked_contact`) and the author blocks' cutter (`affiliations::entry_calls`, behind every binding's
`affiliation_calls`) read a list through now read:
- **commands set side by side** whose arguments marks lead (`relocate::side_by_side_wrapper_lines`, inside
  `wrapped_lines_as_lines`): acmart's `\institution{$^1$Univ A}\institution{$^2$Univ B}\country{X}` — sigconf prints
  each `\institution` a line (acmart.cls:2623 `#1\par`) — is two entries, each its own `\institution`; the address
  parts after the last are every entry's (`shared_closing_parts` reads a run of the same wrapper on `\\` lines). Not a
  mark command, a line macro or box, a note's command (`\thanks`, `\footnote`). Witness 2006.16977.
- **a control return** as spacing (`email_block_calls::is_spacing`: latex.ltx:558 `\def\^^M{\ }`): a line ending in `\`
  leaves `\^^M` before the next line's mark, which then parts the entries as `\ ` does. Witness 2510.25684
  (`$^1$University of Wisconsin-Madison \ \ \ \⏎ $^2$…`).
- **a tabular's rows** (`relocate::tabular_rows`): a `tabular` that is a whole line is its rows as lines. The test
  rejects only a `&` at the body's top level (cells side by side) and a `\noalign` (vertical material that may print
  text); the column spec is not read, so a `{cc}` tabular whose rows hold no `&` qualifies. The rules set between the
  rows print no text and drop out (`without_tabular_rules`: `\hline`, `\cline{…}`, `\hhline{…}`, booktabs.sty:62-80,
  136's `\toprule`/`\midrule`/`\bottomrule`/`\cmidrule`/`\addlinespace`/`\specialrule` with their optionals) — left in a
  line outside the alignment, `\hline` raised "\noalign cannot be used here" (review rev104c S3). Witness 2606.28962 (`\IEEEauthorblockA{\begin{tabular}{c} $^{1}$ … \\ $^{2}$ … \\
  \{…\}@… \\ \vspace{-0.3cm}\end{tabular}}`); REVTeX's group rule reads it too, so 0911.3234's tabular `\affiliation`
  goes to each author by its rows' marks (98e's fail-safe had put it once at the block; a `\parbox` keeps the fail-safe).
- **a mark on a spacing nucleus after a plain one** (`relocate::spaced_marks_written`, which `entry_calls` now applies
  as REVTeX's group rule does): the list may open with a plain `$^{1}$`, and that lead turns on the `$N$` reading below
  too. Witness 2106.01286 (`$^1$CITI Laboratory, INRIA, $\quad ^2$LTCI, … $\quad ^3$Technion`). Not a nucleus mark
  glued to the word before it (plain spaces only, no separator, its nucleus printing no gap) and to a letter run after
  it: `Lab for ${}^{3}$He Physics` is the isotope, the entry's text, as `notes::split_marked_pieces` reads a glued
  `$^{3}$He` (review rev104c S2: written as `$^{3}$`, its digit was taken as a label and lost). The word `and` (any
  case) or `\&` before the mark is glue as a comma is, `Univ X, and ${}^2$Lab Y`, `Univ X \& ${}^3$Inst Z`: it
  labels its entry (review rev104c2 F1); other conjunctions (`et`, `und`) are not read and fall into the plain-space
  shape (review rev104c3 finding 4). Open (RED, review rev104c3 finding 1): after `and` a mark glued to a letter run
  some author requests (`Dept of Physics and ${}^{3}$He Lab` under a `$^3$` author) parts the line, "and" and the digit
  lost (repro `revtex_isotope_mark_after_and_is_text_red`).
- **a number set in math alone at a line's start** (`relocate::math_number_mark_at`, at the list's first mark or after a
  `\\`/`\\[len]`): `$1$` is mark 1 where the queued names request it (`$^1$`). Witnesses 0708.2552 (`\affiliation{ $1$
  Gazi University, …\\ $2$ Ankara University, …}`), 0909.5340 (a `$1$` first line over `$^2$`-led ones). Not one
  with an ordinal suffix glued to it (`ordinal_suffix_at`, `symbols::is_ordinal_suffix`: a whole letter run `st`, `nd`,
  `rd`, `th`, a `\textsuperscript{th}`, a `$^{nd}$`): `$3$rd floor` prints "3rd", the entry's text (review rev104c S1),
  but an uppercase `St` before a `.` or a space and a capital is the word "Saint", `$1$St. Petersburg`, `$3$St
  Andrews`, the line's mark read (review rev104c2 F3; a lowercase `$1$st Floor` stays the ordinal; open, RED: `$1$St
  Floor` loses its digit, `revtex_math_number_mark_before_st_floor_red`, and a tie, `$1$St~Andrews`, is not read as
  Saint, review rev104c3 findings 2 and 5); a
  word glued otherwise is the line's text after its mark (0909.5340's `$1$Department`), and no space after the number
  nor a list opened by one is required (1511.00510's `$5$` line under a `$^1$` first line).

**Why.** pdflatex prints each of these as marked lines (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4: an entry is its mark's names'); read as
one entry, the whole run was every author's or the block's. Perl has no Cut (OD #954).

first `\affiliation` line, which the class numbers 1 itself (1903.07834, `revtex_unmarked_first_affiliation_line_red`);

prints "Joint Lab" under both; review rev104c p12); the isotope line above is still parted at its mark, "3He Physics,

loses its "rd", "3 floor" a nameless creator's. Nucleus marks parted by plain spaces inside one line, `${}^1$Univ X
${}^2$Lab Y`, give each author the right entry but leave the mark digits in the contact text ("1Univ X", "2Lab Y";
int131a0 "Univ X", "Lab Y"): the price of the plain-space glue rule (review rev104c2 F2;
`revtex_nucleus_marks_spaced_in_one_line_red`). Outside this reading (census129 cluster 4's other papers): an address
macro line (`\mailsa`, llncs 1604.03221), a second author block in the document (2006.15775), ieeeconf's kernel
`\author` line (2110.11491), authblk's `\affil[\hspace{-1ex}]` label (2502.06575), a legend on an entry (2609.38081).

*Live rule: OD #459.*

### 966. A line of addresses inside an affiliation-kind entry leaves the entry, its addresses the entry's e-mails, read once where every route meets (Perl: the line stays in the affiliation's text, copied onto every holder)

**Defect** (census132 cluster 1, ADDR-a; dev20k int133a: 40 papers, 77 creators, 0.200 pp per paper; article 14,
IEEEtran 12, revtex 4). An "Email:" / "E-mail:" / "Corresponding author:" line, a braced list (`{a, b}@x`), a comma
list or `(a; b)` inside an affiliation, alternate affiliation or address stayed in the entry's text — after a line
break, or the whole entry — and was copied onto every holder (the scorer's `email_of_other`, `aff_unexplained`). The
token-level Kind step (#956, `frontmatter_api::kind::kind_entry_addresses`) reads only a line its tokens show; it misses a
document's macros (`\IEEEauthorblockA{\hpcaaffiliation\\\hpcaemail}`, 2608.22602), authblk's `\authorcr`
(2111.01631, 2309.05601), a connective "and" (`E-mail: a@x, \{b, c\}@y, and d@z`, 2302.02638), a nested
`\IEEEauthorblockA` (2410.11002), a font switch or a nested group round a list (2609.01511, 1904.04821), marks inside
the line (`$^1$\{yanhao90, tankl\}@…\quad $^2$yuchenli@…`, 1706.04764; 2209.10056, 2505.11901), an escaped `\_`
(2605.16453), and the lines an author block makes (2207.11193, 1111.6932).

**Fix (the Kind step for an entry's address line).** `insert::kind_address_lines`, at the frontmatter flush after the
placement, the Link step and the frontmatter observer's writing, before the Kind step for a legend (#961): the one place
every route that makes the entry meets, each holder's copy in place. Run before the writer, it made the writer decline
its re-parts (1509.06333's IEEE names merged, 2501.04244's notes lost), so the writer reads today's frontmatter as
before. An entry's line — its children between two `ltx:break`s — is read as printed: text, font wrappers, an
address's link, a mark (a superscript or a not yet parsed formula printing footnote symbols, asterisks of any form,
numbers or one letter; or the symbols a text opening the line prints) kept with its place; anything else (a formula, a note, another link) makes it no line of addresses. Its last address run
(`resolver::address_runs`, the reader the observer takes addresses out by: braced groups, shared-domain lists, "and",
brackets, the e-mail label word), with nothing but separators after it and no template or list the reader cannot part
(`is_pattern_address`, `lists_local_parts`), and its label — the run's e-mail label with the contact words before it
(`names_a_contact`: "Corresponding author:", "Correspondence:", "Contact e-mail:"), brackets aside (`(email: …)`,
hep-ph0611390; `[email: …]`, 1009.1145) — are read by `address_line_cut`:
- nothing printed before the label but marks and separators: the whole line leaves the entry, with its line break;
- words before an e-mail label, or before contact words at a sentence or list boundary (`∗To whom correspondence
  should be addressed; E-mail: x`, 1111.6932, 1808.02718, astro-ph0306103; `…, USA. Corresponding author: x`,
  2305.01135): the label and the run leave, the words stay (the LEGEND row reads them);
- an entry whose only line opens with a mark and is contact words with no e-mail word before its addresses
  (`∗Corresponding author: x`): the words stay, the legend #961 makes its carriers' note; unmarked, they name the
  e-mails (an unmarked legend would stay an affiliation: 77y's block line `Corresponding Author: …`, 1310.7913,
  2012.05702).
Each address becomes an e-mail contact on each holder of the entry (`_entry`, `_kinded`), named by the label as printed
(FIDELITY_CHARTER §4: no printed text dropped — "Corresponding author: ", "E-mail: "), else by the class's name of an
entry of this line alone (REVTeX's `\altaffiliation[Electronic address: ]`), else the role's own, in the font the
address printed in (`_font`), with the marks that lead it on the line (`_linemark`: the line's opening mark and any
before the address, else the previous address's — `$**$ email: cx@…, c\_dee@…` leads both, gr-qc0207058; `$^1$a@x,
$^2$b@y` each its own, 1706.04764, 2505.11901 — or, where marks follow the addresses, the ones after each). The Link
step (`link_entry_addresses`, run again over these entries alone) places them by the charter's chain (user ruling R1,
marks win): the author it spells; else, for a mark-led address, the authors whose names answer the mark (a superscript
of the name, a note's mark, a request in `_annotations`; keyed as printed, `printed_mark_keys`: a run of one symbol one
key, every asterisk form one — user ruling 2026-11-02 — so `∗∗` is I. Chowdhury's and `∗` S. Biswas's in
gr-qc0207058), or the block where none does, never the positional steps (an address list, that is, addresses its mark
leads with siblings, one of them spelling an author who does not answer the mark or its entry naming one, is one per person,
not every carrier's: spelling, then elimination as one line's list when the order holds, else the block — `mark_lists`, 107g,
108a: 2102.08716's list spells `cz` out of the names' order, so the three unspelled stay on the block as on base:
`*equal contributions. David Macêdo, …, and Cleber Zanchettin are with … \{dlm,phdl,cz,tbl\}@…` under two `*` names, 2412.13509's
`hmfu@`; siblings spelling only carriers leave the free carriers, `entry_address_owners`' `free`; a lone address on a line a
shared symbol labels stays every carrier's, user ruling 2026-10-30; a mark the entry's several carriers all
answer and no one else is the entry's own and says no more than the entry: `$^{1}$Instituto …, Spain. E-mail: eca@…`
under two names carrying `1`, astro-ph0005055, goes on down the chain, as does a mark where no name shows or requests
any); else the entry's only carrier, else every
carrier of a symbol-led entry, else one per carrier in order, else the block once. A mark the cut takes out that no name
answers is shown before the first address it leads (`show_line_marks`: authblk's `$^\dagger$Email: zq@…` under names
without `†` gives the block `<sup>†</sup>zq@…`; review rev106a S1). A copy an author holds already gives that contact its printed
label where it carries the role's own name (`carry_printed_label`: `Email corresponding author:` onto S. H. Shekh's
`\email{da\_salim@…}`, 2605.16453). An entry left empty is dropped (`drop_empty_contacts`). Left as printed (the
observer's text reading's, the fail-safe): an address beside words with no label (`Univ A, Town, see data@a.org for
data`), a run a tag follows (`a@x (Matvey)`, 2512.10975), a template (`{name.surname}@`, 2009.04283; `Contact:
forename.surname@`, 2410.09681 — `is_pattern_address` reads forename and its kin, review rev106a S2), a line break
inside a font wrapper (`\small\textit{Correspondence:} …\\`, 2311.04121; one inside a printed brace list, or between its
brace and its domain, is read: #970), a phrase-led alternate affiliation
("Correspondence should be sent to a, b and c.", 1209.3452), a group whose domain follows the brace with no dot
(`{a@mails., b@}tsinghua.edu.cn`, 2602.07769; read since 107c), an affiliation the observer's writer makes (mn2e's "Contact e-mail:",
2008.08137), and an address left inside a legend note (2312.10429, 2501.04244).

**Reach.** The 40 witnesses re-scored (score_tiers, both sides converted alike): 22 papers better, 51 creators flip
right, 0 wrong (149 → 200 of 224); 2608.22602 0 → 10 of 13 (`an107` spells Weili An, its surname with digits, and is hers;

An unbraced shared-domain list is read as the braced one is: 2404.00915 prints `tyhuang, yhliu@mae.cuhk.edu.hk`, and Tianyu Huang holds `tyhuang@mae.cuhk.edu.hk` — the usual reading of such a list, but a reading (review rev106a2). 2504.10237) has the phrase already, and the label is cut as before. **Guards** `perfect_kernel_batch107f::{a_role_tag_after_an_address_is_its_owners_note,
a_held_correspondence_note_keeps_the_email_label}` (repros sectioning-frontmatter/`email_role_tag_after_address_ieee`,
