### 967. A tail inside the personname — a membership grade written after the name's comma, a collaboration an author stands for — is the author's contact, read where every author route meets (Perl: the personname's text, or a creator of its own)

**Defect** (census132 row 10, NAMETAIL; dev20k int133a: 15 papers, 22 creators, 0.119 pp per paper). Text that is no
name stayed in `<personname>`: a membership grade written after the name's comma (`Pei-Yung Hsiao\textsuperscript{3},
\textit{Member, IEEE}`, 2107.05093; `\IEEEauthorblockN{Massimiliano Di Ventra, {\it Fellow, IEEE}}`, 2302.11403;
`\IEEEauthorblockN{…, and Melike Erol-Kantarci, \textit{Fellow, IEEE}}`, 2602.16174) — IEEEtran's own
`\IEEEmembership` makes the grade the author's `membership` contact (ieeetran_cls.rs `\lx@IEEE@membership`), the
written form did not; a collaboration inside a raw class's name-block command, which the kernel's split sets round each
name (icrc2009's `\IEEEauthorblockN{… Monica Brigida\IEEEauthorrefmark{3}\\on behalf of the \emph{Fermi}-LAT
Collaboration}`, 0907.0548; `\IEEEauthorblockN{J.K. de Jong \IEEEauthorrefmark{1}\IEEEauthorrefmark{2}for the MINOS
collaboration.}`, 1111.2718), which the author line's collaboration reading (#946) does not look into; a remark after
the name's notes naming whom the author speaks for with no collaboration word (webofc `Eleni
Petrakou\inst{1}\fnsep\thanks{…} for CAPP/IBS`, 1702.03664); and an `\author` whose whole content is a framed
collaboration (elsarticle's `\author{On behalf of the KM3NeT Consortium}` after its three authors, 1201.5050), a
creator of its own.

**Fix.** `\lx@add@author` and `\lx@add@creator` (frontmatter_fields.rs `creator_call`; Perl Base_Utility.pool.ltxml's
token bodies, now read first), the one call every author route makes:
- **A written grade** (`membership_read_out`, defs/frontmatter_fields/names.rs `written_membership_out`): the text after the
  first comma of the name line's own — outside its groups and math, inside the block reader's `\lx@author@withsup{…}` and
  a command the line is set in as its one argument (`name_line_span`) — after which only a grade prints
  (`is_membership_grade`: grade and society words with a rank, `Member`/`Fellow`, among them — `Fellow, IEEE`, `Senior
  Member, IEEE`, `Member, OSA` unbraced — or an abbreviated grade before its society, ascelike's `M.ASCE`) is
  `\lx@add@contact[role=membership]{…}` in its own markup, right after the name; the marks, notes and block-reader
  contact calls written after it (`\thanks{…}`, `\lx@add@affiliation[annotate=3]{…}`: 1611.04834) stay the name's,
  after it, as they print. Only one grade, the line's last: a line printing a grade or a part of one before it between
  its separators (`holds_grade`) holds a name after a grade, and every grade stays (`\textbf{Ann Able, \textit{Member,
  IEEE}; Bob Baker}, \textit{Fellow, IEEE}`: taking the last out alone left the names before it one creator). A degree
  or suffix (`Ph.D., P.E.`, `Jr.`) still qualifies the name; a document's own `\IEEEmembership` definition keeps its
  meaning (63l).
- **A framed collaboration as the whole author, a collaboration inside a name-block command, a remark after the
  notes** — the reading's since P5b (2026-11-12, Option C P5 fact 2): `\lx@add@author` no longer reads them from the
  spelling (`whole_name_collaboration`, `wrapped_collaboration_out`, `name_and_remark` deleted; the reading had
  rewritten every queued call they made). A call or `\and` column printing only a collaboration framed as a remark
  (`Framing::Framed`: "on behalf of", "for", "representing", brackets, dashes) after names is the collaboration contact
  of every name no collaboration covers yet (resolver/lines.rs `frames_the_names`, `framed_collaboration`), its words
  as digested: a macro printing "On behalf of" (segaudit col1), a `\let` copy, `\csname`, `\MakeUppercase`, ties, a
  font group, a `\parbox`, the line's own "and" (`on behalf of the XYZ and ABC Collaborations`), each guarded
  (`perfect_kernel_batchp5b::a_framed_collaboration_call_is_the_names_contact`); brackets and dashes, a third creator
  on the base (the dashed one losing its dashes), are its contact now; so is a class command's bracketed one, revtex's
  `\collaboration{(ATLAS Collaboration)}`, elsart's `\collab{(The CMS-HCAL Collaboration)}` (hep-ex0007045), where Perl
  makes a creator (`\collab` is `\author{#1}`, elsart_support_core.sty.ltxml:71). A line carrying its own mark, note or
  contact is no such call (`frames_the_names_alone`: `[ATLAS Collaboration]\thanks{…}` stays a creator with its note,
  review revP5b; "for"/"on behalf of" with a note is the names' contact as on the base, `speaks_for`). None before any
  name, and an unframed one — the name alone or after a bare "the" — frames none (`\collab{The XYZ Collaboration}`,
  webofc's `\and The SND Collaboration`, 1912.05868): creators, as before.
  The raw name-block shapes (0907.0548, 1111.2718) and the remark after the notes (`speaks_for_after_notes`,
  1702.03664) are the reading's rows C2-C5 (`remark_pieces_joined`). ptephy's `\collaborator{(The X Collaboration)}`
  (2101.03480, 2404.08725) is its four names' contact. RED `elsarticle_author_framed_collaboration_with_a_note_red`
  (post-merge): such a call's own note becomes a nameless creator. RED (post-merge, P5BA; review revP5b): a bracketed
  collaboration call or column with an affiliation of its own (`article_and_column_bracketed_collaboration_with_affiliation_red`,
  `elsarticle_author_bracketed_collaboration_with_its_address_red`, `…_with_a_keyed_address_red`) is the names'
  contact, its affiliation a nameless creator's or the last name's, where the PDF prints it as an author block of its
  own; the "for the" form of the shape was so on the base.
- **The observer's reading** (resolver/lines.rs, `is_membership_part`): a grade, or the pieces the line's commas cut it
  into (`\textit{Senior Member}, \textit{IEEE}`), after a name's comma is that name's `membership` item, no part of
  the name, so the writer's re-part finds each reading name in today's names (vgtc's `\author{Stephen Kasica; Charles
  Berret; and Tamara Munzner, \textit{Senior Member}, \textit{IEEE}}`, 2009.02373: with the grade still in the
  reading's name the re-part declined and the `;`-joined names stayed one creator). The writer gives a grade back to
  its name (`name:qualifier`, as before) where today's holds no contact of its role and text (writer/mod.rs
  `give_back_grades`), so the reading leaves a grade out only where `\lx@add@author` took it out or today's holds the
  same grade as a contact — never out of a
  macro's text (`\IEEEauthorblockN{\AuthorOne,~\AuthorTwo,~…}`, each `\AuthorN` "Name, {\em{Grade, IEEE}}",
  1510.03162) nor out of a membership the author filled with the next name (`\IEEEmembership{Member,~IEEE, Hua~Wei,
  Member,~IEEE}`, 2507.19818). A grade the re-part had nothing to write from, or two authors' alike today's held once,
  declined it and left the line one creator (the bundle A/B int136a vs int135e). **RED (review rev106c2 S1,
  synthetic):** the give-back decides document-wide — a contact of that grade on any author (a binding-made
  `\IEEEmembership`) keeps another author's identical grade out of its name, and the merge returns:
  `grade_given_back_per_creator_red.tex` (3 → 2 creators, silently), `grade_macro_names_and_membership_one_block_red.tex`
  (3 → 1, with an Error), `grade_macro_block_beside_written_grade_red.tex` (3 → 2, with an Error; r1 too). The fix
  decides per creator, matching today's creator by name; no real paper found (the grade-macro papers 1510.03162,
  1803.08650, 1412.0349, 1809.06699, 1406.1340 are as on int135e).
- A content of fewer than three tokens is no name line to look into (`name_line_span`; an author line opened by layout,
  `\vspace{-2em}\hspace{-25pt}…`, 2002.03043, 1307.6590, panicked the first build).

### 969. An affiliation that is a URL or a membership grade is the block's link or its carriers' grade, and an entry a creator holds twice is held once, read where every route meets (Perl: an affiliation contact per call, copied onto every holder)

**Defect** (census132 LEGEND and the KIND-misc duplicate pocket; scorer `aff_unexplained`, `duplicate_contact`). A
line printing a URL alone under an author block — IEEEtran's `{\texttt{\url{https://github.com/…}}}` after
`\IEEEauthorblockA{…}\\`, which the binding wraps into a block of its own (2511.18438), an author block's link line
(2507.19490) — was an affiliation on every author; IEEE_lsens's `\IEEEauthorieeemembermark{2}Senior Member, IEEE` line
(a raw class's mark) an affiliation (2310.02678, 2505.15137); and one entry reached one author twice: one call placed
twice by two routes (a revtex group's affiliations, 1207.1783, 2006.15775, 1207.6694, 1206.0114; PoS's "on behalf of the
Fermi-LAT Collaboration", given to every name and twice to the last when the empty name after it is coalesced into it,
1909.05984; 2108.00864, 2405.14358, 2501.11284), a marked line written again under a later name, whose label
the first name's mark requests twice (easychair 1204.6725), two calls under one label (2603.14883's two
`\cortext[cor]{Corresponding author}`; sn-jnl's `\affil*[1]{Rotman…}` and `\affil[1]{Rotman…}`, 2608.23810, printed
twice by pdflatex), a supplement's `\author{…}\affiliation{…}` written again
after `\maketitle` (2311.16348, 1407.0849).

**Fix.** At the frontmatter flush after the legend Kind step (#961), `insert::kind_link_and_grade_contacts`: a creator's
affiliation contact carrying the role's default name whose whole printed text is one link printing as a URL does (its
target, `http(s)://…`, `www.…`: `sole_link`; a department's name set as a link stays, 1812.03371) is a `url` contact —
the block's own creator's, once (`block_creator`, #159), when it is the block's line: no mark labels it and every author
holds a copy (2511.18438); else each holder's, a line a mark labels its owners' (`\IEEEauthorblockA{\IEEEauthorrefmark{1}
\url{…}}`). One whose text is a membership grade ("Senior Member, IEEE", "Graduate Student Member, IEEE", "Life Fellow,
IEEE", "Member, ACM": grade words, "Member" or "Fellow", a comma, a society whose grades follow a name — the names
reader's `NAME_GRADE_SOCIETIES`, IEEE, ACM, OSA, ASCE, …; one per line: `reads_as_membership_grade`; "Senior Fellow,
IAS" is a position) is its carriers' `membership` contact, as IEEEtran's `\IEEEmembership` makes one (ieeetran_cls.rs
`\lx@IEEE@membership`). Then `insert::drop_repeated_contacts`: two contacts of one role and one name on one creator
printing the same text (spacing aside; case, marks and notes kept) keep the first in print order where they are one
entry — copies of one source call (`_source`: the annotation's queue ordinal, set when `\lx@annotate@frontmatter@now`
digests it, else the entry's own at insertion; every copy keeps it, and the e-mails the address-line Kind step makes of
an entry take it), lines of one label (`_label`), or a call made after `\maketitle` placed the frontmatter (`_latecall`,
`queue_digest::frontmatter_entry_is_late`) restating one the creator holds. Two printed lines of different entries that
share their text are two entries, both kept (lines of one label are one entry, printed twice or not — the label's
reading, 2608.23810): an address's "Groningen" and the next one's (0808.4092, 1106.1785, 2608.29625, 2609.05568,
2406.03340, where 106b r1's text-only key dropped printed lines, review rev106b B1), amsart e-mails differing in case,
an address written again with a footnote of its own, aa's `\thanks{\email{x}}` beside the institute's `\email{x}`, both
printed (2005.03567), aa's `\mail{x}` "Correspondence to" beside the `\email{x}` (two names, `perfect_kernel_batch97b`).
A copy on another creator stays (a shared entry is each holder's). Generic: no class names.

**Not reached** (one line each): two calls of one author printing one text that the class prints once — REVTeX's two
`\email{x}` (2402.07705, one "†" footnote in the PDF), its two `\thanks{These authors contributed equally}`
(2302.04271) —, a class's merge of equal entries, which no binding declares; aastex's `\correspondingauthor{Name

two_printed_lines_alike_both_stay, a_late_restatement_is_held_once}` (repros `legend_kind_link_line_is_the_blocks`,

### 970. A name spells by its base letters and its transliteration; a `{…}@domain` list set over several lines is one address list (Perl: an address spells no one; the list stays in the affiliation's text)

**Defect** (html_feedback #7233, Bundle 5 ADDR-b). (1) An address spelled a name by its base letters alone:
`mo.schaeffler@` spelled no one for "Moritz Schäffler" ("schaffler"), nor `bo.baecker@` for `Bo B\"acker`. The
author block's text reader (`visible_name_text`) drops an accent command and keeps its base letter, and the
frontmatter observer's callers folded the digested name with `resolver::base_letters` before building its keys, so the
transliteration was lost twice (WISDOM #103). (2) A `\{…\}@domain` list set over two `\texttt` lines (`\\` between)
was never read as addresses when one entry spelled no author: the author block welds both lines into the affiliation
above them; the frontmatter observer's reading takes a list out only when every entry has an owner (its fail-safe:
the writer makes no block creator); and the flush's Kind step for an address line (#966) declined a line holding a
line break. The reporter's seven e-mails stayed glued into Kesselheim's "Department of Physics, University of
Cologne", silently.

**Fix (1), one place.** `NameKeys::of` reads the name's letters as printed (`name_text::spelling_name_text`: an
accent or letter command whose letter has a transliteration is that letter — `\"a` ä, `\"{u}` ü, `\r a` å, `{\ss}`
ß, `\o` ø, `\aa` å, `\ae` æ, `\oe` œ) and keys both folds of them: `resolver::base_letters` (now also `æ` a, `œ` o,
`ß` s, as the author block's `letter_command` reads `\ae`, `\oe`, `\ss`) and `resolver::transliterated` over the one
letter table `resolver::transliteration` (ä ae, ö oe, ü ue, ß ss, å aa, ø oe, æ ae, œ oe; upper case likewise). A name
scores the better of its two spellings (`spelled_owners`); no threshold moved: a word's length class (surname of three
letters or more, short surname, a given name held anywhere, the six-letter prefix) is its base spelling's
(`SpelledWord`: `Wei L\"u`'s "lue" stays a short surname, so `bluesky@` spells no one). A tie between a literal and a
transliterated spelling is a tie: an address carries no umlaut, so `mueller@` beside Hans Mueller and Jörg Müller is
neither's by its spelling, and the rest of the placement order decides it (user ruling 2026-11-05, dropping review
rev107a finding 1's tie-break). A surname's six-letter prefix scores only the local part's letters
outside its given name's match (`andrea.rossi@` Andrea Rossi's, not Andrea Andreassen's "andrea" counted twice — a
pre-existing wrong owner; `soeren.hansen@` Søren Hansen's beside Søren Sørensen). Every spelling site passes the name
unfolded: the author block's e-mail readers, the flush's Link step and `kind_address_lines`, `Resolver::respell_emails`,
the observer's `spelled_name`, `links::link_prints_a_handle`. Whom an e-mail moves to (`respell_emails`) is picked
by the name as printed and its transliteration, a spelling of the name as printed (`NameKeys::as_printed`; user ruling
2026-11-05: `joerg.mueller@` is Jörg Müller's, "also written Joerg Mueller"): an AASTeX 5
`\author{J\"org M\"uller and Ann Able}\email{joerg.mueller@x.org}` goes to Müller, and FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 #420's
example, `\email{mueller-group@x.de}` on Anna Smith's own call beside `\author{J\"org M\"uller}`, moves to him as
its ASCII twin does; a base-letter fold only keeps an address on its holder (`muller-group@` stays hers, #938).

**Fix (2), at the flush.** The Kind step for an address line reads a list set over several lines as one line: a line
break inside a printed brace the line opened (`LineText::read`, a newline in the line's text), or between its closing
brace and the `@` of its domain (`domain_goes_on`; 1902.04228's `{majid,…}` / `@deakin.edu.au`); the entry lines a
brace opens and a later one closes are joined, with the breaks between them (`entry_lines`); and where the author
block made the list's lines contacts of their own (an `\and` column's lines: the head an affiliation `{ann.able,…,`,
the tail an e-mail `xq.zz,cy.coe}@x`), those contacts are joined onto the head's line when the joined line is a line
of addresses alone (`join_split_address_contacts`). Its addresses (`LINE_LIST`) are placed over every author as the
author block's reader places the list on one line, FIDELITY_CHARTER §4's order (`email_owners::list_owners`): the

(`LocalPart::standing`, `LocalPart::joined_standing`; brief 107f r2, replacing r1's A/B-tuned thresholds): a name's
key counts where it stands in the local part — its letters, with words parted by `.` `_` `-`, a digit, any other
character, its start and its end. *At full strength*: a whole word, a word's prefix or suffix (`ricky_ang@` Lay Kee
Ang's, not Shengyuan A. Yang's "yang" across the `_`, 2604.02636; `kee.ang@`, `ang2@`), or strictly inside a word
between the name's own initials, at most two characters on each side, counted in characters (`rjosem@` José M.
Rodríguez-Nogales', 1809.06911; `kmfonsecar@` K. M. Fonseca Romero's, 1202.4210). *Weakly*: a key of four letters or

2004.06253; `eetanggz@` Guozhi Tang's, 2106.10681; `ylwanguestc@` Yinglong Wang's, 2208.05114), and a joined spelling of
five letters or more ending a word it does not open (`sechenqi@` Qi Chen's "chenqi", 2003.00397; a joined spelling opening a
word counts at full strength, its separators read through: `j.huang@`). *Not at all*: a key of three letters between other

separator, a joined spelling inside a word or of fewer than five letters ending one (`pyli@` no Yanan Li's "yli",
2105.07637). A truncated surname's first six letters or more stand by the same
predicate (`mkaufman@` Kaufmann's). **A weak spelling never decides** (`spelled_owners`): it owns an address only no
other name spells; where several do, the names are ranked with and without their weak spellings, and the two rankings
agreeing give the owner, else every name either ranks first ties — and the placement order goes on (the list's order,

*Live rule: OD #805.*

### 972. A list of addresses one contact prints for several people is each address's e-mail on its owner; a brace set in math is the brace it prints (Perl: the list stays one contact, copied onto every holder; `${$a,b$}$@x` one address)

**Defect** (census138 ADDR-b; dev3 int138a: 8 papers, 0.083 pp per paper). (1) A class's verbatim `\email` argument
(llncs's `\email Semiverbatim`, Perl llncs.cls.ltxml:54; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1210) reads `$\{$fargyriou,mikebekos,symvonis$\}$@math.ntua.gr` with
its math shifts as characters, so the list was one unread address "${$…$}$@…" on a nameless creator (1106.2694,
2308.00146, 1602.04934); pdflatex typesets the math and prints "{fargyriou,mikebekos,symvonis}@math.ntua.gr". (2) A
contact printing a list of addresses for several people stayed one contact: elsarticle's shared `\cortext[cor1]{Corresponding
authors:\\zjsong@…; Chenxizhang@…}` and REVTeX's `\thanks{Corresponding Authors (a; b; c; d)}` were copied whole to
each carrier (2302.03296, 2508.07950), and the names printed beside the addresses (`\email{: xiazh@… (Zhenhua Xia);
lianghongstefanie@… (Hong Liang)}` on Hong Liang's call, 2009.14655; `\cortext{… Abrar Faiyaz (abrar\_faiyaz@…) and Md
Nasir Uddin (nasir\_uddin@…)}`, 2507.07920) were text of the one e-mail or note.

**Fix (1)** (`frontmatter_fields::contacts::math_braces_as_printed`, in `\lx@add@email` and `\lx@split@addresses`): `$\{$`, `$\lbrace$`
are the `\{` they print, `$\}$`, `$\rbrace$` the `\}`, the shifts read as characters or as shifts; anything else in math
stays. The list is then read as the text-brace list everywhere it already is (the Link step, the observer). A braced
group of one local part, `$\{$meier.schindler$\}$@…` (1602.04934: a typo for a comma, as printed), stays one address,
now printed "{meier.schindler}@…".

**Fix (2)** (`address_lists::distribute_address_lists`, at the flush after the Kind step for an address line, before
`write_role_notes`): a contact of an author — an e-mail, a correspondent or a thanks contact — printing two addresses or
more (`listed_addresses`: plain addresses, a braced group written out, each with the name printed in brackets after it
or before its bracketed address) gives each address as an e-mail to its owner by FIDELITY_CHARTER §4's order: the author
whose name is printed beside it (by its letters, base-folded; the strongest evidence, above spelling); else the author it
spells; else, among the contact's carriers, the consistent order or the elimination (`email_owners::list_owners`); else
the block's own creator (#159), once. The printed names are no e-mail's text. The contact's other words stay its
carriers' ("Corresponding authors:"), a contact left with none dropped; an e-mail keeps the call's name (REVTeX's
`\email[Corresponding author]`, which `write_role_notes` then makes each owner's note), a correspondent's or thanks'
addresses take the e-mail's own. Parted only where it is a list for several people: a contact two creators or more hold,
or one whose every address has an author's name beside it; an e-mail whose list prints other words (`\{ann,bob\}@a.org
(corresponding)`, perfect_kernel_batch92c), a list none of whose addresses finds an author (PoS's `\speaker`
e-mail line, whose names are no creators yet at the flush, 1711.04132), or a document with a name not yet written is
left as printed. The list is cut out of the contact in place (`cut_ranges`, `cut_printed`; round 2, review rev107f B2):
the address spans (with a name printed beside one, where it is an author's); between two addresses the separators —
spaces, line breaks, `;` `,` `&`, an "and" or "or", dropped only there; around a run of them the space before it,
brackets it leaves empty, a `;` or `,` after it, a stop after it where a label or nothing opens it; in a note, an
e-mail label opening the run after other words (`… addressed. Email: a @ x or b @ y.` leaves `… addressed.`,
2307.11827). Each text node keeps its other characters, an element all of whose text is cut goes, and every other node
stays: 2311.15476's `\cortext` keeps "Corresponding authors:", its break and its DOI link (doi.org links 16, as on
int139a; r1 had rebuilt the note as text, 14), and a note's math and its words' "and"/"or" stay. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch107f::a_shared_note_keeps_its_other_nodes_as_printed` (repro
`email_list_shared_note_keeps_prose_and_markup`), RED (107f r1) → GREEN. Round-2 A/B over `pop107f.tsv` vs int139a4
(int139a + 107e): 39 changed, all frontmatter (13 witnesses, 26 selected, 0 controls), E 2,869 = 2,869, F 7 = 7,
Warnings equal, `fm_checks.py` 1-7 clean; the 38 papers r1 also changed hold the creators r1 gave them.
Witnesses: 2009.14655 (Xia and Liang each their address and the "Corresponding author" note), 2507.07920, 2302.03296
(`zjsong@` Zhijian Song's, `Chenxizhang@` Chenxi Zhang's), 2508.07950 (`chunfeng.lian@` Lian's, `cong6406@` Cong's;
`wzy218@`, `jhma@` — the list in reverse author order, which the order step does not read — the block creator's).

**Reach.** A/B `pop107f.tsv` (4,589: the 15 witnesses of A–D, the 4,074 dev20k/dev3 papers whose output holds an e-mail on a creator its name shares no whole part with, a list contact, a math-brace or a bracketed name beside an address, 500 `popint125a_s10k` controls; 4,583 converted) vs int139a3: 43 papers changed, all frontmatter (13 witnesses, 30 selected, 0 controls — 1811.05727's one formula parsed differently under load, byte-identical alone), E 2,869 = 2,869, F 7 = 7, Warnings equal on the final binary; `fm_checks.py` 1-7: no creator merged or lost, no e-mail held by more creators, no growth, no fragment. Every changed paper read against its source and PDF: better, or the `$` signs gone only (1602.04934, 2404.14236). Re-score of the 43 (score2 + score_tiers, both sides): 17 papers' verdicts changed, 63 → 87 of their 95 creators right; the two the scorer calls worse are its limits (2410.15681: its source reading keeps the blockA address lines as affiliations; 2602.00582: it gives `byang@` to Kangjia Yan by the substring "yan", where `\icmlcorrespondingauthor{Jilin Hu}{byang@…}` prints Jilin Hu). The A/B rounds settled the spelling rule's limits (OD #970 "107f") and two fail-safes here (a list finding no author, 1711.04132; the upfront grid's late calls, 1303.3079).

**Guards** `perfect_kernel_batch107f::{a_math_brace_list_is_the_list_it_prints, an_address_list_on_a_contact_is_distributed_not_copied}`
(repros sectioning-frontmatter/`email_list_llncs_math_braces`, `email_list_revtex_names_after_addresses`,
`email_list_elsarticle_names_before_addresses`, `email_list_elsarticle_shared_cortext`, `email_list_revtex_shared_thanks`)
and unit `author_split_tests::a_name_spells_a_run_of_the_local_parts_words` (the math braces), RED (int139a3) → GREEN.
**Left** (one line each): a note (`ltx:note`) holding a list for its carriers is not parted (only contacts); initials tags
`a@x (X.X.); b@y (M.Y.)` match no printed name (2002.08904); an unbraced list beside a printed name not in brackets
(`Ann Able: a@x`) is not read as a name; a list in reverse author order stays unplaced (2508.07950).

**Fix (3) (CR4): a formula of glyphs in an e-mail or URL is its glyphs, for every binding** (Perl: the same `$∼$`, its
`\lx@add@url`/`\lx@add@email` Semiverbatim too). The API's `\lx@add@url` and `\lx@add@email` read the address
Semiverbatim, which turns a `$` already read as a math shift into a character (Perl's `neutralize`), so imsart's
`\ead[label=u2,url]{http://www.math.duke.edu/$\sim$omer}` wrote "…/$∼$omer" where pdflatex prints "…/∼omer" — and so did
any binding's call (`\def\myurl{\lx@add@url{http://www.zebra.edu/$\sim$ann}}`, review revCR3b). Both now pass the address
through `contacts::address_as_printed`: the brace sets of fix (1), then `math_glyphs_as_printed` — a pair of shifts
(characters or shifts) round characters and math symbols that each print one glyph (`math_symbol_glyph`: the text of the
one box a math primitive without arguments makes, `\sim` "∼", `\cdot` "·") is that run, each symbol its glyph as a
character of the address (TeX takes it from the math font), the shifts and spaces dropped; the address stays one text,
so the XSLT's link (its first text node) is whole. A run with a script (`$^*$x@y`'s mark), another command or nothing in it
stays as read (`$x^2$` prints "$x^2$": left, no paper seen). `\lx@address@printed` gives a binding the same reading for an
address it prints itself (imsart's `\printead`, #986). Witnesses 1301.1466, math0608476 (`www.math.wisc.edu/$\sim$swanson`).
Repro `sectioning-frontmatter/imsart_ead_url_reads_a_tex_argument` (RED since CR3b); guard
`perfect_kernel_batchcr4::imsart_ead_url_prints_its_formula`. **CR4b (review revCR4 findings 1 and 4):** both readings
pair the shifts left to right, as TeX pairs them — a pair that is not glyphs (a script, `$$`) stays as read, whole, and
the next pair opens after its closing shift. CR4 resumed one token after such a pair's opening shift, so its closing shift
paired with the next formula's opening one and the text between was "printed", spaces dropped, with no Warning:
2508.20055's `ej$_$dresselhaus@berkeley.edu, s$_$g@berkeley.edu` became "ej$_dresselhaus@berkeley.edu,s_$g@…";
`math_braces_as_printed` had the same restart (`$^a$\{$b$` turned the `\{` between two formulas into a brace). A
character command in math prints its character (`text_glyph`: `\_`, `\{`, `\}`, `\#`, `\%`, `\&`, `\lbrace`/`\rbrace`),
so `$\{a,b\}$@w.edu` is the brace list (each address) and `p$\_$r` "p_r". Repro
`email_math_shifts_pair_as_tex_pairs_them`; guards `perfect_kernel_batchcr4b::email_math_shifts_pair_as_tex_pairs_them`,
`author_split_tests::math_shifts_pair_left_to_right`. **Left:** `$\dag$` (2604.07356; `\dag` is an `\ifmmode` macro,
no math primitive) keeps its dollars.
**IV1 (study IV0): a formula of spacing alone is glue, no text of an address** (Perl: no Kind step, the line stays
in its affiliation, the formula math spacing). `$~\quad~~$` prints glue only (latex.ltx:9411 `\nobreakspace`, :9435
`\quad`), but the Kind step (`kind.rs` `prints_addresses_only` reads command tokens only) took 2205.14113's institute
line `$~\quad~~$ cbray@mines.edu` as addresses alone, and with one address the whole line was the `\lx@add@email`
argument, whose reading kept the glyph-less pair as written: "$˜ ˜˜$ cbray@mines.edu", invented, 0 Warnings; authblk's
`\affil[$$]{\small a@x $\quad$ b@y}` (2302.05182) was parted at the `\quad` inside the shifts ("a@x $", "$ b@y").
`email_lines::spacing_formulas_as_space` reads such a pair (`formula_prints_spacing_alone`: spaces, ties — active, or
other as a Semiverbatim argument holds them — and the space commands of `leading_spacing_end`; the empty `$$` is none)
with the spaces around it as one space between printed text, none at an edge of the line or of a group; every other
formula stays. One rule at three sites: the head of `email_line_calls`, the Kind step's address lines
(`kind_entry_addresses`, a line that is no address line kept as written), and the head of `math_glyphs_as_printed`
(any binding's `\email{$\,$a@x}`). A token test: each site runs before the formula is digested. Repros
`svjour3_institute_spacing_formula_before_address_is_no_text`, `authblk_affil_address_row_spacing_formula_is_no_separator`,
`email_spacing_formula_prints_no_text`; rows of `perfect_kernel_batchcr4b::email_math_shifts_pair_as_tex_pairs_them`
and `author_split_tests::math_shifts_pair_left_to_right`.

### 978. A span's content is read from the digested list, and what a speculative run edits in place is undone

**Content.** The writer makes an entry from the tokens its span covers. A box covers what it prints, so a span stops short of the `$` and `{}` around a script. The walk back from a span over those tokens stopped at any switch: `$\rm ^{3}$He Lab` was no balanced run and the paper was not written (2105.07958's class; `revtex_affiliation_requested_switched_mark_cuts`, 88c's RED). `emitter::Field` reads the formula's extent from the digested list (`events::lex_with_formulas`) and a mark's own print from its event, whatever opens or fills the formula (`\( ^{1} \)`, `\protect\(`, hep-ph0110378, 2307.12984; `${^1}$`, 1410.8534, astro-ph9807043; `\textbf{$^2$…}`, 2605.25195). Brace balance stays a read of the content, forward, and takes a mark's own font group from its opening brace (`{\bf $\rm ^{1}$} Univ X`); a group going on after its mark stays no cut (`\textit{$^{2}$H} Lab`, `cut_run_wrapped_isotope_is_entry_text`). A legend's `${^\dagger}$` keeps its printed mark (2605.10201's shape). `formula_span` is the formula's alone. Guards `perfect_kernel_batchz3::{a_cut_takes_each_formula_whole, a_cut_takes_a_group_it_closes, a_mark_in_its_wrapper_is_read_by_its_own_print}`. A Declaration's span is a run a replay can read (`field_notes::settle_declarations`, `a_declarations_span_is_a_balanced_run`). Dump: `formula_span`, a Declaration's `span` and `label`; no reader yet.

**Isolation.** Perl has no speculative run. Ours undoes what the assignment journal sees; what is edited in place it did not see, in the rehearsal and in the title-page checks alike: `\fontdimen`, a box register's `\wd`, `\ht`, `\dp`, an `\openin` stream (a rehearsal took the document's next line), the pdfTeX generator; and keyvals' "seen" set kept the document's own Warning unsaid. Each is undone or kept apart now. With the observer on and off the XML outside the creators, E, F and W agree on every input of the hostile suite, but for the writer's second digestion of a cut field (below); the census of what a rollback leaves is `FRONTMATTER_SINGLE_ENGINE_PLAN.md` "What a rollback leaves". Guards `perfect_kernel_batchz3::the_rehearsal_leaves_no_trace_*`; repro `observer_rehearsal_leaves_no_trace`.

**A binding's document-wide state** was a thread-local no rollback reaches. It is now one value of the Value table (`state::DocumentState`), bound globally as the package's own macros are, in place outside a journal, a copy at the first change under one: pict2e's graph (pict2e.sty:186 `\global\pIIe@GRAPH`; pdflatex strokes a path left unstroked with the next, `0 0 m 1 1 l 2 2 m 3 3 l S`, and ours stroked it once more per speculative run, on and off), chemnum's counter and first uses (a real first use became a `ltx:ref` with no target), animate's open stack, biblatex's state, a stub's one report. A speculative run's raw read is no read `read_stand_in_copy` skips a copy for; it evaluates no Lua, whose globals no rollback reaches; a load in one is not noted. What a chunk prints is so not in a rehearsal's reading. Each thread-local's row is in the census. Guards `a_bindings_state_stands_for_one_run`, `a_rehearsals_read_is_no_read_of_a_copy`, `a_speculative_run_evaluates_no_lua`.

**A mark's own group** is the digested list's fact, no reading of token catcodes: it prints its formulas alone (`Walker::note_a_formulas_group`), spacing, a switch, a color and a list's comma aside (`{$^1$\,} Univ X`, 1709.01760's shape, which token catcodes regressed); a command printing before them (`{\S $^1$}`) or a word after them is no such group. A run holds its environments in pairs (`\begin{tabular}…`: the last cell, lost in an Error, was the run's end). Guards `a_marks_own_group_is_read_from_its_ink`, `a_cut_holds_its_environments`. A mark's formula that opens a group where a line starts, at the field's start or right after a line break, by what digestion made, starts that group at its brace whatever goes on in it (`Formula::opens_line_in`, `\\ \normalsize{$^{1}$ Shemyakin…,} \normalsize{Moscow, Russia}`, 2005.08290, which fell to a nameless creator with no Error); after a comma it stays no cut, an isotope (`Univ A, {$^{2}$H} Lab, Rome $^{2}$Univ B`, where the base gave Bob "2 H Lab"). An isotope right after a line break is cut as on the base. Guard `a_group_a_mark_opens_at_a_lines_start_starts_at_its_brace`.

**A named change: a replaced `\author`.** 2402.06922 loses four e-mails and the nameless `CISPA` creator the base took from a first `\author`: a second `\author` replaces it, and the PDF prints neither. 2211.01783 loses six e-mails from a nameless creator the same way, and the PDF's title block prints none of them. 1509.01655 goes from 9 creators to 4, a gain: the first `\author`'s doubled names are gone and each e-mail sits on its own author. `fm_checks` flags them LOST; that is right to do and this is not a loss. **A real paper past the budget:** 1810.03464, one call over 8 M reads, its XML identical and one more Warning (`rehearsal_budget`, W 3 → 4).

**A definer in a body the field defined** runs at the macro's call, its tokens at the positions they were written at. Its Declaration's span is that call (`FieldNotes::last_call`, the stamped invoker), never what lies between, which holds printed text Z4 would print twice; a box of the body takes it back. Guard `a_declaration_in_a_body_holds_its_call`.

**The rehearsal's read budget** (R1's `gullet::read_budget`): 8,000,000 reads a run, 24,000,000 a conversion, a skip counted in `Warning:frontmatter:rehearsal_budget`; the data in the census. The content check's own rehearsals under `=2` (a block's own call, `ApiCall::inside_events`) read from an allowance of their own, one run's reads a conversion (`rehearsal::for_the_check`), and their skips are in no Warning (nothing written depends on them; guard `perfect_kernel_batchrc1::the_checks_rehearsals_leave_the_budget`). A block looping where nothing prints it no longer costs a conversion its limits. Guard `a_looping_block_ends_in_the_rehearsal_budget`.

**Since ST1:** the writer's second real digestion of a cut entry says the content's Error once (`writer_second_digestion_says_an_error_twice`, green; pdflatex's one ifthen error). **Open:** whether it still moves auto-numbered `xml:id`s is unguarded (the guard masks ids; revST1). A group no formula's alone, or going on after a mark away from a line's start, is uncut where the base cut it, nothing lost: RED `affiliation_cut_group_siblings_stay_uncut_red`. No Lua in a rehearsal can lose a cut: RED `rehearsal_no_lua_loses_a_cut_red`.

### 979. The reading's rules that move today's output, and a line the writer makes is cut of the addresses it took out (Perl: one creator per `@authorsplits` piece, no reading)

**What moves the output with the switch off.** Only the writer's own gain: a reading's rule changes what the writer writes,
never today's reader. Z14's rules that do: the rehearsal's `BOUND_IN_A_BLOCK` (`rehearsal.rs`: a binding's
`\lx@add@affiliation@marked` read as digested in a block, so its entries part; 2603.28168, 1405.3507, 2303.18104), `\alignauthor`
a column (sig-alternate.cls:283; 1503.06772), a call speaking for a collaboration a contact on the names before it (1201.5726,
1301.6619), a later row read as names (after an "and", past an address piece, a marked row with one odd piece; 2007.10022,
2312.14886, 2409.07809), a line of addresses leaving its entry open (1411.2744). One helper is shared with today's
reader, `name_shaped` (`frontmatter/classify/name_text.rs`): it reads a particle elided onto a capital as the surname's only right after an
initial (`D.~d'Enterria`, hep-ph0311131); anywhere else a place or an institution elides too (`C. Vignat, Universit\'e d'Orsay`,
1009.2396, which Z14 made two creators; `Villeneuve d'Ascq`, `Saint Martin d'Heres`).

**A departure kept: the role heading's word table.** `labels.rs` `after_role_heading`'s `ROLES` (Author(s), Editor(s), Convener(s),
Contributor(s)) is a word table for one paper family, cernrep's hep-ph0311131, with no other reach in the review's census. A later
line it opens is a row of names only where each piece shows a person, a name's cue (`has_person_cue`: an initial, a particle) or
the mark it carries: `Editors: Springer Nature`, `Author: Corresponding Author` stay the block's lines.

**A names row's group of addresses** (`lines.rs` `address_groups_whole`): a group whose printed braces hold the row's commas (the
lexer's `Event::braces`) is one Name again before the names are parted, and its label word goes with its addresses
(`address_runs`), so `E-mails: \{ann, bob\}@a.org, cat@b.org` in an `\IEEEauthorblockN` is no person (2003.02512, which had four
fake creators, its merged-creators Error gone).

**The writer's take-out of an entry's addresses.** The reading takes the addresses an entry prints out as its authors' e-mails
(`owner:entry-address`). The writer gave the entry back whole where today's held no item it could cut to the entry: today's
contacts were removed and the addresses left in the affiliation's text, read back as `written` (2310.19837's shape). Now an entry
whose e-mails today's holds as an author's contact, or prints in an item the address reader cuts, is not given back: today's item
is cut (`cut_entry_addresses`, a cut whose text is several of the reading's entries joined, each once, in any order: an API
call's pieces share its source, no span to order them by — `joins_entries`; read in their texts' order, 1712.07118's `\affil`
lines, hep-ph0108215's and 1605.02212's lettered and starred `\address` lines were no join, and declined), and the line, a block's
or an API call's piece, is made from its tokens and cut of the same addresses (`Op::Make`'s `cut`). An entry given back leaves
`Resolved::taken`, which the plan reads as the entries it makes cut. An address today's prints is no reason to keep the take-out
where the reading gave it the entry's only carrier while the entry prints another author's own address too: the line lists the
block's addresses (2403.12766's `20200142@hznu.edu.cn`, Qian Wang's, which the any-order join alone would write as `$^6$NYU Shanghai`'s
Zheng Zhang's e-mail). **Its fail-safe** (`write_observed_frontmatter`): where the
plan cannot make such an entry cut, an entry kept for an address today's prints is given back whole and the plan writes the rest,
as before Z14r2 (astro-ph0007423's own `\address{e--mail: … and …}`, whose `e–mail:` the cut reads as no label, had been declined
whole); one kept for an author's contact of today's stays taken out, the paper declined, today's contacts kept (2310.19837). A
block line keeping an address the reading left in it (one that spells no author: the chain's fail-safe) is not made where the pass
after the writer would give that address in today's item to its carriers (`insert::entry_line_addresses`, the Kind step's own
line reader, `kind_address_lines`); one it leaves as printed is made so (2203.17007's `firstname.secondname@ericsson.com` in its
`$^{\star \star}$` line, whose paper had been declined, the lines merged on its first author). The read-back compares the final
document with the reading as resolved too (`given_back`, `ab_audit fmshadow`'s column of that name), so a give-back shows there; it is
set only where the read-back finds no difference, so a pass after the writer can hide it, and it runs only under
`LATEXML_FM_SHADOW=1`: it adds no Warning to a conversion (revZ14r2).

**A names row's address glued to punctuation** (`lines.rs` `names_without_addresses`): the name ends where the address's run
starts, its label word with it, or earlier where a word prints an address the run reader parts from nothing before it — OT1's
`|` an em dash, `Kristiaan Pelckmans |kp@it.uu.se|` (1006.4832), whose name had taken the address.

Guards `perfect_kernel_batchz14::{an_entrys_addresses_are_cut_where_its_line_is_made, an_address_group_in_a_names_row_is_read_whole,
an_elided_particle_is_a_surnames_only_after_an_initial, a_role_heading_over_words_opens_no_names}`, Z14r3's
`{an_address_glued_to_a_dash_leaves_the_name, an_api_calls_pieces_join_in_any_order, an_entry_whose_cut_fails_is_given_back,
a_line_keeping_an_address_the_pass_leaves_is_made, an_only_carriers_address_beside_others_is_not_written}`; RED
`a_mark_past_a_marked_lists_leading_run_is_an_event_red` (`Town, USA\\ *ann@x.org` reads `USA1ann@x.org`: 2411.03172, 2510.06608,
2602.11758).
