### 980. The one added step at the flush: a block's creators and contacts written from the reading (once behind a switch)

**The switch and the old driver are deleted (DEL1 tests, DEL2 code).** `LATEXML_FM_EMIT`, `fm_emit_mode` and `set_fm_emit_override` are gone; every call of the `\author` family queues its block whole (`defs/author_macros.rs` `whole_block_call`) and the emitter writes it. The `=0` arms are collapsed in the emitter, the resolver (`Resolver::emitting`/`whole_entries`, each now always on), the rehearsal (the juggles as columns, the budget Warning's one text), the shadow (`reads_now` true unless `LATEXML_FM_SHADOW=0`; the content check reads every inside creator call), the ledger (`out_of_positions` per call only, `Ledger::shadow_extra` removed, `ApiCall::command` always kept) and `frontmatter_stores` (`annotate=all` where the call made every queued creator). The old driver — `add_authors_calls_sectioned` (`author_block/dispatch.rs`), `split_author_calls`, `author_block/line_kinds.rs`, and every `author_block/` and `frontmatter/fallback.rs` item only it reached, deleted by the compiler's dead-code analysis — is gone; its one step still live, the IJCAI sectioned split, is `author_macros.rs` `ijcai_split_call` (the block read as the driver first read it, then `\lx@ijcai@authorsplit`; a block whose marker those steps remove is queued whole). `fallback::whole_block_author` and `tabular_juggles_in_a_whole_block` stay, the emitter's. Byte-identical on the int152c stage2 ids. The `red_at_two` guards that asserted only `=0` output were deleted with the fixtures nothing else used (retrievable at `29de9ed4dc`; the list stays in `docs/parity/FRONTMATTER_REDS_AT_EMIT2.tsv`). The paragraphs below describe the switch as it stood before the deletion.

`LATEXML_FM_EMIT` (`=2` by default since the flip, FLIP1: one whole-block entry per call, the emitter writing it; `LATEXML_FM_EMIT=0` the old driver — the reader at the call and the writer — reachable until Z18-Z19 delete it, its output changed by Route D only through a cut's environment extents, below; `=1` the reader still runs at the call; read once, by `writer::emit::fm_emit_mode`, the one definition every site calls) is Route D's emitter (`FRONTMATTER_SINGLE_ENGINE_PLAN.md`): `emitter::emit::emit_commands` inside `digest_front_matter`, for every paper with a block read. The queued creators and their annotations are replaced by Perl's own calls built from `Resolved`. Perl's counterpart is `\lx@add@authors` (`Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:687`), which cuts a block with `SplitTokens` at the call; this cuts it at the flush, as digested material doesn't exist at the call. Papers with no block and the post-writer passes stay as they are. The writer doesn't run on an emitted paper.

**With the switch off: a cut's environment extents (Z4ar2, main session's ruling).** The writer's cut reads a run's environments from the digestion's frames for every written paper (`emitter::Field::balanced`), not from `content.rs`'s former `environment_step` spelling: a macro pair and `\let` copies count, a `\begin` under `\detokenize` or `\ifx` doesn't (review revZ3r2: int143a E 1, the last cell `d` lost). An environment a formula holds is the formula's, taken whole (`$^{1}$Univ X $\begin{array}{c}a\end{array}$ c, $^{2}$Univ Y` cuts two entries, as int143b's spelling did; review revZ4a). A `\begin`'s step reaches as far as what runs at its position reads, its environment's arguments (`{tabular}{c}`), and a frame change inside that reach is the same step, not a second one (`field_notes::note_environment`). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchz4::an_environment_by_its_frames` (rows: a macro pair, `\let` copies, `\detokenize`, `\ifx`, an array in a formula, a tabular, a `\newenvironment` around a tabular or a center). Every paper the off A/B changed is named in the batch's report.

**Owners.** Perl's keys only: each new item `label=item:F:K` with `annotations=` on its creators; a creator an earlier flush made is reached by Perl's own `author:N`; the block's by `addresses:block`. What a flush emitted is two State mappings (`lx_fm_emitted_creators`, `lx_fm_emitted_items`), as `num_<tag>` carries Perl's counts. No queue attribute, no thread-local beyond the ledger: `ApiCall::command` is the ledger's copy of a queued call, read under the switch only.

**A name or contact is the tokens its span covers** (`event_run`), so fonts, marks, math and breaks come through digestion. A token slice is the API's argument; where it's cut comes from digested facts: a box's own position beside its cover (`Event::marks` on a Name; a wrapper's cover on its first box holds the other names, `\textbf{Ann, Bob}`, 2305.12182), its font (`Event::font` on a Name, `\lx@fm@entry@font`, `{\small $^1$Univ A}`, 1208.4825), `\footnote` against `\thanks` (`Event::footnote`), the formulas (`Field::formulas`), and the environments as their meanings and the digestion's frames say them (`field_notes::EnvironmentStep`, `Field::environments`, which replace `content.rs`'s `environment_step` for the writer too: a macro pair, a `\let` copy, 1507.02068's `\begin{center}` on its first name, a raw `{CJK*}`, 2609.05616; one step each way at a position whose `\begin` or `\end` was heard, a macro's `\begin{tikzpicture}…\end{tikzpicture}` all at its call's, 2210.03748). A contact a mark's formula holds is its text, not the formula its run grows to (an ORCID icon in `$^{1\,\orcidicon{…}}$`, 2210.03748, 2206.03602). One address of a list the reading writes out is the ink printing it in the call's rehearsed argument, the list the run from its first ink to its last (`one_address`; `\textcolor{blue}{a@x}, \textcolor{blue}{b@y}`, review revZ4a; 2211.14973). A call's pieces are the reading's (`call_pieces`, one per piece): no cut at a container (a Layout event) or inside one or a formula, and a piece no balanced run holds is its text, in a Warning; the one-piece fallback reads the reading's count, not the runs cut (review revZ4a: `\begin{ff}…\end{ff}` gave entry 1 "2 Univ Y"). A line break between two printed lines of a piece is the piece's, not cut (`kept_breaks`): a mark's entry runs on to the next mark with its `<break/>`, as Perl prints it and pdflatex sets the line (amsart's address `\\` is `\unskip, \ignorespaces`, amsart.cls:528, a comma in the PDF: 1305.3804's "Turkey, and, Institute", where Perl and CR10b keep `<break/>`s, every word kept) — `\address{$^{1}$ Dept, School of Yak\\ Owl University\\ $^{2}$ …}` wrote "School of YakOwl University", silently (CR9's glue class; CR10b: 2212.03638, 2211.03175, cond-mat0204589, 0904.3899, 1311.0012); a break with no printed line since the last one kept, or none after it, is cut with the contact it parts off (an `E-mail:` line between two), so none is doubled; a paragraph, section or column break is cut as before (guard `perfect_kernel_batchcr10b::address_continuation_line_keeps_its_break`). An environment opening a name's run starts it past its arguments (`\author{\begin{tabular}{c}Ann Able…}`, review revZ4a: "cAnn Able"). An IEEE ordinal the reading joins to a name stays in its tokens (`1\textsuperscript{st} Ann`, 1907.06250, 2605.00900, as the ruling's 2412.10792). What's left of tokens is the API call's own key list (`rekeyed`), brace balance (`in_a_group`, `note_argument`, `past_what_it_set`, which builds an accent's argument, its letter or group, 2406.17108, or a multi-byte character's bytes, 2201.01905: the box's cover stops short of what nothing prints but through it, and an event starting there says it isn't the argument), and the helpers a call site reuses (`rewrite_symbol_superscripts`, `split_wrapped_affiliation_marks`, `entry_mark`, `note_body`, `kind_entry_addresses`).
**Known REDs (review revCR10b):** 1007.2355's glue ("for the PHENIX CollaborationBrookhaven", counted by its markup-loss
Warning, byte-identical before and after CR10b) is not this path: PoS.cls's `\speaker` ends with a control space, the only
separator once the source's `}%` drops the newline, and the reading joins the argument's tail to the next line across
the brace — the event walker would read that control space as a separator (MED). The content check's false "words
missing" Warning on a `{a, b}@x` e-mail line, boxed or not (2211.07344, 2305.15057, CR10b's `fcolorbox_email_line_in_author`
fixture W 1): the author block's side (`words.rs::ink_words` → `labels.rs` ~663 `address_runs`) does not read the line as
one e-mail list. An `\fcolorbox` around a name in `\author` keeps the background colour and loses the frame (synthetic,
markup only; the base dropped the whole creator).

**Marks.** Perl's own split: a per-author class's call whose lines answer none of its marks, or a name list a binding split, keeps them printed on the name (`\lx@add@author`; a line's Mark answering a name's is the digested test, `per_author_marks`; 0705.3952); else they are requests (`\lx@author@withsup`): answered ones leave the name, the rest stay requests `show_unanswered_marks` shows. Beyond Perl (P4b2b, FIDELITY_CHARTER §2, every printed mark shown): every call adding to the names before it (the block's `replace` false: a binding's name list, `\lx@add@authors@list` — authblk, iopart, informs, ptephy, l-aa, JHEP, aistats (`aistats_sty.rs`), osa_journal (opex3, ol2, osajnl2) and apa6 —, a raw class's appended `\author`) whose own lines answer none of its marks keeps them printed — its affiliations are calls of their own, which print theirs (2410.01932; Perl's `\lx@add@authors` hides a name's answered mark). The kernel `\author`'s block, which replaces, still hides both sides where its own lines answer its marks, as Perl (RED `kernel_author_lines_answered_marks_hidden_red`). Guard `perfect_kernel_batchc1::authblk_names_show_their_printed_marks`.

**Order.** Perl's two phases: what no label places attaches as it digests, `relocateAnnotations` appends what a label places, an entry the block prints returning to its queue place (`\lx@frontmatter@queued`, `relocate::at_queue_position`, its zone kept only there). Each source call is its own item, so a shared line keeps the place its call has on each author (0704.3133, 1202.0103).

**Rewrites (named):** a title's note stays its call (`api:title-note`); a line's note the old reader queued stays the document's (`note:unrequested`, `note:address-line`); a call printing no word stays (`\IEEEauthorblockA{\thanks{…}}`, 1502.03038); a `\footnotemark` and an ORCID written on a name stay on it (2203.12964, 2208.05251, the root's `xmlns:svg` with them); an entry's address taken out by the reading goes back with its entry for the Kind steps to cut (`give_back_entry`, 0709.2122); an entry's inner contact goes with it unless the reading gives it to someone else (1312.4509); a call's legend is its carriers' note with its printed mark (`kind_legend_contacts`' shape, 2607.02294); an entry a note holds is read as `\lx@add@thanks` reads it (2102.09361, 2503.08005).

**Measured** on the lists of the experiment S0 (`kit/emit/`, frozen scorer): dev3 (1,028 papers) output 97.86 / 97.11, counterfactual 96.31 / 95.89, real emit 96.37 / 96.17 (S0 96.29 / 95.98), scaled to all dev3 per creator 98.40 (S0 98.31); creator XML identical, ids masked, on 740 of 834 papers where the reading and the output agree, 88.7 % (S0 52.8 %); XML outside the creators 833 of 834; Errors 9 → 10 (1201.5726, `creator_not_a_name` on a reading Z14 repairs), Fatals 0. devh10k (289) output 94.52 / 91.92, counterfactual 95.09 / 91.22, real emit 95.83 / 92.43 (S0 95.22 / 91.36); identical 148 of 189, 78.3 %; outside 188 of 189; Errors 13 → 11 (one up, 1301.6619, `creator_not_a_name`). Items written from text on dev3: 56 in 25 papers (S0 211 in 122), each with its reason under `--debug=frontmatter` (`FRONT emit text`): 15 span letters differ, 11 names, 11 a contact a mark's formula holds (an ORCID icon, written by its id, which the output off loses: 2210.03748, 2206.03602), 7 no balanced run, 4 a note with no argument, 3 note text, 3 no piece, 2 a macro's span. `instructions:u`, off against the base: hello +0.11 %, b5_fill1000 -0.27 %, 1507.02068 +0.26 %, 2103.04797 -0.31 %; on against off: -0.05 %, 0.00 %, +1.00 %, +2.58 % (975 authors). With the switch on 627 of 8,116 tests move, every one because of the emit (322 creator contents, 93 other content, 87 asserts without left/right, 56 marks, 31 order, 20 fonts, 10 `before`, 8 of two causes): none is updated, off moves nothing.

**Left,** each with its witness: an address printed in an entry's run with no separator before it, which only the writer's DOM cut took (astro-ph0610446, cond-mat0610708); `\IEEEauthorrefmark{1}\textsuperscript{,}\IEEEauthorrefmark{2}` keeps only its first mark (1707.03469); a font the old group scoping dropped on a later name now prints as the PDF does (`{\sf A, B}`, 0707.1799: a markup difference for the better); a `before` a per-author line's printed separator set (`\lx@author@printed@before`, 1301.7707); a kept mark a legend answers stays whole (`$^{1,*}$`, 2607.02294), the old writer's `hide_answered_marks`; the space before a macro's picture in an address goes (`$^{1}$Univ A \logo`, `Univ A<picture>`, `emit_a_macros_environment_closes_once`); an ORCID icon in a mark's formula is its id, not its link (2210.03748).

**Counted, never silent.** Every item or name written from the reading's text says so in a Warning with its reason (`by_text`; an ORCID's id, which is its text, aside; one address of a list no ink prints alone, or past the positions, `one_address`). **The word check is the reading's** (`resolver/words.rs`, Z4br2), both ways, against what each block's or creator's call's inks print (its Names, Contacts and Notes; lowercased runs of letters and digits): its block half a pass after the resolver on the ledger and `Resolved` alone (`check_blocks`), its call half the emitter's, on the same `Written`, filtered after the emit by what it wrote (`call_checks`: a call printing an entry another prints too is read once, revtex's `\affiliation{\Argonne}` before the authors, 2103.04797; hep-ex0609057's `\thanks` in an `\affiliation`, a publication note). *Lost* words (`Written::lost_inks`): a block's as a multiset against the names and items read from it; an address run an ink prints whose every address the reading writes as the block's e-mail item first the address's, by position, cut out of the ink from after its label word (its words no name's: `POC: K.\ Hobbs (kerianne.hobbs@us.af.mil)`, 2110.03506; its label the contact's name, written or not: `email: Duncan.Lorimer@…`, 0811.0762; N1r2); an ink every word of which is written taking its words first, an ink of a line an item other than an address is read from before any other (a name before an address spelling it, `\texttt{ann.able@outlook}\\ Ann Able`; an affiliation before a lost line repeating its words, `Dresden, Saxony 01062, Germany (…)`, 2203.10777), an ink the reading parts losing nothing (aa's two addresses in one `\email`, 2306.01880), "Ann" not held by "Annette". *Excess* words (`Written::excess`): a word a block's or a call's names and items write more often than its inks and separators print it, an item counted as often as one holder holds it (two copies in one holder twice, one each owner holds once; a link's target printed where its anchor prints no address of its own, an ORCID's behind a logo or a name, not 2607.28418's `\href{mailto:email@domain}{ann@a.edu; bob@b.edu}` (a picture's anchor's text is its path data, so "prints no words" can't decide it, `a_macros_environment_closes_once`); an address's local part only, a braced list's domain printing once; a note's inner address, whatever its `EmailMeaning`, is the contact's, 2406.13066, siamart's `\thanks{…\email{…}}`, 1804.09455, so an.cls's duplicate, 0807.0895, goes uncounted). The call half counts a call's excess too (N1); 2607.00684's `mtablo@postech.ac.kr` twice in one creator isn't the reading's (it writes it once): the emitter writes the `\email` call whole and the reading's piece of it besides, and the Kind step cuts the whole call's list after the flush, a duplicate no check of the reading sees. Not a loss: an ink a container in an item's span holds, a contact read at its own span (an ORCID link's logo, 2409.13798), one a mark's formula holds (2210.03748), an ink of two letters at most (`Karlu$\rm{\check{s}i\acute{c}}$`, 0911.1045), what a later call replaced or cleared (2412.15554). **An e-mail's label is written as printed**: an address the block prints after its label word is named by it (`name=`), the label its address run's on its line (`printed_email_label`, the reading's `address_runs`), or in any language what the line prints before the run, one word or two and a colon (`Correo electrónico:`, `Courriel :`, review revZ4br2), a list's on each address: `E-mail: \email{…}` with PoS's raw `\email` (1412.5940, 1612.08209, 1812.02252, 1907.01311, 1005.2532, 0802.3384), `Emails:` (2511.22090), `email` (1209.0869), `(e-mail: …)` (1405.3793), a label in the address's own ink (1009.1965, 1807.01821, 1509.01480, 2205.04084, 0704.3639); its words are written then, and a label the emit doesn't write is a lost word, counted (Z4b exempted every leading label, so the kernel's `Email:` written for a printed `E-mail:` was silent: review revZ4b). The gate reads `kit/emit/words.py <off> <on>`: words the on-run's creators lack that the whole document lacks too, counted when a frontmatter Warning names them in its own word list.

**The safety net, graded to the smallest unit that fails (Z4b, Z4br2).** A block whose *names* fail (a Name ink of it losing a word of letters outside its addresses (a word the address reader reads an address in, `addresses_in`), no author's line by its addresses, that is a name: on a line of its names, or one an address its line or its column prints spells as its own, by the reading's rule of an address ranked against the written names in one decision (`Holder`), `LostInk::names_fail`: `philips@` Andy Philips's, though its prefix spells the written Philip Laird, 1908.02923, review revN1r2; a name the reading lost, JAIR's `\name Shaul Markovitch \email …\\`, 1109.6618, 1312.0286, 1111.6082, 1905.12960, 1807.03929, 2003.01013, 2008.13618, a column's name above its address, 1805.08288, 2002.00084, review revN1 — the lexer's Name is any run of ink, so a lost one alone is no name: an e-mail line's label, `Emails:- …`, 2605.21396, a tabular's entry line, 1109.0220, an address's words, `\{firstname\}.\{lastname\}@kit.edu`, 2601.00680, keep their reading; a postcode is no name's, 2501.09580's `Hefei 230026`, whose 168 names Z4br2 wrote whole; or a name's word written more often than it prints) is written whole, the creator Perl's `\lx@add@author` makes of it, decided once a block over the flushes (`written_whole`). Other ink a block prints that the reading holds no place for keeps the reading, the ink a note (its tokens where it loses every word and no address of it is written, else its text from its first lost word to its last in its font with its written address runs cut out by position, `LostInk::note_text`: `POC: K. Hobbs` of 2110.03506's `POC: K.\ Hobbs (kerianne.hobbs@us.af.mil)`, `Germany` of 2203.10777's `Germany (martin.waltz@tu-dresden.de)`, so a written address isn't doubled; its whole text, as the base wrote it, where a written address prints among its lost words; a note no font holds says so in the plain-text Warning): of the author whose line it is (`LostInk::owner`: the one author the addresses its ink prints spell by the reading's own rule, `spelled_name`, a lost name among the candidates; an ink one word holding an `@`, `yiliu.li@outlook`, read as one; 2605.16481's Aiden Yiliu Li, N1; 2110.03506's Kerianne L. Hobbs, 2203.10777's Martin Waltz, N1r2; an ink printing no address goes with its line to the one author the addresses its line prints spell, read from the line's text whole, 2203.10777's `Dresden`, `Saxony 01062`, the `ext.\ 5` after `POC: A.\ Able (ann.able@a.org)`, which had made the block's nameless creator, review revN1r2, 1210.0352's `SE-581 83 Linköping`, `Sweden` on each author as the base writes them; a list's local parts printed apart are one run of addresses spelling its authors and own none, `{\it pzou94, ozel, suresh@gwu.edu}`, 2003.14069, 2102.08981, 1901.01753, 1708.00818, 2307.03645), else of the author block (`role=note`, `label=addresses:block`, the shape the unclaimed-text net keeps a line no field holds in, `insert::keep_unclaimed_net_notes`; not the net itself, whose 3-word floor would drop it and whose Warning would count it twice): 2605.16481 (3 creators, Z4b's whole block 1), 2607.28418 (7, Z4b 1). An entry's excess is counted, not answered: whether a note's digestion keeps an address its contact writes too is digestion's (an.cls's raw `\email` in a `\thanks` keeps it, a duplicate, 0807.0895; siamart's fixture `siamart_class_commands` routes it out, so its Warning under `=2` is a false flag; dropping the entry lost the address there). Each in one counted Warning a block. The reading and its checks are the ledger's (`Ledger::analysis`, made at its generation, `Ledger::generation`, which every change of its entries counts, `Ledger::entries_mut`), dropped with it at a conversion's start, so none outlives its conversion in a persistent worker (review revN1r2); what an emit wrote to its end is the State value `lx_fm_emitted`, the generation it read, undone with State by a speculative run's rollback; a flush with nothing queued at the generation emitted writes nothing again: 1901.01540 (1,202 authors, no `\maketitle`, flushed at each section) cost +32.9 % instructions with the switch on, −2.4 % now. A call written at one flush is never counted lost at a later one (its `lost|<index>` once-key set false when written, 2303.02975). Open (N1r3): an ink no address of its own or of its line owns is still the block's note on its nameless creator (a list's local parts the reading loses where the base writes them as addresses, `{\it aable, bbaker, cat@a.org}` beside three names, 2003.14069, 2102.08981, 1901.01753, 1708.00818, 2307.03645; a line printing no address, 1605.03019, 0907.3600; a funding note after a labelled entry, 2504.09745, its holders' since LO2), and a lost line's inks are a note each (2203.10777's `Dresden`, `Saxony 01062`). **One whole-block writer** (`author_block::whole_block_author`): `\lx@add@author[keys]{…}` of the block, its lines prepared (`lines_prepared`) and their breaks' options gone, for `\lx@add@authors`' tabular fallback (Perl Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:693), `=2`'s queued entry and the emitter's whole block alike. Not line for line with Perl: Rust's `\lx@add@author` (frontmatter_fields.rs `creator_call`) adds `\lx@author@withinst` (an `\inst` an author's request) and its membership and collaboration readouts to Perl's `[role=author,#1]{\lx@personname{#2}}` (:588-589), the lines are normalized as the cut's are (OD #52), and the emitter's and `=2`'s whole block is the call's argument as given — save that the emitter writes each macro whose expansion starts by closing a tabular (a juggle, or a column such as vldb.cls's `\alignauthor`, which nothing splits there) as the line break it prints, one opening the block nothing (`fallback::tabular_juggles_in_a_whole_block`; digested inside the creator's `\lx@personname` it closed a tabular the block never opened: 1511.05911's 4 Errors and 8 names lost, CL3, guard `perfect_kernel_batchcl3::a_whole_blocks_tabular_juggle_is_a_line_break`) — not through `add_authors_calls`' opening rewrites (marks unaliased, notes out of marks, empty and blank-line marks, a notes line joined), which only the cut reads. A creator written whole carries `_merged_checked` (`author_macros::KEPT_WHOLE`), its merge counted by its Warning, not flagged again (`flag_merged_creators`; a tabular block is kept whole on purpose alike). With `=2` a block no rehearsal reads keeps its queued whole entry, in one Warning (past the positions, 2204.09614, 2404.06718; the read budget, 1810.03464), the key set there, where the Warning counts it, not at the queue: a block queued after the frontmatter was digested is digested whole and uncounted, so its `merged_creators` Errors stand (astro-ph9808358). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchz4b::{a_block_losing_other_ink_keeps_its_reading, an_email_label_is_written_as_printed, an_unread_block_is_written_whole, annotate_made_reaches_every_name}` (the last RED until LO2: `annotate={made}` read `lx_author_made`, one entry under `=2`, review revZ4b).

**The net's coordination and separator checks (N1, `resolver/net.rs`), counted, the reading kept.** Two more passes of the reading over a block's digested events and `Resolved`, beside the word check and like it in the emitter's one Warning a block (`warn_net`): *marks* (`uncoordinated_marks`): a creator's request (a mark shown on its name) whose label a line of the block leads with (its first ink's run of marks, `$^1$ $^2$ Univ A`) that no item the creator holds carries by its own label, the label the emitter answers a request by (1703.06483: the mark stays printed on the name); an item's label a line leads with and a name prints that no creator holds; a mark a creator requests printed inside an item, not leading it (an entry not parted at its mark, an e-mail line's marked addresses read into an affiliation). *Separators* (`merged_names`): two Names a `Sep` other than a gap, or a `Break`, parts (only marks, notes and layout between) whose words one creator's name holds, the second no qualifier or remark and the name joined by no rule of the reading's (`RCreator::joins`, a `NameJoin` the resolver records where it joins, its `rule` tag beside it: reversed, `Eckart, A.`, 1501.02171; a qualifier, a remark, a macro's, a gap's, initials' or a layout's join); and a name holding a label before a colon and a space (a role's heading, not a link's `http://`, gr-qc0505029: `Editor: Andrei V. Gritsan`, 2205.07715; `{\bf Authors:} F.~Arleo`, hep-ph0311131; `The GAMBIT Cosmology Workgroup: Patrick Stöcker`, 2009.03287). A gap parts no names (`S. A. \,Levshakov`, 0911.3853). Known false alarms: a binding's comma inside one name part (imsart's `\fnms{William, E.}`, 2110.01945); a note a rule attached unlabelled (2601.12091). Perl has none of these (its `\lx@add@authors`, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:687-694, checks only for a `{tabular}`); they are the one added step's. The role heading is still read by its colon: the font boundary inside a Name (`{\bf Authors:} F.~Arleo`) is a fact the lexer doesn't record (a run carries its first character's font). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchn1::{a_role_heading_in_a_name_is_counted, a_mark_reaching_no_contact_is_counted, an_email_label_in_any_language_is_written_as_printed, a_note_cuts_out_its_written_address, a_lost_name_writes_the_block_whole, a_lost_name_spells_its_own_address, a_list_part_goes_to_no_line_author, no_reading_outlives_its_conversion}`; RED `perfect_kernel_batchz4b::an_unprinted_link_target_is_no_address_red` (2607.28418's `mailto:email@domain` written as an address, the reading's `link_target`).

**The content invariant on the placed output (N2, `resolver/placed.rs`), counted.** The safety net's bar (2) (every word TeX printed in an author block is in the output exactly once, or counted) is checked once more after placement, as the last step of `insert_frontmatter` (Perl's `insertFrontMatter` and `relocateAnnotations`, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:736-740, :891-900), under `=2` only (`emitter::check_placed_content`): the words the ledger's live blocks (`words::live_blocks`, a replaced or cleared block none) and creator calls printed, their rehearsed events, against the placed creators as `emitter::dom` reads them. One definition of a printed word for both sides (`words::ink_words`): every word, a mark excluded by its event, not by its length (a word a Mark event prints is that mark's, as often as the events print it, wherever a text holds it: IEEEtran's nested `\IEEEauthorblockA{\IEEEauthorrefmark{2}Univ B, City}`, 1812.05961; a lost one-letter word is counted, review revN2), an address a unit of its own whose local-part and domain words are none of the text's (1605.03019's `IDSIA` beside `@idsia.ch`, counted lost where it was silent), a glued address read from its first letter to its last (`——meizeh@…`, 1503.06438). A line's Names are read whole, so a list the inks part at commas, or across a line break inside its braces (`Event::braces`), is one list (1605.03019, 2305.13191); a Contact or Note alone; a binding's pieces of one cut list (their `_cutlist`) one text (1808.00588). *Lost*: printed more often than placed, counted as the excess counts it — a shared item (one kind's under one compared text) as often as the inks print its text (`placed::Prints`: a line's words with its separators', a Contact's or a Note's, a column of `\and` or an alignment tab ending a line, an address beside them the e-mail's the reading takes out of the entry — IEEEtran's `\IEEEauthorblockA{…\\ Burwood 3125, Australia \\ ann@deakin.edu.au}`, 2311.03657, 2003.10159; an entry of several lines a run of its block's or call's prints in a row), at least the most copies one creator holds and at most its copies in all, each print taken once and the longest entries first, so an item of another kind printing the same text, or a shorter entry inside a longer one, counts what is left (revtex's two-line `\address{…, Japan\\ CREST, Japan Science and Technology Corporation, …}` beside another author's first line of it, cond-mat0305063) (the main session's ruling on N2r2: a line printed under each author and kept as one shared item is no loss — `Email: rezakord@ipm.ir` in two notes, 0712.1873 —, and a line printed once counts one creator's copies, so a shared entry's copies hide no word lost on a line of other words: review revN2's `IDSIA` printed twice, one copy lost, the shared affiliation printed once and held twice; a lost line printing the shared item's own words is still covered by its copies, review revN2r3's `q1e`, a RED in SYNC's leftovers row 13f, to be counted from the reading's entry spans), a name every copy, an e-mail's addresses every copy —, a publication note, a title's note (elsarticle's `\tnotetext`, 1611.08809), a contact's `name` (with its item, and never its text's where the text opens with it: a class's `Email: `, which the rehearsal's `\email` doesn't print, 2307.11138, 1602.07570; a label the text doesn't print answers no word of it, 2607.28418, though a contact's default kernel label is counted as printed ink whether or not the page prints it, review revN2r3's `q4f`, a RED in row 13g) and a link's `href` (each target once) holding it too. *Excess*: placed more often than printed, a shared item (its compared text) counted the same way, a name every copy, an e-mail's addresses every copy (an address is one person's), against what the inks print and what prints beside them (a separator's word, a link's target, a call's `name=` label, revtex's `\email[Corresponding author e-mails: ]`, 2404.07637; a footnote's text; a publication note; a block's own call). An excess needs every live block and creator call read, and a block written whole exempts the words of the creator it became (the one whose name holds the most of its Name words, more than half; TeX's own digestion of it prints what its separators print: JAIR's `\and` printing "and", which the rehearsal binds to an event printing nothing, 1908.02923; its addresses still count, and every other creator's words do, review revN2). Placed text is parted at every layout part (`dom::words_without_marks`). Two readings of one ink reconcile: an address one side reads where the other reads its local part's words (a list's parts a note keeps, `{\it aable, bbaker, cat@a.org}`, 2003.14069), and a word one side reads glued to the next where the other parts it (`CanadaPerimeter`, 0803.3421; a name and its ORCID's id, `Kim0000`, 2307.03558; a part a mark's event prints taken as printed); a lost one reconciles only with the words both sides read, the placed creators', never a label's, a link's or a note's beside them. A publication note written more often than the notes the reading read print it (their Note events, and a document note's; each at least once, one no event read its own print) is in excess, compared by its letters' words (`placed::note_excess`; a note's text answers a lost word, so the copy alone counts: `Bob Baker$^{2\thanks{…}}$`'s note digested twice, review rck2). Each finding is one Warning per paper counting and naming its words ("Frontmatter content check: N words the author blocks print are missing from the placed frontmatter: IDSIA.", "… N words or addresses appear in the placed frontmatter more often than the author blocks print them: xtra@b.org."); nothing is answered (placement is over). The rehearsal's bound constructors revert as the commands they are bound for (`rehearsal::load`'s `alias`: `\and`, `\And`, `\AND`, `\\`, `\par`, `\email`), and a verbatim argument's `\and` parts its addresses as a break does (`events::raw_lines`): 2106.06418's svjour3 `\email{yjansson@kth.se \and tony@kth.se}` no longer writes a contact `\lx@fm@obs@andtony@kth.se` at `=2`; 1401.5951's `\thanks{\email{…}}` note text and 2106.11154's lni `\orcid` link target no longer print the rehearsal's names. Under `=2` the flush reads every paper as the census does (`shadow::reads_now`), so the check reads the creator calls of a paper with no author block (llncs's `\author` and `\institute`) in production, without `LATEXML_FM_SHADOW=1` too: before, they were left unrehearsed there and the check blind (1401.5951: 2 findings under the census, none without); the `=2` XML with the census and without it was byte-identical on 287 dev3 papers (N2r3). The excess it finds that the reading's check can't: 2607.00684's `mtablo@postech.ac.kr` twice on one creator, an address a note keeps that the emit also writes as a contact (0807.0895, 2208.10209's MNRAS `\thanks{Contact e-mail: mn@ras.ac.uk}`, 2111.01328, 2605.22728). **What TeX printed of a creator call, one rule (RC1):** a call's words count unless its block's events print them — a call outside its block's expansion none of them; its words are its rehearsal's, or its content's text where no rehearsal read it (`ApiCall::unread`: the rehearsal gave up, `SkipReason::OverBudget`, a Fatal, `NotUndone`; a queued creator call the emitter took that no call recorded, a stand-in copy's, `Ledger::unrecorded`); a call its block's own expansion made (`inside`) is rehearsed for the check alone (`ApiCall::inside_events`), from the check's own allowance of one rehearsal's reads per conversion, never the output's budget (`rehearsal::for_the_check`: revtex's `\collaboration` after an `\author` spent it, and a later `\affiliation` lost its rehearsal, review revRC1), and is its block's where the block's events print every one of its words, a block no longer live printing none that TeX printed; the block's own creator entry is the block. A content's text (`ledger::content_text`) parts words as an ink's are parted, reading catcodes, a control sequence's length and a control symbol's character (an accent's `\'` from a spacing `\,`; the two `batche0` pins this read raised, review revCK1b 1): an accent (a control symbol), a one-letter control word or a group inside a word parts nothing (`Universit\"at` one word, not `Universit at`; a dotless i inside its accent's group or after it, `F\'{\i}sica`, `Bras\'\i lia`, review revRC1r2: a 2-character control sequence inside a word — after a letter, a digit or a place read past — or, an accent's control symbol (`\'`, `` \` ``, `\^`, `\"`, `\~`, `\=`, `\.`: `ledger::accent_symbol`) or a one-letter control word, before its first letter (`\'Ecole`, review revH3 2; `\v{S}koda`, `\c{C}elik`, the accent and its argument one printed letter where the word begins, review revCK1b 4), followed past any `}` and one-letter control word — by its letter's catcode, an accent before a word's first letter by its character, no name spelled — by a letter, a digit or a group; past a control symbol it does not look, so `Smith\,\\Univ` is two words, review revG2; a spacing control symbol, `\\`, `\ `, `\,`, `\;`, `\:`, `\>` (`ledger::spacing_symbol`), parts as the space or the line's end it prints does, `Dept\\Muller` two words and `Dept,\\Muller`'s plain `Muller` matched as spelled, review revCK1 2-3; what prints nothing reads no word: a `\\`'s `*` and `[…]` and a tabular's own call, `\begin{tabular}[…]{…}` with its column spec and `\end{tabular}` (`rehearsal::past_line_break`, `rehearsal::past_tabular_call`, the readings the juggle's reopen uses: `\\[2mm]` read "2mm" lost, review revCK1b 5; `\begin{tabular}{c}` read "c tabular", review revI2 1); guard `perfect_kernel_batchfs1::an_open_group_rehearsals_word_matching`), its accents and `\i` unread, each word it read past one in kept with the places (`ledger::ContentText::read_past`), and the check takes such a word, and no other, for the word the other side prints (`placed::reads_as`: the printed word's `base_letters`, with at most one `i` or `j` where a one-letter control word was, the letter a dotless `\i`/`\j` printed, `Fsica` for `física`; a plain word matches as spelled, so a lost `Lu` beside a macro's `Liu` or a lost `Muller` beside a macro's `M\"uller` is counted, RC1f, review revH1; one test for every reconcile of a content's text — a call no rehearsal read, a stand-in copy's unrecorded call, a block that left a group open), as it takes a glued word for its parts; a letter command (`Gro{\ss}e`, a control word) still parts its word. So a call the ledger misreads as `inside` is no longer exempt on trust (IEEEtran's affiliations, 2401.11731, 1801.03314), and a call no rehearsal read is counted, not dropped silently; the budget's Warning says what each mode does with it (off: read as it prints; `=2`: its block written whole, any other call's words not written and counted here). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchrc1`. **A block whose rehearsal left a group open (FS1)** — its frames not back where they started, `rehearsal::Rehearsal::Done::left_open` (`\author{A One \end{tabular}~\begin{tabular}{c} Dept}`: a juggle the reading takes as written — a tie or a bare group between; the plain juggle is a column at `=2` since FB2b4-FB2b6, with `\hskip 1em` between since FB2b8, FS2 — leaves a tabular open, and what follows it is in no box of the digested list, so no event says it; the shape of 1401.6981's sig-alternate juggle) — is not trusted to its events: the words of its content's text (`ledger::content_text`, read at the flush into `Outcome::Events::unread`, so the check reads no token) the events lack count too, a possible loss (a tabular's own call, `\begin{tabular}{c}`, reads none since CK3: `Dept`); a content word the block's events print as spelled is the events', then a word read past an accent or a dotless letter (`M\"uller` read `Muller` for `Müller`, `Fsica` for `Física`, `reads_as`), each print taken once, so the Warning names the lost word (`Lan` beside a printed `Lian`; a plain `Fisica` beside `F\'{\i}sica`) (RC1e, review revG2; RC1f, review revH1). Out of its reach: a word printed once through a macro and lost once as spelled (`\newcommand\auth{A Smith}` … `Dept Smith`, review revH1's h4i: the content text reads no macro, so one `Smith` each side). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchfs1::an_open_group_rehearsals_words_are_counted` (repro `sectioning-frontmatter/author_raw_tabular_juggle_counted`), `perfect_kernel_batchfs1::an_open_group_rehearsals_word_matching` (a row each: `author_raw_tabular_juggle_accented_word`, `…_dotless_i`, `…_control_symbol_parts`, `…_plain_word_exact`, `…_plain_word_unaccented`, `…_lost_beside_printed`, `…_lost_beside_dotless`, `…_accent_command_opens_word`, `…_break_optional_prints_nothing`). Out of its reach: a block the ledger never records (a raw class's `\author`, SolarPhysics: 1808.10103, 1306.3180, 0 creators and no Warning), and an ownership defect that keeps every word (1508.02561's institutes). 2506.02663's "footnote junk" is the `<tags>` of an unpaired `\footnotemark` note, no printed text (`dom::text_without_marks` skips it); its real defect, `qinghai@zju.edu.cn` lost from a `\thanks`, is counted. Left, counted as alarms: an ORCID icon's drawing (`\href{https://orcid.org/…}{\orcidicon}` over a `tikzpicture`: the Contact's text is the picture's path data, 2502.20521) and a label a class prints with no `name` (siamart-like `\orcid` printing `ORCID: `, 2307.11138, 2402.16530), which the rehearsal's events don't record; an accent whose base the rehearsal prints as a Name of its own (`Bo$\check{c}$ní` reads `Bo cní` where the placed text reads `Boˇcní`: 1603.04461, 0805.0350, 0911.1045, 2310.11912, cond-mat0103427, 0705.1518); a class's `\and` printing "and". **A label the writer cut at where it is text (CT1ar):** an in-block entry the emitter writes labelled by a mark glued to the text of another entry of that label in its list (the block's `\and` column) — `calls::split_marked_pieces`'s S1 reading, one list labels each entry once — makes that mark's word, with a separator's word just before it, printed and held by no mark or name (`emit::labelled_entry` records the writer's cut, `Ledger::labelled`; `placed::retold_words` reads the placed ones): 2204.02412's `(CAP$^3$), New York University Abu Dhabi` cut into `Center for Astro (CAP` and `, Univ Z` counts the "3" (W 40 → 41, XML unchanged). A label leading a line (`$^1$Carnegie Mellon\\ $^1$School of Computer Science`, a mark-led address line) or glued to a name reads no text; the brief's first form, any label on two entries of one list, counted 12 such guarded shapes. A cut list is cut at the queue by the S1 reading itself; revtex's `$1$St Floor` line (a line-leading `$1$`, the mark reading's) stays uncounted. Guards `perfect_kernel_batchn2`, `perfect_kernel_batchn2r2`, `perfect_kernel_batchn2r3`.

**`=2`, the whole block queued, reaches `=1` (Z4b).** With each call queuing one entry the call-time readers of the queue (`queued_author_marks`, `queued_author_name_keys`, `queued_creator_count`, `placed_contact_owner`, `AUTHOR_KEYS`' ranges) count entries, not names (a binding's whole-list entry its names at the `\and` family since P2-3b, #995), and their booleans hold (a whole block carries its names' marks). Their positions are answered at the flush, by the reading: an `author:N` label names the N-th queued author entry (`Resolver::author_entries`, one a call under `=2`, a block's whole entry its names; one a creator under `=1`, as the old reader queued them), and an address it places among several names is the one it spells, else the block's (`Resolver::entry_owners`); an address the call placed on the block because the names it held whole spelled it for no one (initials: `gkt@`, 2405.01963) is the one live creator's it spells. dev3 creator XML identical between `=1` and `=2` on 1,023 of 1,028 papers, devh10k 286 of 289; the differences named in the batch's report (0911.3853 and 2608.19750 better, 2205.05623 an e-mail's order, astro-ph9808358's blocks arriving after the frontmatter was digested, 2202.12897's lone address spelling no one the block's where `=1` gave it an author, the unread blocks 2204.09614, 2404.06718, 1810.03464). Guard `perfect_kernel_batchz4b::the_whole_block_queue_reaches_one` (IEEEtran's e-mail line under one `\IEEEauthorblockN`, 2010.07442, 2003.03692, 2510.03288, 2607.02294).

**The flip's prerequisites (F1).** *Positions per call* (#837): a block of 559 names (2204.09614, 18,395 tokens; 2404.06718,
20,918; dev20k's largest 2410.11607, 21,304; longtail3k's 1812.07638, 18,854) is read under the switch, where it was "unstamped:
out of positions" and written whole. *A creator call's keyvals on the Name it prints:* a block's own `\lx@add@creator[role=…]{…}`
(PoS's and JHEP's `\speaker`), bound in the rehearsal to `\lx@fm@obs@creator`, notes its keyvals and its name's positions
(`field_notes::FieldCreator`, the rehearsal's notes on what no box holds); the Name its name prints takes the role
(`events::creator_roles`), the creator (`RCreator::role`, `RCreator::call`) is written with it, Perl's `role=` and `speaker:N`
label (`creator_role`), from the call's name argument, the call left out (`event_run`: written again it queued a second,
nameless creator): 0910.5686, 1007.2355, 1111.2428, 1111.6944. The keyvals are tokens: `\lx@fm@obs@creator` reads them as the
API does (`OptionalKeyVals:Frontmatter`; `FieldCreator::keys`, the role and annotations the KeyVals' last), the block's
outcome keeps them (`Outcome::Events::creators`), and the emitter writes them on Perl's call, `[role=author,#1]`
(Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:586; `creator_keys`), the reading's labels joining the call's own annotations: `name=`, `role=`,
`annotations=` (`a_creator_calls_keyvals_are_written`; dev3 and devh10k hold no in-block call with other keys than `\speaker`'s).
*A link printing a name* (F1r2): a url contact that carries a mark and prints other text than its own target (its scheme and a
closing slash aside, in any case: `prints_its_target`) is read as that text, a Name carrying the link, written whole with it
(`resolver::lines::link_names`, the ORCID links' pass): 1812.07638's 304 `\href{http://inspirehep.net/record/…}{A.~Cerri}$^{1}$`,
304 creators and 3,063 links under `=2` (F1: 2 creators, 2,760 links); "carries a mark" was a proxy, replaced at LO1 by the name
slot (below). *The read-back's cost:* `\lx@add@author`'s membership
readout (`frontmatter_fields::names::written_membership_out`) read the rest of the content past each comma, quadratic on `=2`'s queued whole
entry of 418 names (1507.02068, +7.3 % instructions on against off). A grade is a suffix of grade words, so its commas are read
from the last leftward and the first tail holding a word no grade has ends the reading (every tail before it holds that word):
each tail read once, no cap, the output byte-identical to int145a's (F1's 256-token cap read `{\itshape Fellow,
IEEE\thanks{<300 characters>}}` into the name, `a_grade_with_a_long_note_is_the_grade`); the one writer kept
(`whole_block_author`): 1507.02068 on −2.3 % against off, `instructions:u` (F1r2; F1's cap −1.18 %). Not settled by the same scan: a
tabular block ending `…, Fellow, IEEE\end{tabular}` reads `\end{tabular}` into the grade with the switch off (E=2, int145a's
too). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchf1`.

**The switch-on leftovers in the reading (LO1).** *A link filling a name slot is the name:* a url link printing other text than
its own target that is the only ink between its line's separators (a comma, a word, a gap, `\and`, a tab, a break, the block's
ends) but for the marks and notes a name carries, an inkless link and punctuation, on a line no mark leads, which is its column's
