Wang}\thanks{…}}` and an unmarked `\href{…}{Bob Baker},` between two names, each a url contact of the next name or of a nameless
creator before; 1812.07638 304 creators, 3,118 `<ref>` as before; `Ann Able \\ \href{…}{Project Page}` stays a contact.
*A superscript after an emitted entry's label is its text:* `\lx@sup@setlabel@affiliation` read a line's first mark as its label by
the `_bymark` the label sets, which an emitted entry (its label the emitter's) never has, so every superscript was a label and
dropped: 1812.07638's `(ECT$^*$) )` came out `(ECT) )` with no Warning; the entry's first mark is now recorded from the
emitted item's start and each entry line's (`\lx@frontmatter@item@start`, `\lx@frontmatter@savesups`; since LO2 a key on the
entry's pending entry, `_markread`, which the mark's own formula, a group, doesn't undo), so a class's `\inst{2}` opening its second entry (0807.0752, 1002.3516) and a
nested `\IEEEauthorblockA{\IEEEauthorrefmark{2}…}` (1812.05961) keep their labels. *An address decides only
its own ink* (`Resolver::block`, `row_line`; the emitter's switch on only, `Resolver::emitting`): a line printing an address and
other text, its label word aside (`reads_as_email_label`), under an unmarked line of its column ending in a comma continues that
item and is its holders' (2203.10777, 1210.0352: the city line, notes of one author before, an affiliation of each as the switch
off has it); under one names row and no column, where its addresses spell no one author and its text is no name its address
spells (`LostInk::names_fail`'s), every author's of the row (1605.03019: `IDSIA, 6928 Manno, Switzerland` to all three,
nameless notes and IDSIA nowhere before). The address stays in the affiliation's text, as the Kind steps leave it with the switch
off, but where it spells one author of the row (LO2, below). *A line's addresses by the address reader* (`place_line_contacts`, the switch on only): where `address_runs` reads every
address `addresses_in` does and more, a list of local parts opening its line, `{\it pzou94, ozel, suresh@gwu.edu}` (2003.14069),
is three addresses spelling assigns. *A creator call's `annotations=` are its creator's labels* (`Input::Block::calls`,
`FieldCreator::labels`): `\lx@add@creator[role=editor,annotations={ed}]{Bob Baker}` with `\lx@add@affiliation[label=ed]{Editorial
Office}` gives the office to Bob (a nameless creator's, or Ann Able's, before); the call's labels print nothing unanswered, and
`creator_keys` writes `annotations=` once (the noted keys without it), where Perl's KeyVals makes a key given twice a list
(KeyVals.pm:294-300). Off: the switch-off output byte-identical (the reading's rules that move only the emitter's output are gated
on the switch). Left, each with its shape: 1812.07638's `Contributors:` heading line between two names rows, the six editors'
affiliation (a role heading is the names row's label; the API has no kind for it yet); an in-block `(ECT$^*$)` on a marked line
splits the entry at the symbol with either switch (the lexer's glue inside open brackets fixes it but moves the switch-off output).
Guards `perfect_kernel_batchlo1`; `perfect_kernel_batchn1::a_list_part_goes_to_no_line_author` (the right output now, `=2`).

**The switch-on leftovers, second round (LO2).** *A line's address is its holder's:* a line the names row holds (a row line,
`row_line`, or an unmarked line the row takes by the institution it names) whose addresses all spell one author of the row and
print last on it is that author's e-mail, the line's other text the row's (`Resolver::block`, the switch on only): 2203.10777's
`Dresden, Saxony 01062, Germany (martin.waltz@tu-dresden.de)` each author's city and own e-mail (LO1: the line whole with its
address on each, as the switch off; int146a: the e-mail and three nameless notes; review revLO1 1); `\author{Ann Able and Bob
Baker\\ Univ A\\ Present address: Dept X, Univ Y (ann.able@y.org)}` Ann's e-mail and both authors' text without it, as the
switch off (review revLO1 2). Every address on the line must print at its end, no other ink between or after them (LO2r2, review
revLO2 3: `Dresden, Germany (bob.baker@a.org); Leipzig (bob@b.org)` keeps its reading). The emitter writes the rest from its own
tokens, cut inside the ink the address ends at the first address's own first token — past every token the item's letters need, by
the writer's own check of a span's letters (`emitter::repart::prefix_tokens` over `plan::block_span_tokens`) — less the spaces,
separators, commands and bracket opening the address, a bracket the cut leaves open closed by its own token after the address, and a
mark before it kept as its ink (LO2r2, review revLO2 2 and base: the shortest letter match wrote `Dresden [Germany`, `(Tel. 351
463`, and `Dresden$^{\dagger}$, Germany` by its text, the `†` lost; now `Dresden [Germany]`, `(Tel. 351 463)`, `Dresden † ,
Germany`, as the switch off); an address spelling no one, or printed mid-line, stays in the text. *A note after a block's labelled
entries is the block's* (LO2r2, ruling: Perl): a note after an entry's last other ink, or on a line under a labelled entry (a line of
notes alone, `{\small\thanks{…}}`, or after the line's text), is no name's — the entry's span ends before it
(`Resolver::labelled_entries`, the block's unmarked line under a `Continued::Pending` entry; the switch on only) — and the emitter
writes it as Perl prints it, digested inside the entry's contact where `\thanks` is `\lx@add@pubnote@thanks` (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:
331-332): one `<pubnote>` of the document from its own tokens (`emitter::emit::block_pubnote` over `document_note_call`; any note the
reading gives the block alone that a plain `\thanks{…}` or `\footnote{…}` prints, the rest the block's creator's as before).
2504.09745's `$^{\ddagger}$Ericsson Canada\thanks{…}` one pubnote, held by no author, as Perl (LO2: each `‡` author's thanks, Ali
Afana's and Yahia Ahmed's a general funding note; int146a and LO1: a nameless creator's note in two Warnings, and a pubnote the
entry's own tokens digested; the switch off: a pubnote per relocated `‡` entry, two); `$^{2}$Univ B, City\\ \thanks{…}` one
pubnote (int146a and LO2: the last name's, Cy Cole's). A note inside an entry, ink after it, is as before. *The tail a raw macro appends to
`\@author`* (`frontmatter_stores` `author_tail_calls`, `annotate={made}`): with `=2` the call queues one entry, a count reaching
its last name alone, so where the call made every queued creator the tail is `annotate=all`, Perl's every parent
(`relocateAnnotations`, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:520), each name's row as with the switch off (review revZ4b 4; pdflatex prints such
a tail in the last `\and` column, under every name of a one-column block). *Nits (revLO1 3-6, revN1r3 4-5):* the emitted entry's
first mark read is a key on its pending entry (`_markread`, `with_digesting_entry_attr`: Perl keeps an entry's facts on it,
:502-508), not a State flag; `Resolver::emitting` was `LATEXML_FM_EMIT=2`, as `whole_entries` (both removed with the switch);
`FieldCreator::labels` cleans as the API cleans a label (`clean_frontmatter_labels`, Perl's `cleanFrontmatterLabels`, :360-372:
`annotations={\ref{ed}}` answers `label={\ref{ed}}`, a nameless creator's before); the ledger's count of changes has one write
path, `Ledger::entries_mut`, taken only where an entry changes (with the switch on: off, which keeps no reading, a change is made
in one pass, unread first, `Ledger::change_each`, LO2r2), and the conversion's reset drops the reading and the count. A label is
cleaned on both sides (LO2r2, review revLO2 4): a call's `label=` is read as Perl's `cleanFrontmatterLabels` cleans it where that
is what the names request, as a creator call's `annotations=` (`Resolver::api`, the switch on only) — `label={\rm Ed Office}`
answers `annotations={\rm Ed Office}`, both `Ed_Office`, Bob Baker's office (LO2: read as marks, its words `E,d,Office` a mark on his
name; int146a: a nameless creator's). Off: byte-identical. Guards `perfect_kernel_batchlo2`, `perfect_kernel_batchlo1::an_address_decides_only_its_own_ink` (whole creators with
either switch), `perfect_kernel_batchz4b::annotate_made_reaches_every_name`, `emitter::emit::tests::the_reset_drops_the_reading_and_its_count`.
*A note a contact command makes* (LO3): a block's Contact event whose kind is a note — jheppub's, jcappub's and jinstpub's
`\note{…}` inside an `\author`, `\lx@add@contact[role=note]{…}` (Perl's jheppub.sty.ltxml:39) — is written as the contact command
it is, the call inside taking the item's label, as every contact command of a block is (`emitter::emit::item_call`); written as
an `ltx:note` around the call, where an API call means nothing (`\lx@frontmatter@itemonly`), every such note was lost with the
switch on (1403.1099, 2001.06318 "Corresponding author.", 2308.04217's three "Speaker at …" notes; the content check counted
them); REVTeX's `\frontmatter@footnote{…}` (`\lx@add@contact[role=thanks]`) the same. Each author's `<contact role="note">`
as off and Perl. Guard `perfect_kernel_batchlo3`.
*Notes and addresses the reading dropped* (LO4), each with the switch on alone: (a) a block's contact command is written as
the command it is only where its span prints that one Name, Contact or Note event; a macro holding a name and the command
(`\newcommand{\ann}{Ann Able\note{…}}`), two commands (`\note{…}\note{…}`) or `Dan Dorn\emailAdd{…}` spans them all, and the
whole macro was written for each item — the name a note of its own, a note moved to the next author (review revLO3 1). It is
its text, a contact command's note a `<contact role="note">`, each counted as a macro's span; an address so written loses its
font. (b) The one address of a class's list left over (OD #809) goes to the author marked as the corresponding author by the
switch-off step's facts read on the reading (`Resolver::listed_corresponding`, `place::marked_corresponding_author`): a note of
theirs naming them so — a contact command's note too, jheppub's `\note{Corresponding author.}` (1901.08773, 2510.11030, which
gave it a nameless creator) —, or a mark they request whose legend says so: a labelled affiliation's, a contact command's note's
own mark (`\note[*]`, its call's `_mark` key, `Event::note_mark`) or the footnote counter's number it prints under, save where
an affiliation is labelled with that number; none marked, the one `*` no legend explains where the address says it is the
corresponding author's (2308.06532). (c) An `\email` in an author's note whose meaning is a binding's routes its address to the
current author (Perl's `\lx@add@email`), so it is the note owner's e-mail, not a link left in the note's text (ruling
2026-10-20 #4), which the written note printed nowhere; a guess the fallback class locks is the binding's meaning (OmniBus's
`\email`, `\email:locked`, OD #408, `ledger::email_meaning`): 2511.14713's siamart `\thanks{…, \email{wning@vt.edu},
\email{amiedlar@vt.edu}.}`, both addresses Ning Wan's as off and Perl. Off: byte-identical. Guard `perfect_kernel_batchlo4`.
*Switch-off mechanisms ported* (P2), each with the switch on alone, the switch-off code the spec: (C) cas's one unlabelled
`\affiliation` (`_share=authors,annotate=run`, `cas_labelled_entry`) is every author's, before it and after it, as
the old split's `share_row_contacts` shared it (deleted at P27b) when it is the queue's only one (`Resolver::sole_shared_run`, answered in
`answer_pending`): the reading gave it to its run, the first author (2506.17280, 2106.02306, 2201.00009, 2207.13923,
2411.19633, 2606.24054). (NT) A role note is the note the switch-off output writes: a `\thanks` whose text opens with a mark
the names request is an affiliation entry only where `\lx@add@thanks` makes it one (`starts_with_affiliation_mark`, OD #52:
`$^` or `\textsuperscript` whose first character is an ASCII digit; here the leading Mark of role `sup`/`math` whose printed
text opens with a digit, P2r2), never a `\footnote` (`\lx@add@note`); an affiliation whose whole text is a legend is then a
note (the Kind step for a legend); any other is its mark's carriers' legend note, its kind the switch-off procedure's in its
order (strict porting, P2r2), save one departure: a note printing e-mail addresses that is no legend stays the entry the
reading made it, each address its spelled carrier's (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4's symbol-line rule; the switch-off note keeps every
address in its text on its owner): IEEEtran journal's `\thanks{\IEEEauthorrefmark{1}The authors are with …, E-mails: a@, b@,
c@}`, 1610.05419, 2405.06709 (review revP2: as a note each carrier held every address) (`Resolver::keep_note`, `emitter::emit::item_call`'s `an_entry`) — `\thanks{\IEEEauthorrefmark{2} Also with …}`
(1107.5730), `\thanks{$\diamond$ Work conducted during an internship …}` (2205.02029), elsarticle's
`\footnote{\textsuperscript{1}These authors contributed equally …}` (2110.12892); with two carriers of the mark the note is both
(the charter's symbol-line rule; off gives it to the note's owner alone). An entry the Kind step for a legend reads
(`insert::kind_legend_contacts`, OD #961) carries the label that prints in a key of its own, `_printedlabel`
(`frontmatter_api::PRINTED_LABEL`, beside the flag `_labelprints=true`; P2 held it as `_labelprints`'s value, a flag and data
in one key): the call's `label=` its binding
prints (authblk's `\affil[*]{Corresponding author …}`, 2605.31330, 2606.17567, 2201.11910, 2602.03863, 2605.11756), which the
emitter's routing label replaced (`emitter::emit::rekeyed`), or the first mark an emitted entry's content printed
(`\lx@sup@setlabel@affiliation`'s record on the digested stub, `frontmatter_api.rs`), read by `insert::legend_mark`; a legend
whose address the reading left in its text (2605.31330's `(Email: t.han@tees.ac.uk), Le Hong Trang`, 2411.08381's
`Correspondence to: a and b`) waits for the address cut (E1). (B) A name whose font wrapper holds its mark or note
(`\textbf{Yan Yan$^{1}$\thanks{…}}`) is written from its own tokens in the wrapper's font (`emitter::emit::event_run`): the whole
cover kept the answered mark on the name and wrote the note twice (2309.13682, 2212.02936, 2305.16982, 1310.2822, 2503.17340);
the note is now the reading's, once, not bold (the PDF's footnote font). The same cause where the name's tokens cannot be cut
(`\newcommand{\ann}{Ann Able\thanks{…}}`, one token for both events, review revLO4): the note its tokens print is digested
with the name and not written again (`block_names`' `on_names`). Off: byte-identical. Guard `perfect_kernel_batchfmp2`.

**P1b (E1, the strict port of RT1's rows 54-58; `=2` only).** An address printed inside an entry's text (an `\institute`, an
`\affil`, a `\thanks` entry, a block line read on) is cut out into its owner's e-mail as the switch-off writer cuts today's XML
(`plan::cut_entry_addresses`, `dom::address_cut`, `Op::Address`, `Op::CutAddresses`), translated onto the entry's tokens, no DOM
pass. *The fact:* the lexer records where each character of a name prints (its box's cover and its own token, on a line
printing an `@`; a note's text from its body's) and the font each `@` prints in, at its token's position, in a table beside
the events (`events::InkTable`, the block's ledger entry `Outcome::Events::inks`, a call's rehearsal), not on each `Event`:
24 bytes more on every event cost 1901.01540's thousand-author block +0.35 % instructions at `=2` (int149a's `Event` padded
by 24 bytes: 13,877 M → 13,926 M), the table +0.04 %; and the reading's take-out keeps its bytes (`Taken::lined`, `cuts`,
`runs` with their label words). *The cut* (`emitter/address_cut.rs`): the reading's text located in its events' text (a
note's, the span's, or the lines from it on, line by line where the reading trimmed a line's separator: 1203.0253,
2405.03617), each cut byte a position; row 54, all holders cut or none, per entry; row 55, a separator the cut takes at an end
takes what prints nothing up to the kept ink (the break and the mark of `\\$^*\,$a@x`) but never a mark leading the kept ink
after it (`Univ X, {\tt a@x}, $^1$Dept`, review revP1b S1), a cut taking a kept character's token
or a note declines, one is parted around a contact read apart (`(\email{a@x}; b@x)`, 1106.3045), and each printed run the cut
touches (the text's spaces as printed) must be the reading's whole, else the entry is given back (`kwb,flynn,walter.scheirer@nd.edu`,
a run the reading reads as one address after prose; also one glued to a list's comma: 1903.10019); each part grown to a balanced
run over tokens printing nothing (`{\tt(a@x)}`, astro-ph0610492); row 56 (the switch-off writer's wrapper, `dom::address_cut`),
each address the call wrapping it alone, whole, where nothing else prints in its cover and the cut takes it
(`\href{mailto:a@x}{a@x}`, 2608.15371; `\textit{a@x}`) and it is no contact command, whose call the e-mail's item would
mute (1109.3369's `\email{…}`), else its own tokens with the switches of the group its run's first
address opens in (`{\tt\small a@x; b@x}`'s second), else in the font its `@` prints in (`InkTable::fonts`: `{\it Contact
e-mail: a@x}`, 2008.08137; each of `\texttt{a@x, b@y, c@z,}`, 2608.14026; a `\thanks` body's `\texttt{E-Mail: a@x}`,
2405.06709; `\begin{small}…a@x\end{small}`, 1312.5468), a list's written-out address its text in that font (RP1's
`EntryCut::mail`; one a contact command prints, whose call the item would mute: 1109.3369); row 57, the e-mail named by the
run's label (`E-mail: `, 2311.02475), and the label the Kind step for an address line reads before the run
(`insert::address_line_cut`, RT1 rows 64-67, 72) goes with it — decided in the reading's take-out under `=2`
(`Resolver::take_out_entry_addresses` → `resolver::labels::take_labels`, P1c: the entry's text the reading keeps and the
e-mails' names are the take-out's, the emitter only writes them) — where the reading keeps its words and
nothing of the addresses: the whole line and its break where only marks and separators stand before the label, else from the
words' end, the e-mail named by it (`Corresponding author: `, the role-note step's correspondence note of the address's owner;
`Correspondence: `, `Contact e-mail: `) — the label's words no longer an affiliation, of another author for authblk's unmarked
`\affil[ ]{Corresponding author: \textit{a@x}}` (2305.02090, 2404.05566; elsarticle's `\address[*]`, whose label its
binding does not print, 2107.10505; 1510.03749, 1807.09187, 2008.08137); a legend's (its binding prints its label, authblk's `\affil[*]`, or a mark opens its
text) stays for the Kind step for a legend unless an e-mail word is among them (row 66: 1812.03816 its carriers' note marked
`*`; 2004.06340, 2012.13817's `corresponding author, email …` the e-mail's label); a separator a cut takes at an end gives
back as many of the tokens printing nothing there as a balanced run needs (the brace closing the kept ink's group before a
whole line's break, `\textit{… China}\\ \textit{*Corresponding author: a@x, b@x}}`, 2405.13751); row 58, the e-mails the reading's,
written as `\lx@add@contact` items before the cut entry. Row 57a's whole-paper decline is per entry: a cut that can't be made is
given back whole to the Kind steps, as before. The entry is its whole as it printed, written by its own path (`item_call`) with
the runs taken out of its tokens (`Field::content_cut`: the block path's `event_run`, a note's argument, an API call's command
argument; an entry whose lines no balanced run holds line by line, each cut inside one line's run, `lines_run`: 1312.5468 —
or a whole line's, which goes with one break beside it, the other breaks kept: 2604.06805, 2509.07459, P1c);
a path that doesn't cut writes its text, counted (`an entry's addresses cut`). The checks read every entry whole
(RP1's: 1610.05419). Witnesses fixed (`=2` creators = off): 2011.02560, 2104.05078, 2204.02371, 2406.02913, 2410.06013,
2508.09777, astro-ph0610446, 1912.07315, 2106.07466, 2503.07161, astro-ph0412523, cond-mat0610708, 1106.3045, 1203.0253,
1310.7021, 1604.05586, 1811.10103, 2004.11812, 2206.00099, 2211.06034, 2310.05733, 2405.03617, 2405.13751, 2503.07190,
2603.08078, astro-ph0610492, physics0603032, 2606.17067, 1707.05998; 1705.06453's e-mails (a ` -` left, the reading's own
cut). The label before an address (P1br2, review revP1b B1): P1b's cut ran before the Kind step for an address line, which at
LO4 `=2` read the entry given back whole and took `Corresponding author: a@x` whole into the e-mail's name; P1b left the
label an affiliation. The `rekeyed`/`_labelprints` cause first named explains only the marked `\affil[*]` shape, which RP2's
`_printedlabel` (P2) already gives its carriers' note; the unmarked `\affil[ ]` (2305.02090, 2404.05566) never reaches the Kind
step for a legend (it prints no mark: ruling 2026-11-04) and was the Kind step for an address line's. P1c (review revP1br2
S2): P1br2 decided that label in the emitter and rewrote the reading's items by text equality and a rule-name suffix; the
take-out now decides it (one pass), its legend read off the entry's own input (`entry_legend`: a note's body or the block
entry's events opened by a mark, an API call's printed label `_labelprints` or its events) — output equal on every witness
but the fixes named above. Open (RED, no guard): an icon or a rule inside the link or wrapper of a cut address
(`\href{mailto:a@x}{\rule{1ex}{1ex}\,a@x}`, review revP1br2 S3, repro `emit_a_cut_never_takes_an_icon`) goes with the e-mail;
the switch off cuts the text alone, which needs the link's characters' own positions (the lexer reads `\href`'s text as its
argument's ink). Off: byte-identical. Guards `perfect_kernel_batchp1e`, `perfect_kernel_batchp1c`.
**KB2 (the cut keeps `=2`'s improvements; ruling 2026-11-08: strict porting keeps every improvement).** `=2` gives an entry
back whole where P1b's cut would strand the phrase its address completes (`emitter/address_cut.rs` `entry_cuts`,
`strands_a_phrase`): a run with no label word the take-out takes (`take_labels`) after a colon or a "to" the cut keeps, the
words before it on its line naming a contact (`names_a_contact`) — revtex4's `…, USA \\ $^{a}$Author to whom correspondence
should be addressed: a@x` (2306.04726), `Email for correspondence:` (2110.05460), `…, *Corresponding author: \texttt{a@x}`
(2602.09324); a place's colon (`…, France: a@x`, 1103.3532) strands nothing and is cut. It is given back whole only where its
holders are exactly its addresses' owners (`held_by_its_owners`: every creator, or the block, holding an `owner:entry-address`
contact from its source, and no other holder; the author an address spells owns it, FIDELITY_CHARTER §4); every other entry
keeps P1b's cut, its phrase stranded as on the base: neurips's last line `Correspondence to: \texttt{pascal.klink@…}` read onto
the Aalto entry only Pajarinen holds (2004.11812: whole, it put Klink's address in her affiliation and took his e-mail), and an
entry two authors share with one address (authblk's `\affil[1]{…, USA. Correspondence to: ann@alpha.edu}`, review revJ2 k7;
revtex's shared `\affiliation`, k8: whole, it went on both holders and the owner lost her e-mail). A cut e-mail printed as a formula (`dcook12$@$uwyo.edu`, 1409.0847) is written as its text, never its math tokens
(`cut_at`), as off writes it. Off: unchanged. Open: the phrase a shared or foreign-owned entry's cut strands (2004.11812's
"…Finland Correspondence to"); an entry several authors hold whose address one owns (1409.0847's line
under Cook, Dale and Staudaher; llncs's shared `\institute{Univ A, \texttt{a@x}}`, astro-ph0610446, cond-mat0610708,
2309.10932) is cut on every holder, the co-holders' copies losing the address. Two remedies were tried and dropped: keeping
the cut on the owner beside a whole copy on the others is two records of one printed entry, which the content check counts
(`Warning:unexpected:frontmatter`); giving the entry back whole hands it to the Kind steps after the flush, which then lose or
misplace e-mails of the paper's other entries (1103.3532: Chaari's and Pesquet's e-mails lost; 2604.06805: Xiong's
`Correspondence:` e-mail on a nameless creator). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchkb2`; `perfect_kernel_batchp1e`'s read-on case
pins `=2`'s whole entry beside off's cut.

Guards `perfect_kernel_batchz4`.

**TA (a late author block; `=2` only).** An author block arriving while a flush digests its queue, after that flush read it (an `\author` in the `\title`, 1502.01001, 1510.00875, hep-ph0207056, hep-th0111116; in an amsart `\thanks`, 0807.4720; in a re-digested `{opening}`, astro-ph9808358 — the ledger's `AuthorBlock::late`), is read by a flush of its own: its whole-block call is wrapped in `\lx@frontmatter@late` (`defs/author_macros.rs`), which digests it with `\lx@add@frontmatter` / `\lx@annotate@frontmatter` let to the queue's, then runs a nested, re-entrant flush (`digest_front_matter`; the outer flush's sealed-off and label sequences saved and restored, the queue cleared first, so it sees only what the late digestion queued and terminates) — Perl's `\lx@add@authors` runs `@now` there, split at the call (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:799-806). A queue entry a flush digests is marked taken (`emitter::emit::take_digested`: `taken|<index>` in `EMITTED_ITEMS`) before its digestion, so a later, nested flush's emitter writes none of its items again (TA3; memsait's `\@opening` note, astro-ph9808358). A creator call's own nested notes are its creator's (IO1, `resolver/api.rs` `api:creator`; Perl's `\lx@add@author` digests the whole call into the creator), its `\email`/`\orcid` staying in the name, and its `\thanks` written from its argument through `note_call` (IO2). A creator call made inside a note: IO3b, below. Off: byte-identical. Guards `perfect_kernel_batchta1`, `perfect_kernel_batchio1`.

**KEY1 (the mark-keyed entries, RT2's K4, K12-K14; `=2` only).** A printed mark no name requests is no label, as the switch
off reads it (FIDELITY_CHARTER: a mark matters only where it is used). K12 is ported as a give-back, read once every name
is: an API entry a leading mark labels that no name requests keeps its call's `annotate=` placement (`resolver/post.rs`,
`label:unrequested owner:annotate`; 0906.0396, 2111.15565). **Departure:** off gates its mark reading on the call's
`\lx@affiliation@withsup` wrapper (`_withsup=true`); the port drops that gate and gives back lazily, since the eager gate
would drop ruling 1's reading of requested marks on stores and `_unsplit` blocks (review revKEY1: no store or `_unsplit`
shape shown losing a requested mark under the gate — the reason is unwitnessed, the result = off on every witness). K13: a
block line a glyph leads (a Mark of role `text`, `(\S) Inst X`) that no name requests continues the entry above it, as
Perl's block reader splits at superscripts alone (`resolver/blocks.rs`, `Resolver::continue_line`; cond-mat0309053, its
glyphs written as text, counted). K4: a `\thanks` opening with a raised number holding several marked entries is one
affiliation per entry, its lexed text (`Event::body`) cut before each top-level raised mark (`events::mark_led_pieces`, the
API reader's cut), so an entry's own comma stays its text (`$^{1}$Dept A, Univ A, $^{2}$Univ B`, review revKEY1); a
separator word the cut drops between entries is recorded dropped, counted as written; a later glyph is its text
(2509.19480, 2206.07648, 2505.06451). Each piece is sourced at its own span (its first event's start to its last's end, a
mark's formula whole: `Event::extent`), and the writer writes that span's tokens uncut (`emitter::emit` `note_piece`) — one
cut, the reading's —, read within the note's own span, its tokens and the formulas inside it alone (`address_cut::span_tokens_within`;
the span's exact slice where no balanced run of them holds it): a `\thanks` argument is typeset in the footnote (latex.ltx
`\thanks` → `\footnotetext`), never part of the formula around the command, so `Bob Baker$^{2\thanks{$^{1}$Univ A; $^{2}$Univ B}}$`'s
pieces widened to that formula, the `\thanks` digested twice: both affiliations lost, two identical pubnotes, silent (review rck2); sourced at the whole note's span, the writer re-cut it by off's `split_wrapped_affiliation_marks` and lost
a piece where the cuts disagreed (`$^{1}$Univ A; $^{2}$Univ B. $^{*}$Corresponding author.`, review revG5 1). K14: the per-column label rule only where the entry's column holds names
(2404.00915). Off: byte-identical. Left: a name's mark printing a macro's letter beside a number (`$^{\a 1}$`, `\def\a{{a}}`)
read as the one label "a1" (hep-ph0011101; RED repro `macro_letter_in_a_name_mark_is_its_own_label`). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batchkey1`.
**The names line, strictly ported (NL1; rule table RT3, `agent_reports/2026-11-08_ruletable_namesline.md`).** Five rules of
the reading that decided on words where the old reader decided on structure, each translated from the old procedure (off
declines every word-only reading, `writer::repart::by_words`, so these bit at `=2` only). (N1-N3) A names line's piece
carrying its own mark — the next event past layout and notes, or past its comma a mark that stays with it — is a name
whatever its words: the generic split never reads an institution word (`R. New$^2$`, 0904.4122; `S. Michelle
Consiglio,$^{1}$`, 2103.02641; `Alexander New$^2$`, 2311.16860), a per-author class's line a surname after an initial
(`Gary P. Centers,$^{1}$`, 1901.10843; `surname_after_initial` moved into `classify/names_split.rs`); an unmarked piece keeps
the reading's institution (`John Smith, University of Toronto`, the main session's decision). Not ported: N2's whole-list
condition, which chose between splitting a cautious line and keeping it whole (N4), a choice `=2` does not make
(`resolver/lines.rs` `marked_name`). (S1, the reading's own rule) Initials after a comma join a bare surname only, the
word read through its glued initials (`P.A.Vshivtseva$^{a,b}$, E.T.\, Einiev`, 2409.13569; `unglued_initials`). (C2-C5) A
name's collaboration remark is its `collaboration` contact, never part of the name (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4, #946): from the
piece a remark opens in (`lines::remark_start`: a bracket, "for" or "on behalf of"), the pieces of one remark that a note, a
name annotation (`lines::name_annotation`, the old reader's `NAME_ANNOTATIONS`, `classify/notes.rs`, and `\footnotemark`
as `name_takes_annotations` moves them: a request — `\altaffilmark`, `\thanksref`, `\corref`, `\fnref`, `\tnoteref` —,
`\inst`, `\IEEEauthorrefmark`, `\textsuperscript`, `\cite`, a footnote symbol's `$^{*}$`; not a number's `$^{1}$`, which it
keeps in the remark), a box or a command's own gap parts are read whole, their text
joined as the source joins them (`lines::printed_join`: a space only where a token no event covers lies between two
pieces), the notes the name's (`lines::remark_pieces_joined`, after `name_and_remark` and `name_takes_annotations`). A
remark after the name's own event is a run of its own, so the name keeps its event and the remark a span of its own, written
from its tokens in its markup as off writes it (`Kalanand Mishra\footnote{…} (for the \babar\ collaboration)`, 0711.1544,
0804.0020; `Ann Able\thanks{…} (for the \textsc{Atlas} Collaboration)`; 1201.5130). A name whose own event opens the remark
joins with it and the in-name split parts them (elsarticle's `Christian Schmidt (for the BNL-Bielefeld\fnref{col1}
Collaboration)`, 1212.4278, 1408.0414): that contact and the name are written from their text, a Warning each (the joined
event's span holds both; off writes no markup there either). A remark after the name's notes or marks naming whom the author
speaks for is one too (webofc's `for CAPP/IBS`, 1702.03664; `speaks_for_after_notes` moved into `classify/collaborations.rs`,
its words `SPEAKS_FOR` shared with the reading's `speaks_for`); and a line under one name speaking for a collaboration is that
name's contact, sourced at the line's ink, so written in its size (`Carolyn Brown$^1$\\ on behalf of the Bcool project team`,
1310.6507; `{\footnotesize for the Hall A DVCS collaboration}`, 1502.03246), where rev94a S6 joined it to the name. A kern
backing up prints no space (`events::whatsit_width_em`): `\babar`'s `B\kern-0.1em{\small A}` is one word "BABAR", read
"B A B A R" before, its words missing from what the emitter wrote; 1706.00234's `\OW` joins its name by layout alone. (A2)
The ink one command draws inside its box, inside a word, is the word's letters: combelow's `\cb{t}` stacks a `t` over a comma
in an alignment, so its comma and row break part no names and `Bogdan Rai\cb{t}\u{a}` is one name (2507.13598; `Andrei
Negu\cb t`, 2301.00703, kept its ț); a comma or a row break a command prints at its own level, after its box, parts what it
ends as any does (`\newcommand\nlx{\mbox{Jr.}\\}`; `lines::words_through_one_command`, in `read_events` and the content check
alike). (N5, the main session's decision K) An unmarked line under a line of one labelled entry goes on with that entry,
whatever its words read as, as the old reader appends it (`$^1$The Graduate Center, CUNY\\ Computer Science\\ New York, USA`,
2501.04046; hep-ph0511130's `Ionosphere and\\ Radio Wave Propagation`); under two or more entries the line after them is
evidence of a names row (SYNC row 46's `Cat Cole`), so cs0011034's `… and $^2$Centre for Computational Linguistics\\
K.U.Leuven` keeps a junk creator, a residual (`Resolver::block`, `labels::later_line_is_names`' `after_labelled`). With
it, an address several names spell is the corresponding author's only where they are one of them, else the block's, as
the old reader holds it (`Resolver::spellers`; `perfect_kernel_batch64::marked_block_email_line_owner`'s `wang@x.org` under
two Wangs, which the old writer, no longer declining the reading's names, wrote on the corresponding Z. Li). The
concession's give-back of a conceded creator's trailing marks (`repart::give_back_ink`) has no live shape after N1-N3: a
marked piece is a name, and today's keeps a per-author class's line one creator; its in-doubt branch, a prefix mark's, stays
guarded (`perfect_kernel_batch94a::a_conceded_creator_keeps_its_marks`).
Off: byte-identical. Guards `perfect_kernel_batchnl1`.

*The fallback raw, and its rules on the reading* (FB2a). With the switch on, Perl's whole-block creator is its raw call
(`fallback::whole_block_author`: `\lx@add@author[keyvals]{written}`, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:693), at the queued entry
(`defs/author_macros.rs`) and the emitter's (`emitter::emit::whole_block`): measured on 1,538 papers, the 13 raw-token
rewrites of OD #52 helped none and hurt three, digestion doing each one's job in a block nothing splits; the queued call's
digestion had fed the reading a symbol mark (2608.19750's "*Corresponding author" glued into an affiliation, now Ayong Ye's
note), and the gap of `\\[0.5cm]` (hep-ph0207056) and `\hspace{.1cm}` (hep-th0111116, 1511.05911) print as written. Four of
those rules, ported: (1) a parameterless macro whose expansion closes the title page's tabular and opens another
(`fallback::tabular_juggle_between`: sig-alternate's `\def\sharedaffiliation{\end{tabular}\begin{tabular}{c}}`) is bound
in the rehearsal to the column it prints (`\lx@fm@obs@and`), or to its row break (`\lx@fm@obs@break`) when one is printed
between (1301.5612's `\end{tabular}\newline\begin{tabular}{c}`; the old driver wrote every juggle `\\`, which TeX does not
set: FB2b5, review revG3 Q3); a macro that only closes one keeps its
meaning, in an author block and an API call's content alike (an `\author`'s `\etab` closing the block's own tabular,
review revFB2a finding 1; an `\affiliation`'s `\def\ex{\end{tabular}}` closing the tabular its `\bx` opened,
`perfect_kernel_batchz4::an_environment_by_its_frames`) — the old driver keeps its looser test, closing alone
(`fallback::closes_a_tabular`), until the flip: digested as defined it left a tabular open, its lines in no box, so the shared affiliation was
lost with no Warning — the content check counts only what the events hold (0712.1016, 1704.03168, 1301.5612); (2) an alignment environment opening after the names at the top
level and ending the block is lines under them, a row Break before it and its container dropped as the old rule drops the
environment (`resolver::trailing_alignment_as_lines` in `read_events`, the old `trailing_alignment_environment_as_lines`:
2609.17357, the "and" of its centred department no separator; a wrapper opening the block was read already, 2609.01563);
(3) a note's text is read in text mode in the rehearsal, as the document digests it (`\lx@fm@obs@note` `mode => text`),
and a note in a formula is written from its own call (`emitter::emit::span_call_tokens`): `$^{2,3}\thanks{The first two
authors contributed equally}$` had lost its spaces (2407.15815, 2603.20851); (4) a URL line under every name of a replacing
block's author list is the block's shared creator (OD #159, `addresses:block`; the old `LinkOwner::Block`, user ruling
2026-10-20, FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 amended 2026-11-05), decided at the block's end, as the old rule's "the names it prints
under are the document's whole author list" (`Resolver::block`'s `block_links`; 2604.20841, 2601.17879, 2604.12896); under
one `\and` column of several it stays the column's; a link printing an institution (`\href{https://www.google.com}{Google}`,
`classify::href_prints_an_institution`, the old rule's `link_prints_an_institution` on the link as printed) is every name's affiliation,
its link kept, as the old rule's exception gives it (review revFB2a finding 3); under one name the URL is that name's, the
group's only author (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4; the old rule's block for a lone replacing author, `line_kinds.rs:61`, is not
ported: off writes that author's too). Two `=2` rules of the reading, no port (FB2b4, FB2b5; review revG3 finding 4: the old
rule never rewrote the inline form, `closes_a_tabular` admitting only a macro taking no argument, and off keeps 1401.6981's one
creator and E=4): (5) the juggle written inline, an `\end{tabular}` closing a tabular the block never opened and reopened
after nothing but spaces and commands with the `[…]`/`{…}` arguments right after them (`rehearsal::inline_juggles_as_columns`, in every
rehearsal; a bare group is no command's, `\end{tabular} {Extra Words} \begin{tabular}` read as written, review revH1
finding 2; what a command between prints, `\mbox{Extra Words}`, goes with the column before, as off orders it — "Extra
Words" a creator and Bob Two lost with 2 Errors before; the writer still writes the column's source, `\end{tabular}` in it,
so those words are lost, counted by the content check), is the column sig-alternate's `\alignauthor` is (sig-alternate.cls:274), or the row break a command between
prints (`\\`, `\\[2mm]`, `\newline`: the break stands, the lines after it the author above's, as the macro's), a skip
(`\vspace{2mm}`) no break — 1401.6981's three columns, three creators, where `=2` had lost authors 2 and 3, and `\\[2mm]`'s
"Univ B" lost with no Warning (review revG3 finding 2); the scan reads what a command reads past spaces as TeX does,
`\\`'s `[…]` (`\@ifnextchar`: latex.ltx `\@normalcr`/`\@xnewline`, `\@tabularcr`/`\@xtabularcr`;
`\\ [2mm]`'s "Univ B" lost with no Warning before, review revH4 finding 1) and a glue or dimen spec written out after
`\hskip`/`\vskip`/`\kern` (tex.web §448-461; `\hskip 1em`, h3e, a column); its `*` only right after it, as the
binding `\lx@fm@obs@break OptionalMatch:*` and Perl's `readMatch` (Gullet.pm:604) read it (`\\ *[2mm]` read past
the space ended a mode it never opened, 1 Error, review revI1 finding 2; now the juggle as written, counted); a
`\vskip` between ends the paragraph, the row break the PDF prints (review revI1 finding 3), where `\vspace` in the
line is latex.ltx `\@vspace`'s `\vadjust`, a column; a `{…}` only right after its command; (6) a column holding no name of its own after the last name
(`Resolver::block`'s `shared_column`: no line in it or a later column reads as names, its first line an institution) is
the shared affiliation of every name above it, whichever spelling opens it — 0712.1016, 1704.03168 (the PDF centres it
under every name; the last author's alone before, off too), `A One \and Bob Two \end{tabular}\begin{tabular}{c} Univ Shared`
("Univ Shared" a third creator before, review revG3 finding 1); a plain `\and` column too (`A One \and Bob Two \and
Department of Physics, University of Y`, a third creator before; `A One \\ Univ A \and Bob Two \\ Univ B \and Institute
for Advanced Study \\ Princeton`, the institute on each name after its own affiliation, where the PDF prints it as a third
column under no name — review revH1 finding 3). A nameless column *between* named columns stays a creator (review revH1
h2h). REDs for the reading (review revH1): a juggle read as written, after a bare group or a tie, keeps `=2`'s old reading, Bob Two an affiliation and "Univ B" lost — counted: the rehearsal
leaves the reopened tabular open, so the content check counts the words of the block's content text its events lack
(FS1's count, `B c tabular Univ`; FB2b6's branch, without it, was silent; guard
`perfect_kernel_batchfs1::an_open_group_rehearsals_words_are_counted`, repro
`author_raw_tabular_juggle_bare_group_between_counted`); a juggle macro printing words between
(`\def\x{\end{tabular}\mbox{W}\begin{tabular}{c}}`) is bound to the column alone, its words unread, counted by the
title page's unclaimed-words Warning. (1), (2), (4), (5) and (6) with the switch on alone, (3) a
fact of the rehearsal (popZ01, 1,873 papers off: 0 changed); off: byte-identical. Guards `perfect_kernel_batchfb2a`.

IO3b (`=2` only): a creator call a document note makes (amsart's `\thanks{Supported by X. \author{Bob Baker}\address{Univ B}
\email{bob@b.org}}`, 0807.4720) is a fact of the note's rehearsal — outside a block the rehearsal binds the queueing sink
`\lx@add@frontmatter` to `\lx@fm@obs@add` (`rehearsal.rs`), which leaves the constructor `\lx@fm@obs@creatorcall` before
calling the sink's own meaning, read by the lexer as `EventKind::ApiCall` "ltx:creator" (`events/mod.rs`). Such a note is
digested as Perl digests it: no flush's reading answers its contacts (`Resolver::api`'s `ltx:pubnote`), its pubnote item is
not wrapped in `\lx@frontmatter@itemonly` (`emitter::emit::emit_commands`), so each contact goes to the creator newest when

e-mail, Ferrero only his own (before: Juriaans none, Ferrero Juriaans's e-mail too); the content check requires the contacts after the
creator call and the note's binding e-mails placed, the note's other text beside (`resolver::api::note_owned_contacts`).

`=2` too). Not covered: the order of creators — a note making Bob, then `\author{Carl}`, gives Ann, Carl, Bob at `=2` where Perl and off give Ann, Bob, Carl (the PDF prints Ann, Carl, Bob; review revH4 4). Guard `perfect_kernel_batchio3b::a_note_making_a_creator_is_digested_as_perls`.

### 981. The flip's no-harm pass: what the emitter declines rather than err or lose, and the few rules shared with the switch off

The flip (`=2` the default, #980) is gated on no harm: no Error and no content at `=2` that the switch off doesn't raise or keep
(user 2026-11-07; for the residual, user 2026-11-09). The no-harm pass compared, paper by paper on the dev sets, Errors (37
papers erred at `=2` only) and **whole-document words** (`kit/emit/docwords.py`; the creators' words alone had missed body
footnotes and whole affiliations). Perl's shape is the fallback throughout: a block the emitter can't write cleanly is
**written whole** (Perl's one creator per `@authorsplits` piece, `Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:691-693`) with a counted Warning.

**Declined (written whole, counted).** A name or contact whose ink crosses an alignment's cells (`repart::joined_across_cells`,
`crosses_columns`, from the digested `Layout{role="cell"}` events; 1304.3138, 1504.01048, 2101.00440 and eleven more erred
"Stray alignment &"); its own digestion moving the footnote counter where no name carries the move (`counter_moved`, the
`\c@footnote` value after each invocation that prints nothing; 1507.05018); a footnote mark held by no name and no item
that steps the counter, a bare `\footnotemark` (`mark_dropped`; 1111.1979) — one given its number (`\footnotemark[n]`,
`\samethanks[n]`: latex.ltx's `\@xfootnotemark`, which steps nothing, `Event::given_number`) moves no later mark, so the names
are written as read and its loss counted by a Warning naming it (1912.01737, 1811.08622, 1911.13299, 2511.12633, 2101.04763;
user 2026-11-09: a decline never throws away a right reading); names one shared macro prints whose run also prints a note or mark (`names_overlap`;
synthetic); a declaration whose span holds a macro reading past it (`declaration_reads_past`, `content::reads_past` with the
whole reach): `\footremember{#1}{#2}` = `\footnote{#2}\newcounter{#1}…` defines after the note it prints, so its span is the
macro alone, and its replay read past the entry (2505.04436, 1511.09009: a Fatal each). The footnote-counter and definition declines write the block as Perl's
`\lx@add@authors` splits it, not whole (#988). A cut holding an alignment's `&`
outside the environment the run holds whole is refused (the item's text, counted; `Field::content_cut`), as is a cut holding
a conditional cut apart (`content::conditional_cut`: `\ifFull and \else \and \fi Joseph A. Simons`, 1409.0597; symmetric — an
`\if…` whose `\fi` is outside the run cuts too, else it stays open to the end of the document, `\iffull Bob Baker\fnm{2}\fi`,
synthetic; a switch's name not executed where it stands, `\newif\iffull`, counts as one, which no meaning tells apart, so
such a run is refused as well; a run is first grown over the `\fi`s right after it that close what it opens, an entry
printed by its last branch, `\ifx\zz\end Q\else X\fi`) and a name's run its balance grew over another name (`emit::event_run_at`: a
`flushleft` the names sit in, 1208.0597). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchne5`, `perfect_kernel_batchne8`. An IJCAI sectioned
block whose class defines `\emails` only inside its `\author` (ijcai19.sty:127, a raw `\@maketitle`) holds a rehearsal Error at
the marker: the reading ends at the first held marker whose section prints an address (an `@` in the events' text;
`resolver::Input::Block::markers`, `blocks::address_section`), the address section the class
split's, its e-mail call written as queued as off writes it (one counted Warning) — the reading had continued `$^4$CENIA
Chile` onto the e-mail line and written the affiliations twice and the addresses as an affiliation (2501.02356). Guard
`perfect_kernel_batchne6::an_ijcai_emails_section_is_the_class_split`. Only a block holding `\affiliations` or `\emails`
is IJCAI-sectioned (`AuthorBlock::sectioned`, `author_macros::ijcai_block`), not every block of a sectioned caller: a plain
`\author` under a raw `\@maketitle` defining its own `\name`/`\email` holds Errors there too, and its reading ended at
`\email`, its address a note (guards `perfect_kernel_batch63::author_markup_title_code_forms`,
`perfect_kernel_batchn1::a_lost_name_spells_its_own_address`; JAIR 1908.02923).

**Carried, not lost.** A note's footnote step in the creator where its name prints, in source order, and past a `\thanks` a mark
follows (`note_steps`; 2505.07115, 1610.06031); labels written back into keys as characters (`key_tokens`, `annotations_key`;
1910.05766, 2607.18332); a text-mode script character the rehearsal erred at, printed with a Warning (`\lx@fm@script@char`,
Perl's recovery `TeX_Math.pool.ltxml:425-428`; 2204.01080); a contact command whose definition reads more required arguments
than the rehearsal's binding keeps its meaning (`binding_required_arguments`; pnastwo's `\affil#1#2`, whose misbinding left a
TeX group open and swallowed 1312.3323's body footnotes); an author block's own `annotations` holding a command carried by its
creators (2308.08363); a call the reading writes nothing of written as queued — never a sequenced list of two or more, whose
order it would break (1901.02012); a taken creator call the reading never recorded written as queued (dmtcs, 1810.10099); a
sub-lettered mark written whole where its pieces go unanswered (`RCreator::whole_marks`; 1705.11109's "50A,50C"); a note's
content taken from its digested text where the first argument is a plain id (`note_argument`; SCITEPRESS `\orcidAuthor`); the
label a class's own `\email` prints kept as the contact's `name` and printed once (`own_email_properties`, `drop_printed_name`;
2603.18265's "Email address for correspondence:"). The rehearsal records the entries a block would have queued
(`AuthorBlock::queued`), so a nested `\date` lost with the block is counted (2503.02741).

**Shared with the switch off (each byte-identical off on the dev witnesses but the one named).** The API: an inner contact that
names nothing takes its enclosing entry's `_name`, as it takes its labels (`frontmatter_api.rs` `\lx@annotate@frontmatter@now`;
Perl's has no name inheritance; 0812.0465's JHEP3 "E-mail:"), and `_nameprinted` marks a `name` the content also prints (no
Perl key). The reading: a glued mark's letter that is also another entry's label stays with the entry printing that sub-entry
(`post.rs` `sub_labels`; 2201.02056's `67a,67c`, which gave 33 authors 48 "Also at" affiliations; 1202.2048's `$^{18a}$` keeps
institute 18 + legend a); the surname-first rule declines where a gap joins the next name to the initials (`next_name_joins`;
cond-mat9905290 off 7 → 6 creators, right by its PDF); "representing " speaks for a collaboration (`SPEAKS_FOR`;
hep-ex9903035); the IJCAI marker is read before the whole-block branch, and a `labelseq=author` entry is `author:N` as Perl's
`CleanLabel` (2202.05511).

**The residual (user 2026-11-09: flip with it as named REDs).** What `=2` still loses against off, per dev paper, with its
witnesses: `docs/parity/FRONTMATTER_CONTENT_RESIDUAL_AT_EMIT2.tsv` — ≈ 0.1 % of dev papers losing three or more words (e-mail
local parts, some affiliations, funding and copyright lines, an abstract inside a revtex3 `\address`), ≈ 0.3 % one or two
label or separator words. Guards: `perfect_kernel_batchne1`, `_batchne2`, `_batchne3`, `_batchcl6`-`_batchcl9`.

*Live rule: OD #981.*

### 982. A block calling a binding's list setter is the emitter's: the setter's call written as it is, its entries the list the marks request (DEL3)

**Perl:** `\author{… \inst{1} … \institute{A \and B}}` digests its block whole at the call; the binding's `\institute`
(sv_support.sty.ltxml:40-42, inst_support.sty.ltxml:36-38, aa.cls, llncs.cls) clears the affiliations and queues its
pieces `labelseq=affiliation`, numbered for the `\inst` marks. **Was (CL2b, `=2`):** the emitter stayed out of any paper
with such a block (`LIST_SETTER_IN_BLOCK`), each block written whole and the S2b writer (`write_observed_frontmatter`)
comparing it with the reading — its last `=2` path. **Now:** the emitter reads the block as any other
(`emitter/emit.rs` `stays_out` has no list-setter decline). For each written block whose ledger records a list setter
(`AuthorBlock::list_setter`, the binding's definition holding `\lx@clear@frontmatter`): (1) the rehearsal's Contact of
each call that reads it whole (`\lx@fm@obs@affil`, its span opening with the setter's command) is the call
(`list_setter_runs`); its items and everything inside it leave the reading (`without_list_setters`), and its balanced
tokens (`list_setter_call`, `span_tokens_of`) are written after the flush's items, as the whole block digests it after
the names' own contacts — the binding's digestion numbers or labels its entries; (2) a call the reading cut into the
entries its marks label (`\institute{${}^1$Univ X\\ ${}^2$Univ Y}`) stays the reading's items; (3) either way the names
keep the marks they print, as any block's (`per_author_marks`: 2502.07804's hand-typed `${}^{1}$`, which pdflatex, off
and Perl print — review revDEL3 B1), an `\inst` printing nothing and requesting its entry; (4) the marks net skips a
block whose call is written (the reading holds none of its entries); the insertion's orphan Warning still counts a
request no entry answers; (5) the call written is the flush's last, and it replaces what its clear
(`\lx@clear@frontmatter{ltx:contact}[role=affiliation]`) would at the block (the block's list is the one `\maketitle` prints — the last list set before it; a top-level `\institute` *after* the block is NOT yet cleared, revDEL3b R1, RED below): an
affiliation call queued before the block and an earlier call of the block leave the reading (`replaced_by_setter`) and
the content check (`Ledger::replaced`) — digested inside the flush, the call's own clear meets an empty queue
(`place::digest_front_matter` takes the queue first; review revDEL3 S1). The S2b writer no longer ran at
`=2` (the flush emitted); DEL4 deleted it (#837 "Deleted (DEL4)"). Witnesses: cond-mat0605195 (svjour, the setter in the last `\and` piece's group: the four
creators and their institutes byte-identical to the writer's output, the stay-out Warning gone), 2502.07804 (svjour,
marked lines after comma-parted names: creators equal; the ORCID links are written as the emitter writes every `=2`
`\href` item, `ltx_href` with the paper's icon, where the whole block's `\lx@author@href` made OD #960's `ltx_orcid`).
Population: 2 papers of 73,251 A/B-population papers (a source scan for `\institute` inside `\author`, 252 candidates
converted; llncs's top-level one is taken out by `take_institutes`, eptcs's is no list setter). Repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/list_setter_in_block_{sv_inst,sv_marked,llncs,aa,inst_support,sv_marked_typed,sv_earlier_institute,sv_two_calls}.tex`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batchdel3` (one per binding's setter definition; for (3) and (5)
`batchdel3_typed_marks_stay_on_the_names_of_a_written_setter_call`, `batchdel3_a_written_setter_call_replaces_a_list_before_the_block`,
`batchdel3_the_last_setter_call_of_a_block_is_written`); `perfect_kernel_batchcl2::a_list_setter_in_an_author_block_is_read_by_the_emitter`.

*Live rule: OD #980.*

### 984. The emitter keeps only an affiliation entry's own text, and the Link step places every inner e-mail of it (Z18c: llncs's old split's rules, in the emitter)

**Perl:** an affiliation's content is digested whole (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:742-753); an `\email` inside it is an
annotation of its own, the separators and labels around it stay in the affiliation's box, and only the first annotation
digested inside an entry inherits the entry's label (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:497-501 reads the last stub alone), so a
second `\email` annotates the last author. **Was:** llncs's unmarked lists went through the binding's own split
(`\lx@llncs@author`) and the shared row (`shared_row::row_email_calls`, #901), which took each e-mail unit out with its
separators and label; every entry the emitter writes from an API call (llncs under `\inst` marks, svjour3, aa) kept them —
`\institute{Univ X\\ \email{p1@x.edu}, \email{p2@x.edu}}` under `\inst{1}` gave "Univ X ," on both authors (Z18b's 15
llncs papers), `…; Email: ;`, `Unity Technologies Corresponding author:`, svjour3's "Univ B " — and its e-mail calls
after the first stayed on the last author as their own call (`owner:call`): three addresses under three names gave the
third author two. **Now:** (1) an affiliation-kind entry the emitter writes from an API call
(`emitter::emit::item_call`) is written by `entry_email_cut` (`classify/entry_emails.rs` since P27b), which cuts by the row's own unit cut, one copy
both callers shared (`row_email_calls` and it: `unit_cut`, `UnitCut::labelled_address`, the reassembly `kept_without`,
the call reader `read_call`; Z18d, review revZ18c S1): each class e-mail call takes the separators before it back to the text or call before it, the e-mail label naming it
(`Email:`, its contact's name) and a label of its own (`call_label`: `Corresponding author:`, `(Corresponding author)`,
in its text); a line break stays where text the entry keeps follows (2310.01324's `\url` line); an entry whose inner
contacts are items of their own (`\lx@frontmatter@itemonly`) loses the calls only, a label staying its text
(2606.02634's `Correspondence:`). (2) Each call after the first that reads as whole addresses (`read_call`: one address in printed braces
too, `\email{\{b2@x.edu\}}`, which had stayed on the last author, revZ18c S2) is written by the entry's
label (`\lx@row@email`), so the Link step's chain (`insert::link_entry_addresses`, #956) places it among the entry's
carriers; a template or an unread list stays as written. (3) The chain (`entry_address_owners`) gains the row's two
facts (`EntryOwnerFacts`): no order where an address spells several names, none the carrier at its place (`x1@, x2@,
lee@` under Ann Lee, Bob Lee, Cid Cole: the block's; 2102.08148's `jtchen721@` at Jintai Chen's place beside Danny Z. Chen
stays his), and the one address left of several carriers the corresponding author's, never a template's (2408.14427).
(4) An entry whose inner e-mail the reading wrote out whole (`ruling3:written-out`, every address the call prints read)
keeps no copy of the call (2607.09128's `$\{$npcarpenter\,|\,giacobazzi$\}@$arizona.edu`; one written out in part keeps
it, 2410.20769). (5) One address in printed braces is that address to the Link step (2410.04091's
`\email{\{fatima.iribu@gmail.com\}}`, on every carrier before); a tie parts addresses (`;~cms@`, 1701.08125); an address
of a plain list is written without the list's trailing separators (1908.05750) and with no Warning, nothing but its text
printed (2501.11774), unless the text written holds a control sequence's name or a tie (`\email{\{a, b\}@x\footnote{…}}` writes
`a@x\lx@fm@obs@fnnote`: each address counted "markup lost", revZ18c S3; 2008.05861's `…hk~~`, uncounted before), never for
an address merely not well-formed (`\{a,b\}@x\_y.org` prints `a@x_y.org`, all it is: review revZ18d finding 1); an address line ending an entry takes the separator the line before it ends in (`address_cuts`:
2407.18381's `(EPFL), \\ \texttt{…}`). **Not moved here** (the reroute's own, kept with it): the `\\` line rules of a whole
llncs list (a names line after an affiliation line, a line after an inline `\and`, a name carrying an ORCID). **Residuals:**
separators after an entry's last call
stay (`Naples, Italy,`, 2605.21246, 2210.09234, 1408.0510, as in the old split); a later template call stays on the

above a names line 612 identical (2505.20009 killed on both sides, 2503.14381 not compared); the 1,434 stage2 ids 30 changed, all read: 23 a trailing space or break out of an affiliation, 3 separators, 3 a duplicate placed once, 2009.10916's libraboli@ the block's once; 0 words lost; cost ≤ +0.42 % per document. ### 987. IEEEtran's author blocks under authblk's `\author` are read as the class reads them, added after the authors before; a nested names block spliced in, a stop after an italic grade closing the names (CR6, CR10a, CR10c)

**What.** ieeetran_cls.rs `\lx@IEEE@authblk@author` (authblk's `\author` once IEEEtran's binding hooks authblk's load,
#950). A body holding `\IEEEauthorblockN` (`\author{\IEEEauthorblockN{Ann Able,~\IEEEmembership{Member,~IEEE}, Bob Baker
and Cy Coe}\thanks{…}}`) went to authblk's one creator call, inside which the binding's `\IEEEauthorblockN`
(`\lx@add@authors@append`) is a nested author call that printed nothing in the rehearsal: the creator was dropped, every
author lost with 0 Warnings. Now such a body is read as the class's own `\author` reads it (`printed_refmarks`,
`author_block_body`: the grid transposed, bare trailing text wrapped, each name's grade its `membership` contact), run in
a group with `\and` empty (`\lx@IEEE@authblk@blocks`) — without the class's `\lx@IEEE@author@begin`/`@end`, so its
authors are added after those before them as authblk adds every `\author`'s (authblk.sty:114-145), where the class's own
`\author` replaces them — then authblk's bookkeeping (`\lx@AB@author@state`, `\lx@author@after`). A labelled call gives
each block's names its label (`\lx@IEEE@authorblockN@labelled` → `\lx@add@authors@append[annotations={label}]`), as
authblk's `\author[1]{Ann Able, Bob Baker}`, so `\affil[label]` reaches them.

**Why.** pdflatex prints every name (IEEEtran.cls's `\IEEEauthorblockN` under authblk's `\author`). Perl:
`\IEEEauthorblockN` is `#1` (IEEEtran.cls.ltxml:144) and authblk's unlabelled `\author` without `\and` one
`\lx@add@creator` (authblk.sty.ltxml:55), so it keeps the names as one creator, no grade (IEEEtran.cls.ltxml:143).

**Witnesses** (int154u → CR6): 2402.16140, 1611.02001, 1810.08035, 2409.09417 (0 creators → 3, 4, 3, 3, the grades as
membership contacts), 1708.05281 (one nameless creator holding every line, 4 Warnings → 6 authors, each with its marked
affiliation and e-mail, 0 frontmatter Warnings). 2602.05517 (no authblk) and 1,434 stage2 papers byte-identical.

**CR10a (both paths, `author_block_body`; `without_stop_after_grade`).** A names block written inside another's names
(`\author{\authorblockN{\authorblockN{Ann Able, \IEEEmembership{…}, Bob Baker \\ and Cy Coe, \IEEEmembership{…}.} \\
\thanks{…}}}`, 1511.03982) was the same nested author call inside the outer's argument: every author lost, 0 Warnings.
`unnested_name_blocks` splices each inner block's argument into the outer one (its command and braces dropped), which
is then read as any block; pdflatex prints each name (a names block only sets its style), Perl keeps them in one
creator. The old alias `\authorblockN`'s name lines have their grades read as `\IEEEauthorblockN`'s
(through CR10c's `with_block_names`; since P5a the grade is the reading's, OD #1016). The full stop after a grade written as italic text (`{\em Member, IEEE}.`,
`\emph{…}.`, `\textit{…}.`; `grade_text`, the names reader's `grade_words(…, true)`) closes the names as one after
`\IEEEmembership{…}` does: the line after a `\\` that ends so (`\IEEEauthorblockN{…, Hesham ElSawy, {\em Senior Member,
IEEE},\\ Mohamed-Slim Alouini, {\em Fellow, IEEE}, and Tareq Y. Al-Naffouri, {\em Senior Member, IEEE}.}`, 1810.08035)
was read as the first names' affiliation (0 Warnings), and a one-line block so ended cut its grade into a membership
"Fellow" and an affiliation "IEEE." (2 Warnings). A stop after an italic non-grade (`{\em Zebra University}.`) stays.
Witnesses (int154q → CR10a): 1511.03982 0 creators → 3 with their grades, 1810.08035 3 creators → 5. Repros
`class-bindings/ieeetran_nested_blockn_names`, `class-bindings/ieeetran_blockn_italic_grade_stop`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batchcr10a::{nested_names_block_keeps_every_author, italic_grade_before_stop_ends_the_names}`.
**Left:** a plain-text grade before the stop (`…, and Dee Dale, Member, IEEE.}` after a `\\`) still reads the line as
an affiliation, 0 Warnings (words kept); the content check flags a repeated italic grade (`{\em Senior Member, IEEE}`
twice) as 3 missing words though both are kept (pre-existing, base the same).

Repros `class-bindings/ieeetran_authblk_blockn_names`, `class-bindings/ieeetran_authblk_blockn_calls_accumulate`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batchcr6::{authblk_author_reads_ieee_author_blocks, authblk_author_blocks_accumulate_and_take_labels}`.

**CR10c (`author_block_body`).** The old block names `\authorblockN`/`\authorblockA` (the binding's `\let`s of
`\IEEEauthorblockN`/`\IEEEauthorblockA`) are rewritten to those, once, before any step reads the body, and only while
they still mean them (`with_block_names`, `defined_as`, as `printed_refmarks` treats `\authorrefmark`; since P2-8a any
`\let` copy of either, and before the route too, #995's P2-8a paragraph); each step reads the one name. Read by name in four of the steps and not in the labelled path, `\author[2]{\authorblockN{Cy Coe,
Dee Dale}}` with `\affil[2]{Univ Z}` left Univ Z a nameless creator's, the names without it, 0 Warnings (review
revCR67, CR6 S1). An outer names block holding its own `\IEEEauthorblockA` before an inner names block is one left
unclosed, not a wrapper (`\IEEEauthorblockN{Arslan Shaukat\\ \IEEEauthorblockA{…}\\ \IEEEauthorblockN{Umer Asgher}
\IEEEauthorblockA{…} }`, 2605.20445): it is closed before that affiliation block and the rest read at the top level,
the stacked blocks pdflatex prints (`affiliation_before_names`); spliced in (CR10a), the next author's name and lines
were the first author's. A wrapper whose argument holds no affiliation block before an inner names block is still
spliced (1511.03982). `grade_text` is the names reader's own `grade_words(…, true)` of the printed letters (exported
from `classify`), no second table. Witnesses (int154o → CR10c): 2605.20445 a nameless creator holding Umer Asgher's
e-mail and "Umer Asgher" an affiliation, 2 Warnings → four named authors, each with the affiliation and e-mail under
the name, in the PDF's reading order (#128), 0 Warnings; the other 3,368 of CR10a's 3,369 ids byte-identical
(2505.20009 killed on both sides), the `\authorblockN` papers (1112.5995, 1312.2338, 1511.03982) among them.
Repros `class-bindings/ieeetran_unclosed_names_block_before_affiliation`,
`class-bindings/ieeetran_authblk_labelled_old_block_name`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batchcr10c::{unclosed_names_block_closes_before_its_affiliation, old_block_name_takes_the_label}`.
**Known REDs (revCR10c, synthetic only, no corpus witness):** a document that `\def`s (or `\renewcommand`s) the old
name to the new one (`\def\authorblockN#1{\IEEEauthorblockN{#1}}`) fails `defined_as`, so its blocks' grades are not
read: 1 Warning (`unclaimed … member ieee fellow`), int154o read them
(`class-bindings/ieeetran_def_old_block_name_loses_grades`); an unclosed names block wrapped in another names block is
still spliced, the hoist one level deep (the inner branch skips `affiliation_before_names`): 1 creator holding the
second author and affiliation, 0 Warnings, pre-existing (`class-bindings/ieeetran_wrapped_unclosed_names_block`).
