### 988. The footnote-counter and definition declines write the block as Perl's `\lx@add@authors` does, split where Perl splits it (CR7)

**Defect.** The emitter's `counter_moved` and `declaration_reads_past` declines (#981) wrote the block with
`whole_block_author`, one `\lx@add@author` of it: Perl's **tabular** branch only (`Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:691-693`). Perl
splits a block holding no `{tabular}`, `{minipage}` or `\halign` (:694-719), so the Warning's "as Perl's whole-block creator"
was false and the authors merged into one creator: the definition decline 6 of 6 papers (0809.5152 5→1, 1110.6375 11→1,
1404.5602 4→1, 2404.18592 2→1, 2503.21719 3→1, 0906.2789), the counter decline 13 of 17 (1003.2281 6→1, cs0404029 6→1,
2410.22720 4→1, 1305.0854, 1510.04579, 1609.02993, 1609.03951, 2004.03371, 2007.01340, 2605.00602, 1210.5741, 1302.3028).

**Fix.** Those two declines write `fallback::perl_author_calls` of the block: Perl's three branches
(`perl_author_branch`), the dequeue the emitter's own. Tabular: `whole_block_author` as before. Marks
(`positionOf($stuff, T_SUPER, \textsuperscript)`): lines cut, a names line cut at its commas into
`\lx@add@author{\lx@author@withsup{…}}`, a line led by a mark (position < 8) `\lx@add@affiliation{\lx@affiliation@withsup{…}}`,
a line of no mark continuing the entry before it. Otherwise: pieces cut at `\and`/`\And`/`\AND`/`\quad`/`\qquad`, each an
author whose `\\` lines are `\lx@add@affiliation`s. The pieces are digested in order, so the footnote counter and a
definition step as TeX steps them. A tabular juggle (`\alignauthor`) parts two authors there, as `\and` (Perl's OmniBus makes it
empty). The Warning names the branch taken ("the block is written as Perl's \lx@add@authors splits it at its separators, its
pieces digested in order"). The block's creators take their Perl labels (`author:N`, `perl_block_pieces`), so a later
block's items address their own. Each name the reading read takes the label of the creator whose names hold it, matched by
name, not by count (`perl_piece_of`: most of its words of two or more letters, accents folded, each found whole among the
words of the piece's names line, its notes' arguments aside (`outside_notes`, `visible_name_text`), at least half, the names
in order, a name after the first searched from the second creator on), so an item the reading gave the names goes to each (a revtex `\affiliation` after `\author{Ann\footremember{…}{…}
and Bob}`). Equal counts need not be the same names: `Robert Heath, Jr.… and Ann Able~~~~Bob Baker` is Perl's "Robert
Heath", "Jr.", "Ann Able~~~~Bob Baker" and the reading's "Robert Heath, Jr.", "Ann Able", "Bob Baker"; matched by count, Ann's
`\affiliation` went to "Jr." (review revCR67 S4). Matched inside glued letters, "li" of `J. K. Li` was found in `Ann
Blinn\footremember{zz}{Visiting Paris.}` and Ann took Li's e-mail (review revS5CR7b S1: the two-letter surnames Li, Wu, Xu,
Ma, Yu). A name no piece after the first holds (one a macro spells) goes to the first creator, as the block written whole
did. An item a printed mark labels (an API call's leading mark, `api:leading-mark`, or a `_withsup` line's) goes to each
creator whose piece prints that mark, never to the one the reading's names gave it, and to the block's own creator where
none does: what the block prints after each name up to the next — a mark's labels, or a contact's whole text — is its
piece's (`piece_marks`, `printed_mark_labels`). cicp's `Lixiu Dong\affil{1}, Cheng Wang\affil{3}, …` (`\affil{n}` =
`${}^{n}$`, read as the in-block affiliation "n", so no name requests a mark) under `\address{\affilnum{1}…\\\affilnum{2}…
\\\affilnum{3}…}` gave every address to the reading's owner of the call, the last name: 2004.03371 and 2410.22720 stated
false affiliations, and 1510.04579's one address reached one of its three authors (review revS5CR7b B1). The creator the
reading's corresponding author maps to carries `_corresponding` (`perl_block`), so the Link step's one left-over address of
an entry still goes to that author (#984; review revS5CR7b S5-1). As Perl's `next unless $block->unlist` (:714), an empty
name between two cuts (`\corrauth, and Zhengru Zhang`) makes no creator. The other declines (`names_fail`, cells, `mark_dropped`,
`names_overlap`, the unread block) still write it whole.

**Divergences from Perl's split** (the kernel's own lists, #52): Perl's comma and " and " cut only a names line, never a
`\\` line under it. Perl's `@authorsplits` cut 1302.3028's PoS `\\ Department of Physics, College of Science, Swansea
University, …` into four authors, and its `@authoraffilsplits` " and " cut 1110.6375's `D. Schmidiger,\\ E. Wulf, S. Zhao
and A. Zheludev$^\dag$`. The marks branch's line cuts are `author_affil_splits` (no " and ", `\newline` added; 2605.00347),
its names lines cut at the comma and " and ". A line of no mark cut at a line break (`\\`, `\newline`) or a `\quad` continues
the entry before it and keeps that cut, which Perl's `Tokens(…)` drops: 1609.02993's "Soumith ChintalaFacebook AI Research"
and 1110.6375's "G. EhlersOak Ridge" lost their words glued. One cut at the `\and` family (`\and`, `\And`, `\AND`,
`\alignauthor`) starts an author, the kernel's boundary (#52(g), `author_and_splits`): `Ann Able$^{1}$… \and Bob Baker\\
$^{1}$Univ X` is two authors, as pdflatex prints them, where Perl glues one "Ann AbleBob Baker"; that line is a names
line, cut at its commas as one is (`\and Bob Baker, Carl Cole\\` two authors, review revS5CR7b S3). Both split branches drop a
`\\[len]`'s and a `\\*`'s option before their cuts (`strip_linebreak_options`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #75; Perl's own comment,
:670): 2007.01340's creator read "[1em] Julia Fukuyama", Perl alike. `position_of` and
`literal_and` moved from `author_block/` to `frontmatter/classify/separators.rs` (Perl's `positionOf`, `$literaland`).

**Fail-safe (review revCR7c B1, B2, S1).** Before the split is used, `emit::split_owns_falsely` checks that it states no
owner its marks don't support; where it does, the block is written whole (`whole_block_author`, as before CR7) and the
decline's Warning says "the block is written whole, as Perl's whole-block creator". Each call's tokens as cut
(`PerlCalls::cut`, a subsequence of the block's) are found in the block in order, and each digested event belongs to the
creator whose call holds its first token. A creator's piece fails where (i) an item in it — a note, or a line under its
names — leads with a printed mark (a note's text's first mark; a mark, or an in-block affiliation's label, that is its
line's first ink after the piece's first) that the piece prints on none of its names, or (ii) it is not the first and its
first ink is a mark (an address line made a creator). Perl's comma cut gave 1110.6375's `T. Yankova$^\ast$,\thanks{$^\ast$Permanent
address: …} D. H\"uvonen` note to Hüvonen, whose name prints no ∗ (Perl alike: a false affiliation); a `\\ \affil{2} Univ
Y` line under `… and Carl Cole\affil{1}` went to Carl, each `\\` line being its piece's last name's (:713-719; Perl alike);
0809.5152's `\\\vspace{6pt} \vspace{3pt} $^{a}${\em{Istituto …}}`, its mark past position 8, read as a names line whose
`\lx@author@withsup` made the address a creator with its mark moved after the text — Perl keeps both address lines inside
the last creator's name, after a `<break/>`, and makes no address creator. Of the 23 decline papers, 0809.5152 and
1110.6375 are written whole, byte-identical to the base, and 2503.21719 by (iii); the other 20 are unchanged by them.
Since GRP1 (2026-11-13) the Taylor & Francis blocks no longer decline: their `\received` declaration, replayed as far as
its call read, does not read past the block, so 0809.5152 gives 5 creators and 1110.6375 11, each with its marked
affiliation, and 0906.2789 the same creators; the date is the source's, which the PDF prints (cJAS2e.cls:459-463 sets
`\@author` before `\@received`), not the class default the decline's whole block printed (0906.2789's `{\em …}`
affiliation loses its italic, uncounted: post-merge).
(iii) A creator the reading made of the block whose name no creator's names hold (`emit::split_loses_a_name`,
`perl_piece_of` of its words in `perl_names_words`, read only for a block a decline writes as Perl's split; PB) — the reading's
creators, not its Name events, which hold comma pieces the resolver reads as an affiliation ("Dept of Physics"): 1511.09009's aaai `Yi Zhang\footremember{yi} \\, Yanghua Xiao\footremember{yh} \\, Seung-won Hwang…`, each `\\`
the macro's second argument so pdflatex prints one line of four names, is cut at the first `\\` (the kernel cuts only a
names line at its commas, #52), and `\footremember` then took each `\lx@add@affiliation` as its argument: "Seung-won
Hwang, Wei Wang" were lost (counted by a Warning, 5 words) and ‡ and § printed †. Written whole, all four names and
marks are kept, as before CR7. Perl's own comma cut makes 14 creators (5 Errors) there; following it would undo #52, so the
fail-safe stands. A piece of the split printing no word is the name a macro spells (`\cat$^{1}$` of
`\newcommand{\cat}{Cat Cole}`): `perl_piece_of` gives that name the first such piece, so it is no loss and its marks are
its creator's (`piece_marks`; PBb, review revPB S1: PB wrote that block whole). **Known weakness (revPBb S1, no failing
probe):** the wordless-piece fallback never uses a piece up — `split_loses_a_name` searches each name from piece 0 and
`piece_marks` restarts at the previous piece — so two macro-spelled names in a row take the same piece (the second
one's marks the first one's; revPBb `p1_two_macro_names` still converts right), and one wordless piece could hide a
name the split really loses (revPBb `p6`/`p7` still fire); the fix is to take each wordless piece once, in order.
Repros `pb_split_loses_name`,
`pbb_macro_spelled_name`; guards `perfect_kernel_batchpb::{a_split_losing_a_name_keeps_the_block_whole,
a_name_a_macro_spells_is_no_lost_name}`.

**Left (Perl's own, kept):** a line of no mark continues the entry before it, so a second group of names after an
affiliation line joins the creator before it. Every `\\` line of a split piece after its first is
an affiliation of its last name (:713-719), so 2503.21719's `…Lourens Waldorp\footrecall{uva}, \\Quentin F.
Gronau\footremember{uon}{University of Newcastle, Australia}, and Eric-Jan Wagenmakers\footrecall{uva}` would be an
affiliation of Waldorp: the line reads as names only with the document's `\footremember` arguments set aside, which no
token reading of the kernel can tell from text (`is_note_macro` declines a macro an argument of which `\newcounter`
takes). (iii) now writes that block whole: 3 → 1 creators, holding all five names of the PDF with every note, 0 words
lost, where the base (int155a0) made Gronau and Wagenmakers Waldorp's affiliation.

**Known REDs of the fail-safe (review revCR7d, synthetic, Perl the same; the base wrote each whole):** (S1) a later piece that starts with a note, not a mark — `\author{Ann Able,\thanks{Permanent address: Univ Z.} Bob Baker…, Carl Cole}` — gives the note to Bob: the check catches a mark-led piece, not a note-led one; (S2) an address line whose mark comes after its text (`{\it Dept. of Physics, Univ X}$^{a}$`) still becomes an author creator. (S3, no false owner) the check reads Perl's raw split, not the routed result, so a few shapes CR7c already routed right fall back whole (`\and Bob Baker\affil{b}\\ \affil{a} Univ X…`, a mark printed only in a note). 1110.6375 is now written whole (the fail-safe), so it no longer witnesses the split's behaviour above. Probes: `/home/deyan/data/pk_wt/scratch_revCR7d/probe/p1..p6.tex`.

**A definition the block can't replay (FNR1).** `emit::declaration_reads_past` declines a block in two cases. (1) A
declaration holds a macro whose undelimited arguments run past it (`content::reads_past`): a macro printing a note then
defining, `\newcommand{\footremember}[2]{\footnote{#2}\newcounter{#1}…}`, defines past the note its arguments made, so
replayed it read the next declaration's tokens and on past the entry — `\footremember\footremember…`, its
`\newcounter{\footremember}` a counter of no name, every theorem then missing its `{` and a Fatal (2505.04436,
1511.09009). (2) A definition whose call prints too: the rehearsal drops it from the replayable declarations (a replay
would print it twice), so where the reading writes the call apart — a note, a contact, a mark the names request — it took
no effect, and a spaced `\footnoteremember{uni}{…}` (` \footnote{#2} \newcounter{#1} \setcounter{#1}{\value{footnote}} `)
left the later authors' `\footnoterecall{uni}` an undefined counter (2407.13730, 2606.19583: one mark dropped, one empty).
Such a call is kept (`field_notes::PrintingCall`, `ledger::Unsaid::printing`) with the definees the block introduces
(undefined once the rehearsal is undone: a class's state a paper's call sets, PoS's `\global\@speakertrue` 1009.6192,
manyfoot's `\@thefnmark` 2511.01971, is the class's to read) and whether they are global; one local to a group of its call
is not (`\begingroup\def\thefootnote{}\footnote{…}\endgroup`: 2602.15181, 0903.4816, 2311.17684). The block declines only
where no name's run holds the call (`emit::unwritten`, shared with `counter_moved`), it prints a note, a contact or a mark
there, and a later token of the block reads a definee (`emit::printing_read_later`, `content::reads_definition`): its
control sequence, or a counter's name as an argument (`\footnoterecall{uni}`, `\value{uni}`), in the tokens or one level
into a document's macro they call. A local definition is read only up to the next top-level `\and`, which ends the
author's tabular cell (latex.ltx `\and`). A definition nobody reads keeps the replay: the common `\footremember` template
with no recall (2209.10798, 2604.20516; review revFNR1 u01-u03). Where the decline would write the block whole (the CR7d
fail-safe, `split_owns_falsely`) and only a printing call drives it, the replay is kept too. Written as Perl splits it, a
declined block's notes are digested from their tokens, so no plain-text Warning is due there; its decline Warning counts
it. A call printing a name is written with it (`\blockN{Bob Baker}`'s `\gdef`, `emit_a_declaration_keeps_its_calls_argument`).
Left (REDs): a re-assigned meaning a later author reads (`author_note_macro_resets_an_existing_counter_red`); under a
class with no binding the title's notes step no counter (`omnibus_title_footnotemark_prints_fnsymbol_red`, so 2407.13730's
recalls print "0"); the rehearsal reads the block in no cell group, so a local definition read past its `\and` moves the
call's argument into the next name (`author_note_macro_local_def_read_past_its_cell_red`); the replay writes such a note
as plain text, its markup lost and counted (`footremember_note_markup_written_as_plain_text_red`, 2604.20516). Repros
`footnoterecall_three_authors_spaced_remember`, `footnoterecall_two_authors_control`,
`author_note_macro_defines_what_a_later_author_reads`, `author_mark_macro_defines_what_a_later_author_reads`,
`author_mark_macro_steps_a_counter_on_each_name`, `author_note_macro_with_a_local_thefootnote`,
`footremember_unread_keeps_the_replay`, `footremember_unread_on_a_marked_names_line`, `footremember_unread_after_a_comma`,
`author_note_macro_local_def_ends_with_its_cell`, `footrecall_read_where_the_split_would_be_whole`,
`footnoterecall_held_in_a_document_macro`; guard
`perfect_kernel_batchcr7::a_definition_its_call_prints_takes_effect_in_order`.

Repros `cr7_fncounter_and`, `cr7_ne5_footremember`, `cr7_marks_branch_footremember`, `cr7_split_lines_keep_commas`,
`cr7_split_items_to_each_name`, `cr7b_linebreak_option_cut`, `cr7b_and_cut_starts_author`, `cr7b_split_items_by_name`,
`cr7c_split_names_whole_words`, `cr7c_and_line_comma_cut`, `cr7c_split_corresponding_left_address`,
`cr7d_split_affil_line_false_owner`, `cr7d_split_note_mark_false_owner`, `cr7d_split_address_line_as_author`;
guards `perfect_kernel_batchcr7::{a_counter_decline_writes_the_block_as_perl_splits_it,

a_split_keeps_the_commas_of_its_lines, a_split_gives_each_name_its_items,
a_split_at_a_linebreak_option_leaves_no_option_text, a_line_of_no_mark_cut_at_and_starts_an_author,
a_split_gives_each_name_its_items_by_name, a_split_matches_names_by_whole_words,

### 991. eptcs's author block and OmniBus's `\authors` list go whole to the reading; an e-mail list reads as it prints (Z18k, Z18k2, Z18k3)

**Perl.** Perl has no eptcs binding (the class is read raw through OmniBus) and OmniBus's `\authors{}` prints nothing
(`OmniBus.cls.ltxml:74`, `DefMacro('\authors{}', Tokens())`).

**Was.** Both bindings split their lists with `author_block`'s token reader: OmniBus's `\authors` called
`split_author_line` and wrote one `\lx@add@author` per piece, so `\affil{1,2}` became the affiliation text "1,2" and a
numbered `\affiliation{n}{…}` landed on a nameless creator (2003.03010, 2103.05990, 2209.10103, 2512.09915's
`\affil{7,8}`); eptcs's binding split each `\and` cell into names and placed its `\email` lines itself
(`row_email_owners`), merging a row of boxed names (1210.2456's "Sabine Broda Nelma Moreira").

**Now.** (1) OmniBus's `\authors{list}` is `\lx@add@author@split{list}` (as llncs's unmarked `\author`, #984), each
`\affil{…}` of numbers rewritten `\inst{…}`, the request of those numbered affiliations (omnibus_cls.rs
`numbered_affil_marks`); another `\affil{text}` stays an affiliation. (2) eptcs's block is written as the class prints
it (eptcs.cls v1.5-v1.7: the author `tabular` :170-174, `\institute` :188-190, `\email` :191): each `\and` cell a column, its `\institute{…}` and `\email{…}` `\\` lines under its names,
the whole list to `\lx@add@author@split`; a line under a whole `tabular` of names is a
`labelseq={affiliation},_share={authors}` entry (1407.7928). (3) The reading's e-mail text (`events::raw_lines`) is the
argument as it prints where a box's source would glue or add words: a box printing only spacing is a space, not its
source (`\email{a@x \qquad b@y}`: Z18k's WIP reroute had read the address `\qquadb@y` and the word "qquad"; 1101.4424
reads as the base did, W 46 → 45); every inkless whatsit that is no formula and no note — a skip, a `\label`, an
`\includegraphics`, a phantom — is a space; a box, no script or mark, whose ink holds an `@` is its ink
(`\makebox[0cm][c]{a@x}\hspace{40mm}…`: 1210.2456; `\mbox{able@x.org, baker@x.org}`, `\mbox{E-mail: able@x.org}`,
which had written a note "mbox" or the box's source, review revZ18k R1). Any other box stays as written (settled
dead-end: every whatsit read as its ink — a mark `\textsuperscript{\Letter}` glued to its address, 2410.20769, and the
braces of `{jsliwinski,wattenhofer}@ethz.ch` were lost, 2206.10050; 1905.00862 and 2403.11192 changed too; all four
stay byte-identical to the base under the `@` rule). (4) The emitter writes one address of a block's e-mail list
in the font the class's e-mail command sets it (`calls::email_command_address`: eptcs's `{\footnotesize\tt #1}`), and one
address of an API call's list without the spacing its printed run opens with (`emit::one_address`: llncs's
`\email{a@x \quad b@y}`, 2310.01324, which had written `\quadb@y` as text and each address twice). (5) The token split
these bindings were the last to reach is deleted: `split_author_line`'s closure (`names_split.rs`, `separators.rs`,
`name_text.rs`) and `row_emails.rs`, `author_block/` 3,364 → 2,552 lines. (6) In the reading's names line
(`resolver/lines.rs` `names_line_events`) a bracketed piece after a separator (a comma, "and") that carries its own mark is
a name of its own, marks win (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 R1): OmniBus's `Y. Dong\affil{6}, \add[ver3]{S. Curry}\affil{1}`
(2308.02720, trackchanges' `\add` undefined, printing "[ver3]S. Curry") and llncs's `Bob Baker\inst{2}, [v3]{Cy
Cole}\inst{1}` had joined the two as one creator holding both affiliations, silently (review revZ18k B1; the llncs path
on the base too). A remark with no mark of its own, a qualifier and a collaboration spoken for still join. A join of two
pieces each carrying its own mark that any rule still makes (`Bob Baker\inst{2}, Jr.\inst{1}`) is the safety net's
counted Warning (`net::merged_names`: "a separator its author block prints between names parts no creators").

**Decided by the charter.** 2402.13328 (`\authors{Igor Shevchenko and Dan Crisan}`, no marks, `\affiliation{1}{…}`
`\affiliation{2}{…}`): the numbered entries stay at the block as written (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1195);
the base had paired them by position.

**Residual.** 2304.02524's `\email{$^{a, b}$ \{…\}@quantinuum.com, $^{c}$ john@…}`: each address now goes to its marked
author, but the line also stays a counted note of the block reading `a, b$ {tuomas.laakkonen, k.mei}@quantinuum.com, $^c`
— TeX source (`$`, `^`) plus the addresses already placed on their authors (the content check counts them duplicated).
The base wrote the same text as a nameless e-mail contact.

**Guards.** `perfect_kernel_batchz18k::{eptcs_email_list_a_control_word_parts_keeps_the_font, eptcs_email_row_of_boxes, eptcs_email_box_holding_addresses_is_its_ink,
llncs_email_list_quad_parted_keeps_the_font, llncs_author_bracket_piece_marked_is_a_name,
llncs_author_marked_qualifier_join_is_counted, omnibus_authors_affil_number_lists,
omnibus_authors_bracket_piece_marked_is_a_name}` (the first a keep-guard of the reroute, green on the base too); the
eptcs table and cell shapes stay `perfect_kernel_batch84b`'s. Repros
`tools/perfect_kernel/repros/class-bindings/{eptcs/eptcs_email_row_of_boxes, eptcs/eptcs_email_box_holding_addresses_is_its_ink,
llncs_email_list_quad_parted_keeps_the_font, llncs_author_bracket_piece_marked_is_a_name,
llncs_author_marked_qualifier_join_is_counted, omnibus/omnibus_authors_affil_number_lists,

`omnibus/pdflatex/aguauthors.cls`, kept apart so a repro converted in place reads its class as unknown (OmniBus).
(7) The exemption of (6) holds only for a piece that prints words after its bracket closes (`bracket_spans_whole`,
Z18o): a marked piece the bracket spans whole is a remark, joined to the name before it, the join the safety net's counted
Warning — `Ann Able\inst{1}, (deceased)\inst{2}, Bob Baker\inst{2} and [corresponding author]\inst{1}`, `Ann Able\inst{1}
and [equal contribution]\inst{1}`, article's `Ann Able$^{1}$, (deceased)$^{\dagger}$` had each made the remark a creator
of its own, 0 Warnings (review revZ18k3 R1, synthetic; 2308.02720 stays at 11 creators). The joined name keeps what
prints between them (`Ann Able<sup>1</sup>, (deceased)`), and the remark's mark requests on the joined creator. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batchz18o::marked_bracket_remark_is_no_name`; repros
`class-bindings/llncs_author_marked_bracket_remark_{is_no_name,after_and_is_no_name}.tex`,
`sectioning-frontmatter/article_author_marked_bracket_remark_is_no_name.tex`.
(8) **eptcs's cells cut by meaning (P2-4, Option C P2).** The binding cuts its block into cells where it holds a
separator meaning the kernel's `\and` — eptcs.cls's column break (`\@maketitle` sets `\@author` in a `tabular[t]{c}`,
:170-174, which latex.ltx's `\and` closes, opening the next) — as the separator query reads it (`eptcs_cls.rs` `cells`;
`argument_separators`, #995, whose `ArgSeparator::span` gives a separator's own tokens where no name, mark, contact or
note prints from them, the emitter's criterion, #993): written, held in a macro of the document's
(`\newcommand\nx{\and}`) or a `\let` copy, a cut wherever its tokens are whole units of the block's top level (no group
or environment holds them). The span is the separator's own run (`separators.rs` `own_run`, P24b): an `\end{tabular}` glued
to it (`\end{tabular}\and`, `\end{tabular}%⏎\and`, `\end{tabular}\relax\and`, `\end{tabular}\nx`) makes no box, so the
separator's box covers it (core `token::field_cover_pending_merge`), and the span leaves those tokens to the table they
close (the rehearsal's environment steps, as the emitter's balanced runs take them); a `\relax` before the separator is
its own, a unit too. Without it the span started on the `\end`, inside the table's unit, and `cells` dropped the cut the
spelling split made: the next column's institute was every author's (P24, B1 of revP24). It was a split by spelling (`split_tokens` at `\and`/`\And`/`\AND` and an alias of
`\and`'s own definition, so a `\let` copy was cut already) that saw one cell at a macro-held `\and`: a name after a table
of names was glued to the table's last name, its institute every name's (Univ C on all three authors, 0 Warnings), and a
table after the `\and` was a line under the name before it, or the gate (`eptcs_structured`, a cell opening with a table)
missed it and the kernel's line read the block (one creator "Ann Able and Bob Baker Cy Cole bob@b.edu cole@c.edu", 1
Warning each). The columns are no longer rejoined by a written `\and`: each column a cut opens follows the separator's
own tokens, which the reading cuts at their `Sep(And)` (#993). A separator of another meaning (the document's renewed
`\and`, amsmath's math `\And`) ends no cell (trap T8), where the spelling split cut at `\And`, `\AND` and a renewed
`\and`; none of the 73 eptcs census papers writes one in its `\author` (a source scan). The split by spelling stays
only where the query reads nothing (`None`: inside a rehearsal, over the queries' allowance, a block past the field's
positions).
Left in the binding, deciding structure the reading cannot see yet (rule 5 of the P2-4 brief): the table of names
(`leading_table`, `read_table`, `table_rows`, `multicolumn`), its `&` columns joined by an `\and` the binding writes —
reading a table in an author cell as names is a reading rule that does not exist; and the class's `\institute{…}` and
`\email{…}` written as `\\` lines under their column (`cell_items`, `read_cell`; eptcs.cls:188-191, where each prints `\\`
first), which the rehearsal reads as the binding's affiliation and e-mail calls with no break before them. The
macro-held and `\let` rows of the plain cells stay `perfect_kernel_batchoc1::eptcs_cells_part_at_a_macro_held_and` and
`perfect_kernel_batchsep1::eptcs_cells_part_at_a_let_copy_of_and`. ### 992. AASTeX's `\affil` e-mail lines are the API's to place: the line goes as the affiliation it is written as, the Kind and Link steps place its addresses (Z18l)

**Perl.** `\affiliation{#1}` is `\lx@add@affiliation{#1}` (aas_support.sty.ltxml:118): every line, an e-mail line
too, an affiliation of the last author.

**Was.** The binding read its e-mail lines itself, with `author_block/`'s token readers (97f r2, rev126a N2): a line
holding only addresses (`labelled_email_line`: the label behind what prints nothing, a group around the line; 1112.1037,
1311.3535, 2603.19228) became `\lx@add@contact@placed[role=email]` calls (`placed_email_line_calls`), the label their
`name={label }`, the owner the address's spelling first and a leading mark only a request of the first author showing it;
an `\email` set in a line was taken out of it and placed so (`take_placed_line_emails`). A second copy of the API's e-mail
label rule (`split_email_label` / `named_email_calls` in the Kind step, `insert::cut_email_label` on the printed text),
and an owner decided on tokens in the binding (FRONTMATTER_SINGLE_ENGINE_PLAN trap T1, T4).

**Now.** aas_support_sty.rs `\affiliation` writes every line as the affiliation entry it is — labelled `altaffil:N` in
the entries loop, else by `group_or_marked_affiliation` — and the API places its addresses with the rules every binding's
entry goes through: the Kind step (`kind_entry_addresses`) takes a line of addresses out of the entry, its label the
contacts' name (`named_email_calls`: `name={label~}`, the name ending in a no-break space where the binding wrote a
space), and the Link step (`insert::link_entry_addresses`, `entry_address_owners`) gives each address the author it
spells, else the entry's one carrier, else the block; the empty entry is dropped (`drop_empty_contacts`). An `\email`
written in a line digests inside its entry (`\lx@aas@email@author`, the class's `\lx@address@textfont`, as every other
aas `\email` prints) and is placed the same way: 1503.02933's `zhangqm@` Q. M. Zhang's, not the five holders'. A line a
requested mark leads goes to the name requesting it even where its address spells no one (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 R1, marks
win): `\affil{$^*$ Email: zz@uni.edu}` under `Bob Baker\altaffilmark{2,*}`, in a block of `\\` lines or an `\affil` of
its own, had gone to the block's nameless creator. The hand-printed number a queued `$^{N}$` requests stays the
binding's (0909.0058), no e-mail rule. Deleted with the readers, the binding the last to reach them: `email_block_calls.rs`
(`labelled_email_line`, `line_labelled_emails`, `placed_email_line_calls`, `take_placed_line_emails`,
`email_command_calls`), `email_owners.rs` (`labelled_emails`, `mailto_addresses`, `after_symbol_mark`, `unwrapped`,
`split_top_level_list`, `EmailAddress`) and `links.rs` (`mailto_line`), with their tests in `author_split_tests.rs`
(`mailto_line_is_a_labelled_email_line`, the labelled half of `email_addresses_skip_colour_arguments`); their witnesses
astro-ph0611258, 2604.10316, 2606.28166, 2602.16540, 2505.23260, 2602.12235, 2601.00240, 2601.07974, 2604.04847,
2604.23002, 2604.25444, 2605.18563, 2605.29064, 2605.29893, 2606.01600, 2606.03014 read by the API's copies.
`author_block/` 2,552 → 2,069 lines (Z18m then moved the rest unchanged to its owners and deleted `author_block/`:
FRONTMATTER_SINGLE_ENGINE_PLAN, row "`author_block/`'s survivors").

**Measured** (vs int155a1-rel, both on int154a's dumps, `kit/conv.sh` through `pool_run.sh`): the aas census (1,166:
aastex*, emulateapj, aaspp4, aas2pp4, aas_support) and the 1,434 stage2 ids, 2,600 papers, E/F/W identical on every
one; 4 changed — astro-ph0408475, 1808.01089, 0911.1770 the label's space a no-break space; 1503.02933 the address in the
class's `\email` font.

**Residual (RED, no aas corpus witness: revZ18l scanned the 1,166 aas census sources):** an e-mail line led by a mark no
name requests (`\affil{$^*$ Email: zz@uni.edu}`) is the block's e-mail with the mark in its content,
`<sup>∗</sup>zz@uni.edu`; in the block form the base kept `<sup>∗</sup>` too, and only an `\affil` of its own had the
mark dropped, uncounted, by the deleted reader. REVTeX's `\affiliation{$^*$ Email: …}` differs: the e-mail goes to that
affiliation's author with the `∗` dropped. The label's no-break space is the Kind and DOM paths' form; the text-reading
path still writes an ordinary space.

**The stopgap carrier and the mailbox link (Z18o; review revZ18l F1, F2, introduced by Z18l, synthetic).** (F1) Under
`$^N$` names aas declares `annotate=new`, whose walk (Perl's `new`, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:520-536) gives an unmarked
`\affil` to the last author even when every author it reaches holds an affiliation already: that carrier is the run's
stopgap, no mark or label (the place, Z18o2 below), and `owner:only-carrier` had made him the owner of an address no one spells
(`\affil{Email: zz@x.org}`, a bare `\affil{zz@x.org}`, `\affil{Correspondence: \href{mailto:zz@x.org}{zz@x.org}}`, an
unrequested `\affil{$^*$ Email: zz@uni.edu}` whose `∗` was dropped). The reading now tags such an entry's e-mails
(`RUN_LEFTOVER`, observer/resolver/api.rs) and, for a mark-led entry no name requests, its `annotate=` placement
(`Resolver::stopgap`), and the Link step reads them with no carrier (`answer_inner_emails`; the text reading
`take_out_entry_addresses`): the block's, once, the unrequested line's `∗` kept (`<sup>∗</sup>zz@uni.edu`). Only a walk's own
stopgap: a `run` continuing the contact before it (`\author{Bob Baker}\affil{Univ B}\affil{Email: zz@x.org}`, printed
under him) and a sole author keep their carrier; a requested `$^\dagger$` line stays its requester's. **The place (Z18o2; review revZ18o R-A, introduced by Z18o, synthetic, 0 of the
1,166 aas census papers):** a run that is the whole group of names printed since the role's last call is no stopgap
(`Resolver::print_group`, read on the unmarked line's walk and on `Resolver::stopgap`): emulateapj prints each group of
`\author` calls with the `\affil`s after it, so in `\author{Ann Able$^{1}$}\affil{$^1$Univ A}\author{Bob
Baker$^{2}$}\affil{$^2$Univ B}\affil{Email: zz@x.org}` (or `\affil{$^*$ Email: zz@x.org}`) the line is in Bob's own block
and his — Z18o gave it to a nameless creator, silently. The group in print decides, not the `\author` call: two calls
before their shared `\affil` print as one call's `Ann Able$^{1}$ and Bob Baker$^{1}$` does, and the line stays the
block's. The tag reaches the flush: the entry's own rule carries it, the emitter writes it as `_stopgap`
(`frontmatter_api::STOPGAP_ENTRY`), and the Link step (`insert::link_entry_addresses`) reads every copy so written as no
carrier of an address no one spells — `\affil{Univ C; zz@x.org}` under `$^N$` names gives Univ C to Bob Baker (Perl's

### 993. An author call parts at the `\and` its spelling hides: the reading cuts the rehearsed block, or an API creator call, at its own `Sep(And)` events (OC1, Option C's P1; the API route OC1c) (absorbs #994)

**Perl.** Every binding splits an author list by its tokens before digestion: `SplitTokens` matches a token whose meaning
is the separator's, the separator itself or a `\let` copy (`Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:114-140`, `@authorsplits` :679;
`Equals` by meaning, `Common/Object.pm:100-103`; SEP1 below, formerly #994), so a separator held in a macro (`\author{\aut}`,
`\newcommand\nx{\and}`), printed by a document wrapper (`\pair{Ann Able}{Bob Baker}`, `\pair` printing `#1 \and #2`)
or spelled `\csname and\endcsname` leaves one piece: one creator, "Ann Able and Bob Baker" (Perl 0.8.8 under OmniBus,
inst_support.sty.ltxml:33-38; llncs, llncs.cls.ltxml:43; IEEEtran, journal and conference grid). pdflatex prints two
authors in each.

**Now.** Each class route queues the piece its split left as a block (`\lx@add@author@split`: OmniBus's
`inst_support_sty.rs` `\author`, llncs's whole and marked `\author`; the kernel's `\lx@add@authors`: IEEEtran's plain
`\author`, `\lx@IEEE@author@plain`, and eptcs's unstructured one; eptcs's cells whole, #991), the rehearsal digests the
hidden `\and` to its event constructor (`rehearsal.rs` `ALWAYS_BOUND`), and the reading's names line cuts the block at
that `Sep(And)`, as TeX parts it: two creators, each `\inst` picking its numbered `\institute`. The IEEEtran grid is
argument passing, not a cut: each `\IEEEauthorblockN` is a call of its own, and the class's `\def\and{}`
(`\lx@IEEE@author@blocks`) makes a macro-held `\and` between them print nothing, as IEEEtran.cls's. This held before OC1 (the 2026-11-07 bindsplit
probes om1, ln1, ie1 and ep1, one merged creator at int143b, are green at int156a, through #980, #984 and #991); OC1
pins each of these block routes (OmniBus, llncs whole and marked, IEEEtran plain and grid, eptcs). The splits by
spelling stay in front of the reading, redundant for the names it now cuts, and are P2's to remove
(`FRONTMATTER_SINGLE_ENGINE_PLAN.md` row P2): `\lx@splitting{\lx@add@author@split}{\and\And}` in inst_support, aa,
sv_support, webofc and ptephy; llncs's marked split; the IEEEtran grid and wrap (`ieeetran_cls.rs` `author_block_body`,
`wrap_bare_author_block_text`) and both of its routes by spelling (`ieeetran_cls.rs:364` `\author`, `:391`
`\lx@IEEE@authblk@author`, `contains("authorblockN")`; since P2-8a both read the body by meaning,
`blocks_as_printed`, `calls_names_block`, the grid's columns by the separator query, #995's P2-8a paragraph); eptcs's cells (cut by meaning since P2-4, #991 (8)); `note_and_numbering` (`frontmatter_stores.rs:4481`);
nowfnt's `\and` blocks (`frontmatter_stores.rs:6000`); and the 11 gates on a literal `\and` the plan's row counts.

**The API route (OC1c; OC1b, revOC1 B1, revOC1b S1-S3).** A binding that hands one whole argument to the API makes one
creator call holding the `\and`, which Perl keeps whole (acmart.cls.ltxml:89 `\lx@add@creator{#1}`; authblk.sty.ltxml:52-55
by spelling): acmart's `\author` with no comma (`acmart_cls.rs` `\lx@acmart@author`, `separates_names`), quantumarticle's,
authblk's and ecai's where their spelling test finds no separator (`authblk_sty.rs` `author_call` falls back to
`\lx@add@creator`; ecai routes only a literal top-level `\and` to the block). pdflatex prints two authors (acmart.cls:2726
`\let\and\@typeset@author@line`). The call's content is the whole `\lx@personname{\lx@author@withinst{…}}` group, so its
`\and` is a `Sep(And)` at nest 1, inside the `\lx@personname` Layout: the reading's cut
(`resolver::api::creator_call_pieces`, shared by `Resolver::api` and the emitter) takes an `\and` at that level, where every
piece holding ink holds a name (one inside a container of the name or a note is that container's; `Ann Able \and
\thanks{…}` stays whole). OC1b's cut tested nest 0 and never fired (measured by an event print on `acm_mixblock.tex`). The
emitter writes such a call as one creator call per piece (`emit::creator_call_cut`): the call's own command, keyvals (role,
label, annotations) and wrappers, the group holding the `\and`s holding the piece's run — from its first event's position to its last's, or
all between its two `\and`s where that run is unbalanced — by positions from a fresh rehearsal of the content (the
ledger's events carry none, `ApiCall::errors`), where each `\and`'s own tokens (a literal one, `\csname and\endcsname`, an
active character) part no ink; else, a macro holding names and `\and`s together
(`\author{\aut}`), each name by its text with a counted Warning (`by_text`), only where each piece prints its name alone
(else the call stays whole, its merge counted by `merged_creators`). A call whose ink is not all inside the `\and`'s
group (an event of `Name`, `Mark`, `Contact` or `Note` whose span starts at or before the group's open brace or ends past
its close: `\author{Ann {Able \and Bob} Baker}`, `\author{\textsc{Ann Able \and Bob Baker} Jr.}`, `{…}$^*$`) stays whole
too: each piece is wrapped in the tokens before and after that group, so ink there would print once a piece and invent
names (revOC1c B1: "Ann Able Baker" / "Ann Bob Baker"; "Ann Able Jr." / "Bob Baker Jr. Jr."). In a paper with no author block, where the emitter
otherwise stays out (`emit.rs` `stays_out`), the queued entry is replaced by its pieces' calls (`cut_creator_calls`), the
rest of the queue digested as Perl's, and an `annotate={run:<cap>}` after it (authblk's unlabelled `\affil`, `affil_run`,
the authors queued since the last `\affil`) counts the pieces (its cap read off the ledger's `ApiCall::attrs`), so the `\affil` goes to every name,
as pdflatex prints it under the shared mark. Every cut call is matched to its own queue entry (the first unclaimed one
spelled as it is) and the added pieces are summed per annotation before any entry is rewritten, each annotation rewritten
once from its original cap: two cut calls before one `\affil` (`\author{\autA}\author{\autB}\affil{Univ X}`) put all four
names under it, where a rewrite per call left the second call's ledger lookup, keyed by the tokens the first had
rewritten, without a cap and the first name without the affiliation (revOC1c B2). The wrapper is told by its Layout role, the API's own container, not a
document's spelling: the e0 fences' `resolver` pins rose by one each (`TOKEN_READS` 20 → 21,
`OBSERVER_BACKSLASH_LITERALS` 3 → 4), the emitter's none. Beside a block the emission's per-creator loop writes each creator of the cut call as its piece, its
own `author:N`. Witnesses 1909.10278 (one merged creator, E 1 → two, the affiliation on both and the shared
`\email{{dlerch,dmegias}@uoc.edu}` on the last piece, E 0; the PDF prints it under both names, the open shared-contacts
residual) and 2501.11185 (one merged creator
holding both institutes, W 1 → two, each with its institute line, W 0); 15 of the census's 873 acmart papers spell a
literal `\and` with no top-level comma (a source scan). Routes, enumerated by the one choke point every API creator call
passes, `queue_front_matter` → `ledger::record_api_call` (tag `ltx:creator`, not made by a block's own expansion), whose
binding callers a grep for `\lx@add@(creator|author|editor|translator)` (not followed by `@` or a letter) and
`\lx@add@frontmatter(@now)?{ltx:creator}` over `latexml_package/src`, `latexml_contrib/src` and `latexml_core/src/binding`
finds (28 files, 3 of them comments only: openmoss, selfevolagent, sn_jnl): acmart (`\author`, `\editor`), quantumarticle,
authblk, ecai, arximspdf, aipproc, icml_support (`\icmlauthor`), jmlr (`\Name`), czipreprint, meta_class, interspeech,
bytedance_seed, mrm, ceurart, lmcs, lipics, bmcart, beilstein, brief and g_brief (sender), jhep and omnibus (`\speaker`,
`\editors`), ams_support (`\contrib`, `\commby`, `\translator`), amsppt (`\translator`), and the core store reroute
(`store_setters.rs`: `editor`, `editors`, `speaker`); the engine's own callers in `latexml_engine/src` are not listed. Probed and green: acmart
(literal, `\csname`, active character, wrapper, macro-held; beside a block), authblk macro-held, quantumarticle literal and
macro-held (two creators; no oracle, TL 2025 pdflatex fails on the class). jmlr's `\Name{Ann Able \and Bob Baker}` now
gives two creators where the base gave one with `merged_creators`; pdflatex prints "Ann Able and Bob Baker" in one
`\Name`, jmlr's `\and` printing the word there (jmlr.cls:336, inside `\jmlrpreauthor`'s group), so the cut is a spelling
rule: the rehearsal binds the name `\and` (`ALWAYS_BOUND`) and jmlr's meaning is not in force when it reads. Kept (no text
lost, 0 census papers; review revOC1c S1), RED in the catalog: the fix is the jmlr binding's, giving `\and` the word
meaning inside `\Name`, not a class test in the engine. Not cut: a call in a paper whose author block no rehearsal read (`stays_out` with a
`SkipReason`: the queue is Perl's), and a call a block's own expansion made (`ApiCall::inside`). The others unprobed (most
have no class file in TL 2025). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchoc1c::{an_api_creator_call_parts_at_its_own_and,
an_api_creator_call_with_ink_outside_its_group_stays_whole, each_piece_of_a_cut_call_keeps_its_keyvals}`; repros
`class-bindings/acmart_author_{and,csname_and,active_and,wrapper_and,macro_held_and,and_call_beside_a_block}_parts_the_names.tex`,
`class-bindings/acmart_author_and_in_a_{group_with_ink_before,font_with_ink_after}_stays_whole.tex`,
`class-bindings/acmart_editor_and_parts_the_names_keeps_the_role.tex`,
`sectioning-frontmatter/{authblk_author_macro_held_and_parts_the_names,authblk_two_macro_held_calls_before_one_affil,authblk_two_alike_macro_held_calls_each_own_affil}.tex`;
the catalog RED `class-bindings/jmlr_name_and_prints_the_word_red.tex`. Residuals, red at int156a and outside this mechanism: a
`\let` copy of `\and` (`\let\nx\and`) kept the kernel's meaning in the rehearsal, which bound its vocabulary by name,
so the block held no `Sep(And)` (one merged creator and `Error:frontmatter:merged_creators` under article, eptcs and

`ieeetran_cls.rs` `\author`), so a grid held in a macro goes the plain route (one nameless creator) and one inside a

P2-8a paragraph). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchoc1::{a_block_parts_at_the_and_its_spelling_hides,
