"Univ B" inside its wrong merge). Known RED, pre-existing: two contacts on one name, `\and Bob Baker\institute{Univ
B}\institute{Univ C}`, give Ann Univ B and Bob Univ C where pdflatex prints both under Bob (the reading's per-contact
ownership; identical on int157a under OmniBus; under `article` no worse than the base, which put all three on Ann;
repro `class-bindings/author_one_block/omnibus_author_name_with_two_institutes_after_and_red.tex`). Guard `perfect_kernel_batchp21d::a_column_is_read_on_its_own_ink_not_its_contacts`;
repros `class-bindings/author_one_block/omnibus_author_{name_with_institute_after_and,
table_glued_to_and_name_with_institute,last_of_three_with_address,column_of_contacts_alone_is_shared}.tex`.

**P2-1b (P21b): sv_support's split removed, aa's kept.** sv_support's `\author` makes one `\lx@add@author@split{#1}`
call. The queue's readers read each queued `ltx:creator` entry as one name, so the whole list was one: the
`\lx@sv@institute@` gate (an itemized `\institute` list spelling two or more queued names whole is the authors' list) failed,
and the list and every address went to the last author (2312.14898). `queue_reading.rs` `queued_author_names_spelled`
now parts each entry first (`entry_names`) where the reading cuts it: at each `\and`-family separator not inside a layout container (a brace group is none, so
`{A \and B}` parts inside its braces) that `argument_separators` reads, at its own tokens (`ArgSeparator::span`, the field eptcs's cells part at too, #991 (8):
a literal, a `\let` copy, a macro holding only the separator, the document's macro `\and`; never an environment closed right before it — an `\end{tabular}`, `\end{minipage}`, a user environment),
whatever it means at `\institute` — the rehearsal binds `\and` whatever it means (`ALWAYS_BOUND`), and each sv class sets its
own in its `\@maketitle` before the names print (svjour3.cls:608 in 2312.14898's copy; svjour, svmult and svproc likewise, revP21b), so a document's `\renewcommand\and{\unskip, }` still gives three creators and
the shared list, as P21's split did. A separator whose tokens print ink too (a macro holding names and the `\and`) and
an entry the query cannot read (`None`) part nothing: the entry stays one name. P21b gave the field as a position
(`ArgSeparator::position`), which a macro holding the `\and` lacked; P24b's span gives it, so `\newcommand\sep{\and}`,
`\author{Ann Able \sep Bob Baker}` parts as the reading cuts it, two names, and an `\institute` list naming both is the
authors' list (int158a: one name, both addresses and the list on Bob Baker). An `\end{tabular}\and` entry's list is still not the
authors' list (the gate's count stays at most one; both addresses on Bob Baker, int158a the same): catalog repro
`class-bindings/author_one_block/svjour3_author_table_glued_to_and_list_stays_red.tex`. The queue readers, by route: changed, `queued_author_names_spelled` (one caller,
`sv_support_sty.rs` `\lx@sv@institute@`); unchanged, `queued_author_name_prints` (it reads all the names' words together,
so a part changes nothing), `queued_author_marks`, `queued_requesters` and `queued_name_marks` (one entry per position;
the kernel `\author`'s block is one entry too, so parting their positions is the plan's P4 row: P2-3b, #995, parts a
binding's whole-list entry, a position a name; P2-3c the kernel's). aa kept its split here:
without it, `\corrauth`'s contact lost `name="Corresponding author: "` when a later name held a `CJK*` environment
(2608.21138), the emitter writing the contact as its item (`\lx@frontmatter@itemonly{…}`), not as the `\corrauth` call —
the events' walker's, a mechanism of its own (P2-1c, below).
Guards `perfect_kernel_batchp21b::sv_institute_list_reads_a_whole_author_entry_by_its_names`,
`perfect_kernel_batchp24b::sv_institute_list_reads_an_entry_parted_at_a_macro_held_and`; repros
`class-bindings/author_one_block/svjour3_institute_list_names_a_{whole_author_block,whole_author_block_document_and,macro_held_and_entry}.tex`.

**P2-1c (P21c): aa's split removed; P2-1 is complete outside llncs.** aa's `\author` makes one
`\lx@add@author@split{#2}` call after its clear (`aa_cls.rs`). What kept the split was the events' walker, not the
emitter: a `{CJK*}` environment leaves horizontal mode (`cjk_sty.rs` `before_digest => leave_horizontal`), whose `\par`
packs the block's line so far into a paragraph list (`stomach::repack_horizontal`, Perl's `List(@para, mode =>
'horizontal')`), and the walker read every inner list as a braced group (`events/mod.rs` `Walker::walk`), so the
paragraph made an earlier name's `\inst` a mark whose group held the contact after it; the emitter writes a contact a
mark's formula holds by its text (`emit.rs` `in_a_mark`, the ORCID-icon rule), so `\corrauth` lost its `name` and an
`\email` its typewriter font. With the split, each name was its own block and no paragraph held the contact. A
paragraph's list (its `mode` property `horizontal`; a group's list has none) is now no group at the block's own level:
its boxes are walked at the level around it (`paragraph_is_no_group`), as TeX's `\par` closes no group (scope: P21e,
below). The S1 routes now: inst_support's,
ptephy's, webofc's (P2-1), sv_support's (P2-1b) and aa's `\author` make one call; llncs's `\lx@llncs@author@split`
still splits (by meaning since P2-3, #995), and the `\institute` splits (aa, inst_support, sv_support, llncs) are not author splits. Byte
identity against int158a over aa's 563 papers, the stage2 1,434 and 2608.21138: 1,990 identical, 3 with no main file on
both, 4 changed, all by the split's removal alone (the no-split build gives the same XML): 2408.11004, 2509.22322,
2604.10287, whose `\author{\small …}` now sets `fontsize="90%"` on every name, as pdflatex sets the whole list (the
first name alone had it); 1407.3707, lateral: its note "Corresponding authors: R. López-Coto, \email{rlopez@…}, D.
Hadasch, \email{hadasch@…}" (on López-Coto, `$^\star$` on Hadasch) gives López-Coto his address and loses Hadasch's on
int158a, and gives Hadasch his and loses López-Coto's now, each loss counted by the content check's Warning. 2608.21138
keeps `name="Corresponding author: "`. Residual, not root-caused (RED catalog repro
`aa_corrauth_before_a_cjk_part_of_its_own_name_red.tex`): a `{CJK*}` in the `\corrauth` author's own name, after the
call (`Ann Able\inst{1}\corrauth{a@x} (\begin{CJK*}…\end{CJK*})`), writes the contact twice, with the content check's
Warning — on int158a once with its `name` and once without, here twice with it. Guard `perfect_kernel_batchp21c::a_contact_keeps_its_call_beside_a_cjk_name`; repros
`class-bindings/author_one_block/aa_{corrauth,email}_beside_a_cjk_name_in_one_block.tex`,
`aa_corrauth_after_a_cjk_name_in_one_block.tex`.

**P2-1c's scope (P21e): only a paragraph of the block's own list is no group.** The walker flattens a paragraph's list
only where it is a child of the walked list (`Walker::lists` one) in a walk by `lex_with_inks` — a block's, or a
creator call's content alone (`reading.rs`, `separators.rs`, `emit.rs` callers) — not of a note's body, a link's text,
a contact's or a box whatsit's lines (`raw_lines`), which the walker lexes on its own (`lex_body_with_inks`,
`Walker::body`). A paragraph inside a box's body (a minipage, a varwidth, a `\parbox`: one list deeper), inside a braced
group, or inside a note's body stays a group, as before P21c. Flattened there, the box became a mark's group:
`enclose` spans the box by `deep_span`, which reaches its unshown position and width arguments, so 2608.17538's
`\dedicatory{\begin{minipage}[t]{0.47\linewidth}\centering\textsuperscript{1}…}` read "t]0.47" and `\centering` into
each contact (two "Missing number" Warnings) and a `\parbox[t]` one wrote each contact as the empty box; and the
contact beside a braced mark lost its source run, written as its address alone (`\lx@frontmatter@itemonly`):
2402.02104's `\texttt` e-mail in a `{varwidth}`/`{minipage}`, 2601.03873's `\thanks{…\href{mailto:…}{…}}` in
`\parbox{\textwidth}{\Large{…}}`. The three papers' XML is int157a's again; 2608.21138 and P21c's four changed papers
keep int158a's. Guards `perfect_kernel_batchp21e::{a_paragraph_in_a_box_stays_a_group,
a_paragraph_in_a_box_keeps_a_contacts_markup}`; repros `class-bindings/author_one_block/`
`amsart_dedicatory_{box,parbox}_paragraph_stays_a_group.tex`, `authblk_minipage_paragraph_keeps_a_typewriter_email.tex`,
`mnras_parbox_paragraph_keeps_a_mailto_link.tex`.

**P2-1's setters in notes (EJ1): a setter inside an emitted note writes its entry once.** A frontmatter setter that
makes no creator, run inside an author block (ejpecp's `\EMAIL`, `\@add@frontmatter{ltx:note}[role=email]{#1}`, in a
`\footnote` or `\thanks` of `\AUTHORS`), is noted by the rehearsal (`AuthorBlock::queued`) and written by the emitter as
queued (`emit.rs` `recover_queued`). A note the emitter writes from its argument (`note_argument`) digested the setter a
second time. Under P21's one block (OmniBus's `\author`, which ejpecp loads) every note followed by a space or an `\and`
is written from its argument; int157a's split by spelling trimmed each piece, so its note mostly closed the piece and
was written by its text (a "note no argument" Warning), running no setter. Hence a second `<note role="email">` per such
note (int157a → P21e): 1406.5876 1 → 2, 1904.02213 3 → 4, 2206.01959 2 → 3, 1904.07135 4 → 8. 1904.02213's second note,
whose argument ends in a space (`\BEMAIL{dong.yao@duke.edu} }`), was written twice by int157a already. Now an item the
emitter writes from a block whose rehearsal ran such a setter opens with `\lx@frontmatter@setters@of{<the block's ledger
index>}`, which sets `emit::SETTERS_RECOVERED` (cleared for every queued entry, `place::digest_queued_entry`) where the
recovery wrote that block's entries, at this flush or an earlier one. Under it `\lx@add@frontmatter@now` writes nothing
(not a creator). The recovery stays the one writer, so each address is one note, in the PDF's author order: the four
papers 1, 2, 2, 4 notes, one per address (1904.02213 better than int157a). The note keeps its markup (no Warning) and
its whitespace before the `\EMAIL` (`Univ X⏎`; int157a's text was `Univ X`). A note closing the block is still written
by its text, with its Warning. An API call's items are not marked: the recovery writes no call the reading writes from
(`written`), so the item runs the setter itself. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batchej1::a_setter_in_an_author_note_writes_its_entry_once`; repros `sectioning-frontmatter/`
`ejpecp_footnote_email_setter_written_once.tex`, `ejpecp_footnote_emails_between_authors_written_once.tex`,
`ejpecp_thanks_email_setter_written_once.tex`.

**P2-7 (P27): authblk's `\author` gates by meaning; the run's cap counts calls.** authblk's two gates
(`authblk_sty.rs` `author_call`, `lines_of_names_before_affil`) tested the spelling of a token meaning `\and` or `\And`
anywhere in the names. They ask the separator query (#995) for a kernel `\and` at the names' own level instead
(`separated_by_and`): written, `\And`, held in a macro of the document's, a `\let` copy, a `\csname and\endcsname`. A
separator of another meaning — a document's renewed `\and` (trap T8), amsmath's `\And`, a class binding's stand-in — is
no kernel column. A binding's `\AND` `\let` to the kernel's `\and` (inst_support on the OmniBus path) now counts, where the
spelling test missed it (revP27 N1; probe `\documentclass{nosuchclass}`, same creators). Where the query reads nothing
(inside a rehearsal, over its allowance, a group left open, an argument too long for the field) the spelling decides, as
before.
The query is asked once per `\author`, and only where a comma or the word "and" does not decide. A macro-held `\and`
now takes the list path (`\lx@add@authors@list`, the reading's block cut), as the written one does, not `\lx@add@creator`
(the emitter's cut of the call, OC1c above). Same creators either way; the content check's false excess Warning on two
calls of one macro is gone. The list path's run then met a reading defect: authblk's unlabelled `\affil` caps its run at
the `\author` calls queued since the last `\affil` (`affil_run`, `annotate=run:<n>`), and the reading's `record_run`
counted that cap in names. `\author{Cy Cole}\author{Ann Able, Bob Baker}\affil{Univ X}` (run 2) stopped at Ann Able and
Bob Baker and gave Cy Cole none, silently, where pdflatex prints all three under Univ X. The written shapes had this
defect before P2-7 (a comma list, a written `\and`, after a name or another list); the macro-held one inherited it with
the gate. The cap counts calls now (`resolver/api.rs` `record_run`, `calls_from`: a creator's call is its `source`). The
other `run:<n>` writer, `queue_digest.rs` `run_cap_past_labels` (the stores' line calls), counts queued author entries
too. The e0 pin `TOKEN_READS` `authblk_sty.rs` 23 → 22. The gates still call the old reader's `has_author_block_separator`,
`lines_under_names_read_as_names`, `line_breaks_as_name_separators` and `holds_a_macro_printing_a_link` (the layout
separators, not the `\and` family), so no old-reader line is freed. The S8 half of P2-7, the emitter writing the declined
no-author-block flushes so that `shared_row::share_row_contacts` and `shared_row/` can go, is not done here (a batch of
its own, P27b: #901's last paragraph): `share_row_contacts`' only effect found is a no-block llncs flush of several authblk `\author` calls
(`\lx@add@creator` each), where the emitter, let through for a flush holding a `_share` contact, gives the same output;
letting every no-block flush through misplaces icml's labelled contacts. Byte-identical with int158a on authblk's census
(1,569 of 1,571 compared), stage2 (1,434), a 300-paper raw-class sample (299), z18n_declined40 (40) and
z18n_declpop2345 (2,342). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchp27::{authblk_affil_run_counts_author_calls,
authblk_and_gates_read_the_separator_by_meaning}` and `perfect_kernel_batchoc1c::an_api_creator_call_parts_at_its_own_and`'s
`authblk_two_alike_macro_held_calls_each_own_affil` row (5 → 4 Warnings); repros `sectioning-frontmatter/`
`authblk_affil_run_{name_before_a_list,two_lists}.tex`, `authblk_and_let_copy_and_csname_part_names.tex`,
`authblk_renewed_and_is_no_kernel_column.tex`, `authblk_macro_held_and_line_before_affil.tex`.

**P3: a name a macro call prints with its marks is written as the call.** A token a macro's expansion makes carries
the call's field position (`token::inherit_field_prov`), and the first box digested from the call takes the call's
cover (`field_cover_pending_merge`, OD #715). So a name a call prints with its marks — ptephy's
`\name{\fname{Yoshiharu} \surname{Kawamura}}{1,\ast}` (`#1\lx@inst@mark{1}\lx@inst@mark{\ast}`, `ptephy_cls.rs`) — has
the call for its span (a document's `\nm{Ann Able}{1}`, `#1$^{#2}$`, is not covered: its formula mark is no call's, Known RED
`omnibus_author_name_macros_with_marks_keep_them_red`; revP3 NIT), and its marks the call's position, before the
name's own tokens. The emitter (`emit::event_run_at`) read such a mark as printed before the name inside a wrapper
(`\textbf{$^2$Tencent Hunyuan}`, 2605.25195), found no run and wrote the name by text with the Warning "a name its
events don't spell"; and the last call's name, whose cover stops short of the call (its arguments the field's last
tokens, `gullet::field_cover_of`), was written from inside the call, the marks argument as the name's text ("Bob
Baker2"). Now a mark the call's expansion prints (`emit::made_by_its_call`: no position of its own, no formula or
group but its cover) is no mark before the name unless its event comes first, and such a kept mark whose cover holds
the name's grows the name's run to that call (`emit::block_names`, never over another name): the call is written
whole, which digests to the name and its marks as the block did, as every other ptephy name is written (Perl's
personname holds the call). A mark with a position of its own stays as it was: a wrapper's after the name,
`\textbf{Yizheng Sun\textsuperscript{1}}` (2606.08894), is written apart (P2 B; a draft reading every mark by event
order wrote "Yizheng Sun 1" into 14 papers' names). The 4 ptephy witnesses (1304.2086, 1601.07691, 1304.7885, 2210.05569)
lose the by-text overcount; a symbol mark is kept as the PDF prints it (`Yoshiharu Kawamura<sup>∗</sup>`). P3's
second half is AUT1, below. Left (REDs): a call in a `\parbox` (`ptephy_name_inside_its_call_in_a_parbox_red`) and a document macro's formula mark
(`omnibus_author_name_macros_with_marks_keep_them_red`), whose marks `made_by_its_call` does not read as the call's. The
links and marks that part a name inside a call (`ptephy_name_split_by_a_{link,mark}_invents_a_creator_red`) are the
reading's, not the writer's. Guard `perfect_kernel_batchp3::a_name_inside_a_macro_call_is_written_from_the_call`; repros
`class-bindings/author_one_block/{ptephy_name_inside_its_call_is_written_from_the_call,
ptephy_name_and_cite_inside_its_call_is_written_from_the_call, article_author_name_macro_with_a_font_keeps_it,
article_author_wrapper_mark_after_the_name_stays_apart, ptephy_author_list_glued_trailing_mark_leaves_the_name}.tex`.

**AUT1 (P3's second half: names held in a document macro).** `\author{\aut}`, Frontiers' `\author{\Authors}` (30 of
35 census Frontiers papers), CVPR's `\author{\authorBlock}`: every event the macro's expansion digests to has the call's
one position (`token::inherit_field_prov`), so no name had a run of the block's tokens and each was written by its text,
its markup lost, counted ("a name its events don't spell", "a macro's span", "a creator call cut where a macro holds its
names"). The core's field hook now carries the expansion (`FieldInvocation::Expanded(&Tokens)`,
`gullet::note_field_expansion`: the batch's only core change); the rehearsal keeps the expansion of each own field token
calling a document macro of no parameters (`field_notes::HeldExpansion`). Where two names, contacts or notes share one
span inside such a call, the block is rehearsed again with the expansion in the call's place (`reading::unfold_held_names`,
up to `UNFOLD_LEVELS` = 4 nested macros, the footnote steps carried put back first), and its events and the unfolded
tokens (`AuthorBlock::unfolded`, read through `AuthorBlock::read_tokens` by every positional reader of the emitter) are
the block's: a held block reads as its inline twin. An API creator call is unfolded the same way before its cut
(`emit::rehearsed_unfolded`, acmart's and authblk's `\author{\aut}`). Not unfolded, still by text and counted: a macro
with parameters, whose cover past its arguments is unknown where the call ends the field (RED
`article_author_macro_with_parameters_holding_names_red`), a macro a class or package defined, and a re-read that fails
(over budget, out of positions, a conditional left open across the run): the by-text arms (`block_names`' shared-span
return, `cut_at_separators`' by-text arm, the contacts' "a macro's span") are that fallback now. With it, a block that
keeps its marks on the names (`per_author_marks`: OmniBus, a raw class's, revtex's) shows a request whose superscript
it prints after the name's runs and before the next name's, in no written run, as an unkept one
(`emit::NameMarks::unwritten_after`; the block's superscripts and written runs read once per block, each name's a range query): a mark past a gap or a comma (`Ann Able\, $^{1}$ ,`, `Dee Dunn,$^{4}$`, revtex's `Ann
Able,$^{1,*}$`'s `∗`), held or inline, was lost silently (2209.05831, 2201.04171, 2609.18180, 2403.18314; hep-ph0301204,
hep-ph0411288 inline). Cost (instructions:u vs int167a, median of 5 interleaved runs): 2103.04797 and 1901.01540
±0.01 %; hep-ph0301204 (210 names) +0.60 % and a 1,000-name `revtex4-1` `\author{AnnA AbAA,$^{1}$ …}` +4.6 %, the
emission of the marks each gains (the probe's inline twin `AnnA AbAA$^{1}$,`, output unchanged: −1.2 %). A leading mark (`$^2$Bob Baker`) is no such mark and stays as it was. Perl
splits at the `\author` call by spelling and gives such a block one creator (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:679-720). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batchaut1::a_macro_of_names_is_read_as_its_inline_twin`, the macro-held rows of `perfect_kernel_batchoc1`,
`oc1c`, `p21`, `p24`, `p27`, `sep1`, `lo4`, `hg1`; repros `class-bindings/author_one_block/article_author_*` (AUT1's),
`omnibus_author_macro_of_names_mark_after_a_gap_is_shown`; REDs `omnibus_author_math_mark_in_the_name_run_is_italic_red`,
`article_author_macro_with_parameters_holding_names_red`. Witnesses 2103.13804, 2504.00496, 2112.09018, 2206.01053,
2311.15269, 2609.00161.

**GRP1 (a declaration replayed as far as its call read).** The emitter replays a block's declarations (`emit::declarations`)
cut from the tokens its events were read from (`emit::declaration_cuts` over `AuthorBlock::read_tokens`; AUT1 had cut the
unfolded spans from the folded list: 2605.24599's `email}`). A declaration's span ends where its call read
(`FieldDeclaration::read`, kept by `field_notes::note_call_read` from the covers of the call's own expansion: babel's robust
`\foreignlanguage` reading its arguments in `\bbl@foreign@x`, `\ifthenelse`'s `\@firstoftwo` reading the branches), not at
the one token whose cover it had, so the name or branch the call prints takes it back (2606.14878, 2605.24599). A box made
while the call's own invocation still runs (`stomach::field_position_encloses`: a macro `\begin` running the kernel's
`{CJK*}`, openjournal.cls's atbeginend copy) is inside it too (2606.12938). A declaration made after a token of its call's
arguments printed keeps its span as noted (`FieldDeclaration::read` 0), as before: NE5's `\footremember` declined by
`declaration_reads_past`, a robust `\mbox{#1}\gdef\lastnm{#1}` replayed for a later name. A span the read tokens cannot give whole (out of them, its
groups unbalanced) is not replayed: `declaration_reads_past` declines the block with its counted Warning — a defensive branch,
reached by no known input (revGRP1's 12 probes; by the code, only a span starting before the block). Guard
`perfect_kernel_batchaut1::a_declaration_is_replayed_as_far_as_its_call_read`; RED
`amsart_author_macro_lines_with_email_array_split_red`.

**SEP1 (absorbed from #994): the rehearsal binds a `\let` copy of an author-line separator or note command by its meaning, as the command it copies.** Perl: `\let\nx\and` then `\author{Ann Able \nx Bob Baker}` gives two creators, Ann Able and Bob Baker (Perl 0.8.8,
run on the repro): `\lx@add@authors` splits at `@authorsplits` (`\and`, `\And`, `\AND`, …; `Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:679`)
by `SplitTokens` (:114-140), whose `Equals` compares two tokens by their meanings (`Common/Object.pm:100-103`,
`lookupMeaning`; `Core/Token.pm:318-320` `equals` is the by-name one), so `\nx` matches `\and`; a `\let\nx\relax` or a
`\def\nx{\and}` is not split (Perl 0.8.8, `--debug=frontmatter`). A copy taken before `\renewcommand\and` is split too:
it matches `\And`/`\AND`, which keep the kernel's meaning (`Let('\And', '\and')`, `latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1095-1096`).
pdflatex prints two authors: `\nx` is `\and`.

Before SEP1 the rehearsal bound the author line's vocabulary by name only (`observer/rehearsal.rs`
`install_event_bindings`, `ALWAYS_BOUND`: `\and` to `\lx@fm@obs@and`, `\\` to `\lx@fm@obs@break`, `\thanks`, `\footnote`
to their events). A `\let` copy kept the command's own meaning (the kernel `\and` a constructor printing " and ",
`sect05.rs`), so the block held no `Sep(And)` to cut: one creator "Ann Able
and Bob Baker", `Error:frontmatter:merged_creators`, under article, eptcs and IEEEtran journal (OC1's `\let` probe); a
copy of `\thanks` printed the kernel's note and the creator held none; a copy of `\footnote` had its note text ("footnote",
the mark, "Univ A") read into the name.

Now, before the by-name bindings, `let_copies_of_bound_commands` collects the commands the block reaches — spelled in its
tokens, or held in the bodies of the document's own macros it spells (`DefinitionOrigin::Document`, at most 256 macros
per block) — whose meaning is a definition made for an `ALWAYS_BOUND` command flagged bound by meaning (`\and`, `\And`,
`\AND`, `\\`, `\thanks`, `\footnote`): `defined_as` it, so a `\relax` or an undefined name is no copy of a separator a
class `\let` to `\relax` or left undefined. It is not compared with what the command means now, as the command itself
is bound by its name whatever its definition: a copy taken before the document renews the command
(`\let\nx\and\renewcommand\and{\unskip\ and\ }`, `\let\oldthanks\thanks\renewcommand\thanks[1]{}`) keeps the
separator or the note in TeX (SEP1b); a test against the command's current meaning had left it unbound, one merged
creator, the note lost. This binds a copy of a class's own `\and` too (amsart.cls:599's word-printing `\and`, then renewed:
two creators, the printed "and" kept as Bob Baker's `before`), as TeX does, where Perl's `Equals` would not split at it —
Perl's split on a renewed `\and`'s older copy holds only for the kernel's `\and`, through `\And`/`\AND`'s `Let` copies
(`latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1095-1096`). The distinct commands read are kept in a hash set (`Token` hashes what its equality compares; a `Vec` searched linearly was quadratic:
a 300-macro synthetic, 1.14 G instructions → 10.2 G under SEP1, 1.19 G since).
Each is `\let` to the command's event constructor, in the rehearsal's group. A name bound by its own name
(`ALWAYS_BOUND`, `BOUND_WHEN_DEFINED`: fixacm.sty's `\let\alignauthor\and`, 1801.02123) or one the binding declares a
block break keeps that binding. Class macros are not read into: a copy a class's own code makes (latex.ltx's
`\@normalcr`, revtex's `\and@latex`) is the class's business.

SEP1's reach (a source scan of the 35,942 census papers, `\let\X\and|\And|\AND|\\|\thanks|\footnote` and `X` in an
`\author`/`\authors` argument): a copy of `\and`/`\And`/`\AND` used in an author argument, 0 papers beyond fixacm's
`\alignauthor` (bound by name already; 294 papers define such a copy, 289 of them in a class or package); of `\\`, 5
(all `\newline`, bound by name); of `\thanks`, 73 (72 `\footnote`, bound by name; acl.sty's `\Thanks`, 2407.16574); of
`\footnote`, 170 (169 `\thanks`, bound by name; www-notes.cls's `\Affiliation`, 1712.07684, `\let` to `\footnote` only inside
`\preauthor`, `\@gobble` outside it). Byte-diff against OC1b (3,283 papers: the scan's 570, the article 614, the llncs
699, int152c's stage2 1,434; 3,263 converted on both sides, the other 20 on neither): one paper changed, 2407.16574,
better (its two `\Thanks` notes, a `pubnote` each before, now Eunseop Yoon's and Chang D. Yoo's, as the PDF marks them);
E/F/W totals equal on every list. Not bound by meaning: the rest of `ALWAYS_BOUND` (`\par`, `\label`, `\footnotemark`, `\footnotetext`,
`\newline`, `\linebreak`, `\inst`), whose copies (`\endgraf`, `\@@par`) are kernel and class internals.

SEP1's guards `perfect_kernel_batchsep1::{a_let_copy_of_and_parts_the_names, eptcs_cells_part_at_a_let_copy_of_and,
a_let_copy_of_a_note_command_is_its_note}`; repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/author_let_copy_of_{and_parts_the_names,and_parts_the_names_ieeetran,and_in_a_macro_parts_the_names,and_before_renewal_parts_the_names,thanks_is_the_note,thanks_before_renewal_is_the_note,footnote_is_the_note}.tex`,
`class-bindings/eptcs/eptcs_author_let_copy_of_and_parts_the_names.tex`.

*Live rule: OD #993.*

### 995. Option C P2's foundation: a binding-callable query on an argument's separators by meaning, and the emitter's cut of a numbered contact call (P20)

**Perl.** No such query: Perl's bindings part an argument by spelling (`SplitTokens`, `Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:114-140`),
and a numbered list (`labelseq=`, `Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:489` `CleanLabel($n, $labelseq)`) reaches the API already split
by its binding (llncs.cls.ltxml's `\institute`).

**Now.** Two mechanisms the P2 reroutes call (the bindings stop pre-splitting by spelling; plan
`agent_reports/2026-11-10_P2P_report.md`). No binding called either at P2-0, so the corpus was byte-identical; since
P2-4, eptcs's cells call the query (#991 (8)), which gives each separator's own tokens too (`ArgSeparator::span`, where
no name, mark, contact or note prints from them), and since P24b the queue's name reader parts at the same field (#993
P2-1b; P21b's `ArgSeparator::position` is gone). The span is the event's run past the environments closed right before
it (`own_run`: an environment closed right before the separator — an `\end{tabular}`, `\end{minipage}`, a nested table, a user environment — whose cover its box took, is the environment's; revP24b N1).
- *The query* (`observer/separators.rs` `argument_separators(&Tokens) -> Result<Option<Vec<ArgSeparator>>>`, re-exported
  as `latexml_engine::base_utilities::{argument_separators, FmArgSeparator, FmSepMeaning}`; TeX front-end
  `\lx@fm@separators{<tokens>}`, expanding to the meanings' names comma-separated, empty for none, `unread` where no
  rehearsal could be made or it left a group open). The argument is rehearsed (`rehearsal::rehearse`, everything undone;
  the footnote steps it carries put back) from the queries' own allowance (`rehearsal::for_a_query`, as `for_the_check`
  runs the content check's: one rehearsal's reads per conversion, never the reading's `READS_LEFT`, its `LEFT_OUT` put
  back), so a query moves no reading — four costly queries before `\maketitle` under `LATEXML_REHEARSAL_READ_BUDGET=1500`
  had spent the reading's budget and merged the block's two authors into one creator. Each `Sep(And)` event at nest 0 is
  reported with its family command and the meaning of the token that printed it, read outside the rehearsal, the one in
  force at the call site (the binding's `\author`, `\institute`):
  - `Kernel`: the kernel layer's `\and` constructor (`latex_constructs/sect05.rs`, which `\And`/`\AND` are `\let` to), the
    definition `\and`'s own (`get_cs()`). Narrower than the pool-constructor test `frontmatter_stores.rs` `kernel_and_list`
    made before P2-6, which now asks this (P2-6, below): `texvc_sty.rs:132` `Let!("\\and", "\\land")` is `Raw`, no kernel
    separator; the old test is the gate's reading only where the query answers `None`.
  - `Binding` (`DefinitionOrigin::is_binding_made`), whatever the definition prints: aas_support's real `\and`
    (`aas_support_sty.rs:358`), stand-ins for a class's column break printing a space or nothing (colm2025
    `colm2025_conference_sty.rs:23-24` `\And`/`\AND`, `jmlr_cls.rs:104` and `jmlr2e_sty.rs:35` `\And`, `jair_sty.rs:22,24`
    `\hskip`, `neurips_sty.rs:145-146` no-ops), a word (`ims_support_sty.rs:51` `\AND`), a `&`
    (`elsart_support_sty.rs:280` `\AND`), amsmath's math `\And` (`amsmath_sty.rs:1960`, no separator). A binding's `\let` copy of the kernel `\and` (`inst_support_sty.rs:66` `\AND`, `ijcai_sty.rs:33-34` `\AND`/`\And`, `epl_cls.rs:109` `\And`) is `Kernel`: its definition is `\and`'s own. Enumerated by grep
    of `\\and"`/`\\And"`/`\\AND"` on definition lines in `latexml_package/src`, `latexml_contrib/src`,
    `latexml_engine/src`. `Binding` alone says neither "a separator" nor "none". The P2 callers' gates (below) ask kernel
    or not, which needs no split; a caller that must tell them apart reads its own binding's definition. A caller swapping
    a spelling gate (l_aa, ecai test the token `\and`/`\And`; authblk did until P2-7) for `Kernel` changes the answer
    wherever `Binding` or `Raw` arises.
  - `Raw`: a raw file's, the document's, or no separator's meaning.

  The printing token is the one the separator's own run covers where it is no macro, else the family command (a macro holding
  the separator, a class's macro `\and` or its `\let` copy, a `\csname and\endcsname`). Trap T8: the rehearsal binds
  `\and`/`\And`/`\AND` to its event whatever the class means (`ALWAYS_BOUND`), so a `Sep` alone does not say the class
  parts names there (smfart's `&`, 2508.07946); a gate asks for the meaning too. The meaning is the call site's: a class
  that defines or `\let`s `\and` only inside its title macro is read as the kernel's there, as `kernel_and_list` reads it —
  jmlr.cls's word `\and` (jmlr.cls:336, inside `\jmlrpreauthor`, run by its `\maketitle`) answers `kernel` at `\author`
  while the title prints "Ann Able and Bob Baker" (Known RED `separators_query_jmlr_title_time_and_red`; a title-time
  reading is a mechanism of its own). `None`: a call inside a rehearsal (no journal opens), over the queries' allowance,
  a run whose assignments could not be undone (they stay, as any rehearsal's), or one that left a group open (no kernel
  author line holds a `\begingroup` without its `\endgroup`).
- *The emitter's cut of a numbered contact call* (`emit::labelseq_call_cut`, `labelseq_piece`): a `labelseq=` contact call
  the reading cuts at its `\and`s (`resolver::api::labelseq_pieces`, now shared by the reading and the emitter, as
  `creator_call_pieces` is) is written as one call per piece — the call's own command, keyvals and wrappers kept
  (`with_content`), the piece alone, the reading's label — where the reading numbered it (`api:labelseq`). The cut is
  OC1c's (#993), extracted unchanged as `cut_at_separators` (by tokens where each `\and` parts no ink; else by text, one
  counted Warning per piece written); a contact call's own content is the group when no wrapper group holds the `\and`s.
  Before, the emitter wrote the whole call for each entry (every author held "Univ X and Univ Y", the kernel `\and`
  printing the word). The cut is made once per call per flush (`emit::CallCuts`), not once per entry. Not cut here, taken
  by the path before it: a call with an `\and` inside a layout container, or a piece holding a mark, a contact or a note
  (an item the reading places apart, which a whole piece would print again) — `\institute{Univ X \email{a@x} \and Univ
  Y}` is written by text, each author's institute (one counted Warning each), the e-mail to its owner.

**Who calls them** (P2-4: eptcs's cells, the query, `eptcs_cls.rs` `cells`; P2-2: OmniBus's and aa's `\institute`, the
query through `split_at_kernel_separators`, below; P2-5: l_aa, ecai, interact, pasj00, gretsi, lipics,
`and_by_meaning::and_runs`; P2-7: authblk's two `\author` gates, the query, `authblk_sty.rs` `separated_by_and`, #993's
P2-7). **Who will call them** (the P2P batches, by its rule-6 scan: `lx@splitting`, `split_tokens(`, `SplitDelim::`, literal
`\and`/`\And`/`\AND` in `latexml_package/src`, `latexml_contrib/src`, `frontmatter_stores.rs`, `base_utilities/defs`,
`frontmatter/classify`): the emitter's cut — P2-2 (S2: `inst_support_sty.rs:58`, `aa_cls.rs:93` and its gate :75-80,
`sv_support_sty.rs:69`; P22b took the first two through the query instead, below), P2-3 (llncs `:189`, gate :208), P2-6 (the numbered stores, `frontmatter_stores.rs:3148-3151`);
the query — P2-2 (aa :80), P2-5 (`l_aa_cls.rs:108`, `latexml_contrib/src/ecai_cls.rs:56`), P2-6
(`frontmatter_stores.rs` :3216, :3225 `kernel_and_list`, :3239, :3378, :7483, :7697). Not enumerated by that scan (P2P's list): the engine beyond those directories (observer, insert, place);
`split_top_level_lines` (revtex, relocate); `\lx@split@addresses`; `frontmatter_api/` (affiliations.rs:416-429,
line_marks.rs:16, cut.rs, kind.rs: P4); `classify/separators.rs:212-224`, `name_text.rs:36`,
`old_reader/space_parted.rs:205`, ijcai.rs (P3/P4); splits on `\\` alone or commas; `\def\and{…}` meanings (argument
passing, stays). The scan is heuristic (one macro level, no class-file wrappers).

**P2-2 (P22b, P22c): landed by the binding's cut, not the emitter's.** OmniBus's `\institute` (`inst_support_sty.rs`,
which webofc and ieeetj load too) and aa's (`aa_cls.rs` `\lx@aa@institute@dispatch`) cut their list first at the
kernel's `\and` by meaning, then each segment at `\and`/`\And` by spelling, and queue one `\lx@add@contact[role=affiliation,labelseq=affiliation]`
call per piece, so the reading and the emitter see the calls they saw before. The one shared helper is
`observer/separators.rs` `kernel_separator_runs` (re-exported with `split_at_kernel_separators`): the own runs
(`ArgSeparator::span`) of the separators the query reads `Kernel`, each whole units of the argument's top level (no
group or environment holds them), `None` where the query reads nothing; eptcs's `cells` (P2-4) now calls it instead
of its own copy (its unit scanners moved unchanged to `base_utilities/tokens.rs`, beside `split_tokens`:
`tokens_top_level_units`, `tokens_unit_end`, `tokens_read_argument`, `tokens_environment_end`).
`split_at_kernel_separators(arg, delims)` cuts `arg` at every such run where it stands, as eptcs's `cells` does, and
splits each segment between the runs by spelling unchanged (`tokens.rs` `split_tokens_segment`: its trimming, its
protection of braces, math, parentheses and environments inside the segment, and its empty last piece dropped on the
list's last segment only — a segment a run ends keeps it, as the whole list's split keeps the piece a delimiter ends);
no token is rewritten. It returns the pieces with the number of runs that hold no delimiter by `split_tokens`' match
(`tokens.rs` `delimiter_token_matches`): the cuts by meaning alone. What it adds: a macro holding only `\and`, and a
`\let` copy of the kernel's `\and` made before the document renews `\and` (the spelling's alias match reads the renewed
meaning). A run inside balanced parentheses, which the spelling split protects, is cut too, as TeX's column break parts
them — a written kernel `\and` as well as a copy or a macro-held one (`Univ A (North \myand South), Town` gives
"Univ A (North" and "South), Town"; pdflatex breaks the column there) — and a macro-held `\and` opening or closing the
list is a cut with nothing on its far side ("Univ A" and "Univ B" where the base gave "and Univ A" and "Univ B and";
pdflatex prints no "and"). In each the base had written an "and" the PDF does not print, which the content check
counted with a Warning (revP22c N1, synthetic).
P22b's first form wrote each missed run as a literal `\and` and let the spelling split cut it: where the split protected
the run (in parentheses) the piece printed what `\and` meant then, not the author's token — after `\let\myand\and
\renewcommand\and{\unskip, }`, "Univ A (North, South)" for the base's "(North and South)" (review revP22b B1); cutting
first rewrites nothing. T8: a separator the spelling cut keeps
its cut whatever the query says it means (`Raw`: a document's renewed `\and`, an undefined `\And`; `Binding`: amsmath's
`\And`), since today's output depends on it and aa.cls's title-time `\and` (:866) parts its institutes there whatever the
preamble made of it; a macro holding institutes and the separator together has no span and stays one piece, which the
reading cuts (pins rows 3 and 6). Routes changed (rule 6):
- `inst_support_sty.rs` `\institute`: `\lx@splitting` → `\lx@splitting@by@meaning` (`base_utilities/defs/general.rs`,
  `\lx@splitting`'s expansion shared as `split_calls`);
- `aa_cls.rs` `\lx@aa@institute@dispatch`: the gate counts each cut by meaning alone made on top of the written top-level
  `\and`s (a macro-held `\and` gives two pieces, not the sole institute; aa.cls's own count misses it, its title-time
  `\and` numbers it), and the dispatch writes the pieces' calls itself (`split_calls`; `\lx@aa@institute@split`
  deleted), so each cut by meaning the gate counts is one the calls are made from (revP22b S1: P22b counted a run its
  split then protected, one piece sent to the split route rather than the sole institute's). A written `\and` at the
  argument's top level that the spelling split protects (inside `$…$` or an environment) is still counted and not cut,
  as on the base (revP22c N2; no pdflatex-clean shape found);
- `eptcs_cls.rs` `cells`: the shared helper, no change of output.

Not routed, open: sv_support (`sv_support_sty.rs:71`; each piece's `\at` is parsed as it expands, `\lx@sv@institute@`,
so that reading moves first); llncs routed in P2-3, below. Byte-identical against the spelling split (`2ff10b7ff9`, `kit/conv.sh`) on 3,006 papers
(aa 563, sv 406, OmniBus 200, webofc 30, eptcs 73, raw-class 300, stage2 1,434; 6 with no main file), E/F/W equal on
each; 0909.4443's one difference is a run-to-run math-id variance of the base (both binaries give one md5 on a rerun).
That run was P22b's form; the cut-first form (P22c) is byte-identical against the same base on 1,811 of them: all of

E/F/W equal on each; 0909.4443 as above, its md5 that of P22b's).

and the pins
`perfect_kernel_batchp22::an_institute_list_split_by_spelling_today`, unchanged.

²South)") — read by the separator query at every level (`separators.rs` `argument_separators_at_every_level`, the
query's own events without its own-level filter; unread, the spelling); else (c) the superscript-labelled block or (b)
the sole institute, as before. Not at every level: the query records no `\and` inside a contact call's argument, so an
`\and` inside `\email{…}`, which `\institutename` numbers all the same (llncs.cls:875), leaves one piece and takes the
sole-institute shape — each author the institute and one e-mail, a pairing pdflatex does not print (int160a1 gave the
block both; synthetic, no corpus reach; RED `class-bindings/institute_one_call/llncs_institute_and_inside_an_email_numbers_the_list_red.tex`,
review revP23). A document macro holding institutes and `\and` together (`\newcommand\insts{Univ A \and Univ B}`,
unmarked authors) moves likewise, from every author to the block, as pdflatex numbers both. A document macro holding only `\and` now parts the list: with marked authors int160a1
gave the same XML (the sole institute's reading cut it), with unmarked ones it took the sole institute and gave both
institutes to every author, a pairing pdflatex does not print; now the two numbered institutes are the block's, as the
written `\and` gives them (85b's `llncs_several_institutes_without_marks_stay_the_blocks`). The marked `\author` list
(`\lx@llncs@author@split`) is cut the same way at the call (`\lx@splitting@by@meaning{\lx@add@author@split}{\and\And\\}`),
one queued entry per piece: a macro-held `\and` now makes two entries, so the superscript-labelled institute's e-mail
line, one address per author, goes to the authors in order (int160a1: one entry, the line the block's). An unmarked
list stays one block (Z18e). `\lx@splitting`'s one caller left is `sv_support_sty.rs`'s `\institute`. Not done, the
brief's aim: the marked list as one `\lx@add@author@split` block the reading cuts. Tried (patch kept in the P23 report):
on llncs's 699 papers 9 changed, all worse — 4 lose an `\{…\}@…` address line's per-author addresses to the block
(2403.04183, 2409.06210, 2412.12966, 2512.24562; repros `llncs_marked_block_ambiguous_spelling_is_no_place.tex`,
`marked_affiliation_list_email_line_leaves_no_empty_contact.tex`), because the queue's positions
(`queue_reading.rs` `queued_author_marks`, `queued_requesters`, the Cut's `place_address_runs` count) and the resolver's
`author:N` (`Resolver::author_entries`) count queued entries, not names; parting the queue's entries by
`entry_names` alone moved the labels to positions the resolver does not count (the plan's P4 row, which owns both;
P2-3b below parts both); 2
read a marked names line after `\and \\` as an affiliation (1902.08498, 2605.10631, Z18b's shape); 2407.13764,
2607.15806, 2607.21595 moved a mark or a URL line. RED catalog repro
`class-bindings/author_one_block/llncs_comma_parted_marked_list_email_line_is_the_blocks_red.tex` (a comma-parted marked
list is one entry today too). Byte-identical against int160a1 (`1f3949ecad`, `kit/conv.sh`) on 2,430 papers (llncs 699,
stage2 1,434, raw-class 300, the binding's 12 comment witnesses; 4 with no main file), E/F/W equal on each;
hep-ph0502035's one difference is a run-to-run math-id variance of the base (two reruns give the candidate's md5).
Guard rows in `perfect_kernel_batchp22b::an_institute_list_cut_at_the_kernel_and_by_meaning` (repros
`class-bindings/institute_one_call/llncs_{institute_list_macro_held_separator_unmarked,institute_list_macro_held_separator,institute_list_and_inside_a_box_stays_one_piece,marked_author_list_macro_held_separator}.tex`).
A `\let` copy of `\and` is no llncs input: `\institutename` and `\@maketitle` redefine `\and`, and the copy keeps the
kernel's `\end{tabular}` (pdflatex, 13 errors).

**F0, P4a (2026-11-11): the marks query and the queue's requests on it.** `observer/argument_marks.rs`
`argument_marks` reads an argument's Mark events from the same rehearsal as the separator query
(`separators::read_argument`, the queries' one allowance, `rehearsal::for_a_query`): marks at the argument's own level (#1009), outside its notes, no number suffix;
`None` is unread, never "no marks". The queue's reading (`queue_reading.rs`) rehearses each queued author's name once
(`queued_name`) and keys its requests by the printed text, as `\lx@sup@request@affiliation` does (#919:

printing the mark (`\newcommand\ua{\textsuperscript{1}}`) now requests its label, and the Cut's uncut copies give way
by the same requests (`cut.rs` `place_uncut_copies` asked `queued_requesters`, since P4b2 the decision's
`requested_entry_labels`; its token loop and `requesting_authors` deleted, review revF0 B1: amsart's `\address` list repeated under macro-printed marks kept the uncut copy and lost the
cut's unrequested entry). Deleted: the meaning tracking
(`meanings_hold`, the commands and symbols seen), so a name read before a later `\let` keeps its first reading
(`queue_reading_alias_after_names`: same creators, the Cut no longer re-cuts). An unread name falls back to its spelled
operands, one `--debug=frontmatter_marks` line each, until P6. Kept on the token reading until P4c, which shows the
mark on the binding cut (FIDELITY_CHARTER §2): `affiliation_is_marked`, the stores' gates
(`queue::queued_creators_have_marks`) and the names' `name_marks_of`; else a macro-held mark moved the list onto the binding cut, which drops the
printed marks. Byte-identical against int160c on 494 papers (300 author_marks, 148 author_user_mark_macro, 50
raw-class marked; 3 without a main file), E/F/W equal, 0 fallback lines. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batchc1::queued_marks_read_as_digested` (rows `queue_marks_ams_macro_marks_{three_entry_copies,
repeated_list}` for B1); RED catalog repros `sectioning-frontmatter/llncs_macro_held_institute_list_comma_red.tex`
(P4S risk R2) and `revtex_accented_name_mark_lost_red.tex` (a name's accented mark lost, pre-existing).

**FMK1 (2026-11-12): a math character's glyph is ink.** Our `\mathchar`, `\delimiter`, `\Udelimiter` and `\mathaccent`
are whatsits carrying the character in their `glyph` property (`tex_math.rs`, `latex_constructs_rust_only.rs`), where
Perl's `\mathchar` is a Box of it (`TeX_Math.pool.ltxml:576-580`); the text walkers read no property but `alignment` and
`text`, so a script of `\mathchar`s printed nothing. flexisym makes digits, letters and punctuation math-active
`\mathchar`s (`\DeclareFlexSymbol`, flexisym.sty:244-258; cmbase.sym:68, 77, 128), so under it the marks query read `$^{2,3}$` as no mark
(2312.00656: uai2023 + authblk[noblocks] + flexisym; F0's reading gave 7 creators without their marks and every
affiliation on each, no Warning). `util_text::printed_own_text` (FMK1's `printed_glyph`) gives the glyph a whatsit prints
where it shows nothing else — since LOGO1 also a constant constructor template's text (`\LaTeX`, `\TeX`, `\LaTeXe`: amsldoc's
`\author{…, \LaTeX\ Project}` was the creator "Project", no Warning; guard `perfect_kernel_batchlogo1`) —
and each reader of a whatsit's print reads it: `ink_text` (the observer's event text), `ink_word_text` (the title page
check), `typesets_content`, the observer's `script_ink` (a mark's label) and `queue_digest::label_ink` (a printed
label). Under flexisym a name's marks now read as without it (the authblk twin row without flexisym).
A/B against int162a on 476 papers (177
flexisym/breqn, 199 author_marks, 100 controls): E/F equal, 3 changed, all flexisym — 1809.04032 and 1903.10294 better
(each author's own affiliation and e-mail by the marks), 2312.00656 back to int161a's shape (authblk's trailing note:
RED `authblk_noblocks_trailing_note_list_red`). Guard `perfect_kernel_batchc1::queued_marks_read_as_digested` (rows
`queue_marks_flexisym_{authblk_noblocks_list,authblk_boxed_note,ieeetran_line,letter_symbol_marks}` and the twin
`queue_marks_authblk_noblocks_list`).

**P2-8a (P28): IEEEtran's routes and grid read the body by meaning.** IEEEtran's `\author` (`ieeetran_cls.rs`
`\author`) and authblk's (`\lx@IEEE@authblk@author`) chose their route by the body's spelling
(`contains("authorblockN")`) and read the grid's `\and`/`\\` on tokens: a body held in a macro took the plain route (one
nameless creator, the names lost), a wrapper's call (`\pair{…}{…}` printing `#1\and#2`, `\cell{…}{…}` printing a
block pair) was read as bare text by the block route's token steps (creators scrambled or doubled), blocks written
through `\let` copies of the block commands lost an author (Bob Baker lost, Ann Able twice), a row break held in a
macro or a `\let` copy of `\and` left the grid in column order, and a names list held in a macro on the plain route
lost its grades (`name_memberships` read `\aut`; since P5a the grade is the reading's contact, #1016, kept either way).
Both routes now read the body by meaning before the route:
`blocks_as_printed` expands each top-level call of a document macro holding author structure (a names block,
`\and`/`\And`/`\AND`, `\\`, or a token meaning one, in its definition or a document macro it calls, read as
`rehearsal::let_copies_of_bound_commands` reads a block's macros), `with_block_names` writes every `\let` copy of a
block command as the command (it read only the two old names), and the route is whether the body then calls
`\IEEEauthorblockN` (`calls_names_block`; the spelling test is deleted). The grid's columns are the separators the
query reads at the body's brace level (`grid_columns`, `argument_separators`, whatever they mean: IEEEtran's
`\and` is its column whatever a document made it, as the spelling read it); where the query is unread or a
separator's tokens print something else too (`span` `None`), `split_top_level` cuts as before, reading a `\let` copy
of `\and` as the command; rows are the top-level `\\` (or a copy). The brief's routing through `argument_separators`
was taken for the grid's columns, not the route: the route asks whether the body calls a names block, which the
separator query does not answer. Rule 6, the routes changed and kept:
- changed: both routes (`calls_names_block` after `blocks_as_printed` and `with_block_names`, replacing
  `contains("authorblockN")`); the grid's columns (`grid_columns`, `split_top_level` its fallback); rows and the
  fallback's columns by meaning (`split_top_level`, `Token::defined_as`); `with_block_names` (any `\let` copy);
- kept: `transpose_ieee_author_grid`'s token transposition — the grid rule over `Sep(And)` × `Break` in the reading
  needs the grid's events, which the reading lacks (each `\IEEEauthorblockN` is its own `\lx@add@authors@append` block
  in the ledger, `defs/author_macros.rs` `record_author_call`; the separators and row breaks between blocks are never
  recorded); a block-call fact (the whole `\author` argument one ledger block, its blocks the reading's) comes first;
- kept: `unnested_name_blocks`, `wrap_bare_author_block_text` (and its `document_notes`);
- P2-8b: `printed_refmarks` (`name_memberships` and `block_name_memberships` deleted by P5a, #1016).

Byte-identity against int158a on IEEEtran's census papers, ieeeconf's, the stage2 1,434 and the raw-class 300: the
P28 report; merged onto int168a (P28m), its A/B against int168a: the P28m report. On int168a the names blocks a
document macro holds keep their grades: `blocks_as_printed` writes the blocks before P5a's `block_grade_stops` and
`\lx@IEEE@grade` read them (#1016). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchp28::{ieee_grids_read_by_rows_and_lists_keep_their_order,
ieee_plain_route_reads_names_and_grades, ieee_block_calls_by_meaning_take_the_block_route,
ieee_wrapper_calls_are_read_as_they_print, ieee_grid_row_and_column_by_meaning}`; repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/{ieeetran_author_grid_two_by_two_reads_by_rows,ieeetran_author_grid_three_by_two_reads_by_rows,ieeetran_author_grid_with_marks_and_a_note,ieeetran_author_blocks_one_row_keep_their_order,ieeetran_author_blocks_one_column_keep_their_order,ieeetran_author_plain_route_reads_names_and_grades,ieeetran_author_grid_in_a_macro,ieeetran_author_grid_regular_in_a_macro,ieeetran_author_grid_through_a_wrapper,ieeetran_author_grid_wrapper_cells_in_rows,ieeetran_author_grid_row_break_in_a_macro,ieeetran_author_grid_let_copy_of_and,ieeetran_author_blocks_let_copies_of_the_block_commands,ieeetran_author_blocks_in_a_macro_keep_their_grades,ieeetran_author_plain_route_names_in_a_macro}.tex`.
`blocks_as_printed` leaves a body no such macro reaches as it is (a document macro printing layout only, `\linebreakand`,
is left to digestion) and a macro inside a group (a block's argument) to its block; `with_block_names` writes a copy only
while it means the command (a document may define `\authorblockN` its own way, as `\authorrefmark` in
`printed_refmarks`), before the route and again in `author_block_body` (authblk's labelled path left `\authorblockN`
its own: a nameless creator, the names lost, #987).

**When the body is read (P28m2).** pdflatex's `\author` stores its argument (`\def\@author{#1}`) and `\maketitle`
expands it, with the definitions in force there; the block route reads it at `\author`, as its blocks are author calls
the queue holds. So the class's `\author` keeps the body and its reading (`\lx@IEEE@author@reread`), and the next
outermost flush (`place.rs` `digest_front_matter`, through `queue.rs` `reread_author_body_at_flush`) reads it again
before its rehearsal: where the reading now differs (`\renewcommand\aut` after `\author` or in `\AtBeginDocument`, a
`\g@addto@macro`, `\aut` or a `\let` copy defined only after `\author`), the route is taken again, its
`begin_author_body` taking back what the first call queued and its ledger blocks (`record_author_body_clear`, the last
block too), and the resolver keeps none of a cleared block's items, a nameless one's too (`cleared_blocks`); an
unchanged reading digests nothing. Before it, P2-8a printed the macro's definition at `\author` (revP28m S1: Ann Able
and Bob Baker invented, the printed Cy Coe lost, silently). authblk's `\author` drops a pending reread (it appends;
the class's route would take its authors back) and still reads its body at the call. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batchp28::ieee_author_body_read_at_the_flush`; repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/{ieeetran_author_macro_renewed_after_author,ieeetran_author_macro_renewed_at_begin_document,ieeetran_author_macro_defined_after_author,ieeetran_author_plain_macro_renewed_after_author}.tex`.
Read so, a macro-held body reaches the marked-address placement of the written one: 2510.10414's
`\IEEEauthorblockN{\varAuthors}\varInstitutions` put Ben-Jian Dong's address on a nameless creator until that placement
read the mark (P28m3, #52(j)'s marked affiliation list). Guard
`perfect_kernel_batchp28::marked_block_address_goes_to_the_name_showing_the_mark`.
RED, post-merge (P28C): an anonymous-review conditional (`\ifblind Anonymous Authors\else <blocks>\fi`), literal or in
the macro, reads its printed words as a nameless creator's affiliation
(`ieeetran_author_blind_conditional{,_in_a_macro}_red.tex`).
The take-back is generic: the resolver's `cleared_blocks` drops every item of a block a later `\author` clears, in every class that
clears (the kernel `\author`, llncs, aa, sv as well as IEEEtran) — svjour3's `\author{\thanks{Grant Q.} \\ Univ Q}` replaced by a second
`\author` no longer keeps a nameless "Univ Q" creator and its note, as LaTeX's replaced `\@author` prints neither (revP28m2; no non-IEEE
guard row yet: post-merge P28G).

**P2-3b (P23b, 2026-11-12): the queue's `author:N` positions count names.** An author entry a binding's whole-list call
queued (`\lx@add@author@split`: sv_support's, aa's, OmniBus's, webofc's, ptephy's, llncs's unmarked `\author`;
`ledger::queuing_hook`) holds one position a name the reading parts it into at the `\and` family (`queue_reading.rs`
`entry_pieces`: `entry_names`). Every reader of the positions reads that one numbering:
`queued_author_marks`, `queued_requesters`, `queued_author_name_keys` (per piece), `queued_author_positions` (the Cut's
`place_address_runs` count, `placed_contact_owner`, the OSA group's `_group`, `\lx@add@authors@list`'s start),
`queued_row_start`, `positions_of_last_entries` (`relocate.rs`' REVTeX group rule), `sequenced_contact_labels`
(`queued_position_names`, read before the flush takes the queue). The count is recorded on the ledger block that queued
the entry (`ledger::record_entry_names`, the block found by its flush and queue position), and the resolver counts by it (`Input::Block::names`, `Resolver::author_entries`):
the n-th position the block's n-th creator where the reading made one a name, else each the whole entry (the spelling
decides an e-mail, as for one name's entry). A whole-list `\author` with an e-mail line of one address a name now gives
one address to each author (int169a: the block's); 1308.2757's llncs list (`\and\\`, five addresses for five names,
"mehrabi@" spelling two Mehrabis) gives Saeed Mehrabi his by order, as the PDF lists them. The kernel `\author`'s block
stayed one position (until P2-3c, below): parted, two names requesting a raw class's numbered institute (`class_numbered_institutes`) send its
one e-mail line back into the store's entry, whose call the emitter cannot cut, and the address is lost (astro-ph0508574's
cjaa.cls, 0911.3853's mem.cls; lost on int169a too with two addresses: fixed by P2-3c, below). llncs's marked list stays
cut at the call: one block (tried, by rows and whole) reads `\inst{1,2}*` beside another name's `\inst{1*}` as a shown
"∗" too (2407.13764; the same on int169a under aa/OmniBus: fixed by P2-3c, below), and whole, a names
row after `\and \\` as an affiliation (1902.08498, 2605.10631). A comma-parted marked list stays one position (the
reading's comma cut is not readable at the call: RED `llncs_comma_parted_marked_list_email_line_is_the_blocks_red`), as
does a macro printing names and the separator together (RED `svjour3_marked_list_macro_holding_names_and_separator_red`).
A/B against int169a (`632698e1d8`) on 2,630 papers (llncs 635, aa/svjour3/webofc/ptephy 153, stage2 1,432, raw-class
298, the 12 witnesses, 100 controls): 1 changed (1308.2757), E/F/W equal. `instructions:u` (median of 5 interleaved runs
against int169a) +0.38 % (2103.04797), +0.14 % (1901.01540), XML identical. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batchp23b::a_whole_list_entry_holds_a_position_a_name` (repros
`class-bindings/author_one_block/{svjour3,aa,omnibus}_marked_list_email_line_one_address_a_name.tex`,
`svjour3_marked_list_{marks_in_a_note_and_a_box,address_under_one_names_affiliation,macro_holding_only_the_separator}.tex`).

**P2-3c (P23c, 2026-11-12): two readings a whole-list block needs.** (1) *A name's `\inst` marks are its own.* The
emitter keeps a kept name's `\inst` request only where the reading made it this name's (`RCreator::class_requests`, the
resolver's `class_requests` moved onto the creator, read by `answer_pending`, `share_unpicked` and the emitter alike);
read per block, a `*` printed after Ann's `\inst{1,2}` matched Bob's `\inst{1*}` and was shown again as "∗" beside the
"*" her name keeps (2407.13764's shape under aa and OmniBus). (2) *An e-mail command printing nowhere in a numbered store's run.* A
class's numbered store (`class_numbered_institutes`) is read without the e-mail command of a line of addresses where
that command, digested with the meaning TeX runs (a raw file's rerouted setter's own, #936), prints nothing in place —
its addresses in `\@thanks`, a note, nowhere (the speculative run's text outside its notes, `queue_digest::printed_ink`;
`Contact\footnote{#1}` prints its "Contact" in place, so its line stays whole). The store's
call decides it, on the store's lines (`\lx@add@store@affiliations`, `classify::store_unprinted_emails_unwrapped`): no
flag reaches the cutter, whose address-line readers read a raw command's line and its addresses alike
(`email_line_calls` sets a raw command's address as written, `email_command_address`). Such a line under an entry, not
one address of the one author requesting it, goes back into the entry, so the entry's Kind step takes its addresses
out and its Link step gives each the author it spells (#956); left wrapped, cjaa.cls's `\email` (its address set in
`\@thanks`) printed nowhere and the addresses were lost, counted (astro-ph0508574, 0706.3426). A command printing in
place (mem.cls's `{e-mail: \tt#1}`, a document macro with prose) keeps the line whole, every word kept and the label
placed twice, counted (RED `raw_class_in_place_email_label_under_numbered_institute_red`); a binding's call makes its
contacts where it stands. A binding's list (aa, IEEEtran) is never unwrapped. A/B against P23b (`49b1490df2`) on
P23b's 2,630 papers and 164 raw classes with `\institute` and `\inst`: 0 changed; narrowed (P23d) against P23c on 923
(the review's 769 `\and` lists with marks, notes or e-mail commands, the 164, 13 cjaa/mem witnesses): 1 changed,
0911.3853's mem.cls line whole again (its printed "e-mail:" and typewriter kept in the contact, one Warning more).
Decided at the store's call (P23e, no flag threaded into the cutter): the same 923 against P23c, the same 1 changed,
byte-identical to P23d's; 2103.04797 −0.03 % instructions, XML identical.
(3) *The kernel `\author`'s list holds a position a name* (`entry_pieces` reads `\lx@add@authors@adaptive`'s entries as
`\lx@add@author@split`'s): a raw class's numbered store with an e-mail line of one address a name after its last entry
gives each author one, in order (the block's before). Two readers follow: `author_creator_total` (the `\lx@author@keys`
ranges an `\author[key]` records) counts positions (`queued_author_positions`), and `ledger::record_entry_names` records
whenever the reading reads (a replayed class setter's read is kept by the queue's reading; a replay or a rehearsal queues
no block, so none is found for its entries) — review revP23b's two findings. A/B against D1+D2 (`5096ce95c6`) on P23b's
2,630 papers, 448 kernel `\author` lists (article, amsart, revtex, report, amsproc; `\and`, an e-mail, `\thanks` or
marks) and 141 raw classes alike: 2 changed, astro-ph0508574 better (W.H. Gao's e-mail after the institute it is printed
under), 2210.01917 a 180 s timeout on both alone (noise). Guard row `kernel list, raw class store` of
`a_whole_list_entry_holds_a_position_a_name` (repro `class-bindings/author_one_block/kernel_raw_class_email_line_one_address_a_name.tex`). llncs's marked list stays
cut at the call: as one block a row (cut at its `\\`s only, its `\and`s the reading's) a row of names each led by its
`\inst` mark is read as affiliation entries (`\inst{1}Ann Able \and \inst{2}Bob Baker \and \inst{3}Cat Cole`: no author,
the guarded `llncs_inst_leading_marks_keep_their_names` lost) — the same reading as aa's and OmniBus's whole list on the
base (RED `class-bindings/author_one_block/aa_leading_inst_marks_names_read_as_affiliations_red.tex`, int169a too) and as
the whole list's names row after `\and \\` (1902.08498, 2605.10631). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchp23b::{a_star_after_an_inst_mark_is_the_names_text,

### 996. What is appended to `\@author` after the author setter stored it is the author block's continuation: rows before its first `\and`, more authors after it, also under a binding whose `\author` stores nothing in `\@author` (FX24; RR1 gap 24)

**Perl.** `\author` reads only its argument (`latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1076-1079`
`\def\@shortauthor{#1}\def\@author{#2}\lx@add@authors{#2}`), and `\maketitle` clears `\@author` without printing it
(:1099-1107): whatever a class or document appends to `\@author` after the call (`\g@addto@macro\@author{…}`) is lost.

**Now.** LaTeX's `\@maketitle` prints `\@author` whole (article.cls:247), so the tail is printed with the names. Since
59d each kernel `\author` call's tail without `\and` is handed to the creators that call made, as author-block rows
(`\lx@author@handed`, `\lx@author@flush`, `\lx@author@tail`). FX24 (frontmatter_stores.rs `author_tail_calls`):
- *A tail holding `\and`* (`\newcommand\coauthor[1]{\g@addto@macro\@author{\and #1}}`; jaa.cls, pramana.cls
  `\addauthor`) is split at its first top-level `\and`, by spelling as the stores' other tail reads are (#995):
  what comes before it is rows of the call's creators (`row_calls`, unchanged), what follows one more author block,
  `\lx@add@authors@append{…}`, read as an `\author` argument is (split at its own `\and`s, a `\\` line under a name its
  affiliation). Before, such a tail was dropped whole and, with the title-page check gluing the words around `\and`
  (FX25), uncounted.
- *A binding whose `\author` stores nothing in `\@author` and whose class prints it with what is appended*: the
  binding declares it in its frontmatter conventions (`TitlePageDecl::author` `AuthorPage::Block`: authblk, whose own
  `\@author` prints the block, authblk.sty:167-171; llncs, whose `\@maketitle` prints `\@author`, llncs.cls:1035), read
  off the binding owning the `\author` meaning (`ledger::author_tail_declared`). `queue_front_matter` records `\@author`'s
  value as each creator is queued (`note_author_seen`, `lx_author_seen`; the kernel `\author`'s `\lx@author@handed`
  clears it). At `\maketitle`, with no kernel call handed, the tail after that value is read the same way, its rows
  every queued creator's (the line is printed under the whole block). amsart's title page prints `\authors` (its
  `\g@addto@macro\@author{\and Bob B}` makes no creator; pdflatex prints only the first author), elsarticle's
  `\elsauthors`, the fallback class's (OmniBus, inst_support) is unknown (a tail there stays out of the output, named by
  the title-page check as annotated, an Info, where the binding declares its class's own author page or the class is
  OmniBus's guess; elsewhere a Warning: #953 "FX27").
- *Either route reads a tail only where the title page in force prints it* (TP1, #953 "TP1"; FX24b's walk before): at
  `\maketitle` the title-page reading's run answers where code a raw file or the document wrote ran without
  article.cls's stand-in (its tail mark printed or not; amsart under a document's `\@maketitle` printing `\@author` reads
  the tail, FX26's RED, now `amsart_author_tail_printed_by_document_maketitle_is_kept`); else the walk
  (`own_title_page_prints_author`): a stand-in copy's title page answers for itself (`copy_title_page_prints`); else the
  refused `\maketitle` (`\lx@dropped@maketitle`), or else a `\@maketitle`, that a raw file or the document defined is
  walked through the live code it reaches (`reads_of_branches` over `executed_code`, following the macros of File or
  Document origin): it prints `\@author` when it reads it, or reaches LaTeX's or a binding's `\maketitle`/`\@maketitle`
  by its current meaning; reaching the kernel's marker (`\lx@kernel@maketitle`, directly or in a `\let` copy), the page is
  the class's, as with neither definition: the binding's declaration answers (`ledger::author_tail_declared`; LaTeX's
  `\author` prints it). Before `\maketitle` (an appending `\author`'s flush) the walk and the declaration alone answer. A
  document's `\renewcommand\maketitle` or `\def\@maketitle` printing only the title, a raw class's own title page, or its
  `\maketitle`/`\@maketitle` over `\LoadClass{article}` print no tail, so none is read — neither more authors nor 59d's
  rows (review revFX24 finding 1). The speculative title-page run's sentinels (`before_title_page_runs`) do not answer
  here: `\@author` is never one of their candidates. A document that adds to LaTeX's `\@maketitle` or redefines it through
  a `\let` copy of it now has its tail read (revFX24b's REDs, now `article_author_tail_under_appended_maketitle_is_kept`,
  `article_author_tail_under_let_copied_maketitle_is_kept`; guard
  `perfect_kernel_batchfx24::an_author_tail_the_title_page_prints_is_read`). Not covered: a `\let` copy of `\@author`
  taken after the tail and printed by the document's `\@maketitle` (the run marks `\@author`, not the copy): the tail
  lost, counted by the check's Warning (RED `article_author_tail_printed_through_let_copy_of_author_is_lost_red`, guard
  `perfect_kernel_batchfx24::an_author_tail_printed_but_not_read_is_counted`).
- *The binding route's rows* (`row_calls`, FX24b): the tail printed under the whole block is an address the block's
  authors share, the frontmatter API's existing gate `\lx@add@affiliation@shared` (author_macros.rs,
  `shared_affiliation_calls`): its e-mail lines one address run placed as a block's address lines are
  (`place_address_runs`: one address for each author of the row in their order, else each on the author it spells,
  else one contact an address on the block's shared creator), its other lines one author-block row of every creator.
  The kernel route's rows stay 59d's (`affiliation_calls`, one row a line). Placing them inside the moved Cut
  (`frontmatter_api/affiliations.rs`) is fenced (`perfect_kernel_batche0::the_moved_cut_and_kind_take_no_new_decision`).

Witness 2511.15315 (procdoc2/authblk; three e-mails appended under the block, each spelling its author): int158a held
none, FX24 wrote the line on every creator, FX24b gives each address to its author (procdoc2.cls:77's `\@maketitle` reads
`\@author`). Not done (RED repros): a row after an `\author` naming several people goes to all of them where LaTeX prints
it in the last column only (`class_affil_row_after_and_names_goes_to_every_author_red.tex`, 59d's choice); under authblk
a tail appended between two `\author` calls is lost, counted (`authblk_author_tail_before_a_later_author_is_lost_red.tex`:
the later author's record holds the tail); a `\let` copy of `\and` is read as a row
(`article_author_tail_let_and_stays_a_row_red.tex`, the separator-meaning batch's). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batchfx24::{a_coauthor_appended_to_author_is_kept, a_class_coauthor_after_its_rows_is_kept,
an_authblk_coauthor_appended_to_author_is_kept, an_authblk_email_line_appended_to_author_is_kept,
an_author_tail_the_title_page_does_not_print_is_not_read, an_llncs_author_tail_is_kept,
an_amsart_author_append_invents_no_creator}`; repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/{article_coauthor_appended_to_author_is_kept,authblk_coauthor_appended_to_author_keeps_the_name,class_coauthor_appended_to_author_keeps_the_column,authblk_email_row_appended_to_author_goes_to_its_owners,article_author_and_tail_unprinted_by_own_maketitle_makes_no_creator,article_author_row_tail_unprinted_by_own_maketitle_makes_no_row,raw_class_own_maketitle_author_tail_makes_no_creator,raw_class_renewed_maketitle_author_tail_makes_no_creator,raw_class_renewed_at_maketitle_author_tail_makes_no_creator,elsarticle_author_tail_outside_frontmatter_makes_no_creator,authblk_author_tail_unprinted_by_document_maketitle_makes_no_creator,llncs_author_tail_printed_keeps_the_author}.tex`.

### 1009. A binding's marked affiliation list is cut by the API's Cut, as the binding declares it, each mark shown (Option C P4c)

**Perl.** `\IEEEauthorblockA{…}` is one `\lx@add@affiliation` (IEEEtran.cls.ltxml:145) and iopart's `\address{…}` one
`\lx@add@affiliations` (iopart_support.sty.ltxml:53); no list is cut at its marks, so every author gets the whole block,
and `\IEEEauthorrefmark` expands to nothing (IEEEtran.cls.ltxml:154), so Perl prints no mark.

**Rust.** A binding hands its marked list to the one Cut (`frontmatter_api::cut_list`) through
`\lx@add@affiliation@marked`/`@shared` (`author_macros.rs` `marked_list_calls`) with its declaration, `MARKED_LIST_CUT`
(a `CutParameters`): every printed mark cuts it once the names print theirs (`affiliation_is_marked`); an address line
behind an e-mail label is entry text; a printed comma closing the list and the notes after it stay as printed (no part
repeated on every entry); the call's placement (`annotate=new`) is dropped, the marks place the entries. The API's own
Cut keeps `API_CUT` (two requested marks, labelled address lines, the closing separator trimmed, a wrapper's trailing
parts every entry's). Each entry shows its mark (FIDELITY_CHARTER §2, P4S Q1). The binding calls the Cut itself: a
flush digests a block's affiliation with `\lx@annotate@frontmatter` let to its `@now`, which no Cut reads. The marks
gate reads the marks an argument prints at its own level (`argument_marks`, `prints_list_marks`): the level its words
print at, inside the box when one box holds them all (names in a `\parbox` or a tabular, acmart's `\institution{…}`), a
mark at or above it or in a box of its own, one holding no word (`at_own_level`: P4cR1, a `\raisebox` refmark,
2307.12121; apa6's `$^{1}$\mbox{Univ A}`, 2508.05776), a note's leading label counted for a list. The cutter splits the
list at its top level only, so a list printed entirely inside one box is one entry (post-merge RED
`ieee_marked_list_inside_one_parbox_is_one_entry_red`). A cut that labels no entry of a one-entry list leaves it whole
(the call cut again would not end). The binding's own cutter (`binding_cut_list_attr`) and the token gate
(`queued_creators_have_marks`) are deleted.
The binding lists' own cutter (`affiliation_calls`: `\lx@add@affiliations` for l-aa, epl, ijcai, interspeech, ptephy and
beamer, llncs's `\lx@llncs@institute@sup`, the class stores `\lx@add@store@affiliations`/`@authorblock`, the `\author`
tail's `row_calls`) keys a marked entry `_markshown=names` (`cut::mark_shown_attr`, the Cut's own test, which both call):
it shows its mark where the names the flush writes show its label (the one `\lx@sup@setlabel@affiliation` sets from
what the mark prints, where it compares it) — the requests each name's written runs print where
`per_author_marks` keeps its marks, a superscript, no `\inst` or binding request, no creator call's own label
(`emitter::NAMES_SHOWN_LABELS`, `marks_in`; reset at each flush, the outer flush's restored after it; a range mark,
`$^{1-2}$`, is read whole on the names' side, so its entries hide their marks: RED
`llncs_range_mark_names_entries_hidden_red`) — so the names and
the list show or hide each mark together (P4f, P4fb: a printed icon, `\inst{1,3}\textsuperscript{(\Letter)}`, labels
no entry, 2505.02655, 2607.21595, 2609.19654; of 1804.00518's names led by `$^n$` only the first keeps its mark, so
only entry 1 shows its). llncs shape (c) and l-aa show both, as pdflatex and
Perl (whose `\\`-separated institute is the first author's whole); IJCAI, epl and ptephy's `\name`, whose names hide theirs, hide
both, as Perl.
IEEEtran's `\author` reads an `\IEEEauthorblockA` at the top level of another's argument as conference mode prints it,
on rows of its own in the outer's column (IEEEtran.cls:4653-4665): one led by a mark, or after a line of marks alone
(its label, read by the binding's mark reader `leading_line_label`: `\IEEEauthorrefmark{1}`, `$^a$`,
`\textsuperscript{b}`), is lifted out as a block of its own, the outer's text around it bare text again; an unmarked
one is spliced into the outer's lines, a `\\` before and after it (`ieeetran_cls.rs` `unnested_affiliation_blocks`;
1710.07993, 2004.11080, 2107.11588, 2605.02682, 1405.1593: each outer mark had been an affiliation alone, or a nested
marked block went to the wrong authors). A bare run
before the block's `\IEEEauthorblockA` whose lines each lead with an ordinal and then read as a name
(`3\textsuperscript{rd}Cy Cole`, relocate.rs `ordinal_name_line`; not "2nd Floor, Bldg 5") is a names block per line
where a names block leads with an ordinal, the template's name lines (1806.11431; as an affiliation it took the block's
authors).
**Why**: one cut for every printed list; the binding's former cut dropped the marks it cut at (2601.01850, 1204.4183).
**Witnesses**: IEEEtran 1705.01774, 1801.04010, 1504.01072, 1811.06030, 2310.18257, 2511.18221, 2512.10732,
2609.16600 (each the base's entries with their marks shown); 2508.17623 (names in a `\parbox`, the link line kept);
1801.00540 ("Red Hat Inc.," keeps its comma); 2605.05837 (the funding `\thanks` once); iopart 1205.6912; 2307.12121, 2311.01786 (a
`\raisebox` refmark: the e-mail line the names' run), apa6 2508.05776 (each entry its name, the `$^{*}$` note once);
llncs 1209.0041 and l-aa astro-ph0002407 (each entry its mark, P4f); ptephy_v1 1703.03659 (`\affil{1}$^{1}${…}`: one
mark, the names' `\name` marks requests).
**Guard**: `perfect_kernel_batchc1::marked_list_cut_as_its_binding_declares` (32 rows).
**Open (post-merge REDs)**: `ieee_marked_list_email_block_last_address_nameless_red`,
`ieee_marked_list_star_led_names_entries_nameless_red`, `iopart_marked_list_unmarked_first_line_every_authors_red` (the
base's placements, pinned as today with each mark shown); `ieee_nested_affiliation_block_in_group_red` (an inner block
inside a group of the outer's argument stays nested); `ieee_sibling_affiliation_blocks_last_author_only_red` (a second
sibling block after a names block of two goes to the last author, `annotate=new`); the binding lists' cutter under names
hiding their marks hides the entries' too (`llncs_inst_names_marked_institute_marks_hidden_red`,
`beamer_marked_institute_marks_hidden_red`: AUMK) and under names printing none loses them uncounted
(`llncs_unmarked_names_marked_institute_marks_lost_red`); a second llncs `\maketitle` writes its names as text, its
entries on the first block's authors (`llncs_second_maketitle_names_are_text_red`); names led by marks parted at commas
lose every mark past the first uncounted (`llncs_comma_names_led_by_marks_later_marks_lost_red`).
